package motorph.deduction;

import java.math.BigDecimal;

/**
 * SSS contribution from the compensation range table used in CP2.
 * The first threshold the monthly gross is below sets the contribution;
 * at 24,750 and above the contribution is 1,125.
 */
public class SSSDeduction extends Deduction {

    private static final BigDecimal[] THRESHOLDS = amounts(
        "3250", "3750", "4250", "4750", "5250", "5750", "6250", "6750", "7250", "7750",
        "8250", "8750", "9250", "9750", "10250", "10750", "11250", "11750", "12250", "12750",
        "13250", "13750", "14250", "14750", "15250", "15750", "16250", "16750", "17250", "17750",
        "18250", "18750", "19250", "19750", "20250", "20750", "21250", "21750", "22250", "22750",
        "23250", "23750", "24250", "24750"
    );

    private static final BigDecimal[] CONTRIBUTIONS = amounts(
        "135", "157.5", "180", "202.5", "225", "247.5", "270", "292.5", "315", "337.5",
        "360", "382.5", "405", "427.5", "450", "472.5", "495", "517.5", "540", "562.5",
        "585", "607.5", "630", "652.5", "675", "697.5", "720", "742.5", "765", "787.5",
        "810", "832.5", "855", "877.5", "900", "922.5", "945", "967.5", "990", "1012.5",
        "1035", "1057.5", "1080", "1102.5"
    );

    private static final BigDecimal MAX_CONTRIBUTION = new BigDecimal("1125");

    public SSSDeduction() {
        super("SSS");
    }

    /** @param baseAmount combined monthly gross */
    @Override
    public BigDecimal computeDeduction(BigDecimal baseAmount) {
        validateBaseAmount(baseAmount);
        for (int i = 0; i < THRESHOLDS.length; i++) {
            if (baseAmount.compareTo(THRESHOLDS[i]) < 0) {
                return CONTRIBUTIONS[i];
            }
        }
        return MAX_CONTRIBUTION;
    }

    private static BigDecimal[] amounts(String... values) {
        BigDecimal[] result = new BigDecimal[values.length];
        for (int i = 0; i < values.length; i++) {
            result[i] = new BigDecimal(values[i]);
        }
        return result;
    }
}
### /home/user/repo_review/full_repo/testingester-main/6/-/src/motorph/deduction/PhilHealthDeduction.java
package motorph.deduction;

import java.math.BigDecimal;

/**
 * PhilHealth employee share: 3% of monthly gross, split 50/50 with the
 * employer, so the employee pays 1.5%. Minimum 150, maximum 900 (CP2 rules).
 */
public class PhilHealthDeduction extends Deduction {

    private static final BigDecimal PREMIUM_RATE   = new BigDecimal("0.03");
    private static final BigDecimal EMPLOYEE_SHARE = new BigDecimal("2");
    private static final BigDecimal MINIMUM        = new BigDecimal("150");
    private static final BigDecimal MAXIMUM        = new BigDecimal("900");

    public PhilHealthDeduction() {
        super("PhilHealth");
    }

    /** @param baseAmount combined monthly gross */
    @Override
    public BigDecimal computeDeduction(BigDecimal baseAmount) {
        validateBaseAmount(baseAmount);
        BigDecimal share = baseAmount.multiply(PREMIUM_RATE).divide(EMPLOYEE_SHARE);
        return share.max(MINIMUM).min(MAXIMUM);
    }
}
### /home/user/repo_review/full_repo/testingester-main/6/-/src/motorph/deduction/PagIbigDeduction.java
package motorph.deduction;

import java.math.BigDecimal;

/**
 * Pag-IBIG contribution: 1% if monthly gross is 1,500 or less, otherwise 2%,
 * capped at 100 (CP2 rules).
 */
public class PagIbigDeduction extends Deduction {

    private static final BigDecimal LOW_RATE      = new BigDecimal("0.01");
    private static final BigDecimal HIGH_RATE     = new BigDecimal("0.02");
    private static final BigDecimal LOW_THRESHOLD = new BigDecimal("1500");
    private static final BigDecimal MAXIMUM       = new BigDecimal("100");

    public PagIbigDeduction() {
        super("Pag-IBIG");
    }

    /** @param baseAmount combined monthly gross */
    @Override
    public BigDecimal computeDeduction(BigDecimal baseAmount) {
        validateBaseAmount(baseAmount);
        BigDecimal rate = baseAmount.compareTo(LOW_THRESHOLD) <= 0 ? LOW_RATE : HIGH_RATE;
        return baseAmount.multiply(rate).min(MAXIMUM);
    }
}
### /home/user/repo_review/full_repo/testingester-main/6/-/src/motorph/deduction/WithholdingTaxDeduction.java
package motorph.deduction;

import java.math.BigDecimal;

/**
 * Withholding tax from the BIR monthly brackets used in CP2.
 * <p>
 * Unlike the other deductions, the base amount is <b>taxable income</b>:
 * monthly gross minus SSS, PhilHealth, and Pag-IBIG. PayrollProcessor computes
 * those contributions first, then passes the taxable income here.
 * </p>
 */
public class WithholdingTaxDeduction extends Deduction {

    // Upper limit of each bracket (inclusive)
    private static final BigDecimal BRACKET_1_MAX = new BigDecimal("20832");
    private static final BigDecimal BRACKET_2_MAX = new BigDecimal("33332");
    private static final BigDecimal BRACKET_3_MAX = new BigDecimal("66666");
    private static final BigDecimal BRACKET_4_MAX = new BigDecimal("166666");
    private static final BigDecimal BRACKET_5_MAX = new BigDecimal("666666");

    // Amount over which the bracket rate applies
    private static final BigDecimal BRACKET_2_FLOOR = new BigDecimal("20833");
    private static final BigDecimal BRACKET_3_FLOOR = new BigDecimal("33333");
    private static final BigDecimal BRACKET_4_FLOOR = new BigDecimal("66667");
    private static final BigDecimal BRACKET_5_FLOOR = new BigDecimal("166667");
    private static final BigDecimal BRACKET_6_FLOOR = new BigDecimal("666667");

    // Fixed tax at the start of each bracket
    private static final BigDecimal BRACKET_3_BASE_TAX = new BigDecimal("2500");
    private static final BigDecimal BRACKET_4_BASE_TAX = new BigDecimal("10833");
    private static final BigDecimal BRACKET_5_BASE_TAX = new BigDecimal("40833.33");
    private static final BigDecimal BRACKET_6_BASE_TAX = new BigDecimal("200833.33");

    // Rate on the amount over the floor
    private static final BigDecimal BRACKET_2_RATE = new BigDecimal("0.20");
    private static final BigDecimal BRACKET_3_RATE = new BigDecimal("0.25");
    private static final BigDecimal BRACKET_4_RATE = new BigDecimal("0.30");
    private static final BigDecimal BRACKET_5_RATE = new BigDecimal("0.32");
    private static final BigDecimal BRACKET_6_RATE = new BigDecimal("0.35");

    public WithholdingTaxDeduction() {
        super("Withholding Tax");
    }

    /** @param baseAmount taxable income (monthly gross minus SSS, PhilHealth, Pag-IBIG) */
    @Override
    public BigDecimal computeDeduction(BigDecimal baseAmount) {
        validateBaseAmount(baseAmount);
        if (baseAmount.compareTo(BRACKET_1_MAX) <= 0) {
            return BigDecimal.ZERO;
        }
        if (baseAmount.compareTo(BRACKET_2_MAX) <= 0) {
            return baseAmount.subtract(BRACKET_2_FLOOR).multiply(BRACKET_2_RATE);
        }
        if (baseAmount.compareTo(BRACKET_3_MAX) <= 0) {
            return BRACKET_3_BASE_TAX.add(baseAmount.subtract(BRACKET_3_FLOOR).multiply(BRACKET_3_RATE));
        }
        if (baseAmount.compareTo(BRACKET_4_MAX) <= 0) {
            return BRACKET_4_BASE_TAX.add(baseAmount.subtract(BRACKET_4_FLOOR).multiply(BRACKET_4_RATE));
        }
        if (baseAmount.compareTo(BRACKET_5_MAX) <= 0) {
            return BRACKET_5_BASE_TAX.add(baseAmount.subtract(BRACKET_5_FLOOR).multiply(BRACKET_5_RATE));
        }
        return BRACKET_6_BASE_TAX.add(baseAmount.subtract(BRACKET_6_FLOOR).multiply(BRACKET_6_RATE));
    }
}
### /home/user/repo_review/full_repo/testingester-main/6/-/src/motorph/service/PayrollProcessor.java
package motorph.service;

import java.math.BigDecimal;
import java.math.MathContext;
import java.time.LocalDate;
import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.LinkedHashMap;
import java.util.LinkedHashSet;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Map;
import java.util.Set;
import java.util.TreeMap;
import motorph.deduction.Deduction;
import motorph.model.AttendanceRecord;
import motorph.model.Employee;
import motorph.model.Payslip;

/**
 * Runs the payroll workflow: hours -> gross pay -> deductions -> net pay -> Payslip.
 * <p>
 * Works only with parent types (Employee, Deduction), so there are no checks on
 * employee status or deduction type. The deductions are passed into the
 * constructor: a list of contributions computed on monthly gross (SSS,
 * PhilHealth, Pag-IBIG) and a separate withholding tax computed on taxable
 * income. Adding a new government contribution only needs a new Deduction
 * subclass in that list.
 * </p>
 * <p>
 * Cutoff rule (from CP2): the 1st cutoff (days 1-15) has no deductions and net
 * pay equals gross pay. The 2nd cutoff (day 16 to month end) takes the whole
 * month's deductions once, computed on the combined gross of both cutoffs.
 * </p>
 */
public class PayrollProcessor {

    // === SUMMARY KEYS (computePayrollSummary) ===
    public static final String SUMMARY_TOTAL_EMPLOYEES  = "Total Employees";
    public static final String SUMMARY_TOTAL_GROSS      = "Total Gross Pay";
    public static final String SUMMARY_TOTAL_DEDUCTIONS = "Total Deductions";
    public static final String SUMMARY_TOTAL_NET        = "Total Net Pay";
    public static final String SUMMARY_AVERAGE_NET      = "Average Net Pay";

    // Cutoff labels come from AttendanceRecord.getCutoffLabel(), e.g. "June 16-30, 2024"
    private static final String SECOND_CUTOFF_MARKER  = " 16-";
    private static final String SECOND_CUTOFF_PATTERN = " 16-\\d{2},";
    private static final String FIRST_CUTOFF_DAYS     = " 1-15,";

    private final List<Deduction> contributions;
    private final Deduction withholdingTax;

    /**
     * @param contributions  deductions computed on monthly gross, in payslip order
     * @param withholdingTax deduction computed last, on taxable income
     */
    public PayrollProcessor(List<Deduction> contributions, Deduction withholdingTax) {
        if (contributions == null || withholdingTax == null) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Contributions and withholding tax are required.");
        }
        for (Deduction contribution : contributions) {
            if (contribution == null) {
                throw new IllegalArgumentException("Contribution list must not contain empty entries.");
            }
        }
        this.contributions = List.copyOf(contributions);
        this.withholdingTax = withholdingTax;
    }

    /** Returns the deduction names in payslip order (contributions, then tax). */
    public List<String> getDeductionNames() {
        List<String> names = new ArrayList<>();
        for (Deduction contribution : contributions) {
            names.add(contribution.getName());
        }
        names.add(withholdingTax.getName());
        return names;
    }

    // === CUTOFFS AND HOURS ===

    /**
     * Returns every cutoff label found in the attendance records, oldest first.
     * Used to fill the cutoff selection list.
     */
    public List<String> getAvailableCutoffs(Map<String, List<AttendanceRecord>> attendanceByEmployee) {
        Map<LocalDate, String> labelsByDate = new TreeMap<>();
        for (List<AttendanceRecord> records : attendanceByEmployee.values()) {
            for (AttendanceRecord record : records) {
                labelsByDate.putIfAbsent(record.getDate(), record.getCutoffLabel());
            }
        }
        Set<String> cutoffs = new LinkedHashSet<>(labelsByDate.values());
        return new ArrayList<>(cutoffs);
    }

    /**
     * Sums the hours worked in one cutoff.
     *
     * @param records     one employee's attendance records
     * @param cutoffLabel the cutoff to total, for example "June 1-15, 2024"
     * @return total hours, or 0 if no records match
     */
    public double computeHoursForCutoff(List<AttendanceRecord> records, String cutoffLabel) {
        long minutes = 0;
        if (records != null) {
            for (AttendanceRecord record : records) {
                if (record.getCutoffLabel().equals(cutoffLabel)) {
                    minutes += record.computeMinutesWorked();
                }
            }
        }
        return minutes / 60.0;
    }

    /**
     * Returns the employees with no hours in the cutoff, so the GUI can warn once
     * before they are computed with 0 hours (CP2 behavior).
     */
    public List<Employee> findEmployeesWithoutAttendance(List<Employee> employees,
            Map<String, List<AttendanceRecord>> attendanceByEmployee, String cutoffLabel) {
        List<Employee> missing = new ArrayList<>();
        for (Employee employee : employees) {
            List<AttendanceRecord> records = attendanceByEmployee.get(employee.getEmployeeId());
            if (computeHoursForCutoff(records, cutoffLabel) <= 0) {
                missing.add(employee);
            }
        }
        return missing;
    }

    // === DEDUCTIONS AND NET PAY ===

    /**
     * Computes each deduction for one month, in order: every contribution on the
     * monthly gross, then withholding tax on taxable income (monthly gross minus
     * the contributions, floored at 0). No type checks: each Deduction runs its
     * own formula.
     *
     * @param monthlyGross combined gross of the 1st and 2nd cutoff
     * @return deduction name to amount, in payslip order
     */
    public Map<String, BigDecimal> computeDeductionBreakdown(BigDecimal monthlyGross) {
        Map<String, BigDecimal> breakdown = new LinkedHashMap<>();
        BigDecimal taxableIncome = monthlyGross;
        for (Deduction contribution : contributions) {
            BigDecimal amount = contribution.computeDeduction(monthlyGross);
            breakdown.put(contribution.getName(), amount);
            taxableIncome = taxableIncome.subtract(amount);
        }
        breakdown.put(withholdingTax.getName(), withholdingTax.computeDeduction(taxableIncome.max(BigDecimal.ZERO)));
        return breakdown;
    }

    /**
     * Totals all government deductions for one month: the sum of
     * computeDeductionBreakdown(), so the total always matches the itemized lines.
     */
    public BigDecimal computeTotalDeductions(BigDecimal monthlyGross) {
        return sum(computeDeductionBreakdown(monthlyGross));
    }

    /** Net pay = cutoff gross - deductions, never below 0. */
    public BigDecimal computeNetPay(BigDecimal cutoffGross, BigDecimal totalDeductions) {
        return cutoffGross.subtract(totalDeductions).max(BigDecimal.ZERO);
    }

    // === PAYSLIPS ===

    /**
     * Builds the payslip for one employee and one cutoff ("One Employee" mode).
     * Accepts any Employee subtype; allowances come from the subclass's own
     * computeAllowances().
     *
     * @param employee    the employee to pay
     * @param records     that employee's attendance records (may be empty)
     * @param cutoffLabel the cutoff to pay
     */
    public Payslip generatePayslip(Employee employee, List<AttendanceRecord> records, String cutoffLabel) {
        if (employee == null || cutoffLabel == null || cutoffLabel.trim().isEmpty()) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Employee and cutoff are required.");
        }
        double hoursWorked = computeHoursForCutoff(records, cutoffLabel);
        BigDecimal grossPay = employee.computeGrossPay(hoursWorked);

        Map<String, BigDecimal> breakdown;
        BigDecimal allowances;
        if (isSecondCutoff(cutoffLabel)) {
            // Monthly items are settled once, here: deductions on the combined gross of both cutoffs,
            // and the month's allowances (listed only; not added to net pay, as in CP2).
            double firstCutoffHours = computeHoursForCutoff(records, getFirstCutoffLabel(cutoffLabel));
            BigDecimal monthlyGross = employee.computeGrossPay(firstCutoffHours + hoursWorked);
            breakdown = computeDeductionBreakdown(monthlyGross);
            allowances = employee.computeAllowances();
        } else {
            breakdown = zeroBreakdown();
            allowances = BigDecimal.ZERO;
        }
        BigDecimal netPay = computeNetPay(grossPay, sum(breakdown));
        return new Payslip(employee, cutoffLabel, hoursWorked, grossPay, breakdown, allowances, netPay);
    }

    /**
     * Runs payroll for every employee in one cutoff ("All Employees" mode).
     * Same steps for every Employee subtype.
     */
    public List<Payslip> processPayroll(List<Employee> employees,
            Map<String, List<AttendanceRecord>> attendanceByEmployee, String cutoffLabel) {
        List<Payslip> payslips = new ArrayList<>();
        for (Employee employee : employees) {
            payslips.add(generatePayslip(employee, attendanceByEmployee.get(employee.getEmployeeId()), cutoffLabel));
        }
        return payslips;
    }

    /**
     * Totals a list of payslips: employee count, total gross, total deductions,
     * total net, and average net. Uses full-precision amounts (as CP2 did), so
     * the totals are rounded only when displayed.
     *
     * @throws IllegalArgumentException if the list is empty
     */
    public Map<String, BigDecimal> computePayrollSummary(List<Payslip> payslips) {
        if (payslips == null || payslips.isEmpty()) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("There are no payslips to summarize.");
        }
        BigDecimal totalGross = BigDecimal.ZERO;
        BigDecimal totalDeductions = BigDecimal.ZERO;
        BigDecimal totalNet = BigDecimal.ZERO;
        for (Payslip payslip : payslips) {
            totalGross = totalGross.add(payslip.getGrossPay());
            totalDeductions = totalDeductions.add(payslip.getTotalDeductions());
            totalNet = totalNet.add(payslip.getNetPay());
        }
        BigDecimal count = BigDecimal.valueOf(payslips.size());

        Map<String, BigDecimal> summary = new LinkedHashMap<>();
        summary.put(SUMMARY_TOTAL_EMPLOYEES, count);
        summary.put(SUMMARY_TOTAL_GROSS, totalGross);
        summary.put(SUMMARY_TOTAL_DEDUCTIONS, totalDeductions);
        summary.put(SUMMARY_TOTAL_NET, totalNet);
        summary.put(SUMMARY_AVERAGE_NET, totalNet.divide(count, MathContext.DECIMAL128));

### 4.3 What the ERD visually communicates

The diagram's connector network places `Employee` near the right side and connects it to `Address`, `Position`, and `Supervisor`. `Position` is connected to `Department`, while `Supervisor` links back to `Employee`. `Schedule` links to `Employee` and to the separate `Rest Day` table. `Attendance` links to `Schedule`.

The leave cluster places `Leave`, `Leave Balance`, `Leave Type`, `Leave Accrual History`, and `Leave Monetisation` near one another. Their connectors depict the leave-request, leave-balance, leave-type, accrual-history, and monetisation associations.

The payroll cluster links `Payroll` with `Earnings`, `Deductibles`, and `Summary`. `Payslip` is connected to `Payroll`. `Other Transactions` is connected to `Payroll`. `Government Deductibles` and `Contributions` connect government records and contributor-specific amounts, while `Government Tally` is attached to monthly `Summary` totals.

The reference-data portion places `Address` with `Cities` and `Regions`, `Cities` with `Regions`, and the tax/rate/month/holiday/leave-type entities around the calculation and reference tables.

### 4.4 Important visual-only schema details

The image makes several details especially clear:

1. `Schedule` contains `restDayID` rather than the `restDay` `SET` column described in the Data Dictionary and prose table list.
2. A standalone `Rest Day` table exists in the ERD, with seven weekday Boolean fields.
3. `Employee` in the ERD does not visibly contain `departmentID` or `governmentID`, although these are in the Data Dictionary's Employee field list.
4. `Address` in the ERD visibly contains `regionID`, although the Database Design prose definition of Address lists only `addressID`, `cityID`, `building`, `street`, and `postalCode`.
5. `Supervisor` in the ERD visibly contains `departmentID`, although the Database Design prose definition of Supervisor lists only `supervisorID` and `employeeID`.
6. `Rates` visibly marks `implementationYear` as the primary key, although the Database Design's table constraint section says the Rates table has no primary key, and the Data Dictionary does not list `implementationYear` at all.
7. `Government Deductibles` visibly shows both `monthID` and `governmentID` as key fields, consistent with a composite key.
8. `Contributions` visibly shows `(governmentID, contributor)` as a composite key.
9. `Government Tally` visibly shows `summaryID` and `contributor` as key fields, although the Data Dictionary calls `summaryID` its primary key “(assumed)”.

The exact consequences of these discrepancies are not resolved by the three documents. See [Section 16](#16-cross-document-discrepancies-and-unresolved-design-questions).

## 5. Visual reconstruction of the data-flow diagrams

**Source locations:** Data Flow Diagram PDF, pages 2–6. The actual diagrams are image-based; the following sections convert their labels, arrows, and visual groupings into text.

### 5.1 DFD notation and reading conventions

The worksheet expressly calls for **Gene & Sarson notation**. The diagrams use:

- rounded or rectangular cyan/teal shapes for external entities such as Employee, Supervisor, Human Resources, Payroll Staff, and System Admin;
- yellow/orange-topped process shapes for system processes, numbered `0.0`, `1.0`, `2.0`, `3.0`, and the decomposed Level 2 process numbers;
- lavender/purple data-store shapes, generally labelled with a `D` identifier and a store name; and
- directed connectors, with text labels describing the data or action moving along each connector.

The diagrams are process-and-data-flow views. They do not show every physical database column, and a data store in a DFD is not necessarily a one-to-one representation of a single relational table. The DFD uses larger logical stores such as `Employee Repository`, `Logs`, and `Payroll`, then subdivides them into named components in the Level 2 diagrams.

### 5.2 External entities

Five external actors appear across the DFDs:

| Actor | Role represented in the diagrams |
|---|---|
| **Employee** | Supplies attendance and time-in/time-out information; views employee information and payslips; views personal payslip information in the payroll Level 2 view. |
| **Supervisor** | Views team-member information and team payslips; adjusts team attendance; handles leave requests; handles or initiates leave monetisation; submits team-member wage and adjustment information; views team benefits/deductions. |
| **Human Resources** | Updates employee details; views employee and payroll details; participates in PII access approval and PII viewing/updating on approval; views relevant employee, attendance, and leave information. |
| **Payroll Staff** | Views and verifies employee and payroll details; views employee government PII on approval; updates payroll, payslip, benefits, and deductibles; validates and verifies payroll details and monthly reports. |
| **System Admin** | Manages configurations and users; views all employee information; participates in PII access approval; handles backup and archival; initiates the annual archival prompt; updates optional/system-controlled values in the detailed payroll diagram. |

The actors are distinct. The diagrams do not collapse HR, Payroll Staff, Supervisor, and System Admin into one generic administrator role.

### 5.3 Data stores in the DFD

| Identifier | Store name | Diagram placement / contents represented |
|---|---|---|
| `D1` | Employee Repository | Level 1 store for employee information. |
| `D1.1` | Employee Address | Level 2 subdivision for employee address data. |
| `D1.2` | Job Profile | Level 2 subdivision for employee job-profile data. |
| `D1.3` | Personally Identifiable Information | Level 2 subdivision for PII, shown beside Government Info Access. |
| `D2` | Logs | Level 1 store for operational logs, expanded into attendance, leave, changelog, and leave-monetisation logs. |
| `D2.1` | Attendance / Attendance Logs | Attendance and time activity used for work-hour derivation and timesheet validation. |
| `D2.2` | Leave / Leave Logs | Leave records used to derive paid-leave details and support leave management. |
| `D2.3` | Changelog / Changelogs | Employee-information change history. |
| `D2.4` | Leave Monetisation Logs | History of leave credits converted to monetary value. |
| `D3` | Payroll | Level 1 store containing wage, payroll, payslip, and benefits/deductibles information. |
| `D3.1` | Wage | Basic remunerative values and wage values. |
| `D3.2` | Benefits & Deductibles | Benefit and deduction values, including adjustments and computed deductions. |
| `D3.3` | Tax Table & Rates | Tax table and rates used to compute contributions. |
| `D3.4` | Payslip | Generated payslip records. |
| `D3.5` | Monthly Summary Report | Generated monthly summary report. |
| `D4` | Cold Storage | Destination for old logs and payroll records held for later compression. |

The Level 1 diagram names `D1 Employee Repository`, `D2 Logs`, `D3 Payroll`, and `D4 Cold Storage`. The Level 2 diagrams split the first three into more granular stores. These identifiers should be preserved when discussing the submitted diagrams.

### 5.4 Context-level DFD (`LV0: Context Diagram`)

**Source image:** DFD PDF, page 2. The context diagram represents the entire `MotorPH Payroll System` as one process, numbered `0.0`, surrounded by the five external entities.

#### 5.4.1 Employee flows

- **Employee → MotorPH Payroll System:** `Attendance and Time In/Out`.
- **MotorPH Payroll System → Employee:** `View Employee Information` (the information is supplied by the system in response to the employee's view/access activity).
- **MotorPH Payroll System → Employee:** `View Payslip`.

The diagram therefore presents the employee as both an input source for attendance/time data and a recipient of employee information and payslip output.

#### 5.4.2 Supervisor flows

- **MotorPH Payroll System → Supervisor:** `View Team Payslips`.
- **Supervisor → MotorPH Payroll System:** `Adjust Team Attendance`.
- **Supervisor → MotorPH Payroll System:** `Handle Leave Requests and Monetisation`.
- **Supervisor → MotorPH Payroll System:** `Handling Team Member Benefits / Deductions`.
- **MotorPH Payroll System → Supervisor:** `View Team Members' Employee Info`.

The diagram distinguishes the supervisor's ability to view team information from the supervisor's submission or handling of team attendance, leave, monetisation, and benefits/deductions matters.

#### 5.4.3 Human Resources flows

- **Human Resources → MotorPH Payroll System:** `Update Employee Details`.
- **Human Resources → MotorPH Payroll System:** `Update PII (On Approval)`.
- **MotorPH Payroll System → Human Resources:** `View PII (On Approval)`.
- **MotorPH Payroll System → Human Resources:** `View Employee and Payroll Details`.
- **Human Resources → MotorPH Payroll System:** `PII Access Approval`.

The approval condition is part of the flow labels. The diagram does not present PII viewing or updating as unrestricted operations.

#### 5.4.4 Payroll Staff flows

- **MotorPH Payroll System → Payroll Staff:** `View and Verify Employee and Payroll Details`.
- **MotorPH Payroll System → Payroll Staff:** `View Employees' Government PII (On Approval)`.
- **Payroll Staff → MotorPH Payroll System:** `Update Payroll, Payslip, and Benefits/Deductibles`.

The government PII view has an explicit approval condition. Payroll Staff also have a separate update flow for payroll-related records.

The term `Basic Payroll Computation` is the process name. The source does not give a mathematical formula for gross pay, deductions, net pay, overtime, holiday pay, undertime, or any other component.

**Important difference:** The Data Dictionary marks `holidayName` and `holidayDate` individually as unique fields. The Database Design instead specifies a composite unique combination of name and date. These are not equivalent rules: independent uniqueness prevents two holidays from sharing a name or date, while pair uniqueness prevents only a duplicate name/date pair.

### 11.4 `Months`

| Column | Data type / size | Description | Data Dictionary constraint |
|---|---|---|---|
| `monthID` | `Enum` | Unique month identifier. | The field is described as an enum; no additional field-level constraint stated. |
| `monthlyWorkdays` | `Integer`, size 2 | Number of workdays in the month. | `Min(1)`, `Max(31)`. |

**Database Design constraints:** PK `monthID`; no FK; no separate unique constraint because `monthID` is already an Enum; `monthlyWorkdays` must be between 1 and 31.

### 11.5 `Rates`

**Purpose:** Holds statutory rate values for Pag-ibig, PhilHealth, and SSS.

| Column | Data type / size | Description | Data Dictionary constraint |
|---|---|---|---|
| `piEmployerRate` | `Decimal(5,3)` | Global employer Pag-ibig rate. | `Min(0)`; `NOT NULL`. |
| `piEmployeeRate` | `Decimal(5,3)` | Global employee Pag-ibig rate. | `Min(0)`; `NOT NULL`. |
| `piMaxContribution` | `Decimal(5,3)` | Maximum Pag-ibig contribution. | `Min(0)`; `NOT NULL`. |
| `phRate` | `Decimal(5,3)` | Global PhilHealth rate. | `Min(0)`; `NOT NULL`. |
| `sssRate` | `Decimal(5,3)` | Global SSS rate. | `Min(0)`; `NOT NULL`. |

**Database Design additional field:** The Database Design prose table and ERD include `implementationYear`, data type `SmallInt` (shown as size 4 in the diagram), described as the year the rates were implemented. The Data Dictionary omits this field.

**Database Design constraint conflict:** Its prose table says PK `None`, FK `None`, Unique `None`; the check-constraint text says all fields must be provided (`NOT NULL`) and rates must be greater than or equal to zero. The ERD, however, visibly marks `implementationYear` as `PK`. The documents do not resolve whether implementation year is intended to identify each rate set.

**DFD role:** `D3.3 Tax Table & Rates` provides the rates used by Process `2.4 Government Deductibles` to compute contributions. The System Admin has an `Update Rates (opt*)` flow to the store.

### 11.6 `Tax Table`

| Column | Data type / size | Description | Data Dictionary constraint |
|---|---|---|---|
| `taxBracket` | `Integer` | Identifier for the tax bracket. | `Min(1)`; Primary Key. |
| `minCompensation` | `Decimal(19,4)` | Minimum income for the bracket. | `Min(0)`; `NOT NULL` in the Database Design constraints. |
| `maxCompensation` | `Decimal(19,4)` | Maximum income for the bracket. | `Min(0)`; `NOT NULL` in the Database Design constraints. |
| `bracketWidth` | `Decimal(19,4)` | Income range width for the bracket. | `Min(0)`. |
| `taxRate` | `Decimal(19,4)` | Tax rate for the bracket. | `Min(0)`; `NOT NULL` in the Database Design constraints. |

**Database Design constraints:** PK `taxBracket`; no FK; `taxBracket` uniquely identifies the withholding-tax criteria and consequent requirement. The check-constraint wording says `taxBracket` must “at least have and be greater than 1” (the source wording is unclear), that `minCompensation`, `maxCompensation`, and `taxRate` must be present, and that monetary values must be non-negative.

**Unresolved wording:** The Data Dictionary's `Min(1)` indicates a minimum of 1. The Database Design's prose has a malformed phrase that could be read as “at least have and be greater than 1”. It is unsafe to silently convert this to `>= 1` or `> 1` without an implementation decision.

### 11.7 `Leave Type`

**Purpose:** Defines the leave categories and their accrual rules.

| Column | Data type / size | Description | Data Dictionary constraint |
|---|---|---|---|
| `leaveType` | `Enum` | Classification of leave. | `NOT NULL`. |
| `mandatory` | `Boolean` | Indicates whether the leave type is mandatory. | No additional constraint stated. |
| `defaultAccrualRate` | `Decimal(4,2)` | Standard rate at which leave accrues for this type. | `Min(0)`. |
| `accrualFrequency` | `Enum` | Frequency of leave accrual. | No additional constraint stated. |
| `maxAccrual` | `Decimal(4,2)` | Maximum allowable accrual for the leave type. | `Min(0)`. |

7. The `Payroll` record links to the wage record through `wageID`.

The source uses both `Wage` and `Earnings` as naming conventions: `D3.1 Wage` is the DFD store name, while the relational table is called `Earnings` and holds `wageID`. The relationship matrix states Payroll → Earnings is 1:1.

### 14.6 Government deduction and contribution trace

1. The employee's Government record holds the identifiers used for government-related payroll processing.
2. `D3.3 Tax Table & Rates` stores the tax bracket and contribution-rate reference information.
3. System Admin has an `Update Rates (opt*)` flow in the Payroll Level 2 DFD.
4. Process `2.4 Government Deductibles` utilises rates to compute contributions.
5. It appends computed information to `D3.2 Benefits & Deductibles` through `Append to Deductibles`.
6. The relational `Government Deductibles` table holds employer contribution, employee contribution, and withholding tax by government record and month.
7. The `Contributions` table stores specific PhilHealth, Pag-ibig, and SSS amounts with a contributor identifier.
8. `Deductibles` stores the government link and total deductions.
9. `Government Tally` holds overall contribution totals by contributor and is linked to `Summary`.
10. The monthly summary compilation process collates payroll and contribution information and generates a Monthly Summary Report.

The table names and relationships distinguish individual government identifiers, monthly deductible amounts, contributor-specific contribution values, and monthly tally totals. The documents do not give the exact reconciliation formula between Government Deductibles, Contributions, Deductibles, Government Tally, and Summary, so the precise arithmetic relationship must not be assumed.

### 14.7 Basic payroll computation and payslip generation

1. Process `2.5 Basic Payroll Computation` receives Time Activity from Timesheet Validation.
2. It retrieves basic remunerative values from `D3.1 Wage`.
3. It applies adjustments from `D3.2 Benefits & Deductibles`.
4. It computes `Net Pay and Constituents` and sends them to `2.6 Payslip Generation & Distribution`.
5. Payroll Staff can `View, Validate, and Verify Payroll Details` at the computation stage.
6. Process `2.6` appends the payslip to `D3.4 Payslip`.
7. Employee can view personal payslip information, Supervisor can view team information, and HR can view payslip/report information.
8. The `Payslip` relational table records pay-period start and end dates, standard hours, overtime hours, holiday overtime hours, PTO hours, undertime, days worked, holidays worked, rest days worked, and gross income.
9. `Payroll.netPay` records final pay after deductions; the Database Design says `hourlyRate`, `dailyRate`, and `netPay` must be non-null.

- hourly, daily, or monthly salary conversion;
- ordinary overtime;
- holiday overtime;
- holiday pay;
- rest-day pay;
- paid time off compensation;
- undertime;
- benefits totals;
- deduction totals;
- withholding tax;
- SSS, PhilHealth, or Pag-ibig contributions;
- employer versus employee contribution shares;
- government disbursement totals; or
- employee/employer disbursement totals.

The schema provides fields where amounts are stored. The DFD identifies which processes use those amounts. Neither gives the arithmetic rules.

### 17.3 No actual rate schedules or tax brackets

The `Rates` and `Tax Table` tables define the places where rates and brackets are held. The PDFs do not provide actual statutory percentages, amounts, income thresholds, bracket widths, tax formulas, effective dates, or the date on which rate changes take effect.

### 17.4 No complete business rules for leave

The data model provides leave categories, accrual frequency, accrual rate, maximum accrual, leave balances, requests, approvals, and monetisation. It does not list the actual leave categories or define:

- how leave is earned within a period;
- when accrual is posted;
- whether accrual is prorated;
- how leaves are approved or rejected;
- how requests that exceed the balance are handled;
- whether a request reserves credits before approval;
- how overlapping leave requests are handled;
- which leave types can be monetised;
- how monetisation is valued; or
- how an approved leave request affects attendance data and payroll.

### 17.5 No complete security implementation

The overview identifies RBAC and a two-person approval requirement for PII, but does not provide a complete role-permission matrix, specific permission names, authentication factors, encryption method, key custody, logging retention, masking rules, access review cycle, or PII access-request workflow.

### 17.6 No complete archival policy

The DFD shows the labels `1YO`, `2YO`, an annual prompt, cold storage, later compression, and subsequent deletion. It does not define the precise age calculation, file format, compression method, archive integrity check, restore process, backup schedule, legal exceptions, or audit evidence.

### /home/user/repo_review/full_repo/testingester-main/9/-/oop/src/motorphemployee/oop/GovernmentContributionCalculator.java
package motorphemployee.oop;

/**
 * GovernmentContributionCalculator - abstract base for every statutory deduction
 * (MS1 Week 3/4/5 CRC rows).
 *
 * PayrollCalculator works with THIS type only, never with SSSCalculator or any other
 * concrete subclass. Adding a new deduction later means adding a subclass and one line
 * in the calculator list - no change to the orchestrator.
 */
public abstract class GovernmentContributionCalculator {

    private final String contributionName;
    private final String contributionCode;
    private boolean isActive;

    protected GovernmentContributionCalculator(String contributionName, String contributionCode) {
        if (contributionName == null || contributionName.trim().isEmpty()) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("contributionName cannot be empty");
        }
        if (contributionCode == null || contributionCode.trim().isEmpty()) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("contributionCode cannot be empty");
        }
        this.contributionName = contributionName.trim();
        this.contributionCode = contributionCode.trim();
        this.isActive = true;
    }

    /** The polymorphic entry point: every deduction type implements only this. */
    public abstract double calculate(double grossSalary);

    public String getContributionName() {
        return contributionName;
    }

    public String getContributionCode() {
        return contributionCode;
    }

    public boolean isActive() {
        return isActive;
    }

    public void setActive(boolean isActive) {
        this.isActive = isActive;
    }

    /** Shared guard: a contribution on an invalid salary is a bug, not a zero. */
    protected double requireValidSalary(double grossSalary) {
        if (Double.isNaN(grossSalary) || grossSalary < 0) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException(contributionName + ": invalid salary " + grossSalary);
        }
        return grossSalary;
    }

    @Override
    public String toString() {
        return contributionName + " (" + contributionCode + ", " + (isActive ? "active" : "inactive") + ")";
    }
}

 * (MS1 Week 3 CRC: "SSSCalculator (Concrete Subclass)").
 *
 * The bracket table is private: outside code only sees calculate(). Brackets come from
 * Home_SSS_Matrix.xlsx (sheet "SSS Contribution Schedule"): lower bound 3,250 stepping by 500,
 * contribution 157.50 stepping by 22.50, "below 3,250" = 135.00, "over 24,750" = 1,125.00.
 *
 * Official matrix (2026-10-27): the official ranges are LOWER-bound inclusive ("3,250 - 3,749.99"),
 * so bracket i covers [lower, lower + 499.99]. CP2 used an upper-bound inclusive `<=` chain,
 * which under-deducted PHP 22.50 whenever the salary landed exactly on a bracket boundary -
 * Issue 5 in oop/matrix-verification.md.
 */
public class SSSCalculator extends GovernmentContributionCalculator {

    private static final double FIRST_LOWER_BOUND = 3250.0;
    private static final double LOWER_BOUND_STEP = 500.0;
    private static final double BELOW_TABLE_AMOUNT = 135.0;
    private static final double FIRST_BRACKET_AMOUNT = 157.5;
    private static final double AMOUNT_STEP = 22.5;
    private static final int BRACKETS = 43;              // 3,250 ... 24,250 + the "over 24,750" row
    private static final double MAX_CONTRIBUTION = 1125.0;

    private static final double[] LOWER_BOUNDS = new double[BRACKETS];
    private static final double[] AMOUNTS = new double[BRACKETS];

    static {
        for (int i = 0; i < BRACKETS; i++) {
            LOWER_BOUNDS[i] = FIRST_LOWER_BOUND + LOWER_BOUND_STEP * i;
            AMOUNTS[i] = FIRST_BRACKET_AMOUNT + AMOUNT_STEP * i;
        }
    }

    public SSSCalculator() {
        super("SSS Contribution", "SSS");
    }

    @Override
    public double calculate(double grossSalary) {
        double salary = requireValidSalary(grossSalary);
        if (salary < FIRST_LOWER_BOUND) {
            return BELOW_TABLE_AMOUNT;
        }
        for (int i = 0; i < BRACKETS; i++) {
            if (salary < LOWER_BOUNDS[i] + LOWER_BOUND_STEP) {
                return AMOUNTS[i];
            }
        }
        return MAX_CONTRIBUTION;
    }

    /** Read-only inspection of the table (used by the console test, never by payroll logic). */
    public int getBracketCount() {
        return BRACKETS + 2;                             // "below 3,250" + 43 rows + "over 24,750"
    }
}
### /home/user/repo_review/full_repo/testingester-main/9/-/oop/src/motorphemployee/oop/PhilHealthCalculator.java
package motorphemployee.oop;

/**
 * PhilHealthCalculator - PhilHealth employee share: 50% of the premium (3% rate with a PHP 300
 * floor and a PHP 1,800 ceiling), so the deduction runs from PHP 150 to PHP 900
 * (MS1 Week 3 CRC: "PhilHealthCalculator (Concrete Subclass)").
 *
 * Official matrix (2026-10-27): the premium formula is carried over from CP2 unchanged, but the
 * EMPLOYEE SHARE is applied. The official matrix states the premium is equally shared between
 * employee and employer (Home_Philhealth_Matrix.xlsx note A6; SAMPLE B10 = 375 on a 25,000
 * basic salary). CP2 returned the full premium, which over-deducted every payslip by 2x -
 * logged as Issue 2 in oop/matrix-verification.md.
 */
public class PhilHealthCalculator extends GovernmentContributionCalculator {

    private static final double EMPLOYEE_SHARE_RATE = 0.5;
    private static final double PREMIUM_RATE = 0.03;
    private static final double MIN_PREMIUM = 300.0;
    private static final double MAX_PREMIUM = 1800.0;
    private static final double LOWER_CAP_SALARY = 10000.0;
    private static final double UPPER_CAP_SALARY = 59999.99;

    public PhilHealthCalculator() {
        super("PhilHealth Contribution", "PH");
    }

    @Override
    public double calculate(double grossSalary) {
        double salary = requireValidSalary(grossSalary);

        // Official monthly premium: 3% of salary, floor 300, ceiling 1,800 (matrix A2:C4).
        double monthlyPremium;
        if (salary <= LOWER_CAP_SALARY) {
            monthlyPremium = MIN_PREMIUM;
        } else if (salary <= UPPER_CAP_SALARY) {
            monthlyPremium = Math.min(MIN_PREMIUM + (salary - LOWER_CAP_SALARY) * PREMIUM_RATE, MAX_PREMIUM);
        } else {
            monthlyPremium = MAX_PREMIUM;
        }

        // The employee pays HALF (matrix note A6: "equally shared"; SAMPLE B10 = 375 of 750).
        return monthlyPremium * EMPLOYEE_SHARE_RATE;
    }
}
### /home/user/repo_review/full_repo/testingester-main/9/-/oop/src/motorphemployee/oop/PagIbigCalculator.java
package motorphemployee.oop;

/**
 * PagIbigCalculator - Pag-IBIG EMPLOYEE share, tiered, with a PHP 100 cap
 * (MS1 Week 3 CRC: "PagIbigCalculator (Concrete Subclass)").
 *
 * Official matrix (2026-10-27): only the employee share is deducted - 1% for 1,000-1,500 and 2%
 * above 1,500, capped at 100 (Home_PagIBIG_Matrix.xlsx B2/B3 employee rates vs D2/D3 totals,
 * cap note A5). CP2 added the employer share (2%) and deducted the total 3%/4% from the
 * employee; that is Issue 3 in oop/matrix-verification.md.
 *
 * Salary below 1,000 has no row in the official matrix, so it returns 0.00 and stays
 * UNVERIFIED rather than guessing a rate.
 */
public class PagIbigCalculator extends GovernmentContributionCalculator {

    private static final double LOWER_BAND_MIN = 1000.0;
    private static final double LOWER_BAND_MAX = 1500.0;
    private static final double EMPLOYEE_RATE_LOW = 0.01;
    private static final double EMPLOYEE_RATE_HIGH = 0.02;
    private static final double MAX_CONTRIBUTION = 100.0;

    public PagIbigCalculator() {
        super("Pag-IBIG Contribution", "PAGIBIG");
    }

    @Override
    public double calculate(double grossSalary) {
        double salary = requireValidSalary(grossSalary);

        double employeeRate = 0.0;

        if (salary >= LOWER_BAND_MIN && salary <= LOWER_BAND_MAX) {
            employeeRate = EMPLOYEE_RATE_LOW;
        } else if (salary > LOWER_BAND_MAX) {
            employeeRate = EMPLOYEE_RATE_HIGH;
        }

        return Math.min(salary * employeeRate, MAX_CONTRIBUTION);
    }
}

## `PayrollCalculator` orchestrator (2026-10-28)

The payroll path is now one method: `calculatePayroll(employee, attendance, periodStart, periodEnd)`
returns an immutable `PayrollRecord`. Nothing in this class asks which calculator or which employee type
it is holding — `grep -c instanceof PayrollCalculator.java` = **0**.

| Phase | What runs | Type it works with (S1 design) |
|---|---|---|
| gross | `workedDays * hourlyRate * 8` | `AttendanceLog` + `Employee` |
| **phase 1** | SSS → PhilHealth → Pag-IBIG in **one loop** | `List<GovernmentContributionCalculator>` (abstract) |
| **phase 2** | BIR withholding tax on `gross - phase 1` | `GovernmentContributionCalculator` (abstract) |
| result | `new PayrollRecord(...)`, fully validated | immutable value object |

Verified run (`console-test-output.txt`, section I, 20 June 2024 working days, hourly rate 205.36):

| Field | Value | Where it comes from |
|---|---|---|
| gross income | **32,857.60** | 20 days × 205.36 × 8 |
| hours worked | **160.00** | 20 days × 8 |
| SSS | **1,125.00** | official cap |
| PhilHealth | **492.864** | (300 + (32,857.60 − 10,000) × 3%) / 2 |
| Pag-IBIG | **100.00** | official employee cap |
| withholding tax | **2,061.35** | 20% of (31,139.736 − 20,833) |
| **net pay** | **29,078.39** | gross − 3,779.21 deductions |

Section I also proves: the result is immutable (no setters), two employee types price differently through
one `Employee` parameter, the calculator list is injectable (SSS-only run changes only the SSS amount),
Issue 1 is refused, and the no-dates overload prices the most recent semi-monthly period.

Two defects in the leave screens, both found by the group's tester after the Week 9 smoke test and
reported in the MS2 Known Issues List (rows 18 and 19).

| What | Evidence |
|---|---|
| Approving a request wrote `leaves.csv` and moved the leave credits immediately, but the request stayed in `pendingleaves.csv` until Save was pressed, so the same leave could be approved again and counted twice | before: `LeaveApproval.approvedActionPerformed` only did `model.removeRow(...)`; `saveActionPerformed` was the only writer of `pendingleaves.csv` |
| Once the approve call site was fixed (commit `683c9f0`), rejected leaves were still written with the reason and the approval swapped, because the reject call passed `(reason, approval)` into `writeToFile(..., approval, reason)` | `git show 683c9f0` touches one call site: a rejected row still lands as `Reason=No`, `Approved?=<reason>` |
| Fix | `LeaveService` is now the only writer on the approve and reject path. One `decide(index, approved)` call removes the request, appends the processed row in header order and moves the credits, and restores all three files if a write fails. `LeaveApproval` keeps the table view only, the manual Save button is gone, and `LeaveManagement` reads `leaves.csv` through the same service |
| Column order | `LeaveService.LEAVE_COLUMNS` is the single definition of `Employee ID, Leave Type, Days, Reason, Approved?`; approve and reject both go through it, so the two call sites cannot disagree again |
| Evidence | `oop/leave-fix-test-output.txt` — 44 assertions, 0 failures: approve, reject, double-processing refused, stale row refused, shifted (ragged) `data.csv` refused instead of being rewritten, unknown employee, zero-credit employee, comma inside a reason, CRLF preserved, rollback after a failed write |
| No regression | `ConsoleBackendTest` still reports **91 passed, 0 failed**; `data.csv` is rewritten with its 24 columns and its original CRLF line endings |
| GUI click-through | **verified 2026-10-31 21:15** (HR login, VS Code F5 → LandingPage): Leave Management → Pending Leaves processed one approve and one reject; both requests left `pendingleaves.csv` on that same click with no Save, the reject row landed as `Reason=Sick, Approved?=No`, and the credits moved `12,0,0 → 11,1,0` (approved) / `11,1,0 → 11,1,1` (rejected). Raw run: `oop/gui-retest-output.txt` |

## Leave credit rule (matches the original program)

Approving a leave deducts exactly **one** credit, no matter how many days the request covers:
a 4-day leave moves the column from 11 to 10, a 2-day leave from 12 to 11. That is what the
baseline program does, so the refactor kept it on purpose.

// baseline 655d43d, LeaveApproval.updateLeaveCredits(...)

        data[21] = String.valueOf(leaveCredits - 1); // Deduct 1 leave credit
        data[22] = String.valueOf(approvedLeaves + 1);
```

# Matrix verification (official vs CP2 vs OOP)

> Scope: 4 deduction formulas (SSS · PhilHealth · Pag-IBIG · Withholding Tax) checked against the 4 official xlsx matrices in `C:\Users\Paul\Documents\MotorPH Files\`.
> Source of "CP2" values: verbatim copy of the 4 static methods from `src/motorphemployee/Dashboard.java:1195–1356` (run under JDK 21). Source of "OOP" values: `oop/src/motorphemployee/oop/*.java` compiled with `javac -Xlint:all` (0 warnings), run through the same harness. CP2 and OOP agree on **all 66 inputs tested** (`run.txt`), so the OOP columns are identical to CP2 by construction.
> Official values are computed from the matrix rules and the matrix cell refs cited below; nothing guessed. Verdict tolerance: |Δ| ≤ 0.005.
> No repo file was modified except this one. Harness + raw output live in the scratch dir (`cache\scratch\q4\`), not in the repo.

## 1. SSS

**(a) Official table** — `Home_SSS_Matrix.xlsx`, sheet `SSS Contribution Schedule`.
- `D2` = 135.00 for "Below 3,250".
- `A3:C46` = 44 rows, lower bound in `A`, upper in `C` (display only), contribution in `D`. Rows 3..46 step 500 from 3,250 (`D3`=157.50) to `A46`=24,750 (`D46`=1,125.00, "Over").
- Matrix ranges are written as `3,250 – 3,749.99` etc., i.e. **lower-bound inclusive**.
- Merged cells A1:C1 and A2:C2 are headers only; the data rows are not merged, so parsing was unambiguous.

**(b) CP2 code** — `Dashboard.java:1195–1292`: `if (totalSalary <= 3250) … else if (totalSalary <= 3750) …` (line 1198 onward), i.e. **upper-bound inclusive** `<=` chain, 45 branches, last branch `else → 1125` (line ~1290). Duplicate `MainMenu.java:1279` identical (diffed).

## 2. PhilHealth

**(a) Official table** — `Home_Philhealth_Matrix.xlsx`, sheet `Philhealth`.
- `A2:C2`: salary ≤ 10,000 → premium rate 3%, monthly premium **300** (floor).
- `A3:C3`: 10,000.01 – 59,999.99 → 3%, premium "300 up to 1,800" (i.e. 3% of salary, between those bounds).
- `A4:C4`: 60,000 → 1,800 (ceiling).
- `A6` NOTE: *"Monthly premium contribution payments are equally shared between the employee and employer."* → **employee share = 50% of premium.**
- `A7:B10` SAMPLE: basic 25,000 → 3% = 750 → **Employee Share (50%) = 375** (`B10`).
- Official employee deduction used below: `0.5 × clamp(0.03 × salary, 300, 1800)`.

**(b) CP2 code** — `Dashboard.java:1294–1310`: `premiumRate = 0.03`; `≤10,000 → 300`; `≤59,999.99 → min(300 + (salary−10,000)·0.03, 1800)`; `else 1800`. **Returns `monthlyPremium` = the full 100% premium**, with the comment "Employee and employer share equally" **but no ÷2 is applied** (line ~1305). The caller (`Dashboard.java:1013–1023`) subtracts this full amount from the employee's pay.

**(c) OOP code** — `PhilHealthCalculator.java`: `PREMIUM_RATE 0.03`, `MIN 300`, `MAX 1800`, same piecewise logic, returns the full premium. Identical to CP2 (javadoc says "carried over 1:1 from CP2").

**Formula check:** the CP2/OOP formula `300 + 0.03·(s−10,000)` = `0.03·s` for s ≥ 10,000, so the *premium* formula **matches the matrix** (verified at 15,000 → 450, 20,000 → 600, 25,000 → 750 ✓ official 750).

###AttendanceLog.java
package motorphemployee.oop;

import java.time.Duration;
import java.time.LocalDate;
import java.time.LocalTime;
import java.time.format.DateTimeFormatter;
import java.time.format.DateTimeParseException;
import java.util.LinkedHashMap;
import java.util.Map;

/**
 * AttendanceLog - the input side of gross pay (MS1 Week 2 CRC: "AttendanceLog").
 *
 * Enforces the integrity rules from the approved design: one clock-in per day, clock-in
 * must come before clock-out, hours never exceed 24 per day, and no future-dated records.
 * Callers only get read-only summaries - there is no way to edit a saved record.
 *
 * Storage note (open question in the Refactoring Plan): CP2 hardcoded a
 * workingDays[] array (MainMenu.java:1066) and no timecard CSV has been imported yet, so
 * this class keeps the records in memory. The public API is CSV-ready: an adapter that
 * feeds rows from attendance.csv needs no change to PayrollCalculator. No attendance data
 * was invented to make this test pass.
 */
public class AttendanceLog {

    private static final DateTimeFormatter DATE = DateTimeFormatter.ofPattern("yyyy-MM-dd");
    private static final DateTimeFormatter TIME = DateTimeFormatter.ofPattern("HH:mm[:ss]");

    /** employeeId -> (date -> {clockIn, clockOut}) */
    private final Map<Integer, Map<String, String[]>> records = new LinkedHashMap<>();

    public void recordClockIn(int employeeId) {
        recordClockIn(employeeId, LocalDate.now().format(DATE), LocalTime.now().format(DateTimeFormatter.ofPattern("HH:mm:ss")));
    }

    public void recordClockOut(int employeeId) {
        recordClockOut(employeeId, LocalDate.now().format(DATE), LocalTime.now().format(DateTimeFormatter.ofPattern("HH:mm:ss")));
    }

    /** Testable overload: records a clock-in for an explicit date and time. */
    public void recordClockIn(int employeeId, String date, String time) {
        requireEmployee(employeeId);
        LocalDate day = parseDate(date);
        if (day.isAfter(LocalDate.now())) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("cannot clock in on a future date: " + date);
        }
        parseTime(time);

        Map<String, String[]> perDay = records.computeIfAbsent(employeeId, key -> new LinkedHashMap<>());
        String[] entry = perDay.computeIfAbsent(date, key -> new String[]{null, null});
        if (entry[0] != null) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("duplicate clock-in for employee " + employeeId + " on " + date);
        }
        entry[0] = time;
    }

    /** Testable overload: records a clock-out for an explicit date and time. */
    public void recordClockOut(int employeeId, String date, String time) {
        requireEmployee(employeeId);
        parseDate(date);
        LocalTime clockOut = parseTime(time);

        Map<String, String[]> perDay = records.get(employeeId);
        if (perDay == null || perDay.get(date) == null || perDay.get(date)[0] == null) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("cannot clock out without a clock-in: employee "
                    + employeeId + " on " + date);
        }
        String[] entry = perDay.get(date);
        if (entry[1] != null) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("duplicate clock-out for employee " + employeeId + " on " + date);
        }
        LocalTime clockIn = parseTime(entry[0]);
        if (!clockOut.isAfter(clockIn)) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("clock-out must be after clock-in: " + entry[0] + " -> " + time);
        }
        double hours = Duration.between(clockIn, clockOut).toMinutes() / 60.0;
        if (hours > 24) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("hours worked cannot exceed 24 in a day: " + hours);
        }
        entry[1] = time;
    }

    /** Validated hours for one employee on one date; 0 when there is no complete record. */
    public double getDailyHours(int employeeId, String date) {
        requireEmployee(employeeId);
        Map<String, String[]> perDay = records.get(employeeId);
        if (perDay == null) {
            return 0.0;
        }
        String[] entry = perDay.get(date);
        if (entry == null || entry[0] == null || entry[1] == null) {
            return 0.0;
        }
        return Duration.between(parseTime(entry[0]), parseTime(entry[1])).toMinutes() / 60.0;
    }

    /** Days with a complete clock-in/clock-out pair inside the period (inclusive). */
    public int getWorkedDays(int employeeId, String periodStart, String periodEnd) {
        requireEmployee(employeeId);
        LocalDate start = parseDate(periodStart);
        LocalDate end = parseDate(periodEnd);
        if (end.isBefore(start)) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("periodEnd cannot be before periodStart");
        }
        Map<String, String[]> perDay = records.get(employeeId);
        if (perDay == null) {
            return 0;
        }
        int days = 0;
        for (Map.Entry<String, String[]> entry : perDay.entrySet()) {
            String[] times = entry.getValue();
            if (times[0] == null || times[1] == null) {
                continue;
            }
            LocalDate day = parseDate(entry.getKey());
            if (!day.isBefore(start) && !day.isAfter(end)) {
                days++;
            }
        }
        return days;
    }

    private static void requireEmployee(int employeeId) {
        if (employeeId <= 0) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("employeeId must be positive: " + employeeId);
        }
    }

    private static LocalDate parseDate(String date) {
        try {
            return LocalDate.parse(date, DATE);
        } catch (DateTimeParseException ex) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("date must be yyyy-MM-dd: " + date);
        }
    }

    private static LocalTime parseTime(String time) {
        try {
            return LocalTime.parse(time, TIME);
        } catch (DateTimeParseException ex) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("time must be HH:mm or HH:mm:ss: " + time);
        }
    }
}

package motorphemployee.oop;

import java.time.LocalDate;
import java.time.ZoneId;
import java.time.ZonedDateTime;
import java.time.format.DateTimeParseException;
import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.Collections;
import java.util.LinkedHashMap;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Map;

/**
 * PayrollCalculator - the orchestrator: attendance + employee in, one immutable PayrollRecord out
 * (MS1 Week 4/5 CRC: "PayrollCalculator (Service Class Using Abstraction)"; Method Dictionary rows
 * calculatePayroll / calculateGross / calculateNetPay).
 *
 * This class is the refactored home of the payroll logic that CP2 copy-pasted into BOTH
 * MainMenu (1,558 lines) and Dashboard (1,442 lines) - four calculate*() formulas, twice. After the
 * After the GUI rewiring there is exactly one implementation of each formula in the whole project.
 *
 * Uses abstraction, not concrete types: the statutory deductions are held as
 * List<GovernmentContributionCalculator>, so a new deduction is a new subclass plus one line in
 * the constructor - this class never changes and never asks "which calculator are you?".
 *
 * Two phases (Refactoring Plan design):
 *   phase 1 - SSS, PhilHealth, Pag-IBIG are computed on GROSS pay (one polymorphic loop)
 *   phase 2 - withholding tax is computed on the TAXABLE income (gross minus phase 1)
 *
 * Official matrices (2026-10-27): the four calculators follow the OFFICIAL government matrices, not
 * CP2, so a CP2 mismatch is expected and documented in oop/matrix-verification.md.
 */
public class PayrollCalculator {

    /** Standard MotorPH work day used by CP2 (MainMenu.java:1090: workedDays * hourlyRate * 8). */
    private static final double HOURS_PER_WORK_DAY = 8.0;

    /** Default payroll period length when the caller does not pass an explicit one. */
    private static final int DEFAULT_PERIOD_DAYS = 15;

    private static final ZoneId PAYROLL_ZONE = ZoneId.of("Asia/Manila");

    /** Contribution codes from the approved design; used to name the amounts, never to branch on type. */
    private static final String CODE_SSS = "SSS";
    private static final String CODE_PHILHEALTH = "PH";
    private static final String CODE_PAGIBIG = "PAGIBIG";

    private final List<GovernmentContributionCalculator> statutory;
    private final GovernmentContributionCalculator withholdingTax;

    /** Production default: the three statutory deductions plus BIR withholding tax. */
    public PayrollCalculator() {
        this(defaultStatutory(), new WithholdingTaxCalculator());
    }

    /**
     * Injectable composition - the constructor a test or a future payroll variant uses.
     * Because the field type is the abstract parent, the caller can swap any calculator.
     */
    public PayrollCalculator(List<GovernmentContributionCalculator> statutory,
                             GovernmentContributionCalculator withholdingTax) {
        if (statutory == null || statutory.isEmpty()) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("at least one statutory calculator is required");
        }
        for (GovernmentContributionCalculator calculator : statutory) {
            if (calculator == null) {
                throw new IllegalArgumentException("statutory calculator list cannot contain null");
            }
        }
        if (withholdingTax == null) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("withholdingTax calculator is required");
        }
        this.statutory = Collections.unmodifiableList(new ArrayList<>(statutory));
        this.withholdingTax = withholdingTax;
    }

    // ---------------------------------------------------------------- public API

    /**
     * Payroll for the most recent semi-monthly period (overload without dates).
     * Same computation as the 4-argument overload - only the period differs.
     */
    public PayrollRecord calculatePayroll(Employee employee, AttendanceLog attendance) {
        requireEmployee(employee);
        requireAttendance(attendance);

        LocalDate periodEndDay = LocalDate.now(PAYROLL_ZONE);
        LocalDate periodStartDay = periodEndDay.minusDays(DEFAULT_PERIOD_DAYS - 1L);
        return calculatePayroll(employee, attendance, periodStartDay.toString(), periodEndDay.toString());
    }

    /**
     * Payroll for an explicit period - the single public entry point of the whole computation.
     *
     * @throws IllegalArgumentException when the employee or attendance is missing, when the period
     *         is invalid, when the computed gross pay is not positive (Issue 1 fix), or
     *         when the statutory deductions would consume the entire gross pay.
     */
    public PayrollRecord calculatePayroll(Employee employee,
                                          AttendanceLog attendance,
                                          String periodStart,
                                          String periodEnd) {
        requireEmployee(employee);
        requireAttendance(attendance);
        LocalDate start = parsePeriodDate(periodStart, "periodStart");
        LocalDate end = parsePeriodDate(periodEnd, "periodEnd");
        if (end.isBefore(start)) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("periodEnd cannot be before periodStart: "
                    + periodStart + " -> " + periodEnd);
        }

        int employeeId = employee.getId();
        double hourlyRate = employee.getHourlyRate();
        int workedDays = attendance.getWorkedDays(employeeId, periodStart, periodEnd);
        double grossIncome = calculateGross(attendance, employeeId, hourlyRate, periodStart, periodEnd);

        // Issue 1: a non-positive gross pay must never reach the deduction tables,
        // otherwise the statutory minimums turn a 0.00 payslip into a negative one.
        if (!(grossIncome > 0)) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("cannot compute payroll for employee " + employeeId
                    + ": gross pay is " + grossIncome + " because " + workedDays
                    + " day(s) of attendance were found in " + periodStart + ".." + periodEnd);
        }

        // ---- phase 1: the three statutory deductions, one loop over the ABSTRACT type ----
        Map<String, Double> statutoryAmounts = new LinkedHashMap<>();
        double statutoryTotal = 0.0;
        for (GovernmentContributionCalculator calculator : statutory) {
            if (!calculator.isActive()) {
                continue;
            }
            double amount = calculator.calculate(grossIncome);
            statutoryAmounts.put(calculator.getContributionCode(), amount);
            statutoryTotal += amount;
        }

        double sss = amountOf(statutoryAmounts, CODE_SSS);
        double philhealth = amountOf(statutoryAmounts, CODE_PHILHEALTH);
        double pagibig = amountOf(statutoryAmounts, CODE_PAGIBIG);

        if (statutoryTotal >= grossIncome) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("statutory deductions (" + statutoryTotal
                    + ") would consume the whole gross pay (" + grossIncome
                    + ") for employee " + employeeId + " - no payslip can be produced");
        }

        // ---- phase 2: BIR withholding tax on the income already net of the three above ----
        double taxableIncome = grossIncome - statutoryTotal;
        double tax = withholdingTax.isActive() ? withholdingTax.calculate(taxableIncome) : 0.0;

        double totalDeductions = sss + philhealth + pagibig + tax;
        double netIncome = calculateNetPay(grossIncome, totalDeductions);

        ZonedDateTime issueDate = ZonedDateTime.now(PAYROLL_ZONE);
        return new PayrollRecord(
                employeeId,
                issueDate,
                start.atStartOfDay(PAYROLL_ZONE),
                end.atTime(23, 59).atZone(PAYROLL_ZONE),
                employee.getBasicSalary(),
                employee.getPhoneAllowance(),
                employee.getRiceSubsidy(),
                employee.getClothingAllowance(),
                grossIncome,
                employee.getGrossSemiMonthlyRate(),
                netIncome,
                sss,
                philhealth,
                pagibig,
                tax,
                employee.getAnnualLeaveCredits(),
                workedDays * HOURS_PER_WORK_DAY,
                hourlyRate,
                0L);                 // absences: no attendance.csv yet (open question), never invented
    }

    @Override
    public String toString() {
        return "PayrollCalculator{statutory=" + statutory + ", tax=" + withholdingTax + "}";
    }

    // ---------------------------------------------------------------- private computation

    /** gross = workedDays * hourlyRate * 8 (Method Dictionary row "calculateGross"). */
    private double calculateGross(AttendanceLog attendance,
                                  int employeeId,
                                  double hourlyRate,
                                  String periodStart,
                                  String periodEnd) {
        int workedDays = attendance.getWorkedDays(employeeId, periodStart, periodEnd);
        return workedDays * hourlyRate * HOURS_PER_WORK_DAY;
    }

    /** net = gross - all deductions (Method Dictionary row "calculateNetPay"). */
    private double calculateNetPay(double gross, double deductions) {
        if (Double.isNaN(gross) || Double.isNaN(deductions)) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("gross and deductions must be numbers");
        }
        if (deductions < 0) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("deductions cannot be negative: " + deductions);
        }
        return gross - deductions;
    }

    // ---------------------------------------------------------------- helpers

    private static List<GovernmentContributionCalculator> defaultStatutory() {
        List<GovernmentContributionCalculator> calculators = new ArrayList<>();
        calculators.add(new SSSCalculator());
        calculators.add(new PhilHealthCalculator());
        calculators.add(new PagIbigCalculator());
        return calculators;
    }

    private static double amountOf(Map<String, Double> amounts, String code) {
        Double amount = amounts.get(code);
        return amount == null ? 0.0 : amount;
    }

    private static void requireEmployee(Employee employee) {
        if (employee == null) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("employee is required");
        }
    }

    private static void requireAttendance(AttendanceLog attendance) {
        if (attendance == null) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("attendance is required");
        }
    }
package motorphemployee.oop;

/**
 * WithholdingTaxCalculator - BIR progressive withholding tax, 6 brackets up to 35%
 * (MS1 Week 3 CRC: "WithholdingTaxCalculator (Concrete Subclass)").
 *
 * Applied AFTER SSS/PhilHealth/Pag-IBIG, so the input is the salary already net of those
 * three contributions - same as CP2 MainMenu.java:1418 / Dashboard.java:1334.
 *
 * Official matrix (2026-10-27): bracket 1 uses the official excess base of 20,833, not CP2's
 * 20,832 (Home_WithholdingTax_Matrix.xlsx bracket text B3 and SAMPLE B20: taxable 23,400 ->
 * 513.40). CP2 over-withheld PHP 0.20 for every taxable income in [20,833, 33,333] - Issue 4.
 * Brackets 2-6 were already exact and are unchanged.
 */
public class WithholdingTaxCalculator extends GovernmentContributionCalculator {

    /** BIR brackets: upper bound of the bracket, base tax, excess over the previous bound, marginal rate. */
    private static final double[] UPPER_BOUNDS = {20832.0, 33333.0, 66667.0, 166667.0, 666667.0};
    private static final double[] BASE_TAX = {0.0, 0.0, 2500.0, 10833.0, 40833.33};
    private static final double[] LOWER_BOUNDS = {0.0, 20833.0, 33333.0, 66667.0, 166667.0};
    private static final double[] MARGINAL_RATES = {0.0, 0.20, 0.25, 0.30, 0.32};
    private static final double TOP_LOWER_BOUND = 666667.0;
    private static final double TOP_BASE_TAX = 200833.33;
    private static final double TOP_MARGINAL_RATE = 0.35;

    public WithholdingTaxCalculator() {
        super("Withholding Tax", "TAX");
    }

    @Override
    public double calculate(double taxableIncome) {
        double income = requireValidSalary(taxableIncome);

        for (int i = 0; i < UPPER_BOUNDS.length; i++) {
            if (income <= UPPER_BOUNDS[i]) {
                // max(0, ...) guards the 20,832.01-20,832.99 gap between the exempt ceiling and
                // the official 20,833 excess base, so the tax can never come out negative.
                return Math.max(0.0, BASE_TAX[i] + (income - LOWER_BOUNDS[i]) * MARGINAL_RATES[i]);
            }
        }
        return TOP_BASE_TAX + (income - TOP_LOWER_BOUND) * TOP_MARGINAL_RATE;
    }
}

import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
import { spawn, execFileSync } from 'node:child_process';
import { mkdtempSync, readFileSync, readdirSync, rmSync } from 'node:fs';
import net from 'node:net';
import { tmpdir } from 'node:os';
import path from 'node:path';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
import { chromium } from 'playwright-core';

const projectRoot = path.resolve(path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), '../..');
const sourceDir = path.join(projectRoot, 'src/main/java/ph/motorph/web');
const gsonJar = path.join(projectRoot, 'lib/gson-2.13.2.jar');
const timeoutMs = 15_000;
const javaClasses = mkdtempSync(path.join(tmpdir(), 'motorph-e2e-classes-'));
const serverChildren = [];
let browser;

function freePort() {
  return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
    const server = net.createServer();
    server.once('error', reject);
    server.listen(0, '127.0.0.1', () => {
      const { port } = server.address();
      server.close(error => error ? reject(error) : resolve(port));
    });
  });
}

function start(command, args, env, label) {
  const child = spawn(command, args, {
    cwd: projectRoot,
    env,
    detached: process.platform !== 'win32',
    stdio: ['ignore', 'pipe', 'pipe']
  });
  child.log = '';
  child.on('error', error => { child.log += `${label}: ${error.message}\n`; });
  for (const stream of [child.stdout, child.stderr]) {
    stream.setEncoding('utf8');
    stream.on('data', chunk => { child.log = (child.log + chunk).slice(-8000); });
  }
  serverChildren.push(child);
  return child;
}

async function waitForServer(url, child, label) {
  const end = Date.now() + timeoutMs;
  let lastError = 'no response';
  while (Date.now() < end) {
    if (child.exitCode !== null) throw new Error(`${label} exited early.\n${child.log}`);
    try {
      const response = await fetch(url);
      if (response.ok) return response;
      lastError = `HTTP ${response.status}`;
    } catch (error) {
      lastError = error.message;
    }
    await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 150));
  }
  throw new Error(`${label} did not become ready (${lastError}).\n${child.log}`);
}

async function stop(child) {
  if (!child || child.exitCode !== null) return;
  try {
    if (process.platform === 'win32') child.kill('SIGTERM');
    else process.kill(-child.pid, 'SIGTERM');
  } catch { /* already stopped */ }
  await Promise.race([
    new Promise(resolve => child.once('exit', resolve)),
    new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 2500))
  ]);
  if (child.exitCode === null) {
    try {
      if (process.platform === 'win32') child.kill('SIGKILL');
      else process.kill(-child.pid, 'SIGKILL');
    } catch { /* already stopped */ }
  }
}

async function main() {
  const apiPort = await freePort();
  const webPort = await freePort();
  const sources = readdirSync(sourceDir).filter(file => file.endsWith('.java')).map(file => path.join(sourceDir, file));
  execFileSync('javac', ['--add-modules', 'jdk.httpserver', '-cp', gsonJar, '-d', javaClasses, ...sources], {
    cwd: projectRoot,
    stdio: 'inherit'
  });

  const apiEnv = {
    ...process.env,
    PORT: String(apiPort),
    HOST: '127.0.0.1',
    WEB_ROOT: path.join(projectRoot, 'web'),
    FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID: ''
  };
  const api = start('java', ['--add-modules', 'jdk.httpserver', '-cp', `${gsonJar}:${javaClasses}`, 'ph.motorph.web.AppServer'], apiEnv, 'Java API');
  await waitForServer(`http://127.0.0.1:${apiPort}/api/health`, api, 'Java API');

  const webEnv = {
    ...process.env,
    API_PROXY_TARGET: `http://127.0.0.1:${apiPort}`,
    VITE_FIREBASE_API_KEY: '',
    VITE_FIREBASE_AUTH_DOMAIN: '',
    VITE_FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID: '',
    VITE_FIREBASE_APP_ID: '',
    VITE_FIREBASE_STORAGE_BUCKET: '',
    VITE_FIREBASE_MESSAGING_SENDER_ID: ''
  };
  const npm = process.platform === 'win32' ? 'npm.cmd' : 'npm';
  const vite = start(npm, ['run', 'dev', '--', '--host', '127.0.0.1', '--port', String(webPort)], webEnv, 'Vite');
  const baseUrl = `http://127.0.0.1:${webPort}`;
  const healthResponse = await waitForServer(`${baseUrl}/api/health`, vite, 'Vite/API proxy');
  const health = await healthResponse.json();
  assert.equal(health.mode, 'local-synthetic-demo', 'E2E must use isolated local process memory, not Firebase');

  try {
    browser = await chromium.launch({ headless: true, args: ['--no-sandbox', '--disable-dev-shm-usage'] });
  } catch (error) {
    throw new Error(`Chromium could not launch. Install the Playwright browser and its system dependencies.\n${error.message}`);
  }
  const page = await browser.newPage({ viewport: { width: 1365, height: 900 } });
  const pageErrors = [];
  page.on('pageerror', error => pageErrors.push(error.message));
  await page.goto(baseUrl);
  await page.waitForSelector('#app-shell:not([hidden])', { timeout: timeoutMs });
  await page.waitForFunction(() => document.querySelectorAll('#employee-rows tr').length === 3, { timeout: timeoutMs });
  assert.equal((await page.locator('#workflow-storage-mode').textContent()).trim(), 'Local API memory');
  assert.equal((await page.locator('#overview-workflow-count').textContent()).trim(), '00');
  console.log('PASS: local workspace loads the three synthetic fixture employees and dynamic overview.');

  let simulatedFailure = { status: 403, error: 'Synthetic rules denial.' };
  const failureHandler = route => route.fulfill({
    status: simulatedFailure.status,
    contentType: 'application/json',
    body: JSON.stringify({ error: simulatedFailure.error })
  });
  await page.route('**/api/workflows', failureHandler);
  await page.reload();
  await page.waitForFunction(() => !document.getElementById('workflow-load-status').hidden, { timeout: timeoutMs });
  assert.match(await page.locator('#workflow-load-status').textContent(), /Synthetic rules denial/);
  simulatedFailure = { status: 503, error: 'Synthetic service outage.' };
  await page.reload();
  await page.waitForFunction(() => document.getElementById('workflow-load-status').textContent.includes('Synthetic service outage'), { timeout: timeoutMs });
  await page.unroute('**/api/workflows', failureHandler);
  await page.reload();
  await page.waitForFunction(() => (document.getElementById('workflow-storage-mode').textContent || '').trim() === 'Local API memory', { timeout: timeoutMs });
  console.log('PASS: workflow authorization/service errors are visible and recover after retry.');

  await page.locator('[data-view="hr"]').click();
  await page.locator('#employee-edit-name').fill('Synthetic Browser E2E');
  await page.locator('#employee-edit-department').fill('QA Demo');
  await page.locator('#employee-edit-role').fill('Browser Tester');
  await page.locator('#employee-edit-location').fill('Taguig');
  await page.locator('#employee-edit-status').selectOption('Active');
  await page.locator('#employee-save-button').click();
  await page.waitForFunction(() => document.getElementById('employee-form-status').textContent.startsWith('Created DEMO-'), { timeout: timeoutMs });
  const createMessage = await page.locator('#employee-form-status').textContent();
  const employeeId = createMessage.match(/DEMO-[A-F0-9]{12}/)?.[0];
  assert.ok(employeeId, 'create response should show a server-generated ID');
  assert.match(createMessage, /shared local API-process memory/);
  await page.locator('#hr-directory-search').fill(employeeId);
  await page.locator('#hr-directory-status').selectOption('Active');
  assert.equal(await page.locator('#hr-rows tr').filter({ hasText: employeeId }).count(), 1);
  await page.locator('#hr-directory-search').fill('no-such-person');

  assert.ok(ticketId, 'ticket submit should return a synthetic ticket ID');

  assert.match(await ticketRow.innerText(), /Synthetic browser ticket E2E/);

    return row && row.textContent.includes('Cancelled');

  console.log('PASS: ticket submit/queue/cancel flow.');
