function renderAttendanceReport(items) {
  state.attendanceReport = items;
  const rows = document.getElementById('attendance-report-rows');
  rows.replaceChildren();
  if (!items.length) {
    showWorkflowTableMessage(rows, 6, 'No synthetic employees are available for this report.');
  } else {
    items.forEach(item => {
      const row = document.createElement('tr');
      row.append(makeCell(`${item.employeeName} · ${item.employeeId}`));
      row.append(makeCell(item.hasScheduleMapping ? `Schedule ${item.scheduleId}` : 'No mapping'));
      row.append(makeCell(String(item.rawRecordCount)));
      row.append(makeCell(item.firstRecordDate || '—'));
      row.append(makeCell(item.lastRecordDate || '—'));
      if (item.hasScheduleMapping) {
        const openButton = document.createElement('button');
        openButton.type = 'button';
        openButton.className = 'button button-quiet workflow-report-open';
        openButton.dataset.employeeId = item.employeeId;
        openButton.textContent = 'View rows';
        openButton.setAttribute('aria-label', `View raw entries for ${item.employeeId}`);
        row.append(makeCell(openButton));
      } else {
        row.append(makeCell('—'));
      }
      rows.append(row);
    });
  }
  const totalRawRows = items.reduce((total, item) => total + (Number.isInteger(item.rawRecordCount) ? item.rawRecordCount : 0), 0);
  document.getElementById('attendance-report-count').textContent = `${items.length} employee ${items.length === 1 ? 'row' : 'rows'} · ${totalRawRows} raw ${totalRawRows === 1 ? 'record' : 'records'} in range`;
  document.getElementById('attendance-report-export').disabled = items.length === 0;
}

async function loadAttendanceReport() {
  const requestNumber = ++state.reportRequestNumber;
  const status = document.getElementById('attendance-report-status');
  status.hidden = true;
  status.textContent = '';
  document.getElementById('attendance-report-count').textContent = 'Loading report';
  document.getElementById('attendance-report-export').disabled = true;
  showWorkflowTableMessage(document.getElementById('attendance-report-rows'), 6, 'Loading raw attendance summary…');
  const params = new URLSearchParams();
  const from = document.getElementById('attendance-report-from').value;
  const to = document.getElementById('attendance-report-to').value;
  if (from) params.set('from', from);
  if (to) params.set('to', to);
  const query = params.toString();
  try {
    const response = await fetch(`/api/reports/attendance${query ? `?${query}` : ''}`, { headers: await apiHeaders() });
    const payload = await response.json();
    if (!response.ok) throw new Error(payload.error || `Request failed (${response.status})`);
    if (!payload || !Array.isArray(payload.items) || payload.hoursCalculated !== false) {
      throw new Error('Unexpected attendance report response.');
    }
    if (requestNumber !== state.reportRequestNumber) return;
    renderAttendanceReport(payload.items);
    status.textContent = 'Loaded raw record counts and date coverage only; no hours or payroll values were calculated.';
    status.hidden = false;
  } catch (error) {
    if (requestNumber !== state.reportRequestNumber) return;
    state.attendanceReport = [];
    showWorkflowTableMessage(document.getElementById('attendance-report-rows'), 6, error.message || 'Could not load the raw attendance report.');
    document.getElementById('attendance-report-count').textContent = 'Could not load report';
    document.getElementById('attendance-report-export').disabled = true;
    status.textContent = error.message || 'Could not load the raw attendance report.';
    status.hidden = false;
  }
}

async function loadEmployees() {
  const requestNumber = ++state.requestNumber;
  const query = search.value.trim();
  showTableMessage('Loading employee records…');
  resultCount.textContent = 'Loading';
  try {
    const url = query ? `/api/employees?q=${encodeURIComponent(query)}` : '/api/employees';
    const response = await fetch(url, { headers: await apiHeaders() });
    const payload = await response.json();
    if (!response.ok) throw new Error(payload.error || `Request failed (${response.status})`);
    if (!payload || !Array.isArray(payload.items)) throw new Error('Unexpected employee response');
    if (requestNumber !== state.requestNumber) return;
    state.employees = payload.items;
    state.totalEmployees = Number.isInteger(payload.total) ? payload.total : payload.items.length;
    if (!query) {
      state.allEmployees = payload.items;
  }
});

function switchView(view) {
  const labels = { overview: 'Overview', employees: 'Employees', attendance: 'Attendance', requests: 'Requests & tickets', team: 'Team roster', hr: 'HR operations', reports: 'Reports', payroll: 'Payroll' };
  if (!labels[view]) return;
  document.querySelectorAll('.page-view').forEach(page => {
    page.hidden = page.id !== `${view}-view`;
  });
  document.querySelectorAll('.nav-item').forEach(nav => {
    const active = nav.dataset.view === view;
    nav.classList.toggle('active', active);
    if (active) nav.setAttribute('aria-current', 'page');
    else nav.removeAttribute('aria-current');
  });
  document.getElementById('crumb-current').textContent = labels[view];
  document.title = `${labels[view]} — MotorPH Payroll Office`;
  if (view === 'attendance' && attendanceEmployee.value) loadAttendance();
  if (view === 'reports') loadAttendanceReport();
}

document.querySelectorAll('.nav-item').forEach(item => {
  item.addEventListener('click', () => switchView(item.dataset.view));
});

export function directoryLabelSummaryRows(employees) {
  if (!Array.isArray(employees)) return [];
  const counts = new Map();
  employees.forEach(employee => {
    if (!employee || typeof employee !== 'object') return;
    [['Status label', employee.status], ['Department label', employee.department]].forEach(([category, label]) => {
      if (typeof label !== 'string' || !label.trim()) return;
      const key = `${category}\u0000${label}`;
      counts.set(key, (counts.get(key) || 0) + 1);
    });
  });
  return [...counts.entries()]
    .map(([key, count]) => {
      const [category, label] = key.split('\u0000');
      return { category, label, employeeRecords: count };
    })
    .sort((a, b) => a.category.localeCompare(b.category) || a.label.localeCompare(b.label));
}
import test from 'node:test';
import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
import { directoryLabelSummaryRows } from '../../web/directory-summary.js';

test('counts stored status and department labels independently and in stable order', () => {
  const result = directoryLabelSummaryRows([
    { status: 'Active', department: 'Operations' },
    { status: 'On leave', department: 'Operations' },
    { status: 'Active', department: 'Finance' }
  ]);
  assert.deepEqual(result, [
    { category: 'Department label', label: 'Finance', employeeRecords: 1 },
    { category: 'Department label', label: 'Operations', employeeRecords: 2 },
    { category: 'Status label', label: 'Active', employeeRecords: 2 },
    { category: 'Status label', label: 'On leave', employeeRecords: 1 }
  ]);
});

test('returns an empty summary for missing collections and skips malformed labels', () => {
  assert.deepEqual(directoryLabelSummaryRows(null), []);
  assert.deepEqual(directoryLabelSummaryRows([null, {}, { status: '', department: 7 }]), []);
});

function freePort() {
  return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
    const server = net.createServer();
    server.once('error', reject);
    server.listen(0, '127.0.0.1', () => {
      const { port } = server.address();
      server.close(error => error ? reject(error) : resolve(port));
    });
  });
}

# Source-grounded acceptance baseline (draft)

**Purpose:** record observable pass/fail behavior already implemented and define safe candidate acceptance criteria before tailoring. This is a working baseline, **not an approved rubric interpretation**. No standalone active MO-IT110 grading rubric was identified among the supplied files in the workspace; the older MO-IT108/107 documents and peer submissions inform scope, while the Terminal Assessment proposal is treated as placeholder material rather than an authoritative detailed specification.

**Scope rules:** fictional data only; use the signed-in user's sandbox in Firebase mode; keep ordinary local-preview persistence explicitly process-memory; do not treat inferred attendance/payroll rules, peer-project choices, employee-to-account identity, reviewer authority, or access boundaries as approved policy. At the user's direction, a clearly labelled 2026 monthly statutory preview is now available with synthetic inputs only; its rules are isolated in a changeable module and it has no API/Firestore/payslip path. Attendance-based or persistent payroll, approvals, and reviewer controls remain gated. See `docs/candidate-policy-review.md`. The user-published development rules remain unchanged.

## Candidate acceptance matrix

| Area | Observable acceptance in current prototype | State | Source / boundary |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Authentication and sandbox | Email/password account creation/sign-in/sign-out on localhost; Firebase requests use the caller's ID token and user-scoped paths. Auth lifecycle smoke uses a disposable account, verifies empty reads, signs out, deletes the account, and makes no Firestore writes. | Verified locally; exact Arena preview origin still unverified | Firebase setup guide, Firestore rules review, browser smoke evidence. No organizational roles or employee-account mapping. |
| Employee directory | Search/detail; create/update only name, department, role label, location, and demo status; server-generated IDs; HR-table text/status filters; read-only synthetic label-count summary. | Implemented and browser tested | Legacy MO-IT108 traceability and API contract. No salary/government IDs, termination, employee delete, schedule assignment, or audit history. |
| Raw attendance view | Select an employee; inclusive optional date range; show/export raw records and record-date bounds. Empty records for unmapped employees are not treated as absence. | Read-only and tested | MO-IT107 data dictionary plus earlier MO-IT108 default-range behavior. No capture/correction flow because the source does not define its input process and the current rules lack transaction-safe schedule/date uniqueness. |
| Attendance coverage report | By configured employee-to-schedule mapping, return raw-row counts and first/last dates for an optional inclusive range; allow drill-through to raw rows and CSV export. Unmapped means “not attributed,” not “absent.” | Implemented; API and browser tested, including an empty signed-in Firebase sandbox | This summarizes stored rows only. No hours, attendance classification, worked days, or payroll period are inferred. |
| Leave request | Submit fictional request with validated type/date range; cancel own pending request; search/status/date-overlap filter history; show submitted/cancelled timestamps and notes; calendar shows submitted request dates only and lets the user draft form bounds from selected dates without submitting or calculating days. | Implemented; local E2E and Firestore live smoke passed | Source set does not define accrual, balances, eligibility, approvals, reviewer scope, calendar approval status, or payroll treatment. Those remain gated. |
| Help-desk ticket | Submit fictional ticket; derive documented queue label; cancel own open ticket; search/filter history; reveal message/timestamps and export CSV. | Implemented; local E2E and Firestore live smoke passed | Queue labels are demonstration labels only. No real delivery, assignment, reviewer authorization, resolution, or notifications. |
| Team and HR operations | Team screen is read-only with search/status filtering and filtered CSV export; HR desk can create/update the allowlisted synthetic directory fields and filter its table. | Partial, owner-sandbox only | No membership model, supervisor relationships, HR role, lifecycle permissions, audit trail, or employee-account binding is defined. |
| Reporting and exports | CSV exports for visible synthetic employees, filtered Team roster, raw selected attendance, attendance coverage, directory status/department label counts, and owner-sandbox workflows; formula-leading values are neutralized. Overview shows current directory, selected raw attendance, and workflow counts. | Implemented and tested | No payroll reports, payslips, monthly pay-period reports, or archival deletion. |
| Temporary 2026 statutory preview | Client-side-only monthly preview accepts explicit synthetic cash pay, SSS compensation, PhilHealth MBS, Pag-IBIG Fund Salary, and taxable compensation bases; shows employee/employer contributions, monthly BIR withholding, net estimate, and employer contribution cost. No API/Firestore/payslip persistence. | Implemented; pure logic tests and local browser E2E | Provisional 2026 current-rule profile; formula/constants are isolated in `web/payroll-rules-2026.js` and `web/payroll-preview-2026.js`. Half-up centavo rounding and monthly tax basis are explicit assumptions. Not production payroll. |
| Attendance-based/persistent payroll | No attendance-derived gross, pay-period allocation, saved payroll, payslip, or payroll report. | Intentionally gated | Still unresolved: chosen cutoff/deduction timing, lunch/hour treatment, leave/holiday treatment, salary conversion, benefits/tax treatment, roles, and accepted end-to-end worked examples. See `docs/candidate-policy-review.md`. |
| Release readiness | Java/web unit checks, local browser E2E, live localhost Auth smoke, build, and dependency audit run. | Development prototype only | No production hosting, role security review, backup/monitoring, or published preview-origin verification. |

## Already done — current foundation

- Raw attendance records are selectable by employee and inclusive date range; default range spans that employee's earliest/latest available records, following the older Requirements Analysis. A separate read-only coverage report summarizes raw row counts and date bounds by configured employee-to-schedule mapping; unmapped is not reported as absent.
- The Payroll workspace contains a disposable 2026 statutory preview from synthetic values; it is not connected to attendance. The default attendance range is not a pay period.

              <p><strong>SSS:</strong> 2025 schedule remains the latest published contribution table found for the 2026 preview; employee 5% and employer 10% apply to MSC up to ₱35,000, with EC ₱10/₱30 paid by employer. <a href="https://www.sss.gov.ph/pay-contribution/">SSS contribution schedule</a></p>
              <p><strong>PhilHealth:</strong> 5% of monthly basic salary with ₱10,000 floor/₱100,000 ceiling, split equally. Commission, overtime and allowances are excluded from the MBS base. <a href="https://www.philhealth.gov.ph/advisories/2025/PA2025-0002.pdf">PA2025-0002</a></p>
              <p><strong>Pag-IBIG:</strong> MFS ceiling ₱10,000; employee 1% at ₱1,500 and below or 2% above; employer 2%. <a href="https://www.pagibigfund.gov.ph/documents/Circular%20No.%20460%20-%20Guidelines%20on%20the%20Pag-IBIG%20Fund's%20Implementation%20of%20Increase%20in%20the%20MFS%20Effective%20February%202024.pdf">Circular No. 460</a></p>
              <p><strong>BIR:</strong> uses the published monthly withholding table from Annex E to RR 11-2018 (effective 2023 onward), not the annualized method used by one third-party library. The monthly/annualized example differs by ₱0.05. <a href="https://bir-cdn.bir.gov.ph/local/pdf/Annex%20E%20RR%2011-2018.pdf">BIR Annex E</a></p>
              <p>All bases are typed separately by the user, and centavo rounding is a provisional half-up rule. No employee status, eligibility, semi-monthly deduction split, non-cash benefits, 13th-month annualisation, or tax adjustment is inferred.</p>

function renderAttendance(records) {
  state.rawAttendance = [...records].sort((a, b) => String(a.date).localeCompare(String(b.date)));
  const orderedRecords = state.rawAttendance;
  document.getElementById('attendance-export-button').disabled = orderedRecords.length === 0;
  applyDefaultAttendanceRange(orderedRecords);
  renderRawAttendanceSummary(orderedRecords);
  attendanceRows.replaceChildren();
  if (orderedRecords.length === 0) {
    showAttendanceMessage('No attendance entries match this employee and date range.');
  } else {
    orderedRecords.forEach(record => {
      const row = document.createElement('tr');
      [record.date, String(record.attendanceId), String(record.scheduleId), record.timeIn, record.timeOut, record.dayType]
        .forEach(value => row.append(makeCell(value)));
      attendanceRows.append(row);
    });

function resetSessionData() {
  state.requestNumber += 1;
  state.attendanceRequestNumber += 1;
  state.reportRequestNumber += 1;
  window.clearTimeout(state.searchTimer);
  state.searchTimer = null;
  state.employees = [];
  state.allEmployees = [];
  state.totalEmployees = 0;
  state.rawAttendance = [];
  state.attendanceReport = [];
  document.getElementById('attendance-report-from').value = '';
  document.getElementById('attendance-report-to').value = '';
  document.getElementById('attendance-report-search').value = '';
  document.getElementById('attendance-report-mapping').value = 'all';
  document.getElementById('attendance-report-sort').value = 'employeeId';
  document.getElementById('attendance-report-order').value = 'asc';
  document.getElementById('attendance-report-status').hidden = true;
  document.getElementById('attendance-report-status').textContent = '';
  document.getElementById('attendance-report-count').textContent = 'No report loaded';
  document.getElementById('attendance-report-export').disabled = true;
  document.getElementById('directory-summary-export').disabled = true;
  document.getElementById('directory-summary-export-status').textContent = '';
  renderRawAttendanceSummary([]);
  state.selected = null;
  state.workflow = createWorkflowState();
  leaveCalendarMonth = new Date();
  leaveDateSelectionStart = '';
  leaveDateSelectionEnd = '';
  document.getElementById('leave-calendar-selection-status').textContent = 'Choose the first date to draft a request range.';
  search.value = '';

| Attendance coverage report | By configured employee-to-schedule mapping, return raw-row counts and first/last dates for an optional inclusive range; allow employee/name/ID/schedule search, mapped/unmapped filtering, field/direction sorting, drill-through to raw rows, and CSV export of visible rows. Unmapped means “not attributed,” not “absent.” | Implemented; API and browser tested, including an empty signed-in Firebase sandbox | This summarizes stored rows only. | Leave request | Submit fictional request with validated type/date range; cancel own pending request; search/status/date-overlap filter history; show submitted/cancelled timestamps and notes; calendar shows submitted request dates only and lets the user draft form bounds from selected dates without submitting or calculating days. | Implemented; local E2E and Firestore live smoke passed | Source set does not define accrual, balances, eligibility, approvals, reviewer scope, calendar approval status, or payroll treatment. function showTableMessage(message) {
  rows.replaceChildren();
  const row = document.createElement('tr');
  const cell = document.createElement('td');
  cell.colSpan = 6;
  cell.className = 'table-message';
  cell.textContent = message;
  row.append(cell);
  rows.append(row);
}

[NODE 4199]
## What works

- Overview with live sandbox counts, searchable employee directory/detail, employee directory sort controls, HR directory search/status filters/sorting, a synthetic directory-label summary, sortable raw attendance register and searchable/filterable/sortable coverage report, Requests & tickets, searchable/sortable read-only Team roster, and a temporary 2026 monthly statutory preview. Employee details open from a native keyboard-operable button without overriding table semantics; result counts and form feedback use polite status regions.
- Java employee/attendance services plus a workflow service. Local preview workflow records are held in Java process memory; Firebase mode uses the signed-in user’s Firestore subcollections.
- Leave requests and tickets validate inputs, derive employee names from the caller’s own synthetic directory, show documented queue labels, and support owner-sandbox cancellation. A monthly leave-request calendar displays pending/cancelled request dates only and can draft form bounds from two selected dates; it does not imply approval, submit a request, calculate days, or show balances. Search/status and inclusive requested-date-overlap filters narrow the leave history table only; they do not change the calendar markers or all-record exports. Row details reveal the submitted note/message and UTC timestamps without adding a reviewer workflow. Both local and Firestore workflow histories are ordered newest first. No reviewer/approval/resolve/delete routes exist. The user has published the rules; live tests confirmed leave and ticket create/cancel persistence, plus cross-user denial.
- Read-only Team roster plus a synthetic directory editor. In Firebase mode, signed-in users can create/edit only name, department, role label, location, and demo status in their own sandbox. Local preview has no user authentication and shares one process-memory store for that API process. IDs are server-generated; delete, termination, schedule, salary, and government-ID fields are not exposed. New records receive no schedule mapping, so their raw attendance view is empty. This is not an HR role or a production employee-admin workflow.
- CSV export for currently visible synthetic employee results, filtered HR directory and Team roster rows, loaded raw attendance rows, visible attendance coverage rows, synthetic directory label-count summaries, and owner-sandbox workflow records. CSV cells are quoted and spreadsheet-formula prefixes are neutralized; exports contain no derived hours or payroll values.
- Temporary monthly 2026 statutory preview: explicit separate fictional bases, SSS MSC/employee/employer/EC, PhilHealth employee/employer shares, Pag-IBIG employee/employer shares, BIR monthly withholding, net estimate and employer contribution cost. Logic is isolated in versioned rules/calculator modules; it is client-side only and is not retained.
- Server-side employee search/detail, HR table search/status filters, a user-scoped attendance-coverage report (raw row counts and first/last record dates by configured mapping), synthetic directory label counts by status/department with CSV export, and dynamic overview counts. Unmapped employees are labeled as unmapped, not absent. The attendance date fields default to that employee's earliest/latest available records, following the earlier MO-IT108 Requirements Analysis; the user can narrow the range. This is not a payroll-period calendar. The attendance API and reports do not derive hours or pay; the separate statutory preview uses only manually entered synthetic monthly bases.
- Firebase email/password sign-in, development-account creation, and password-reset email UI; reset responses do not disclose whether an email has an account. The app stays behind the sign-in gate when Firebase config is complete.
- `/api/health`, employee list/search/detail plus owner-sandbox create/update, raw attendance query and coverage report, owner-scoped workflow list/create/cancel routes, and opt-in demo seed endpoint.
- Verification: `npm run test:web` passes 37 workflow/calendar/filter/sort/CSV/payroll-preview tests; `./test.sh` passes 167 Java checks; `npm run test:e2e` passes the local browser flow for employee create/edit, HR/Team filters and roster CSV, empty unscheduled attendance, raw directory-label summary/CSV, reversed-date rejection, leave/ticket submit/cancel and detail disclosures, calendar date drafting, inclusive leave-range filters, raw attendance summary/sorting/export, report search/filter/sort/drill-through and CSV, temporary 2026 statutory preview with no payroll API call and negative-net blocking, simulated workflow/report authorization and service failures with recovery, reload persistence, and mobile width; `npm run build` passes; `npm audit` reports 0 vulnerabilities. An isolated live Firebase auth-lifecycle browser check passed disposable account creation/sign-in, user-scoped empty Firestore reads, and sign-out on localhost; the account was deleted and no Firestore writes were made. The exact Arena preview-origin sign-in remains unverified.

## Not implemented / important limits

# User-specific working rule (applies across this compiled skills file)

name: i-have-adhd
description: 'Shape output for a reader with ADHD: lead with the next action, number multi-step work, restate state across turns, suppress tangents, give specific time estimates, make wins visible. Invoke with /i-have-adhd; stays on until "stop adhd mode".'

# i-have-adhd

The reader has ADHD. Output is not just brief. It is shaped so an ADHD brain can act on it.

## Persistence

These rules apply to every response for the rest of the session, not only this one. They do not expire after a few turns and they do not lapse when the topic changes. If you are unsure whether they still apply, they do.

Turn them off only when the reader says "stop adhd mode" or "normal mode". Confirm in one line, then return to your default style.

## What ADHD changes about reading

Five facts drive every rule below:

1. Working memory is small. Anything not on screen is forgotten. Do not ask the reader to "keep in mind X."
2. Knowing the answer is not doing the answer. The friction between "got it" and "done it" is where work dies.
3. Starting is the hardest step. The first action must be obvious, small, and doable now.
4. Time estimates feel uniform. "A bit of work" and "a few hours" register the same. Vague estimates fail.
5. Dopamine is scarce. Visible progress matters. Buried wins do not register.

## Rules

### 1. Lead with the next action

The first line is something the reader can do. Not context. Not a plan. The action.

Bad: "Let's think about this. Your auth flow has a few moving pieces..."
Good: "Edit `src/auth.ts:42` to update the token validation."

If the answer is a command, path, or snippet, it goes first. Prose comes after, if at all.

### 2. Number multi-step tasks

If the work takes more than one step, write a numbered list. Each step is one bounded action. No step contains "and then" twice.

Use the fewest steps that still work. Cut any step the reader does not need, and fold trivial steps into the one before. A short path finished beats a complete path abandoned.

Bad: "First open the file, find the function, swap it out, then run the tests."

Good:
```
1. Open `src/auth.ts`
2. Replace `verifyToken` (lines 42 to 58) with the snippet below
3. Run `npm test -- auth.spec.ts`
```

### 3. End with one concrete next action

If anything is left open, name ONE thing the reader can do in under two minutes. Even "open the file" counts.

Bad: "Hope that helps. Let me know if you want to dig deeper."
Good: "Next: run `npm test` and paste the first failing line."

### 4. Suppress tangents

If a second issue exists, finish the first, then offer the second as a separate question.

Bad: "Here's the fix. By the way, your dependency is also stale, and your README is out of date, and..."
Good: "Here's the fix. Separately: there is also a stale dependency. Want me to handle that next?"

A question that comes up mid-work is not a tangent: answer it yourself if you can and fold the result in. If it still needs the reader, surface it once, at the end.

### 5. Restate state every turn

The reader cannot hold "we are on step 3 of 5" between messages. Restate it.

Bad: "Done. Ready for the next part?"
Good: "Step 3 of 5 done: schema updated. Next: backfill the new column. Run the script?"

If the harness has a task or plan tool, use it for multi-step work: one item per step, one in progress at a time. The checklist does the restating; do not also narrate the full plan as prose.

### 6. Give specific time estimates

Vague estimates fail. Ballpark in concrete units.

Bad: "This will take some work."
Good: "About 15 minutes if tests already cover this. An afternoon if not."

### 7. Make completed work visible

Show what now works, in concrete terms. Do not bury wins in a recap.

Bad: "I've made some changes to the auth flow. Among other things..."
Good: "Login now works with magic links. Try: `npm run dev`, open `/login`."

### 8. Matter-of-fact tone for errors

Never use "Uh oh," "Oh no," or "There seems to be a problem." State cause and fix.

Bad: "Uh oh, the test is failing. There seems to be an issue..."
Good: "Test fails at `auth.spec.ts:42`: expected 200, got 401. Cause: missing auth header. Fix: add `Authorization: Bearer ${token}` to the request."

### 9. Cap lists to 5 items

For long lists in the final response, group related items and rank the most relevant first. Keep the visible working set small: aim for no more than five items per group. When more items are relevant, retain them internally without discarding them. Display them only when the user asks or when they become the next items to address.

Never omit relevant items when completeness matters. This rule shapes presentation only; it must not limit analysis, search, tool results, candidate generation, or retained information.

### 10. No preamble, no recap, no closing pleasantries

Forbidden openers: "Great question," "Let me...", "I'll...", "Sure!", "Looking at your...", "To answer your question..."

Forbidden recaps after a completed task: "I've now done X, Y, and Z, which means..."

Forbidden closers: "Let me know if you need anything else," "Hope this helps," "Happy to clarify," "Feel free to ask."

Start with the answer. End when the answer is done.

## When to break the rules

Override the defaults when:

1. User asks to "explain" or "walk me through." Explain fully. Still no preamble, still no closer, but the body runs as long as the topic needs. Add headers so the reader can skim back.
2. Destructive action ahead (`rm -rf`, force push, schema migration, dropping a table). Confirm before acting. Safety wins over brevity.
3. Debug spiral. If the last three turns have been "still broken," stop iterating on code. Name the assumption that might be wrong. Ask one diagnostic question.
4. Real ambiguity in the request. One short clarifying question beats guessing and rewriting.
5. A rule fights the task. When a rule would delete the answer itself, the task wins; the shape stays. Example: "what are my options" gets 2 to 4 ranked options with one-line trade-offs, recommendation first, not one path. The options are the answer.
6. A rule fights the harness. Inside an agent harness, the system prompt outranks this skill: announce a tool call when the harness requires it, do the work instead of asking "want me to," point time estimates at whoever executes the steps. Same principle as 5: the constraint wins, the shape stays.

## Pre-send check

Before sending, delete:

1. The first sentence if it announces what you are about to do.
2. The last sentence if it asks "anything else?" or recaps what just happened.
3. Any "by the way" sidebar.
4. Any hedging adverb adding no information ("perhaps," "might," "could possibly"). Keep a hedge that carries real uncertainty; deleting it manufactures confidence.
5. Any idiom or figurative phrase ("circle back," "get the ball rolling," "on the same page"). Replace with the literal action.

Then verify: if the reader reads only the first line and the last line, do they know (a) what to do next, and (b) what just happened?

If yes, send.

# Legacy MotorPH coursework → current MS2 traceability

**Purpose:** use the user's earlier MO-IT108 MotorPH documents to clarify the current prototype without silently expanding its approved scope. These are earlier-course sources (A.Y. 2024–2025), not the active MO-IT110 MS2 rubric. They can inform design and requirements mapping, but do not override the current boundary: only an isolated synthetic 2026 monthly statutory preview is enabled; attendance-based or persisted payroll remains disabled.

## Sources inspected

- `/home/user/uploads/MO-IT108 - 1st Milestone_ Requirements Analysis Document of MotorPH Payroll System H1103 Torres, A. (1).pdf` — a requirements document with ten functional-requirement groups and non-functional requirements.
- `/home/user/uploads/MO-IT108 - 2nd Milestone_ System Design Document of MotorPH Payroll System H1103 Torres, A. (1).pdf` — module descriptions, scenarios, data concepts, and an RBAC matrix.
- `/home/user/uploads/MO-IT108 - Terminal Assessment_ Business Technology Proposal for MotorPH Payroll System H1103 Torres, A..pdf` — a broad technology proposal. Several major sections still contain template prompts/placeholders, so treat it as vision/context rather than an approved detailed specification.
- `/home/user/uploads/The Code.pdf` — C++ inventory-management iterations using stock fields such as ID, brand, age, date, and status. Despite a MotorPH inventory CSV filename, it is not a payroll system or a reusable MotorPH payroll module. No code from it was integrated.

## What the legacy documents clarify

### Attendance view

The MO-IT108 Requirements Analysis says employees can view attendance metrics over a date range, defaulting from the earliest to latest available record. The System Design expands this into daily logs and counts for present, absent, tardy, overtime, undertime, and leave usage. It also names concepts such as `ClockInStatus`, `ShiftStartTime`, `ShiftEndTime`, `GracePeriod`, `AttendanceTag`, `TotalWorked`, `WorkHourTag`, `AbsentCount`, `PresentCount`, `TardyCount`, `OvertimeHours`, `UndertimeHours`, `LeaveTaken`, and `LeaveBalance`.

This clarifies the intended *shape* of the attendance screen, but not a complete calculation policy. The documents do not provide actual grace-period values, the absence threshold, break treatment, rounding, overnight-shift handling, missing-punch corrections, timezone policy, overtime triggers, or a worked expected example. One field is described as `TotalWorked` based on clock-in/out, but that alone does not settle those rules. Therefore the app now defaults the raw-record filter to the selected synthetic employee's earliest and latest available dates; the user may narrow the inclusive range. This is a data-range convenience, **not** a payroll period, and no hour/category totals are derived.

### Payroll snapshot and pay cycle

The legacy System Design lists proposed snapshot fields such as `PayrollCycleStart`, `PayrollCycleEnd`, `HourlyWage`, `RegHours`, `OTHours`, `PTOHours`, holiday hours/shifts, incentives, tax, other deductions, gross/net pay, and a snapshot timestamp. The Requirements Analysis also names wage components, incentives, statutory/other deductions, payroll reports, and payslip distribution.

These are useful field names and workflow hints, not complete formulas or full current policy. The documents do not give exact semi-monthly cut-off dates, salary-to-hourly conversion, attendance rules, benefits treatment, rounding policy, or a complete expected payslip. A separate synthetic 2026 statutory preview now covers only monthly SSS/PhilHealth/Pag-IBIG and BIR withholding; employee-linked salary snapshots, attendance calculations, saved payroll, and payslips remain disabled.

### Identity and roles

The legacy documents describe Employee, Supervisor/Lead, HR, Payroll Staff, and System Admin roles. Their RBAC matrix distinguishes self/team access, HR/Payroll actions, and approvals for government details; the requirements also call for 2FA and branch-aware access. The current prototype has Firebase Email/Password sign-in and an isolated per-user synthetic sandbox only. It does **not** implement 2FA, branch routing, team membership, HR/Payroll roles, production PII handling, or the legacy RBAC matrix. No real employee information is permitted.

## Ten legacy functional-requirement groups vs current prototype

| Legacy requirement | Current state | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Employee login | **Partial** | Firebase Email/Password sign-in is live; no employee-ID login, 2FA, branch routing, or production session/RBAC policy. |
| 2. Clock in/out | **Not implemented** | No live clocking, QR verification, or attendance-write workflow. |
| 3. Employee attendance | **Partial** | Raw synthetic entries, selected employee, inclusive date filters, and earliest–latest default. No absent/present/tardy/overtime/undertime/leave summaries. |
| 4. Salary tracker | **Intentionally disabled** | The source's snapshot fields do not define a full calculation or authoritative values. |
| 5. Tickets | **Partial, owner-scoped create/cancel** | Fictional ticket submission/cancel and queue labels for overtime, leave, timesheet, payroll, HR, and technical support; nothing is delivered or resolved. Published user-scoped Firestore rules were live-smoke-tested for ticket create/cancel. |
| 6. Leave tracker/calendar | **Partial, owner-scoped create/cancel** | Validated fictional request submit/cancel plus a display-only calendar of submitted/cancelled date ranges; no balance/accrual, approval, payroll treatment, or approved leave calendar. Published user-scoped Firestore rules were live-smoke-tested for leave create/cancel. |
| 7. Team management | **Partial read-only roster** | Shows synthetic directory records; no team membership, schedules, supervisor scope, or approval workflow. |
| 8. HR handling | **Partial synthetic directory maintenance** | Signed-in Firebase users can create/update allowlisted fictional directory fields in their own sandbox; local mode is unauthenticated process memory. No HR role, schedule assignment, delete, onboarding/offboarding, or sensitive PII. |
| 9. Payroll supervision | **Preview-only partial** | A separate synthetic monthly statutory calculator exists; no employee-linked payroll, adjustments, approvals, payslips, or reports. |
| 10. Payroll distribution | **Not implemented** | No payslip generation, email delivery, retry handling, or distribution status. |

## Percent estimate: two different denominators

There is no single valid percentage “against the submitted folders”: those projects have different feature sets, tech stacks, and course scopes, and several are near-duplicates. The ranges below are **feature-completeness estimates, not a grade or quality score**.

- **Agreed current Tasks 1–3 scope: about 85–90%.** Task 1's live Firebase proof is complete. Task 2's browser sign-in and employee selection are verified on localhost, with the exact Arena preview-origin authorization still unverified. Task 3's employee/date inputs and raw-record path are complete; derived attendance-hour totals remain gated because their algorithm and test oracle are missing. The separate monthly statutory preview does not enable attendance-based payroll.
- **Full legacy MO-IT108 functional breadth: roughly 25–35% represented, but less operationally complete.** The app has a real sign-in/data foundation, limited owner-scoped synthetic directory editing, read-only attendance, and owner-scoped leave/ticket create/cancel routes (published user-scoped Firestore rules live-smoke-tested for leave/ticket create/cancel). These limited workflows do not include reviewers or approvals. Clocking, leave balances/approvals/approved calendars, delivered and resolved tickets, actual team/supervisor management, HR lifecycle operations, full payroll calculations (beyond the temporary statutory preview), payslips, reports, RBAC/2FA, and production operations remain unimplemented.
- **Compared with the more complete numbered submissions (especially folders 6 and 9): roughly 25–35% of end-to-end feature breadth.** This prototype is stronger in live Firebase Auth/Firestore integration, browser accessibility/responsiveness, and current test evidence; those reference projects include end-to-end payroll engines/results and broader workflows that this app deliberately does not yet have; the temporary monthly statutory calculator is not an attendance-to-payslip engine. Compared with the smallest procedural/demo submissions, the comparison can reverse because this project already has a live web/data foundation.

The largest gap to “parity” is not another Firebase feature: it is the **unbuilt payroll/business workflow** (validated attendance summaries, approved pay rules, payroll results/payslips, and applicable roles). Do not close that gap by importing unverified formulas from another submission.

## Progress snapshot (2026-11-04)

**Broad peer-level feature-parity estimate: about 58% complete / 42% remaining.** This is a rough feature-breadth estimate, not a grade, code-coverage measure, or production-readiness claim. The target scope is not frozen yet, and policy-dependent items remain gated; the new temporary statutory preview is only one part of payroll and does not substitute for attendance mechanics or a persisted pay run. The user has deferred payroll input staging to a later phase; that pending item is explicitly excluded from this estimate.

- [x] Synthetic, user-scoped employee and workflow foundation; sortable/read-only raw attendance; a separate 2026 monthly statutory preview now runs only from fictional browser inputs and does not persist.
- [x] Browser-level leave/ticket workflows, status/cancel paths, table search/status filters and optional sorting (newest-first default), inclusive leave-request date-overlap filtering, newest-first history in both stores, all-record CSV export, responsive check, and a request-date calendar that drafts form dates without implying approval or submission.
- [x] Read-only raw attendance coverage report with inclusive date filtering, per-employee row counts/date bounds, explicit unmapped status, employee/name/ID/schedule search, mapped/unmapped/all filters, field/direction sorting, CSV export of visible rows, and no hours or absence classifications.
- [x] Overview counts now reflect loaded directory, selected raw attendance, and sandbox workflow records. Leave/ticket detail disclosures expose submitted content and UTC event timestamps without adding new workflow permissions.
- [x] HR directory table has client-side text/status filters, selectable field/direction sorting, and filtered CSV export; read-only Team roster adds independent search/status filters, selectable sorting, and filtered CSV export; Reports includes synthetic directory status/department label counts with CSV export and attendance-report drill-through to raw rows.
- [x] Draft `docs/acceptance-baseline.md` records current pass/fail behavior and gates from supplied sources; it remains provisional because no active rubric was found.
- [x] `docs/candidate-policy-review.md` compares the user's MO-IT107 schema, folder-6 and folder-9 calculations, official statutory sources, and a current net-pay library; outdated prior formulas and the temporary profile are disclosed.
- [x] Temporary 2026 monthly statutory preview added with a versioned rules file, exact-centavo pure calculation, separate statutory bases and employee/employer shares, monthly BIR withholding, no persistence, 39 web unit tests, and local browser E2E.
- [x] Automated local E2E error/recovery checks for simulated authorization denial and service outage across workflow and attendance-report views.
- [x] Verify Firebase Auth sign-out on localhost with an opt-in disposable-account test; the account was deleted and no Firestore writes were made.
- [ ] Verify authentication on the exact Arena preview origin and live Firebase/API deny/failure paths.
- [ ] Freeze the course-project acceptance scope against the supplied rubric and identify source-backed versus policy-gated features.
- [ ] Payroll input staging (deferred by user for a later phase; excluded from the current parity percentage).
- [ ] Implement the remaining policy-backed workflows and release evidence; expand the statutory preview only after reviewing the explicitly provisional 2026 bases/rounding and then resolve attendance-to-gross and pay-period mechanics.

## Already done — current foundation

- Firebase Email/Password Auth and user-scoped Firestore access were live-tested with synthetic accounts. The sign-in page now wires Firebase password-reset email with non-enumerating confirmation text; reset delivery has not been live-tested.
- Employee list, search, and detail selection work; data remains fictional and scoped to the signed-in sandbox.
- Raw attendance records are selectable by employee and inclusive date range; default range spans that employee's earliest/latest available records, following the older Requirements Analysis. A separate read-only coverage report summarizes raw row counts and date bounds by configured employee-to-schedule mapping; unmapped is not reported as absent.
- The Payroll workspace contains a disposable 2026 statutory preview from synthetic values; it is not connected to attendance. The default attendance range is not a pay period.
- Leave request/ticket API routes now validate input, derive employee names from the user's synthetic directory, create records, show status, and allow only cancellation. A display-only personal request calendar shows pending/cancelled date ranges, not approved leave; two date clicks can draft form bounds without submitting. Client-side search/status filters narrow each workflow table, and the leave table additionally filters by inclusive overlap with a requested-date range; native detail disclosures show note/message and submission/cancellation timestamps; local and Firestore lists order newest first; exports remain the full owner-sandbox dataset. Firebase paths are owner-scoped and have no reviewer/approval/delete access; after publication, live smoke testing verified employee create/update, leave and ticket create/cancel/read-back, and cross-user denial. One cancelled leave and one cancelled ticket remain under deleted disposable UIDs because workflow deletion is denied. Local preview stores these records in Java process memory and loses them when the process restarts.
- Team roster is read-only with search/status filters, field/direction sorting, and filtered CSV export; the HR directory table also has client-side search/status filters, field/direction sorting, and filtered CSV export. Reports summarizes only the stored synthetic status and department labels, with a matching label-count CSV export. The directory editor creates/updates only fictional name, department, role, location, and demo status. Firebase mode is user-scoped; local mode has one unauthenticated process-memory store. No team membership, HR authorization, delete, schedules, or lifecycle workflow exists.

# Candidate policy review from prior submissions and current references

**Status: research and changeable demo profile; not approved production policy.** The user invited disclosed candidate inference and specifically authorized a temporary 2026 statutory preview. This document records prior-work candidates and risks. A synthetic-input monthly preview is enabled in the app, but this document does not authorize attendance-hour derivation, saved payroll/payslips, approvals, or role-based access. No official MotorPH payroll rulebook or active grading rubric was found in the supplied set.

## 1. What the inspected MO-IT110 peer implementation says

The supplied peer review copy at `/home/user/repo_review/full_repo/testingester-main/6/-/` contains an explicit, testable candidate model:

- `src/motorph/model/AttendanceRecord.java`: first cutoff is days 1–15; second cutoff is day 16 through actual month end. Login from 08:00 through 08:10 is treated as 08:00; logout after 17:00 is capped at 17:00. It calculates elapsed time directly from those adjusted times and does **not** subtract a meal interval.
- `src/motorph/service/PayrollProcessor.java`: the first cutoff has no deductions and net equals cutoff gross. On the second cutoff, it computes monthly contributions from the combined two-cutoff gross, computes withholding tax after those contributions, and subtracts the whole monthly deduction amount from the second-cutoff gross (floored at zero). Allowances are shown on the second-cutoff slip but excluded from net in that implementation.
- `src/motorph/model/Employee.java`: gross is hourly rate times the calculated minutes. The course-project fixtures also supply semi-monthly and hourly rates.
- The peer has substantial tests and CP2 compatibility comparisons, but its own behavior is still an implementation choice, not an authoritative MotorPH payroll rule.

**Important defect/risk found in that candidate:** an 08:00–17:00 record yields nine elapsed hours because the code caps at 17:00 but deducts no lunch. DOLE's source says normal work hours do not exceed eight hours a day and requires at least a 60-minute meal period off work; a pair of in/out times without a meal record cannot distinguish the unpaid break. The peer rule must not be copied as an hours-worked or overtime algorithm without resolving that mismatch.

The supplied peer review also records 473 of 476 comparison rows and 14 of 14 cutoff summaries matching the CP2 output; three row differences were ₱0.01 due to floating/half-centavo behavior. That is compatibility evidence, not legal-compliance evidence. See `/home/user/repo_review/submission-comprehensive-report.md` and `/home/user/repo_review/submission-feature-pseudocode.md` for the review context. No peer employee or government-ID data was copied into this app or document.

A public MO-IT110 repository surfaced the same 1–15 / 16–month-end pattern and second-cutoff deduction convention, but explicitly says its payroll tables/thresholds are copied from CP2 rather than independently verified. Treat it as corroboration of a *course-project convention*, not a company policy: https://github.com/fdtan/MO-IT110_OOP-MS2_TanFD.

## 2. Current official statutory references located

These sources can support statutory-component research, but they do not establish MotorPH's attendance import, pay-period, allowance, leave, or role policy:

| Component | Source finding | Boundary before implementation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| SSS | The SSS site publishes its contribution schedule effective Jan. 1, 2025: 15% total on MSC up to ₱35,000, split 5% employee / 10% employer; EC is employer-only. The schedule also distinguishes the MPF portion above ₱20,000. | Use the circular/table and verify every bracket and rounding boundary. Do not assume a new 2026 table without a newer official circular. |
| PhilHealth | The 2026 advisory states the 5% contribution rate effective Jan. 2025, with ₱10,000 floor and ₱100,000 ceiling. The 2025 employer advisory says use monthly basic salary and excludes overtime, allowances, 13th-month pay, bonuses and specified absence/undertime reductions from that base. | Confirm the formal-sector share split and exact payroll-period deduction method against the applicable circular. |
| Pag-IBIG | Circular 460 raises the Maximum Fund Salary to ₱10,000 effective February 2024; the employee rate is 1% at fund salary ≤₱1,500 and 2% above, while the employer rate is 2%. | Confirm applicable employee category and effective date; don't extrapolate to voluntary/other member types. |
| BIR withholding | Annex E to RR 11-2018 publishes daily, weekly, semi-monthly and monthly tables effective Jan. 1, 2023 onward. | The chosen tax base, payroll-period method, taxable allowances/benefits, year-end adjustment and rounding need explicit tests. A monthly-only example is not a semi-monthly payroll specification. |
| Hours/premiums | DOLE's official materials specify an eight-hour normal workday, a minimum 60-minute meal period off work, and statutory overtime/night/rest-day/holiday provisions. | The attendance schema lacks meal punches, a defined `dayType` enum, and an authoritative schedule/holiday assignment. Those facts must be supplied or explicitly selected as demo assumptions. |

## 3. A net-pay reference found online — useful, but not a drop-in payroll engine

`ph-payroll` is the strongest technical reference located for statutory components: its README says it uses exact decimal arithmetic, effective-dated rules, source circulars, and fails closed outside covered periods; it documents support from **2026-01** because the 2026 PhilHealth rule is the most recent component. Its scope is monthly basic pay plus statutory contributions/tax, not attendance-hour computation, MotorPH's cutoff handling, leave treatment, or a payslip workflow. It is MIT-licensed and asks users to verify results before relying on it: https://github.com/earnieacts/ph-payroll.

### Documented synthetic example from that reference

For monthly basic pay of ₱25,000, the library documents employee deductions of SSS ₱1,250, PhilHealth ₱625, Pag-IBIG ₱200, withholding tax ₱313.75, and net ₱22,611.25. A manual annualized arithmetic check gives taxable monthly income ₱22,925; annualized ₱275,100; 15% of the ₱25,100 annual amount above ₱250,000 is ₱3,765, or ₱313.75 per month. This is a reference example only—not this app's result or an approved MotorPH payslip.

Two caveats need reconciliation before adoption:

1. The BIR Annex E monthly table uses rounded peso breakpoints (₱20,833 and 15% above that), which yields ₱313.80 for ₱22,925 when read directly. The library's annualized method gives ₱313.75. The ₱0.05 difference needs a verified BIR-period/rounding interpretation and an independent approved example.
2. In the library source, `employerCost` is the sum of employer contributions (₱3,355 in its ₱25,000 example), not basic salary plus those contributions. Do not display that field as total employer payroll cost without changing/renaming it.

A second 2026 calculator repository also advertises complete deductions and net pay, but the repository surfaced with a single commit and no comparable validation evidence. It is a secondary cross-check, not a preferred authority: https://github.com/tenzerodev/rdcruz-ph-payroll.

## 4. Workflow/role patterns in peer submissions

The supplied peer corpus shows patterns, not a consistent permission contract: employee requests, an admin/manager review screen, approve/reject outcomes, leave-credit changes, and separate payroll/admin roles appear in different projects. Folder 9's `LeaveService.java` performs approve/reject and updates request files plus leave-credit counters transactionally, but the service itself has no authorization check. Other projects use different role labels and access patterns. These examples are not sufficient to invent secure Firebase roles or reviewer boundaries.

## 5. Safe recommendation / next decision

1. Keep production-style payroll, attendance-hour reports, approvals and reviewer controls disabled.
2. If the project needs a classroom demonstration before official rules are confirmed, expose the folder-6 conventions only as a **clearly labelled, synthetic candidate profile**, after the user confirms the meal-break, cutoff, deduction timing, allowance, and net-floor choices. Preserve the official statutory calculator as a separately sourced component and reconcile BIR withholding first.
3. Mark any inferred role/workflow matrix as a proposal based on the peer corpus; do not publish it as live authorization until the user approves the exact employee, HR/approver, payroll, and admin boundaries.
4. Keep the external payroll library as a comparison source, not a dependency or oracle; reproduce independent golden values and cite official circulars before expanding beyond the disposable statutory preview into attendance-based or persisted payroll.

## 6. Re-review of the user's database design and later calculator work

The user's ctxt.io document is the **MO-IT107 database design/data dictionary**, not a database file or a set of calculation rules. It does, however, lay out a useful storage model that the earlier review had not connected to a working calculation pipeline:

- `Rates` and `Tax Table` are intended as changeable reference tables; the design mentions a rate `implementationYear`, although this field is missing from the linked Data Dictionary and the design's own key constraints disagree.
- `Government Deductibles` separates monthly employer contribution, employee contribution, and withholding tax.
- `Contributions` stores SSS, PhilHealth, and Pag-IBIG amounts separately for `Employee` and `Employer`.
- `Payroll`, `Payslip`, `Earnings`, `Deductibles`, `Other Transactions`, `Government Tally`, and `Summary` cover the intended input/output and reporting areas. Payslip includes a start/end period and gross income.
- The related DFD describes the order of operations: timesheet validation → wage/adjustments → government deductibles → basic payroll computation → payslip → monthly summary. The System Admin has a rate-update flow.

That design is valuable for the **mechanics before calculation**, but it contains no actual rates, effective date ranges, formula, rounding policy, or worked expected values. In particular, the tax table is not explicit about whether each row is monthly, semi-monthly, or another withholding period, and the monthly government-deduction key shown in the design has no year component. The user-provided full synthesis likewise warns that the PDFs do not state statutory values or arithmetic. The design should be versioned and reconciled before it is used as a persistent production schema.

A different older SQLite file exists in peer folder 1 (`/home/user/repo_review/full_repo/testingester-main/1/-/myMotorPhdb.db`). I inspected its table definitions only—not any records—and found `Users`, `Allowance`, `Salary_Deduction`, `EmployeeAudit`, and `Employee_info`, not the normalized Rates/Tax Table/Government Deductibles design in the ctxt link. It is not a source of verified statutory rates.

### A later prior project did tackle the calculation pipeline

The supplied folder-9 review copy, `/home/user/repo_review/full_repo/testingester-main/9/-/oop/`, contains an actual `PayrollCalculator` orchestrator and separate SSS, PhilHealth, Pag-IBIG, and withholding-tax calculators. Its pipeline is:

1. derive gross as worked days × hourly rate × 8;
2. calculate employee/employer statutory items;
3. calculate withholding after employee statutory contributions;
4. calculate net and build an immutable payroll record.

Its NOTES and console tests report this pipeline exercised. But the formulas are hard-coded as Java `double` constants and the source XLSX matrices cited by its verification note were on a personal Windows path, not among the supplied files. The source values are **not a current 2026 ruleset**:

- SSS caps the employee share at ₱1,125, which predates the 2025 schedule (2026 uses the current schedule effective January 2025: 5% employee / 10% employer on MSC up to ₱35,000, plus employer-only EC).
- PhilHealth uses 3%, a ₱10,000 floor/₱60,000 ceiling and a 50/50 split; the current direct-contributor advisory for formal-sector MBS gives 5%, ₱10,000 floor/₱100,000 ceiling, with allowances and overtime excluded from the MBS base.
- Pag-IBIG caps at ₱100, reflecting the former ₱5,000 MFS; Circular 460 moved the MFS ceiling to ₱10,000 effective February 2024, allowing up to ₱200 per side.
- Its first taxable monthly BIR band uses 20%; Annex E uses 15% from ₱20,833 to ₱33,332. The prior project also does not make a semi-monthly tax table part of its calculator API.

A separate folder-7 `ContributionCalculator.java` also computes semi-monthly values, but doubles the pay-period input to a monthly proxy and reuses old CP2 schedules: SSS max ₱1,125, PhilHealth 1.5% employee amount with ₱900 cap, Pag-IBIG cap ₱100, and a 20% first taxable band. Its payroll code labels overtime pricing as temporary pending confirmation. Folder 3 is even simpler (flat 4.5% SSS, 2% PhilHealth, ₱100 Pag-IBIG, no tax schedule). These show earlier mechanical exploration, but none supply a current validated 2026 profile.

The older folder-6 implementation is even more explicitly a CP2/course-project compatibility profile, not a 2026 statutory table. Neither implementation was copied into the current app.

## 7. Temporary 2026 module now in this prototype

Following the user's instruction, a **client-side-only, synthetic-input preview** has been added to the Payroll workspace. It is deliberately isolated and replaceable:

- Change rates, thresholds, table bands, sources, or the profile ID in `web/payroll-rules-2026.js`.
- Calculation logic is pure and separated in `web/payroll-preview-2026.js`; amounts are parsed and calculated in integer centavos (`BigInt`), not binary floating point.
- `web/payroll-preview-ui.js` only renders the submitted values and result. It sends no payroll API request, reads no employee or attendance record, and persists nothing in Firebase or local storage.
- Current scope is **monthly 2026 statutory preview only**. It requires separate cash-pay, SSS compensation, PhilHealth MBS, Pag-IBIG Fund Salary, and taxable-compensation inputs. That prevents the preview from silently assuming all legal contribution/tax bases are identical.
- It separates employee deductions from employer costs, includes the current SSS employer-only EC amount, uses the BIR **monthly** Annex E table with a provisional half-up centavo rounding rule, and blocks a negative net rather than emitting a negative payslip.
- It does not create/pay a payroll, resolve salary conversion, attendance hours, overtime, leave/holiday earnings, deductions between cutoffs, tax annualisation/adjustment, benefit exemptions, employees, or payslips.

For a fully synthetic ₱25,000 monthly example using ₱25,000 for each input base, this profile produces: SSS employee ₱1,250; SSS employer SS/MPF ₱2,500 plus EC ₱30; PhilHealth ₱625 each; Pag-IBIG ₱200 each; taxable base after employee shares ₱22,925; monthly BIR withholding ₱313.80; net estimate ₱22,611.20; employer statutory contributions ₱3,355; gross plus those employer contributions ₱28,355.00. The difference from `ph-payroll`'s documented ₱22,611.25 is the disclosed monthly-table versus annualized-tax method/rounding difference; the sandbox uses the published BIR monthly table for its monthly mode, not the library result.

The input boundaries and the editable monthly calculation are now covered in `test/web/payroll-preview-2026.test.js`; a browser E2E check confirms the result and that no payroll API call is made. The profile remains a **temporary estimate**, not an approved payroll policy or statutory compliance guarantee.

### Updated sources used for the temporary profile

- SSS's official contribution page links Circular 2024-006 / the schedule effective Jan. 2025: 15% total on MSC (5% employee / 10% employer), up to ₱35,000 MSC; EC is employer-only and set at ₱10 or ₱30 by MSC band: https://www.sss.gov.ph/pay-contribution/
- PhilHealth Advisory PA2025-0002: 5% effective Jan. 2025; monthly basic salary floor ₱10,000 / ceiling ₱100,000; allowances, overtime, 13th-month pay, bonuses and similar items excluded from employer MBS: https://www.philhealth.gov.ph/advisories/2025/PA2025-0002.pdf
- Pag-IBIG Circular 460: employee 1% at Fund Salary up to ₱1,500, 2% above; employer 2%; MFS ₱10,000, effective Feb. 2024: https://www.pagibigfund.gov.ph/documents/Circular%20No.%20460%20-%20Guidelines%20on%20the%20Pag-IBIG%20Fund's%20Implementation%20of%20Increase%20in%20the%20MFS%20Effective%20February%202024.pdf
- BIR Annex E to RR 11-2018: monthly withholding table effective Jan. 2023 onward (current published rate table used for the 2026 estimate): https://bir-cdn.bir.gov.ph/local/pdf/Annex%20E%20RR%2011-2018.pdf

package ph.motorph.web;

import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.LinkedHashMap;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Map;
import java.util.NoSuchElementException;
import java.util.Optional;

/** Process-memory store containing only fictional demo employees. */
public final class InMemoryEmployeeStore implements MutableEmployeeStore {
    private final Map<String, Employee> employees = new LinkedHashMap<>();

    public InMemoryEmployeeStore() {
        addFixture(new Employee("DEMO-001", "Mara Rivera", "People Operations", "HR Coordinator", "Makati", "Active"));
        addFixture(new Employee("DEMO-002", "Eli Santos", "Finance", "Payroll Associate", "Taguig", "Active"));
        addFixture(new Employee("DEMO-003", "Noa Reyes", "Operations", "Operations Lead", "Quezon City", "On leave"));
    }

    @Override
    public synchronized List<Employee> findAll() {
        return new ArrayList<>(employees.values());
    }

    @Override
    public synchronized Optional<Employee> findById(String id) {
        return Optional.ofNullable(id == null ? null : employees.get(id.trim()));
    }

    @Override
    public synchronized Employee create(Employee employee) {
        if (employees.containsKey(employee.getId())) throw new IllegalStateException("Employee ID already exists.");
        employees.put(employee.getId(), employee);
        return employee;
    }

    @Override
    public synchronized Employee update(Employee employee) {
        if (!employees.containsKey(employee.getId())) throw new NoSuchElementException("Employee not found.");
        employees.put(employee.getId(), employee);
        return employee;
    }

    private void addFixture(Employee employee) {
        employees.put(employee.getId(), employee);
    }
}

import { calculatePayrollPreview2026, formatPesoCents } from './payroll-preview-2026.js';

function byId(id) {
  return document.getElementById(id);
}

function value(id) {
  return byId(id).value.trim();
}

function setMoney(id, cents) {
  byId(id).textContent = formatPesoCents(cents);
}

function addBreakdownRow(body, label, employeeCents, employerCents, note) {
  const row = document.createElement('tr');
  const cells = [label, employeeCents === null ? '—' : formatPesoCents(employeeCents),
    employerCents === null ? '—' : formatPesoCents(employerCents), note];
  cells.forEach((text, index) => {
    const cell = document.createElement(index === 0 ? 'th' : 'td');
    if (index === 0) cell.scope = 'row';
    cell.textContent = text;
    row.append(cell);
  });
  body.append(row);
}

export function initPayrollPreview() {
  const form = byId('payroll-preview-form');
  if (!form) return;
  const status = byId('payroll-preview-status');
  const results = byId('payroll-preview-results');

  form.addEventListener('submit', event => {
    event.preventDefault();
    status.classList.remove('payroll-preview-error');
    results.hidden = true;
    const input = {
      period: value('payroll-preview-period'),
      grossCashPay: value('payroll-preview-gross'),
      sssCompensation: value('payroll-preview-sss'),
      philHealthBasicSalary: value('payroll-preview-ph'),
      pagIbigFundSalary: value('payroll-preview-pagibig'),
      taxableCompensation: value('payroll-preview-taxable')
    };

    try {
      const result = calculatePayrollPreview2026(input);
      byId('payroll-results-ruleset').textContent = `${result.rulesetId} · ${result.period}`;
      setMoney('payroll-result-net', result.netPayCents);
      setMoney('payroll-result-employee-total', result.totalEmployeeDeductionsCents);
      setMoney('payroll-result-employer-total', result.totalEmployerContributionsCents);
      setMoney('payroll-result-employer-cost', result.employerCashCostCents);

      const lines = byId('payroll-result-lines');
      lines.replaceChildren();
      addBreakdownRow(lines, 'SSS Social Security + MPF', result.sss.employeeCents,
        result.sss.employerRegularCents, `MSC ${formatPesoCents(result.sss.mscCents)}; 5% employee / 10% employer`);
      addBreakdownRow(lines, 'SSS Employees’ Compensation', 0n, result.sss.ecCents,
        'Employer-only; included in employer contributions total');
      addBreakdownRow(lines, 'PhilHealth premium', result.philHealth.employeeCents,
        result.philHealth.employerCents,
        `5% of MBS base ${formatPesoCents(result.philHealth.premiumBaseCents)}, split equally`);
      addBreakdownRow(lines, 'Pag-IBIG monthly savings', result.pagIbig.employeeCents,
        result.pagIbig.employerCents,
        `Fund Salary base ${formatPesoCents(result.pagIbig.baseCents)} after ₱10,000 cap`);
      addBreakdownRow(lines, 'BIR withholding tax', result.withholdingTaxCents, null,
        `Monthly taxable base ${formatPesoCents(result.taxableAfterEmployeeContributionsCents)} after employee shares`);
      results.hidden = false;
      status.textContent = 'Preview calculated from the entered synthetic bases. Nothing was saved or sent to the API.';
    } catch (error) {
      status.textContent = error instanceof Error ? error.message : 'Could not calculate preview.';
      status.classList.add('payroll-preview-error');
    }
  });
}
import { PAYROLL_RULES_2026 } from './payroll-rules-2026.js';

const CENTS_PER_PESO = 100n;
const BASIS_POINT_DENOMINATOR = 10000n;

export function parsePesoCents(value, fieldName = 'amount') {
  const text = String(value ?? '').trim().replace(/,/g, '');
  if (!/^\d+(?:\.\d{1,2})?$/.test(text)) {
    throw new TypeError(`${fieldName} must be a non-negative peso amount with up to two decimal places.`);
  }
  const [wholeText, fractionText = ''] = text.split('.');
  return BigInt(wholeText) * CENTS_PER_PESO + BigInt(fractionText.padEnd(2, '0'));
}

export function formatPesoCents(cents) {
  const value = BigInt(cents);
  const sign = value < 0n ? '-' : '';
  const absolute = value < 0n ? -value : value;
  const pesos = (absolute / CENTS_PER_PESO).toString().replace(/\B(?=(\d{3})+(?!\d))/g, ',');
  const centavos = (absolute % CENTS_PER_PESO).toString().padStart(2, '0');
  return `${sign}₱${pesos}.${centavos}`;
}

function toCentsFromRule(pesos, label) {
  return parsePesoCents(String(pesos), label);
}

function roundPositiveRatio(numerator, denominator) {
  return (numerator + denominator / 2n) / denominator;
}

function applyBasisPoints(cents, basisPoints) {
  return roundPositiveRatio(cents * BigInt(basisPoints), BASIS_POINT_DENOMINATOR);
}

function sssMonthlySalaryCredit(compensationCents, rules) {
  const minimum = toCentsFromRule(rules.minimumMscPesos, 'SSS minimum MSC');
  const maximum = toCentsFromRule(rules.maximumMscPesos, 'SSS maximum MSC');
  const firstHigherRange = toCentsFromRule(rules.firstHigherRangePesos, 'SSS first higher range');
  const compensationStep = toCentsFromRule(rules.rangeStepPesos, 'SSS compensation range step');
  const mscStep = toCentsFromRule(rules.mscStepPesos, 'SSS MSC step');

  if (compensationCents < firstHigherRange) return minimum;
  const increments = (compensationCents - firstHigherRange) / compensationStep + 1n;
  const msc = minimum + increments * mscStep;
  return msc > maximum ? maximum : msc;
}

function computeSss(compensationCents, rules) {
  const mscCents = sssMonthlySalaryCredit(compensationCents, rules);
  const employeeCents = applyBasisPoints(mscCents, rules.employeeRateBasisPoints);
  const employerRegularCents = applyBasisPoints(mscCents, rules.employerRateBasisPoints);
  const ecThreshold = toCentsFromRule(rules.ecThresholdMscPesos, 'SSS EC threshold');
  const ecCents = toCentsFromRule(
    mscCents < ecThreshold ? rules.ecBelowThresholdPesos : rules.ecAtOrAboveThresholdPesos,
    'SSS Employees’ Compensation'
  );
  return {
    mscCents,
    employeeCents,
    employerRegularCents,
    ecCents,
    employerTotalCents: employerRegularCents + ecCents
  };
}

function computePhilHealth(monthlyBasicSalaryCents, rules) {
  const floor = toCentsFromRule(rules.baseFloorPesos, 'PhilHealth contribution floor');
  const ceiling = toCentsFromRule(rules.baseCeilingPesos, 'PhilHealth contribution ceiling');
  const premiumBaseCents = monthlyBasicSalaryCents < floor
    ? floor
    : monthlyBasicSalaryCents > ceiling ? ceiling : monthlyBasicSalaryCents;
  const premiumCents = applyBasisPoints(premiumBaseCents, rules.premiumRateBasisPoints);
  const employeeShareBasisPoints = BigInt(rules.employeeShareBasisPoints);
  const employerShareBasisPoints = BigInt(rules.employerShareBasisPoints);
  if (employeeShareBasisPoints + employerShareBasisPoints !== BASIS_POINT_DENOMINATOR) {
    throw new RangeError('PhilHealth employee and employer shares must total 100%.');
  }
  const employeeCents = applyBasisPoints(premiumCents, rules.employeeShareBasisPoints);
  return {
    premiumBaseCents,
    totalPremiumCents: premiumCents,
    employeeCents,
    employerCents: premiumCents - employeeCents
  };
}

function computePagIbig(fundSalaryCents, rules) {
  const ceiling = toCentsFromRule(rules.fundSalaryCeilingPesos, 'Pag-IBIG MFS ceiling');
  const lowBandCeiling = toCentsFromRule(rules.employeeLowBandCeilingPesos, 'Pag-IBIG employee-rate threshold');
  const baseCents = fundSalaryCents > ceiling ? ceiling : fundSalaryCents;
  const employeeRate = fundSalaryCents <= lowBandCeiling
    ? rules.employeeLowRateBasisPoints
    : rules.employeeHighRateBasisPoints;
  return {
    baseCents,
    employeeCents: applyBasisPoints(baseCents, employeeRate),
    employerCents: applyBasisPoints(baseCents, rules.employerRateBasisPoints)
  };
}

function computeMonthlyBirWithholding(taxableCents, rules) {
  const firstThresholdCents = toCentsFromRule(rules.firstTaxablePesoThreshold, 'BIR first threshold');
  if (taxableCents <= firstThresholdCents) return 0n;
  const brackets = rules.brackets;
  for (const bracket of brackets) {
    const floorCents = toCentsFromRule(bracket.floorPesos, 'BIR bracket floor');
    const belowCents = bracket.belowPesos === null
      ? null
      : toCentsFromRule(bracket.belowPesos, 'BIR bracket upper bound');
    if (belowCents === null || taxableCents < belowCents) {
      const baseTaxCents = toCentsFromRule(bracket.baseTaxPesos, 'BIR base tax');
      const excessCents = taxableCents > floorCents ? taxableCents - floorCents : 0n;
      return baseTaxCents + applyBasisPoints(excessCents, bracket.rateBasisPoints);
    }
  }
  return 0n;
}

/**
 * Computes a disposable, synthetic-only 2026 MONTHLY statutory preview.
 * Inputs are kept distinct because SSS compensation, PhilHealth monthly basic
 * salary, Pag-IBIG Fund Salary, tax compensation, and cash pay need not be the
 * same amount. Nothing is persisted or sent to the API.
 */
export function calculatePayrollPreview2026(input, rules = PAYROLL_RULES_2026) {
  if (!input || typeof input !== 'object') throw new TypeError('Enter synthetic monthly pay bases.');
  if (rules.effectiveYear !== 2026 || !/^2026-(0[1-9]|1[0-2])$/.test(String(input.period || ''))) {
    throw new RangeError('This temporary ruleset covers 2026 monthly periods only.');
  }

  const grossCashPayCents = parsePesoCents(input.grossCashPay, 'Gross cash pay');
  const sssCompensationCents = parsePesoCents(input.sssCompensation, 'SSS compensation base');
  const philHealthBasicSalaryCents = parsePesoCents(input.philHealthBasicSalary, 'PhilHealth monthly basic salary');
  const pagIbigFundSalaryCents = parsePesoCents(input.pagIbigFundSalary, 'Pag-IBIG Fund Salary');
  const taxableCompensationCents = parsePesoCents(input.taxableCompensation, 'Taxable compensation before employee contributions');

  if (grossCashPayCents <= 0n) throw new RangeError('Gross cash pay must be greater than zero for this preview.');
  if (sssCompensationCents <= 0n || philHealthBasicSalaryCents <= 0n || pagIbigFundSalaryCents <= 0n) {
    throw new RangeError('Enter a positive contribution base for SSS, PhilHealth, and Pag-IBIG.');
  }

  const sss = computeSss(sssCompensationCents, rules.sss);
  const philHealth = computePhilHealth(philHealthBasicSalaryCents, rules.philHealth);
  const pagIbig = computePagIbig(pagIbigFundSalaryCents, rules.pagIbig);
  const totalEmployeeStatutoryCents = sss.employeeCents + philHealth.employeeCents + pagIbig.employeeCents;
  const taxableAfterEmployeeContributionsCents = taxableCompensationCents > totalEmployeeStatutoryCents
    ? taxableCompensationCents - totalEmployeeStatutoryCents
    : 0n;
  const withholdingTaxCents = computeMonthlyBirWithholding(taxableAfterEmployeeContributionsCents, rules.birMonthly);
  const totalEmployeeDeductionsCents = totalEmployeeStatutoryCents + withholdingTaxCents;
  if (totalEmployeeDeductionsCents > grossCashPayCents) {
    throw new RangeError('Employee deductions exceed gross cash pay; preview blocked rather than showing negative net pay.');
  }

  const totalEmployerContributionsCents = sss.employerTotalCents + philHealth.employerCents + pagIbig.employerCents;
  return Object.freeze({
    rulesetId: rules.id,
    period: input.period,
    grossCashPayCents,
    sss: Object.freeze(sss),
    philHealth: Object.freeze(philHealth),
    pagIbig: Object.freeze(pagIbig),
    taxableCompensationCents,
    taxableAfterEmployeeContributionsCents,
    withholdingTaxCents,
    totalEmployeeStatutoryCents,
    totalEmployeeDeductionsCents,
    netPayCents: grossCashPayCents - totalEmployeeDeductionsCents,
    totalEmployerContributionsCents,
    employerCashCostCents: grossCashPayCents + totalEmployerContributionsCents
  });
}

    private void handleAttendance(HttpExchange exchange) throws IOException {
        if (!"GET".equals(exchange.getRequestMethod())) {
            sendJson(exchange, 405, "{\"error\":\"Method not allowed\"}");
            return;
        }
        String employeeId = queryParameter(exchange.getRequestURI().getRawQuery(), "employeeId");
        if (employeeId == null || employeeId.trim().isEmpty()) {
            sendJson(exchange, 400, "{\"error\":\"employeeId is required\"}");
            return;
        }
        try {
            RequestServices services = servicesFor(exchange);
            LocalDate from = parseOptionalDate(queryParameter(exchange.getRequestURI().getRawQuery(), "from"));
            LocalDate to = parseOptionalDate(queryParameter(exchange.getRequestURI().getRawQuery(), "to"));
            AttendanceService attendanceService = new AttendanceService(services.employeeService,
                localScheduleStore, services.attendanceStore);
            List<AttendanceRecord> records = attendanceService.findForEmployee(employeeId, from, to);
            sendJson(exchange, 200, attendanceToJson(records));
        } catch (DateTimeParseException ex) {
            sendJson(exchange, 400, "{\"error\":\"Dates must use YYYY-MM-DD\"}");
        } catch (IllegalArgumentException ex) {
            sendJson(exchange, 400, "{\"error\":\"" + escapeJson(ex.getMessage()) + "\"}");
        } catch (java.util.NoSuchElementException ex) {
            sendJson(exchange, 404, "{\"error\":\"Employee not found\"}");
        } catch (FirestoreException ex) {
            sendApiError(exchange, ex);
        }
    }
