public class Payroll {

    // ── CSV column indices ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    private static final int COL_BASIC = 13;
    private static final int COL_RICE  = 14;
    private static final int COL_PHONE = 15;
    private static final int COL_CLOTH = 16;
    private static final int COL_SEMI  = 17;
    private static final int COL_HOUR  = 18;

    // Standard working days and hours per month
    public static final double WORKING_DAYS_PER_MONTH  = 22.0;
    public static final double WORKING_HOURS_PER_DAY   = 8.0;
    public static final double WORKING_HOURS_PER_MONTH =
        WORKING_DAYS_PER_MONTH * WORKING_HOURS_PER_DAY; // 176

    // =========================================================================
    // ARITHMETIC RELATIONSHIPS
    // basicSalary = hourlyRate * 176
    // semiMonthlyRate = basicSalary / 2
    // =========================================================================
    public static double basicToSemiMonthly(double basicSalary) {
        return basicSalary / 2.0;
    }

    public static double basicToHourly(double basicSalary) {
        return basicSalary / WORKING_HOURS_PER_MONTH;
    }

    public static double hourlyToBasic(double hourlyRate) {
        return hourlyRate * WORKING_HOURS_PER_MONTH;
    }

    public static double semiMonthlyToBasic(double semiMonthly) {
        return semiMonthly * 2.0;
    }

    // =========================================================================
    // LEGACY METHODS — used by PayrollAdminUI (kept for compatibility)
    // =========================================================================

    /** Gross pay = semiMonthly + allowances */
    public static double grossPay(String[] emp) {
        return parseAmount(emp[COL_SEMI])
             + parseAmount(emp[COL_RICE])
             + parseAmount(emp[COL_PHONE])
             + parseAmount(emp[COL_CLOTH]);
    }

    public static double sssContribution(double grossPay) {
        return computeSSS(grossPay * 2) / 2;
    }

    public static double philHealthContribution(double grossPay) {
        return computePhilHealth(grossPay * 2) / 2;
    }

    public static double pagIbigContribution(double semiMonthlyRate) {
        return computePagIbig(semiMonthlyRate * 2) / 2;
    }

    public static double totalDeductions(double grossPay, double basicSalary) {
        return sssContribution(grossPay)
             + philHealthContribution(grossPay)
             + pagIbigContribution(basicSalary / 2);
    }

    public static double taxableIncome(double grossPay, double totalDeductions) {
        return Math.max(0, grossPay - totalDeductions);
    }

    public static double taxDeduction(double taxableIncome) {
        return computeWithholdingTax(taxableIncome * 2) / 2;
    }

    public static double NetPay(double grossPay, double totalDeductions,
                                double taxDeductions) {
        return Math.max(0, grossPay - totalDeductions - taxDeductions);
    }

t java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.logging.Level;
import java.util.logging.Logger;

import com.motorph.model.User;
import com.opencsv.CSVReader;
import com.opencsv.exceptions.CsvException;

/**
 * Service class for handling user authentication.
 * Implements MPHCR-04 requirement for login functionality.
 */
public class AuthenticationService {
    private static final Logger logger = Logger.getLogger(AuthenticationService.class.getName());
    private static final String CREDENTIALS_FILE_PATH = "data/userCredentials.csv"; // If running from
                                                                                    // motorph_payroll_system directory
    // If you run from the parent directory, use:
    // private static final String CREDENTIALS_FILE_PATH =
    // "motorph_payroll_system/userCredentials.csv";

    private final List<User> users;

    /**
     * Constructor that loads user credentials from CSV file
     */
    public AuthenticationService() {
        users = new ArrayList<>();
        loadCredentials();
    }

    /**
     * Loads user credentials from the CSV file
     */
    private void loadCredentials() {
        try (CSVReader reader = new CSVReader(new FileReader(CREDENTIALS_FILE_PATH))) {
            List<String[]> records = reader.readAll();

            // Skip header row
            for (int i = 1; i < records.size(); i++) {
                String[] record = records.get(i);

                if (record.length >= 5) {
                    try {
                        String username = record[0].trim();
                        String password = record[1].trim();
                        int employeeId = Integer.parseInt(record[2].trim());
                        String role = record[3].trim();
                        boolean isActive = Boolean.parseBoolean(record[4].trim());

                        User user = new User(username, password, employeeId, role, isActive);
                        users.add(user);

                        logger.log(Level.INFO, "Loaded user: {0}", username);
                    } catch (NumberFormatException e) {
                        logger.log(Level.WARNING, "Invalid employee ID in credentials file at line {0}", i + 1);
                    }
                } else {
                    logger.log(Level.WARNING, "Invalid record format in credentials file at line {0}", i + 1);
                }
            }

            logger.log(Level.INFO, "Successfully loaded {0} user credentials", users.size());

        } catch (IOException | CsvException e) {
            logger.log(Level.SEVERE, "Failed to load user credentials from file: " + CREDENTIALS_FILE_PATH, e);
            // Create default admin user if file loading fails
            createDefaultAdminUser();
        }
    }

    /**
     * Creates a default admin user if credentials file cannot be loaded
     */
    private void createDefaultAdminUser() {
        logger.log(Level.INFO, "Creating default admin user");
        User defaultAdmin = new User("admin", "admin123", 1, "ADMIN", true);
        users.add(defaultAdmin);
    }

    /**
     * Authenticates a user with username and password
     * 
     * @param username The username to authenticate
     * @param password The password to authenticate
     * @return User object if authentication successful, null otherwise
     */
    public User authenticateUser(String username, String password) {
        if (username == null || password == null || username.trim().isEmpty() || password.trim().isEmpty()) {
            logger.log(Level.WARNING, "Authentication attempt with empty username or password");
            return null;
        }

        String trimmedUsername = username.trim();
        String trimmedPassword = password.trim();

        for (User user : users) {
            if (user.getUsername().equals(trimmedUsername) &&
                    user.getPassword().equals(trimmedPassword) &&
                    user.isActive()) {

                logger.log(Level.INFO, "Successful authentication for user: {0}", trimmedUsername);
                return user;
            }
        }

        logger.log(Level.WARNING, "Failed authentication attempt for username: {0}", trimmedUsername);
        return null;
    }

    /**
     * Validates login credentials
     * 
     * @param username The username to validate
     * @param password The password to validate
     * @return true if credentials are valid, false otherwise
     */
    public boolean validateLogin(String username, String password) {
        return authenticateUser(username, password) != null;
    }

    /**
     * Gets a user by username
     * 
     * @param username The username to search for
     * @return User object if found, null otherwise
     */
    public User getUserByUsername(String username) {
        if (username == null || username.trim().isEmpty()) {
            return null;
        }

        String trimmedUsername = username.trim();
        for (User user : users) {
            if (user.getUsername().equals(trimmedUsername)) {
                return user;
            }
        }
        return null;
    }

    /**
     * Gets all active users
     * 
     * @return List of active users
     */
    public List<User> getActiveUsers() {
        List<User> activeUsers = new ArrayList<>();
        for (User user : users) {
            if (user.isActive()) {
                activeUsers.add(user);
            }
        }
        return activeUsers;
    }

    /**
     * Gets the total number of loaded users
     * 
     * @return Number of users
     */
    public int getUserCount() {
        return users.size();
    }

    /**
     * Checks if the credentials file exists and is readable
     * 
     * @return true if file exists and is readable
     */
    public boolean isCredentialsFileAvailable() {
        try {
            java.io.File file = new java.io.File(CREDENTIALS_FILE_PATH);
            return file.exists() && file.canRead();
        } catch (Exception e) {
            return false;
        }
    }
}

package com.motorph.security;

public class RolePermission {

    private String role;

    public RolePermission(String role) {
        this.role = role;
    }

    public boolean canAccessEmployee() {
        return role.equalsIgnoreCase("ADMIN") || role.equalsIgnoreCase("HR");
    }

    public boolean canAccessPayroll() {
        return role.equalsIgnoreCase("ADMIN") || role.equalsIgnoreCase("FINANCE");
    }

    public boolean canAccessReports() {
        return role.equalsIgnoreCase("ADMIN") || role.equalsIgnoreCase("FINANCE");
    }

    public boolean canAccessLeave() {
        return true;
    }

    public boolean canAccessDashboard() {
        return true;
    }

        // Show loading state
        btnLogin.setText("Signing in...");
        btnLogin.setEnabled(false);

        new SwingWorker<String[], Void>() {
            protected String[] doInBackground() {
                if (EmployeeData.records == null) return null;
                for (int i = 1; i < EmployeeData.records.size(); i++) {
                    String[] row = EmployeeData.records.get(i);
                    if (row != null && row.length > 0 &&
                        row[0].trim().equalsIgnoreCase(empNo)) return row;
                }
                return null;
            }
            protected void done() {
                btnLogin.setText("LOGIN");
                btnLogin.setEnabled(true);
                try {
                    String[] emp = get();
                    if (emp == null) {
                        failedAttempts++;
                        showError("Employee not found. (" + failedAttempts +
                            "/" + MAX_ATTEMPTS + " attempts)");
                        txtUsername.requestFocus();
                    } else if (emp.length <= 19 || !emp[19].equals(password)) {
                        failedAttempts++;
                        showError("Incorrect password. (" + failedAttempts +
                            "/" + MAX_ATTEMPTS + " attempts)");
                        txtPassword.setText("");
                        txtPassword.requestFocus();
                    } else {
                        failedAttempts = 0;
                        lblError.setText(" ");
                        new DashboardUI(empNo, emp).setVisible(true);
                        dispose();
                    }
                } catch (Exception ex) {
                    showError("Login error: " + ex.getMessage());
                }
            }
        }.execute();
    }

    private void showError(String msg) {
        lblError.setText(msg);
        final int[] count = {0};
        final int origX = getLocation().x;
        Timer shake = new Timer(30, null);
        shake.addActionListener(e -> {
            setLocation(origX + (count[0]++ % 2 == 0 ? 6 : -6), getLocation().y);
            if (count[0] > 8) { setLocation(origX, getLocation().y); shake.stop(); }
        });
        shake.start();
    }

            new LineBorder(error ? new Color(200, 50, 50) :
                new Color(200, 210, 230), 1, true),
            new EmptyBorder(6, 12, 6, 12));
    }

--- Payroll calculator ---

package motorphpayrollsystem;

public class PayrollCalculator {

    public PayrollCalculator() {
    }

    public double calculateRegularPay(Employee employee) {
        if (employee == null) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException(
                    "Employee cannot be null."
            );
        }

        double regularPay = employee.calculatePay();

        if (!Double.isFinite(regularPay) || regularPay < 0) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException(
                    "Regular pay must be a valid nonnegative amount."
            );
        }

        return regularPay;
    }

    public double calculateOvertimePay(
            Employee employee,
            AttendanceRecord attendance,
            OvertimeRequest overtime) {

        if (employee == null || attendance == null) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException(
                    "Employee and attendance are required."
            );
        }

        if (overtime == null || !overtime.isApproved()) {
            return 0.0;
        }

        double overtimeHours = attendance.calculateOvertimeHours();
        double approvedHours = overtime.getRequestedHours();

        double payableHours = Math.min(
                overtimeHours,
                approvedHours
        );

        if (payableHours <= 0) {
            return 0.0;
        }

        // Temporary base calculation.
        // Confirm the original CP2 overtime rate before final testing.
        return payableHours * employee.getHourlyRate();
    }

    public double calculateGrossPay(
            double regularPay,
            double overtimePay,
            Employee employee) {

        if (employee == null) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException(
                    "Employee cannot be null."
            );
        }

        if (!Double.isFinite(regularPay) || regularPay < 0 ||
                !Double.isFinite(overtimePay) || overtimePay < 0) {

            throw new IllegalArgumentException(
                    "Pay amounts must be valid and nonnegative."
            );
        }

        double allowances =
                employee.getRiceSubsidy()
                        + employee.getPhoneAllowance()
                        + employee.getClothingAllowance();

        return regularPay + overtimePay + allowances;
    }

# `testingester` numbered submissions — structure, behavior, and course links

**Repository reviewed:** `/home/user/repo_review/full_repo/testingester-main/` (export of `Sitramonicus/testingester`). The numbered projects are nested beneath each `N/-/` directory; folder 8 has one more nested copy of its project root. I read the source layouts, READMEs and setup notes, representative implementation paths, data-file headers, build metadata, and available test/evidence files. I did **not** launch the GUIs or run the projects/tests: several require Windows paths, local MySQL, external Google Sheets, a specific IDE/JDK, or manual interaction. Reported test totals below are claims in project READMEs/logs, not results I reran. I have not reproduced employee records or passwords.

## At a glance

| **4** | CP2 Group 4 is indicated by `sources.txt` paths; no README | Maven/Java Swing with controller, service, model, repository and view packages; CSV | Strong conceptual example of GUI/data/service separation and CSV-backed payroll. No explicit MO-IT110 milestone claim. |

## Folder 1 — SQLite/NetBeans Swing payroll manager

**Location:** `1/-/src/EmployeePayrollMph/`. There are 12 Java source files, many NetBeans `.form` files, images and bundled JARs. `build/classes/` also contains compiled `.class` files and form copies; those are build output, not a second source implementation. The project metadata names `EmployeePayrollMph.EmployeePayrollMph` as its entry point.

**How it works:** the entry frame presents a login form. Its handler queries the SQLite `Users` table using a prepared statement, stores the selected user's ID/name in static fields on `Emp`, records a login event in `EmployeeAudit`, then opens `MainMenu`. The menu opens employee management, allowances, salary update, deductions, payment records, search and audit. The included SQLite database schema has `Employee_info`, `Users`, `Allowance`, `Salary_Deduction`, and `EmployeeAudit` tables.

The `Employee` frame performs employee add/update/delete against `Employee_info`, including an image BLOB. `Allowance` reads an employee, calculates an allowance total, and inserts a row into `Allowance`. `SalaryDeductions` inserts a deduction record. `EmployeeSalary` looks up the employee plus stored allowances/deductions to prepare a payslip; the app bundles iText, and the menu has PDF report export handlers. This is therefore more of a database-backed admin CRUD app than a clean payroll-calculation library.

**Caveats:** the SQLite connector uses a hard-coded Windows path under one developer's `C:\Users\...` directory even though database files are included in the project. Several screens are mainly generated Swing code; `EmployeeAttendance` and `EmployeeLeave` exist, but their presence alone does not establish a complete persisted attendance/leave workflow. The login's role check uses Java string identity (`==`) and contains an empty `if (count == 1);` statement, so the code should not be treated as a reliable authentication example without checking/fixing that flow.

**Course connection:** the code is useful for seeing Swing event handlers, JDBC/SQLite, CRUD and report generation. There is no source evidence tying it to CP1, CP2, MS1 or MS2, so I would not label it as your coursework baseline.

## Folders 2 and 5 — one Swing/MySQL app under two different labels

**Locations:** `2/-/` and `5/-/`. Each has 49 Java files, many NetBeans `.form` layouts and image assets, a Maven file, and two third-party time-picker JARs. The active entry point is `main.main`, which opens `Jframes.LogInNew`; `Archived/` contains four older screens.

**How it works:** the login screen queries the local MySQL `user_accounts` table and routes Admin/IT users to `AdminHomeDashboard`, other users to `HomeDashboard`. The employee dashboard links to profile, salary, attendance, leave requests and overtime requests. The admin side links to employee records, salary/attendance, accounts, leave approvals and overtime approvals. The screens issue SQL directly through `Classes.db`, which connects to a local MySQL database named `motorph`. SQL references tables named `employees`, `user_accounts`, `attendance_records`, `salary`, `leave_requests`, and `overtime_requests`.

There is a `Classes/` package with `Employee`, `Salary`, `Attendance`, `Deduction`, `Payroll`, `UserAuthentication`, `Admin`, `HR`, `Manager`, request and task classes. These communicate the intended domain model, but multiple methods are empty placeholders (for example, model-level payroll/CRUD methods). The working behavior is mostly in Swing-frame event handlers. Salary computation logic appears in both `CreateSalary` and `UpdateSalaryAdmin`, which each query attendance and calculate salary/deductions. This is an example of a GUI-heavy project with some OOP-shaped classes, not a fully separated model/service architecture.

**Important duplication finding:** folders 2 and 5 are not two materially different codebases. A recursive comparison found only four differences: `.DS_Store`, `README.md`, and author-comment lines in `Classes/Employee.java` and `main/main.java`. The executable Java logic, forms, assets and build file otherwise match. Folder 5's README labels it MO-IT103 H1101 Group 1 / CP2; folder 2's README labels it MO-IT110 H2101 Group 3 / OOP. That makes them different submission *packagings/labels*, but essentially the same program. The folder 2 label does not by itself demonstrate that this is your approved MS1 design or your authored work.

**Caveats:** the MySQL schema/setup is not included as a self-contained database export; running requires a local `motorph` database and compatible account setup. Some domain-layer methods are stubs, while substantial behavior is coupled to the UI. The credentials are database-backed, but the source uses direct password comparison; this is not a security design to copy.

**Course connection:** folder 5 is explicitly CP2. Folder 2 is labelled MO-IT110 OOP, but the repository does not include an MS1 design package connecting these classes to an approved design. Treat it as a CP2-style app/OOP comparison unless the mentor confirms more.

## Folder 3 — small CP1/terminal-assessment console exercises

**Location:** `3/-/`. The README identifies a COMPROG1 A1101 Terminal Assessment submission and describes a Phase 1 console payroll system. There are seven Java files, employee CSV/TXT samples, and NetBeans metadata. Six Java files are in package `motorph`; `MotorPH_ReadFromFile.java` is in the default package, so it is a separate runnable entry point.

**How it works:** the files are small, independent demonstrations rather than one integrated app. They show fixed-value examples for hours worked, gross pay and semi-monthly salary; a separate class calculates example deductions; the file-reader program opens `employee_data.csv`, reads salary from a fixed column, applies its own sample deductions, and prints a result. `ComputeGrossPay` has a reusable static multiplication method, while the other examples largely hard-code the employee/time/pay inputs in `main`.

**Caveats:** the README describes a longer planned progression, but the source is still a set of small console programs, not a GUI, database-backed system or connected payroll architecture. The deduction rates differ between files and are explicitly example-style flat rates; they are not a safe source for official payroll rules. The folder's named author is not evidence that the current user authored it.

**Course connection:** this is the clearest CP1/procedural foundation in the numbered set: variables, arithmetic, conditions, methods and basic file reading. It is not evidence of a personal CP2 app. Given the user's CP1-to-OOP path, this may be useful as a prior-learning comparison, but do not describe it as their submission without confirmation.

The CP2 source commit and authorship/permission should be confirmed before adopting any code or presenting it as the user's work.

## Folder 7 — Swing/CSV payroll app with unclear submission identity

**Location:** `7/-/src/motorphpayrollsystem/`. There are 35 Java files, NetBeans forms/assets, and bundled OpenCSV, Commons Lang and AbsoluteLayout libraries. There is no README, no course/team label, and no CSV data file in the folder. The project main class is `MotorPHPayrollSystem`.

**Structure and flow:** the main class tries to create `attendance.csv`, loads employee data through `EmployeeData`, and opens `loginUI`. Login looks up an employee row in a CSV and compares a password against column 20. On success it opens `DashboardUI`. `EmployeeData` keeps the CSV rows in a static shared list and offers add/update/delete/profile methods that rewrite the CSV. The UI includes employee dashboard/profile, attendance clock-in/clock-out and history, employee records, admin employee add/update/delete, payroll screens and a bulk-payroll/export screen. `Attendance` and `CSVUtil` provide CSV persistence; `Payroll`, `ContributionCalculator`, `PayrollCalculator` and `PayrollProcessor` contain pay logic; `FullTimeEmployee`/`PartTimeEmployee` and `EmployeeMapper` provide model objects.

**What is only partial or unclear:** `MotorPH_Employee Data.csv`, required by `EmployeeData`, is not included. Attendance data is created as an empty CSV when absent. `LeaveRequest` and `OvertimeRequest` are domain classes, but a search shows no leave-request workflow in the screens; the overtime request model is stored on the processor but not used by its main processing method. The payroll processor's comments describe overtime as a temporary/unfinished path. So the classes indicate intended scope, not proof every listed capability is operational.

**Course connection:** its class hierarchy and UI/backend concepts could be compared to OOP course topics, but no source evidence ties it to a particular MO-IT110 module, MS1 design or user's own submission. It is not self-contained enough to treat as a runnable reference without its expected employee CSV.

## Folder 8 — MO-IT103 Group 18 console + Swing project

**Location:** `8/-/MO-IT103-Group18-master/MO-IT103-Group18-master/`. There are 36 Java files under `Backend/`, `Console/`, `GUI/` and one top-level labels file, plus NetBeans/Ant metadata, JARs and three local CSV datasets (employee details, attendance and credentials). No README is included.

**Two front ends use the data differently:**

- `Console.TACP2` is a terminal workflow: login with employee number/last name; view profile, daily attendance, weekly hours and payroll. It downloads published Google Sheets CSV over HTTP, so it depends on internet access and the sheet schema.
- The Swing UI starts from `GUI.LogIn` and proceeds to `GUI.MainMenu`. It uses the bundled local CSVs and has profile, attendance, payroll, employee table and employee add/update/delete screens.

The `Backend/` package contains employee/attendance records, CSV loading, payroll processors (regular, final-pay and 13th-month variants), statutory deduction calculators, regular/holiday overtime classes, plus leave and payslip-dispute domain classes. The regular payroll processor uses attendance totals and a `Payslip`; deduction types are separate classes. The GUI exposes employee dispute submission and a payroll-side review/resolve/reject frame.

**Caveats:** leave records shown by the GUI are explicitly hard-coded sample rows because there is no leave data file. Payslip disputes live in a singleton in-memory list, not persistent storage, so the records disappear on process exit. The payroll-side dispute frame itself notes role authorization is not implemented. The console path fetches external sheets; the GUI path reads local data—do not confuse them as one identical data flow. This is a CP2-labeled comparison project, not an MS1-approved design by evidence in this folder.

## Folder 9 — documented MO-IT110 Team 3 CP2-to-OOP project

**Location:** `9/-/`. This is the most documented folder: README, old `README.CP2.md`, `SETUP.md`, `oop/NOTES.md`, parity/matrix reports, console/test outputs, a QA workbook, and code. It has 15 Java files in the original GUI `src/`, 13 in `oop/src/` (12 backend classes plus `ConsoleBackendTest`), and 3 test/probe files. The README identifies the OOP work as MO-IT110 OOP Team 3, and identifies the CP2 baseline as MO-IT103 Group 4. Those are source-repository statements, not confirmation of the current user's authorship or reuse permission.

**Two connected source roots:**

- `src/motorphemployee/` is the earlier CP2 Swing app (login, landing screen, dashboard, employee forms, leave screens and related UI). Its data remains in CSV.
- `oop/src/motorphemployee/oop/` is the OOP payroll backend. `Person` → `Employee` → `RegularEmployee`/`ProbationaryEmployee` is the data hierarchy; `GovernmentContributionCalculator` has concrete contribution/tax calculators; `AttendanceLog` models attendance; `PayrollCalculator` coordinates employee + attendance + calculators and produces `PayrollRecord`.
- `ConsoleBackendTest` provides a console test harness before GUI integration. The GUI's `MainMenu`/`Dashboard` were rewired to call the OOP backend rather than compute payroll themselves.
- `AttendanceRepository` loads the real timecard CSV and supplies worked-day data to the payroll flow. `LeaveService` processes approval/rejection and writes the related CSV files; `LeaveForm` still has a separate direct append path noted as an open issue.

**How the feature sequence works:** employee/attendance CSV → `AttendanceRepository`/`AttendanceLog` → `PayrollCalculator` → contribution calculators → immutable `PayrollRecord` → GUI display. The README and notes describe preserving the CP2 UI while replacing duplicated calculations with one backend. They also document changes to modal popups, attendance sourcing and the add-employee form; these are later implementation refinements beyond the core OOP concept demonstration.

**The explicit module link:** the README maps W2 to encapsulation, W3 to abstraction, W4 to inheritance and W5 to polymorphism, and describes MS1 as 16 unique classes, 35 CRC rows and 97 method rows. It says MS2 implements 12 of the 16 design classes; `Credentials`, `LeaveRequest`, `LeaveManagement` and `HRManager` remain design-only. It states the GUI should present only, payroll math should live in the backend, and backend console tests should precede GUI integration. The repo includes official-matrix verification and CP2-parity evidence; the README says some deduction results intentionally differ from CP2 because the OOP version follows the official matrices, while gross pay matches the CP2 baseline. Do not transfer those tax/contribution assumptions to your assignment without checking its current approved rules.

The README reports 91/91 backend checks and several other dated test/GUI evidence logs. I have not rerun them. The QA workbook in this folder is named for a CP2 Group 4 QA submission; it should not be mistaken for proof that the OOP source was authored by the current user.

**Course connection:** the strongest visible MS1→MS2 teaching example in the repository because its own README and code comments map the OOP concepts and design artifacts into implementation. It is useful for studying the mapping, not automatically reusable submission material.

## Cross-folder conclusions and safe study order

- **Folders 2 and 5 are the same practical implementation** despite their different README labels; study one, not both, unless comparing the packaging/attribution differences.
- **Folders 4, 5 and 8 are alternative CP2-style systems**, not evidence of the user's personal CP2 app. Their persistence choices differ (CSV vs MySQL vs CSV/online sheet), and their features are not interchangeable.
- **Folder 9 is the best source here for tracing explicit MS1 concepts into MS2 code**, while folder 6 is a smaller independent example of the same design-to-implementation idea. Both need authorship/permission confirmation before graded use.
- **Folder 3 is a separate CP1-style reference**, not proof that the user has a CP2 app.
- **Folders 1 and 7 have unclear provenance/course stage.** Use them only as generic technical comparisons until a mentor or repository author confirms their context.

Suggested reading order for understanding—not copying—is: **3** (small console building blocks) → **one CP2 project** (4, 5 or 8; folder 4 is the clearest package-separated example) → **6** (smaller MS2 separation) → **9** (most explicit MS1-to-MS2 mapping and evidence). For your own MS1, start from the official rubric and your actual approved project requirements; use another folder only as a comparison after confirming permission and fit.

## Review boundary

This is a static repository explanation, not a correctness audit or a claim that every advertised feature runs. I read source and metadata but did not execute the projects. Several folders have external setup/data dependencies; exact runtime behavior and payroll-rule correctness require separate, course-specific validation. The repository remains unchanged; this report is the only new deliverable.

# Verify and stop

Translate acceptance conditions into smallest sufficient proof set.

- Reuse still-current results with matching repository state.
- Run focused checks before wider gates.
- Distinguish pass, fail, unavailable, and blocked exactly.
- Do not edit product code unless verification request includes fixes.
- Do not add polish, cleanup, or unrelated tests after criteria pass.

Stop immediately when acceptance proof is complete. Report commands, results, and unresolved risk only.

name: debugging-and-error-recovery
description: Guides systematic root-cause debugging. Use when tests fail, builds break, something that worked yesterday broke, behavior doesn't match expectations, or you encounter any unexpected error. Use when you need to figure out what broke and why — a systematic approach to finding and fixing the root cause rather than guessing.

# Debugging and Error Recovery

## Overview

Systematic debugging with structured triage. When something breaks, stop adding features, preserve evidence, and follow a structured process to find and fix the root cause. Guessing wastes time. The triage checklist works for test failures, build errors, runtime bugs, and production incidents.

## When to Use

- Tests fail after a code change
- The build breaks
- Runtime behavior doesn't match expectations
- A bug report arrives
- An error appears in logs or console
- Something worked before and stopped working

## The Stop-the-Line Rule

When anything unexpected happens:

```
1. STOP adding features or making changes
2. PRESERVE evidence (error output, logs, repro steps)
3. DIAGNOSE using the triage checklist
4. FIX the root cause
5. GUARD against recurrence
6. RESUME only after verification passes
```

**Don't push past a failing test or broken build to work on the next feature.** Errors compound. A bug in Step 3 that goes unfixed makes Steps 4-6 wrong.

## The Triage Checklist

Work through these steps in order. Do not skip steps.

### Step 1: Reproduce

Make the failure happen reliably. If you can't reproduce it, you can't fix it with confidence.

```
Can you reproduce the failure?
├── YES → Proceed to Step 2
└── NO
    ├── Gather more context (logs, environment details)
    ├── Try reproducing in a minimal environment
    └── If truly non-reproducible, document conditions and monitor
```

**When a bug is non-reproducible:**

```
Cannot reproduce on demand:
├── Timing-dependent?
│   ├── Add timestamps to logs around the suspected area
│   ├── Try with artificial delays (setTimeout, sleep) to widen race windows
│   └── Run under load or concurrency to increase collision probability
├── Environment-dependent?
│   ├── Compare Node/browser versions, OS, environment variables
│   ├── Check for differences in data (empty vs populated database)
│   └── Try reproducing in CI where the environment is clean
├── State-dependent?
│   ├── Check for leaked state between tests or requests
│   ├── Look for global variables, singletons, or shared caches
│   └── Run the failing scenario in isolation vs after other operations
└── Truly random?
    ├── Add defensive logging at the suspected location
    ├── Set up an alert for the specific error signature
    └── Document the conditions observed and revisit when it recurs
```

For test failures (npm shown — substitute the repository's own test command, per the test-driven-development skill's Discover the Stack First section):
```bash
# Run the specific failing test
npm test -- --grep "test name"

# Run with verbose output
npm test -- --verbose

# Run in isolation (rules out test pollution)
npm test -- specific-file --runInBand
```

### Step 2: Localize

Narrow down WHERE the failure happens:

```
Which layer is failing?
├── UI/Frontend     → Check console, DOM, network tab
├── API/Backend     → Check server logs, request/response
├── Database        → Check queries, schema, data integrity
├── Build tooling   → Check config, dependencies, environment
├── External service → Check connectivity, API changes, rate limits
└── Test itself     → Check if the test is correct (false negative)
```

**Use bisection for regression bugs:**
```bash
# Find which commit introduced the bug
git bisect start
git bisect bad                    # Current commit is broken
git bisect good <known-good-sha> # This commit worked
# Git will checkout midpoint commits; run your test at each
git bisect run npm test -- --grep "failing test"  # substitute the repository's focused-test command
```

### Step 3: Reduce

Create the minimal failing case:

- Remove unrelated code/config until only the bug remains
- Simplify the input to the smallest example that triggers the failure
- Strip the test to the bare minimum that reproduces the issue

A minimal reproduction makes the root cause obvious and prevents fixing symptoms instead of causes.

### Step 4: Fix the Root Cause

Fix the underlying issue, not the symptom:

```
Symptom: "The user list shows duplicate entries"

Symptom fix (bad):
  → Deduplicate in the UI component: [...new Set(users)]

Root cause fix (good):
  → The API endpoint has a JOIN that produces duplicates
  → Fix the query, add a DISTINCT, or fix the data model
```

Ask: "Why does this happen?" until you reach the actual cause, not just where it manifests.

### Step 5: Guard Against Recurrence

Write a test that catches this specific failure:

```typescript
// The bug: task titles with special characters broke the search
it('finds tasks with special characters in title', async () => {
  await createTask({ title: 'Fix "quotes" & <brackets>' });
  const results = await searchTasks('quotes');
  expect(results).toHaveLength(1);
  expect(results[0].title).toBe('Fix "quotes" & <brackets>');
});
```

This test will prevent the same bug from recurring. It should fail without the fix and pass with it.

### Step 6: Verify End-to-End

After fixing, verify the complete scenario with the repository's own commands (npm shown):

```bash
# Run the specific test
npm test -- --grep "specific test"

# Run the full test suite (check for regressions)
npm test

# Build the project (check for type/compilation errors)
npm run build

# Manual spot check if applicable
npm run dev  # Verify in browser
```

## Error-Specific Patterns

### Test Failure Triage

```
Test fails after code change:
├── Did you change code the test covers?
│   └── YES → Check if the test or the code is wrong
│       ├── Test is outdated → Update the test
│       └── Code has a bug → Fix the code
├── Did you change unrelated code?
│   └── YES → Likely a side effect → Check shared state, imports, globals
└── Test was already flaky?
    └── Check for timing issues, order dependence, external dependencies
```

### Build Failure Triage

```
Build fails:
├── Type error → Read the error, check the types at the cited location
├── Import error → Check the module exists, exports match, paths are correct
├── Config error → Check build config files for syntax/schema issues
├── Dependency error → Check package.json, run npm install
└── Environment error → Check Node version, OS compatibility
```

### Runtime Error Triage

```
Runtime error:
├── TypeError: Cannot read property 'x' of undefined
│   └── Something is null/undefined that shouldn't be
│       → Check data flow: where does this value come from?
├── Network error / CORS
│   └── Check URLs, headers, server CORS config
├── Render error / White screen
│   └── Check error boundary, console, component tree
└── Unexpected behavior (no error)
    └── Add logging at key points, verify data at each step
```

## Safe Fallback Patterns

When under time pressure, use safe fallbacks:

```typescript
// Safe default + warning (instead of crashing)

<!-- S0944 | mattpocock-skills/skills/engineering/codebase-design/SKILL.md -->
---
name: codebase-design
description: Shared vocabulary for designing deep modules. Use when the user wants to design or improve a module's interface, find deepening opportunities, decide where a seam goes, make code more testable or AI-navigable, or when another skill needs the deep-module vocabulary.
---

# Codebase Design

Design **deep modules**: a lot of behaviour behind a small interface, placed at a clean seam, testable through that interface. Use this language and these principles wherever code is being designed or restructured. The aim is leverage for callers, locality for maintainers, and testability for everyone.

## Glossary

Use these terms exactly: don't substitute "component," "service," "API," or "boundary." Consistent language is the whole point.

**Module**: anything with an interface and an implementation. Deliberately scale-agnostic: a function, class, package, or tier-spanning slice. _Avoid_: unit, component, service.

**Interface**: everything a caller must know to use the module correctly: the type signature, but also invariants, ordering constraints, error modes, required configuration, and performance characteristics. _Avoid_: API, signature (too narrow, they refer only to the type-level surface).

**Implementation**: what's inside a module, its body of code. Distinct from **Adapter**: a thing can be a small adapter with a large implementation (a Postgres repo) or a large adapter with a small implementation (an in-memory fake). Reach for "adapter" when the seam is the topic; "implementation" otherwise.

**Depth**: leverage at the interface. The amount of behaviour a caller (or test) can exercise per unit of interface they have to learn. A module is **deep** when a large amount of behaviour sits behind a small interface, **shallow** when the interface is nearly as complex as the implementation.

**Seam** _(Michael Feathers)_: a place where you can alter behaviour without editing in that place; the *location* at which a module's interface lives. Where to put the seam is its own design decision, distinct from what goes behind it. _Avoid_: boundary (overloaded with DDD's bounded context).

**Adapter**: a concrete thing that satisfies an interface at a seam. Describes *role* (what slot it fills), not substance (what's inside).

**Leverage**: what callers get from depth. More capability per unit of interface they learn. One implementation pays back across N call sites and M tests.

**Locality**: what maintainers get from depth. Change, bugs, knowledge, and verification concentrate in one place rather than spreading across callers. Fix once, fixed everywhere.

## Deep vs shallow

**Deep module** = small interface + lots of implementation:

```
┌─────────────────────┐
│   Small Interface   │  ← Few methods, simple params
├─────────────────────┤
│                     │
│  Deep Implementation│  ← Complex logic hidden
│                     │
└─────────────────────┘
```

**Shallow module** = large interface + little implementation (avoid):

```
┌─────────────────────────────────┐
│       Large Interface           │  ← Many methods, complex params
├─────────────────────────────────┤
│  Thin Implementation            │  ← Just passes through
└─────────────────────────────────┘
```

When designing an interface, ask:

- Can I reduce the number of methods?
- Can I simplify the parameters?
- Can I hide more complexity inside?

## Principles

- **Depth is a property of the interface, not the implementation.** A deep module can be internally composed of small, mockable, swappable parts; they just aren't part of the interface. A module can have **internal seams** (private to its implementation, used by its own tests) as well as the **external seam** at its interface.
- **The deletion test.** Imagine deleting the module. If complexity vanishes, it was a pass-through. If complexity reappears across N callers, it was earning its keep.
- **The interface is the test surface.** Callers and tests cross the same seam. If you want to test *past* the interface, the module is probably the wrong shape.
- **One adapter means a hypothetical seam. Two adapters means a real one.** Don't introduce a seam unless something actually varies across it.

## Designing for testability

Good interfaces make testing natural:

1. **Accept dependencies, don't create them.**

   ```typescript
   // Testable
   function processOrder(order, paymentGateway) {}

   // Hard to test
   function processOrder(order) {
     const gateway = new StripeGateway();
   }
   ```

2. **Return results, don't produce side effects.**

   ```typescript
   // Testable
   function calculateDiscount(cart): Discount {}

   // Hard to test
   function applyDiscount(cart): void {
     cart.total -= discount;
   }
   ```

3. **Small surface area.** Fewer methods = fewer tests needed. Fewer params = simpler test setup.

## Relationships

- A **Module** has exactly one **Interface** (the surface it presents to callers and tests).
- **Depth** is a property of a **Module**, measured against its **Interface**.
- A **Seam** is where a **Module**'s **Interface** lives.
- An **Adapter** sits at a **Seam** and satisfies the **Interface**.
- **Depth** produces **Leverage** for callers and **Locality** for maintainers.

## Rejected framings

- **Depth as ratio of implementation-lines to interface-lines** (Ousterhout): rewards padding the implementation. We use depth-as-leverage instead.
- **"Interface" as the TypeScript `interface` keyword or a class's public methods**: too narrow: interface here includes every fact a caller must know.
- **"Boundary"**: overloaded with DDD's bounded context. Say **seam** or **interface**.

## Going deeper

- **Deepening a cluster given its dependencies**, see [DEEPENING.md](DEEPENING.md): dependency categories, seam discipline, and replace-don't-layer testing.
- **Exploring alternative interfaces**, see [DESIGN-IT-TWICE.md](DESIGN-IT-TWICE.md): spin up parallel sub-agents to design the interface several radically different ways, then compare on depth, locality, and seam placement.

package motorph.service;

import java.io.BufferedReader;
import java.io.BufferedWriter;
import java.io.IOException;
import java.math.BigDecimal;
import java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets;
import java.nio.file.Files;
import java.nio.file.Path;

import java.time.LocalTime;

import java.time.format.DateTimeParseException;
import java.time.format.ResolverStyle;
import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.Collections;
import java.util.LinkedHashMap;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Map;
import java.util.logging.Level;
import java.util.logging.Logger;
import motorph.model.AttendanceRecord;
import motorph.model.Employee;
import motorph.model.Payslip;
import motorph.model.ProbationaryEmployee;
import motorph.model.RegularEmployee;

/**
 * The only class that reads or writes the CSV files.
 * <p>
 * Converts raw CSV text into validated Employee and AttendanceRecord objects,
 * and writes objects back to CSV. This is also the only place that looks at
 * the Status column to decide between RegularEmployee and ProbationaryEmployee.
 * Switching from CSV to a database later would only change this class.
 * </p>
 */
public class CSVDataHandler {

    private static final Logger logger = Logger.getLogger(CSVDataHandler.class.getName());

    // === DEFAULT FILE PATHS ===
    public static final String DEFAULT_EMPLOYEE_CSV   = "data/employees.csv";
    public static final String DEFAULT_ATTENDANCE_CSV = "data/attendance.csv";
    public static final String DEFAULT_RESULTS_CSV    = "data/payroll_results.csv";

    /** Employee field names in employees.csv column order. Used for form labels and messages. */
    public static final List<String> EMPLOYEE_FIELD_NAMES = List.of(
        "Employee ID", "Last Name", "First Name", "Birthday", "Address", "Phone Number",
        "SSS Number", "PhilHealth Number", "TIN", "Pag-IBIG Number", "Status", "Position", "Supervisor",
        "Basic Salary", "Rice Subsidy", "Phone Allowance", "Clothing Allowance", "Gross Semi-Monthly Rate", "Hourly Rate"
    );

    // === COLUMN INDEXES (employees.csv, no header row) ===
    private static final int EMPLOYEE_COLUMNS           = 19;
    private static final int COL_EMPLOYEE_ID            = 0;
    private static final int COL_LAST_NAME              = 1;
    private static final int COL_FIRST_NAME             = 2;
    private static final int COL_BIRTHDAY               = 3;
    private static final int COL_ADDRESS                = 4;
    private static final int COL_PHONE_NUMBER           = 5;
    private static final int COL_SSS_NUMBER             = 6;
    private static final int COL_PHILHEALTH_NUMBER      = 7;
    private static final int COL_TIN                    = 8;
    private static final int COL_PAGIBIG_NUMBER         = 9;
    private static final int COL_STATUS                 = 10;
    private static final int COL_POSITION               = 11;
    private static final int COL_SUPERVISOR             = 12;
    private static final int COL_BASIC_SALARY           = 13;
    private static final int COL_RICE_SUBSIDY           = 14;
    private static final int COL_PHONE_ALLOWANCE        = 15;
    private static final int COL_CLOTHING_ALLOWANCE     = 16;
    private static final int COL_GROSS_SEMI_MONTHLY_RATE = 17;
    private static final int COL_HOURLY_RATE            = 18;

    // === COLUMN INDEXES (attendance.csv, has a header row) ===
    private static final int ATTENDANCE_COLUMNS = 6;
    private static final int COL_ATT_EMPLOYEE_ID = 0;
    private static final int COL_ATT_DATE        = 3;
    private static final int COL_ATT_LOG_IN      = 4;
    private static final int COL_ATT_LOG_OUT     = 5;

    private static final DateTimeFormatter DATE_FORMAT =
            DateTimeFormatter.ofPattern("MM/dd/uuuu").withResolverStyle(ResolverStyle.STRICT);
    private static final DateTimeFormatter TIME_FORMAT =
            DateTimeFormatter.ofPattern("H:mm").withResolverStyle(ResolverStyle.STRICT);

    private final Path employeeFile;
    private final Path attendanceFile;
    private final Path resultsFile;

    /** Uses the default files in the data/ folder. */
    public CSVDataHandler() {
        this(Path.of(DEFAULT_EMPLOYEE_CSV), Path.of(DEFAULT_ATTENDANCE_CSV), Path.of(DEFAULT_RESULTS_CSV));
    }

    /** Uses the given files. Lets tests work on copies instead of the real data. */
    public CSVDataHandler(Path employeeFile, Path attendanceFile, Path resultsFile) {
        this.employeeFile = employeeFile;
        this.attendanceFile = attendanceFile;
        this.resultsFile = resultsFile;
    }

    // === EMPLOYEES ===

    /**
     * Reads employees.csv into Employee objects. Blank or incomplete rows are
     * skipped; rows that fail validation are skipped and logged.
     *
     * @return the employees in file order
     * @throws IOException if the file cannot be read
     */
    public List<Employee> loadEmployees() throws IOException {
        List<Employee> employees = new ArrayList<>();
        for (String line : readLines(employeeFile)) {
            if (line.trim().isEmpty()) continue;
            String[] fields = parseCSVLine(line);
            if (fields.length < EMPLOYEE_COLUMNS) continue;
            try {
                employees.add(createEmployee(fields));
            } catch (IllegalArgumentException e) {
                logger.log(Level.WARNING, "Skipped invalid employee row {0}: {1}",
                        new Object[]{fields[COL_EMPLOYEE_ID], e.getMessage()});
            }
        }
        return employees;
    }

    /**
     * Builds a RegularEmployee or ProbationaryEmployee from 19 values in
     * employees.csv column order. Used for CSV rows and for the Add/Edit form.
     * This is the only place where the Status value picks the subclass.
     *
     * @param fields the 19 field values
     * @return the validated employee
     * @throws IllegalArgumentException with a user-readable message if a value is invalid
     */
    public Employee createEmployee(String[] fields) {
        if (fields == null || fields.length < EMPLOYEE_COLUMNS) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("All " + EMPLOYEE_COLUMNS + " employee fields are required.");
        }
        String[] f = new String[EMPLOYEE_COLUMNS];
        for (int i = 0; i < EMPLOYEE_COLUMNS; i++) {
            f[i] = fields[i] == null ? "" : fields[i].trim();
            if (f[i].isEmpty()) {
                throw new IllegalArgumentException(EMPLOYEE_FIELD_NAMES.get(i) + " is required.");
            }
        }

        LocalDate birthday          = parseDate(f[COL_BIRTHDAY], "Birthday");
        BigDecimal basicSalary      = parseAmount(f, COL_BASIC_SALARY);
        BigDecimal riceSubsidy      = parseAmount(f, COL_RICE_SUBSIDY);
        BigDecimal phoneAllowance   = parseAmount(f, COL_PHONE_ALLOWANCE);
        BigDecimal clothingAllowance = parseAmount(f, COL_CLOTHING_ALLOWANCE);
        BigDecimal grossSemiMonthly = parseAmount(f, COL_GROSS_SEMI_MONTHLY_RATE);
        BigDecimal hourlyRate       = parseAmount(f, COL_HOURLY_RATE);

        String status = f[COL_STATUS];
        if (status.equalsIgnoreCase(Employee.STATUS_REGULAR)) {
            return new RegularEmployee(f[COL_EMPLOYEE_ID], f[COL_LAST_NAME], f[COL_FIRST_NAME], birthday,
                    f[COL_ADDRESS], f[COL_PHONE_NUMBER], f[COL_SSS_NUMBER], f[COL_PHILHEALTH_NUMBER], f[COL_TIN],
                    f[COL_PAGIBIG_NUMBER], f[COL_POSITION], f[COL_SUPERVISOR], basicSalary, riceSubsidy,
                    phoneAllowance, clothingAllowance, grossSemiMonthly, hourlyRate);
        }
        if (status.equalsIgnoreCase(Employee.STATUS_PROBATIONARY)) {
            return new ProbationaryEmployee(f[COL_EMPLOYEE_ID], f[COL_LAST_NAME], f[COL_FIRST_NAME], birthday,
                    f[COL_ADDRESS], f[COL_PHONE_NUMBER], f[COL_SSS_NUMBER], f[COL_PHILHEALTH_NUMBER], f[COL_TIN],
                    f[COL_PAGIBIG_NUMBER], f[COL_POSITION], f[COL_SUPERVISOR], basicSalary, riceSubsidy,
                    phoneAllowance, clothingAllowance, grossSemiMonthly, hourlyRate);
        }
        throw new IllegalArgumentException("Status must be Regular or Probationary.");
    }

    /**
     * Returns an employee's 19 values in employees.csv column order, as text.
     * Used to write the CSV file and to fill the Edit form.
     */
    public String[] toFields(Employee employee) {
        return new String[] {
            employee.getEmployeeId(), employee.getLastName(), employee.getFirstName(),
            employee.getBirthday().format(DATE_FORMAT), employee.getAddress(), employee.getPhoneNumber(),
            employee.getSssNumber(), employee.getPhilHealthNumber(), employee.getTin(), employee.getPagIbigNumber(),
            employee.getStatus(), employee.getPosition(), employee.getImmediateSupervisor(),
            employee.getBasicSalary().toPlainString(), employee.getRiceSubsidy().toPlainString(),
            employee.getPhoneAllowance().toPlainString(), employee.getClothingAllowance().toPlainString(),
            employee.getGrossSemiMonthlyRate().toPlainString(), employee.getHourlyRate().toPlainString()
        };
    }

    /**
     * Rewrites employees.csv with the given list. Called after add, edit, or delete.
     *
     * @throws IOException if the file cannot be written
     */
    public void saveEmployees(List<Employee> employees) throws IOException {
        if (employees == null) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Employee list is required.");
        }
        try (BufferedWriter writer = Files.newBufferedWriter(employeeFile, StandardCharsets.UTF_8)) {
            for (Employee employee : employees) {
                writer.write(joinCsvRow(toFields(employee)));
                writer.newLine();
            }
        }
    }

    /**
     * Finds an employee by ID in employees.csv.
     *
     * @return the employee, or null if no employee has that ID
 
MIDDLE OUTPUT OMITTED
mport java.nio.file.Files;
import java.nio.file.Path;
import java.nio.file.StandardCopyOption;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Map;
import motorph.model.AttendanceRecord;
import motorph.model.Employee;
import motorph.model.ProbationaryEmployee;
import motorph.model.RegularEmployee;
import motorph.service.CSVDataHandler;

/**
 * Tests CSV parsing, subclass creation, and saving. Reads the real data files;
 * all writes go to temporary copies so data/ is never changed.
 */
public class CSVDataHandlerTest {

    public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException {
        run();
        finish();
    }

    static void run() throws IOException {
        CSVDataHandler csv = new CSVDataHandler();

        section("CSVDataHandler: loadEmployees()");
        List<Employee> employees = csv.loadEmployees();
        checkEquals(34, employees.size(), "all 34 rows of employees.csv load");
        long regular = employees.stream().filter(e -> e instanceof RegularEmployee).count();
        long probationary = employees.stream().filter(e -> e instanceof ProbationaryEmployee).count();
        checkEquals(23L, regular, "23 rows become RegularEmployee");
        checkEquals(11L, probationary, "11 rows become ProbationaryEmployee (10021 to 10031)");
        checkEquals("Probationary", csv.findEmployeeById("10021").getEmploymentType(), "10021 is Probationary");
        checkEquals("Regular", csv.findEmployeeById("10020").getEmploymentType(), "10020 is Regular");
        checkEquals(null, csv.findEmployeeById("99999"), "unknown ID returns null");
        checkEquals("10035", csv.generateNextEmployeeId(), "next ID = highest (10034) + 1");

        section("CSVDataHandler: loadAttendance()");
        Map<String, List<AttendanceRecord>> attendance = csv.loadAttendance();
        int total = attendance.values().stream().mapToInt(List::size).sum();
        checkEquals(5168, total, "all 5,168 attendance records load (header skipped)");
        checkEquals(34, attendance.size(), "records grouped under 34 employee IDs");

        section("CSVDataHandler: createEmployee() from form values");
        String[] fields = csv.toFields(csv.findEmployeeById("10021"));
        fields[10] = "Regular";
        check(csv.createEmployee(fields) instanceof RegularEmployee, "changing Status to Regular builds a RegularEmployee");
        String[] bad = fields.clone();
        bad[13] = "abc";
        checkRejects(() -> csv.createEmployee(bad), "non-numeric Basic Salary rejected");
        String[] blank = fields.clone();
        blank[4] = " ";
        checkRejects(() -> csv.createEmployee(blank), "blank Address rejected");
        String[] badDate = fields.clone();
        badDate[3] = "02/30/1990";
        checkRejects(() -> csv.createEmployee(badDate), "impossible birthday rejected");
        String[] badStatus = fields.clone();
        badStatus[10] = "Contractual";
        checkRejects(() -> csv.createEmployee(badStatus), "unknown status rejected");

        section("CSVDataHandler: saveEmployees() round trip (temporary copy)");
        Path tempDir = Files.createTempDirectory("motorph-test");
        Path employeeCopy = tempDir.resolve("employees.csv");
        Files.copy(Path.of(CSVDataHandler.DEFAULT_EMPLOYEE_CSV), employeeCopy, StandardCopyOption.REPLACE_EXISTING);
        CSVDataHandler copy = new CSVDataHandler(employeeCopy, Path.of(CSVDataHandler.DEFAULT_ATTENDANCE_CSV),
                tempDir.resolve("payroll_results.csv"));
        List<Employee> loaded = copy.loadEmployees();
        copy.saveEmployees(loaded);
        checkEquals(Files.readAllLines(Path.of(CSVDataHandler.DEFAULT_EMPLOYEE_CSV)), Files.readAllLines(employeeCopy),
                "saving unchanged employees reproduces employees.csv line for line");

        String[] withComma = copy.toFields(loaded.get(0));
        withComma[4] = "Unit 5, \"Tower\" A, Makati";
        loaded.set(0, copy.createEmployee(withComma));
        copy.saveEmployees(loaded);
        checkEquals("Unit 5, \"Tower\" A, Makati", copy.findEmployeeById("10001").getAddress(),
                "address with commas and quotes survives save and reload");
        checkEquals(34, copy.loadEmployees().size(), "still 34 employees after save");
    }
}

    // Tries the possible locations of the databases folder and uses the first one that exists
    private static String resolveDatabasesFolder() {
        String[] candidates = {
            "src/payroll/hub/databases/",                                        // run from NetBeans project folder
            "MO-IT103-Group18-master/src/payroll/hub/databases/",                // run from one level up
            "MO-IT103-Group18-master/MO-IT103-Group18-master/src/payroll/hub/databases/" // run from repo root
        };
        for (String path : candidates) {
            if (new File(path).isDirectory()) {
                return path;
            }
        }
        return candidates[0];
    }

    // Splits a CSV line on commas that are not inside quotes
    public static String[] parseCSVLine(String line) {
        String[] fields = line.split(",(?=(?:[^\"]*\"[^\"]*\")*[^\"]*$)", -1);
        for (int i = 0; i < fields.length; i++) {
            fields[i] = fields[i].trim().replaceAll("^\"|\"$", "");
        }
        return fields;
    }

    // Converts values like "90,000" or "1,500" to a number
    private static double parseNumber(String value) {
        if (value == null || value.isBlank()) {
            return 0;
        }
        return Double.parseDouble(value.replace(",", "").trim());
    }

    // Returns every employee ID in the Employee Details CSV
    public static List<String> loadEmployeeIds() {
        List<String> ids = new ArrayList<>();
        try (BufferedReader br = new BufferedReader(new FileReader(EMPLOYEE_DETAILS_CSV))) {
            br.readLine(); // skip header
            String line;
            while ((line = br.readLine()) != null) {
                String[] f = parseCSVLine(line);
                if (f.length > 0 && !f[0].isBlank()) {
                    ids.add(f[0]);
                }
            }
        } catch (IOException e) {
            System.err.println("Could not read employee data: " + e.getMessage());
        }
        return ids;
    }

    // Builds an Employee object from the CSV row with the given ID, or returns null if not found
    public static Employee loadEmployee(String employeeId) {
        try (BufferedReader br = new BufferedReader(new FileReader(EMPLOYEE_DETAILS_CSV))) {
            br.readLine(); // skip header
            String line;
            while ((line = br.readLine()) != null) {
                String[] f = parseCSVLine(line);
                if (f.length >= 19 && f[0].equals(employeeId)) {
                    return new Employee(
                            f[0],                 // Employee #
                            f[1],                 // Last Name
                            f[2],                 // First Name
                            f[11],                // Position
                            f[10],                // Status (Regular / Probationary)
                            parseNumber(f[13]),   // Basic Salary
                            parseNumber(f[18]),   // Hourly Rate
                            parseNumber(f[14]),   // Rice Subsidy
                            parseNumber(f[15]),   // Phone Allowance
                            parseNumber(f[16]));  // Clothing Allowance
                }
            }
        } catch (IOException e) {
            System.err.println("Could not read employee data: " + e.getMessage());
        } catch (IllegalArgumentException e) {
            System.err.println("Invalid employee data for " + employeeId + ": " + e.getMessage());
        }
        return null;
    }

    /**
     * Builds a RegularEmployee or ProbationaryEmployee from 19 values in
     * employees.csv column order. Used for CSV rows and for the Add/Edit form.
     * This is the only place where the Status value picks the subclass.
     *
     * @param fields the 19 field values
     * @return the validated employee
     * @throws IllegalArgumentException with a user-readable message if a value is invalid
     */
    public Employee createEmployee(String[] fields) {
        if (fields == null || fields.length < EMPLOYEE_COLUMNS) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("All " + EMPLOYEE_COLUMNS + " employee fields are required.");
        }
        String[] f = new String[EMPLOYEE_COLUMNS];
        for (int i = 0; i < EMPLOYEE_COLUMNS; i++) {
            f[i] = fields[i] == null ? "" : fields[i].trim();
            if (f[i].isEmpty()) {
                throw new IllegalArgumentException(EMPLOYEE_FIELD_NAMES.get(i) + " is required.");
            }
        }

        LocalDate birthday          = parseDate(f[COL_BIRTHDAY], "Birthday");
        BigDecimal basicSalary      = parseAmount(f, COL_BASIC_SALARY);
        BigDecimal riceSubsidy      = parseAmount(f, COL_RICE_SUBSIDY);
        BigDecimal phoneAllowance   = parseAmount(f, COL_PHONE_ALLOWANCE);
        BigDecimal clothingAllowance = parseAmount(f, COL_CLOTHING_ALLOWANCE);
        BigDecimal grossSemiMonthly = parseAmount(f, COL_GROSS_SEMI_MONTHLY_RATE);
        BigDecimal hourlyRate       = parseAmount(f, COL_HOURLY_RATE);

        String status = f[COL_STATUS];
        if (status.equalsIgnoreCase(Employee.STATUS_REGULAR)) {
            return new RegularEmployee(f[COL_EMPLOYEE_ID], f[COL_LAST_NAME], f[COL_FIRST_NAME], birthday,
                    f[COL_ADDRESS], f[COL_PHONE_NUMBER], f[COL_SSS_NUMBER], f[COL_PHILHEALTH_NUMBER], f[COL_TIN],
                    f[COL_PAGIBIG_NUMBER], f[COL_POSITION], f[COL_SUPERVISOR], basicSalary, riceSubsidy,
                    phoneAllowance, clothingAllowance, grossSemiMonthly, hourlyRate);
        }
        if (status.equalsIgnoreCase(Employee.STATUS_PROBATIONARY)) {
            return new ProbationaryEmployee(f[COL_EMPLOYEE_ID], f[COL_LAST_NAME], f[COL_FIRST_NAME], birthday,
                    f[COL_ADDRESS], f[COL_PHONE_NUMBER], f[COL_SSS_NUMBER], f[COL_PHILHEALTH_NUMBER], f[COL_TIN],
                    f[COL_PAGIBIG_NUMBER], f[COL_POSITION], f[COL_SUPERVISOR], basicSalary, riceSubsidy,
                    phoneAllowance, clothingAllowance, grossSemiMonthly, hourlyRate);
        }
        throw new IllegalArgumentException("Status must be Regular or Probationary.");
    }

    /**
     * Returns an employee's 19 values in employees.csv column order, as text.
     * Used to write the CSV file and to fill the Edit form.
     */
    public String[] toFields(Employee employee) {
        return new String[] {
            employee.getEmployeeId(), employee.getLastName(), employee.getFirstName(),
            employee.getBirthday().format(DATE_FORMAT), employee.getAddress(), employee.getPhoneNumber(),
            employee.getSssNumber(), employee.getPhilHealthNumber(), employee.getTin(), employee.getPagIbigNumber(),
            employee.getStatus(), employee.getPosition(), employee.getImmediateSupervisor(),
            employee.getBasicSalary().toPlainString(), employee.getRiceSubsidy().toPlainString(),
            employee.getPhoneAllowance().toPlainString(), employee.getClothingAllowance().toPlainString(),
            employee.getGrossSemiMonthlyRate().toPlainString(), employee.getHourlyRate().toPlainString()
        };
    }

    /**
     * Rewrites employees.csv with the given list. Called after add, edit, or delete.
     *
     * @throws IOException if the file cannot be written
     */
    public void saveEmployees(List<Employee> employees) throws IOException {
        if (employees == null) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Employee list is required.");
        }
        try (BufferedWriter writer = Files.newBufferedWriter(employeeFile, StandardCharsets.UTF_8)) {
            for (Employee employee : employees) {
                writer.write(joinCsvRow(toFields(employee)));
                writer.newLine();
            }
        }
    }

    /**
     * Finds an employee by ID in employees.csv.
     *
     * @return the employee, or null if no employee has that ID
     * @throws IOException if the file cannot be read
     */
    public Employee findEmployeeById(String employeeId) throws IOException {
        if (employeeId == null) return null;
        String id = employeeId.trim();
        for (Employee employee : loadEmployees()) {
            if (employee.getEmployeeId().equals(id)) return employee;
        }
        return null;
    }

    public String generateNextEmployeeId() throws IOException {
        long highestId = 0;

            highestId = Math.max(highestId, Long.parseLong(employee.getEmployeeId()));

package motorphpayrollsystem;

public class EmployeeMapper {

    public static FullTimeEmployee fromCSV(String[] emp) {

        if (emp == null || emp.length < 19) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException(
                    "Employee CSV record is incomplete."
            );
        }

        int employeeID = Integer.parseInt(emp[0].trim());

        double basicSalary = parseAmount(emp[13]);
        double riceSubsidy = parseAmount(emp[14]);
        double phoneAllowance = parseAmount(emp[15]);
        double clothingAllowance = parseAmount(emp[16]);
        double hourlyRate = parseAmount(emp[18]);

        return new FullTimeEmployee(
                employeeID,
                emp[1],
                emp[2],
                emp[6],
                emp[7],
                emp[8],
                emp[9],
                emp[10],
                emp[12],
                emp[11],
                riceSubsidy,
                phoneAllowance,
                clothingAllowance,
                hourlyRate,
                basicSalary
        );
    }

    private static double parseAmount(String value) {
        if (value == null || value.trim().isEmpty()) {
            return 0.0;
        }

        return Double.parseDouble(
                value.replace(",", "").trim()
        );
    }

import com.opencsv.CSVReader;

import java.io.*;

public class EmployeeData {

    // ── Data store ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    public static volatile List<String[]> records;
    public static final String CSV_FILE = "MotorPH_Employee Data.csv";

    // Minimum columns expected in each record row
    private static final int MIN_COLS = 21;

    // ── Change listeners (for dynamic JTable refresh) ─────────────────────────
    private static final List<Runnable> changeListeners = new ArrayList<>();

    public static void addChangeListener(Runnable listener) {
        changeListeners.add(listener);
    }

    private static void notifyChanged() {
        for (Runnable r : changeListeners) {
            try { r.run(); } catch (Exception ignored) {}
        }
    }

    // =========================================================================
    // LOAD
    // =========================================================================
    public static synchronized void loadEmployeeData() {
        try (CSVReader reader = new CSVReader(new FileReader(CSV_FILE))) {
            List<String[]> raw = reader.readAll();
            // Pad short rows to MIN_COLS so we never get ArrayIndexOutOfBounds
            for (String[] row : raw) {
                if (row.length < MIN_COLS) {
                    String[] padded = new String[MIN_COLS];
                    System.arraycopy(row, 0, padded, 0, row.length);
                    for (int i = row.length; i < MIN_COLS; i++) padded[i] = "";
                    raw.set(raw.indexOf(row), padded);
                }
            }
            records = raw;
            System.out.println("Employee Data Loaded! Total: " + (records.size() - 1));
        } catch (FileNotFoundException e) {
            System.out.println("CSV file not found: " + CSV_FILE);
            records = new ArrayList<>();
        } catch (Exception e) {
            System.out.println("Error loading employee data: " + e.getMessage());
            e.printStackTrace();
            records = new ArrayList<>();
        }
    }

    // =========================================================================
    // FIELD ACCESSORS — safe, null-checked
    // =========================================================================
    public static String getEmpNo      (String[] e) { return safe(e, 0);  }
    public static String getLastName   (String[] e) { return safe(e, 1);  }
    public static String getFirstName  (String[] e) { return safe(e, 2);  }
    public static String getBirthday   (String[] e) { return safe(e, 3);  }
    public static String getAddress    (String[] e) { return safe(e, 4);  }
    public static String getPhoneNo    (String[] e) { return safe(e, 5);  }
    public static String getStatus     (String[] e) { return safe(e, 10); }
    public static String getPosition   (String[] e) { return safe(e, 11); }
    public static String getSupervisor (String[] e) { return safe(e, 12); }
    public static String getDepartment (String[] e) { return safe(e, 20); }

    private static String safe(String[] e, int idx) {
        if (e == null || idx >= e.length) return "";
        return e[idx] == null ? "" : e[idx].trim();
    }

    // =========================================================================
    // FIND
    // =========================================================================
    public static String[] findEmployee(String empNo) {
        if (records == null || empNo == null) return null;
        for (int i = 1; i < records.size(); i++) {
            String[] row = records.get(i);
            if (row != null && row.length > 0 &&
                row[0].trim().equalsIgnoreCase(empNo.trim())) {
                return row;
            }
        }
        // Only show dialog if called from a UI context
        JOptionPane.showMessageDialog(null,
            "Employee #" + empNo + " not found.",
            "Not Found", JOptionPane.WARNING_MESSAGE);
        return null;
    }

    public static boolean employeeExisting(String empNo) {
        if (records == null || empNo == null) return false;
        for (String[] row : records) {
            if (row != null && row.length > 0 &&
                row[0].trim().equalsIgnoreCase(empNo.trim())) {
                return true;
            }
        }
        return false;
    }

package motorphemployee;

import java.io.IOException;
import java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets;
import java.nio.file.Files;
import java.nio.file.Path;
import java.nio.file.Paths;
import java.time.LocalDate;
import java.time.LocalTime;
import java.time.YearMonth;
import java.time.format.DateTimeFormatter;
import java.time.format.DateTimeParseException;
import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Locale;
