Roadmap to full peer-level MotorPH feature parity

How to read “100%”: the nine submitted folders do not share one feature set, so there is no single objective peer-completion percentage. This roadmap uses the richest relevant comparison: the payroll/attendance/leave workflows in the stronger MO-IT110-style submissions (especially folders 6 and 9), plus the user's earlier MO-IT108 Requirements Analysis and System Design. It is a feature-completion target, not a grade.

Current user constraints remain in force: synthetic data only; no payroll calculations until authoritative rules are provided; no guessed pay-period calendar; no Firebase Console changes by the assistant. The legacy Terminal Assessment proposal contains template placeholders and is not treated as a detailed specification. The Code.pdf is unrelated C++ inventory work and is excluded.

Already done — current foundation
Firebase Email/Password Auth and user-scoped Firestore access live-tested with synthetic accounts.
Employee list, search, and detail selection work; data remains fictional and scoped to the signed-in sandbox.
Raw attendance records are selectable by employee and inclusive date range; default range spans that employee's earliest/latest available records, following the older Requirements Analysis.
Payroll stays gated. The default attendance range is not a pay period.
67 Java checks, production build, live API checks, browser E2E, and responsive checks pass.
Ordered tasks to reach the broader target
1. Freeze a traceable acceptance baseline
Map the active MO-IT110 rubric to the legacy MO-IT108 requirement groups and only the peer features we actually intend to match.
Mark every requirement as required, optional, or excluded; record source, owner, and acceptance example.
Reconcile conflicting legacy sources (for example, old role/2FA workflows vs the current Firebase sandbox).
Preserve the current boundary: synthetic records only; no payroll or attendance-derived pay output until rules are approved.

Done when: every target feature has a source and observable pass/fail acceptance criterion; proposals and template text are not presented as approved policy.

2. Complete the employee and organization foundation
Define the approved synthetic employee, department/position/branch, schedule, and supervisor models.
Add HR-style create/update/deactivate/search workflows if they are part of the target; record changes and validate required fields.
Keep government identifiers and real personal data out of the demo sandbox.
Decide how users map to employees and teams before moving beyond per-user isolated demo data.

Done when: synthetic employee lifecycle operations are validated, auditable, and limited by the approved role policy.

3. Finish attendance capture and summaries
Add time-in/time-out and attendance correction flows only if required; distinguish remote/offsite from verified onsite clocking if matching the legacy design.
Implement QR-based onsite verification only if it is an acceptance requirement; define expiry, replay protection, and device flow.
Add schedule/day-type, grace-period, present/absent/tardy, leave, overtime, and undertime summaries only after each rule is specified.
Define missing/duplicate punches, breaks, overnight shifts, time zone, rounding, corrections, and date boundaries.
Keep user-selected dates inclusive and the earliest/latest default; never substitute an assumed payroll cutoff.

Gate: attendance classifications and hour totals require written rules and an approved worked example. Until then, keep raw entries only.

Done when: approved test cases cover normal, late, absent, leave, holiday/rest day, missing punch, duplicate, correction, and boundary scenarios.

4. Add leave management
Define synthetic leave types, balances/accrual, eligibility, request/cancel states, and approval roles.
Build employee requests, supervisor decisions, balance history, and employee/team leave calendars.
Make approvals auditable and ensure only approved leave affects any later payroll input.

Gate: leave accrual, carry-over, monetization, and payroll treatment need an authoritative policy.

Done when: request, approve/reject/cancel, balance update, calendar, and audit tests pass.

5. Add ticketing and dispute workflows
Define ticket types, fields, routing, queue position, statuses, cancellation rules, and resolution history.
Implement overtime, leave, timesheet, payroll-dispute, HR/general inquiry, and technical-support forms only for in-scope roles.
Notify requestors and handlers, and retain an audit trail.

Done when: each included ticket type has tested routing, authorization, state changes, and user-visible status.

6. Add team and supervisor workflows
Define employee-to-team/branch membership and the supervisor's permitted scope.
Build rosters, availability, schedule viewing/editing, pending-request review, and timesheet correction workflow.
Record reasons and before/after values for every correction; notify affected employees.

Done when: supervisor actions are limited to assigned teams and are fully auditable.

7. Add HR onboarding/offboarding and employee administration
Add synthetic onboarding, profile/branch/position changes, deactivation, clearance queues, and search/update screens if required.
Define effective dates and the effect of mid-cycle changes without guessing payroll behavior.
Ensure inactive accounts lose access according to an approved policy.

Done when: employee lifecycle changes are validated, role-limited, and tested against audit/history requirements.

8. Implement the Java payroll engine — currently blocked
Obtain authoritative rules for pay-cycle boundaries, salary conversion, regular/OT/PTO/holiday/rest-day/undertime treatment, incentives, deductions, statutory contributions, tax, effective dates, and rounding.
Obtain independent worked expected-value cases, including edge cases; reconcile any conflicting legacy or peer formulas.
Implement versioned Java domain/calculation services using exact decimal arithmetic; keep formulas out of browser code and Firebase adapters.
Test each rule independently, then test combined payroll results and reproducibility.

Hard gate: the old documents name payroll components and snapshot fields but do not provide enough arithmetic, current values, or exact cutoffs to calculate correctly. Do not activate this task's outputs until those inputs exist and the user's “keep calculations disabled” instruction is explicitly lifted.

Done when: independent golden cases match every component and a repeat run uses the same saved rule version.

9. Add payroll supervision, adjustments, and approval
Define rate/incentive/deduction adjustment scope (individual/team/branch/global), approvers, separation of duties, and effective dates.
Build review/approve/reject flows with immutable audit events and controlled payroll reruns/corrections.
Generate payroll summaries only from approved, versioned inputs.

Gate: depends on approved payroll formulas, values, roles, and correction policy.

10. Add payslips, reports, and distribution
Define the required payslip fields and privacy rules.
Generate the required output format, store a stable result reference, and verify read-back.
Add payroll reports/monthly summaries only if required.
Add email delivery and retry/status tracking only if required and a safe delivery service is configured.

Gate: no payslip values until the calculation engine is approved.

11. Replace demo isolation with approved identity, RBAC, and PII controls
Define account-to-employee mapping, roles, team/branch scopes, session policy, account recovery, and 2FA requirements.
Implement least-privilege authorization in backend and Firebase Rules; do not rely on UI hiding.
If the older two-person PII approval requirement is adopted, implement explicit requests, two distinct authorized approvals, audit, and emergency policy.
Add access logging, abuse limits, and tests for own/team/branch/unauthorized access.

Done when: an authorization matrix is implemented and every allow/deny path is covered by live or rules-emulator tests.

12. Production hosting and operational safety
Replace the learning JDK server with an appropriately hardened deployment architecture; configure a stable domain, HTTPS, allowed origins, protected configuration, and environment-specific Firebase settings.
Add monitoring, structured error handling, rate/abuse controls, backup/restore, and data-retention procedures.
Load-test the approved scale target; the legacy document mentions 100 concurrent employee records, but the active target must be confirmed before treating that as a release criterion.
Complete a security/privacy review before any real employee or payroll data is used.

Done when: deployment, recovery, performance, and security acceptance tests pass outside the development sandbox.

13. Final regression and submission evidence
Run domain/unit, API integration, Firestore rules, browser E2E, accessibility/keyboard, mobile/tablet, and failure-path tests.
Compare outputs to approved source examples, not just another team's implementation.
Prepare requirement-to-code traceability, architecture/design artifacts, test results, and demo steps without exposing secrets or real data.

Done when: every required acceptance item is evidenced and no unapproved feature or calculation is enabled.

Completion rule

Do not mark “100%” until all tasks selected in Step 1 have passed their acceptance criteria. Tasks 3–10 are broader than current Tasks 1–3; task 8 and all downstream payroll outputs remain blocked by missing rules and the user's current no-calculation constraint. The current prototype is a strong foundation, not yet a complete payroll system.

Open

To reach broad peer-level feature parity, use the 13-step roadmap I’ve opened: docs/peer-parity-roadmap.md. This is a larger target than the current Tasks 1–3.

Freeze the target scope against the current MO-IT110 rubric, your older MO-IT108 documents, and the chosen peer features.
Complete employee administration: synthetic employee/branch/position/schedule models and, if required, HR create/update/deactivate workflows.
Expand attendance: clock-in/out, corrections, scheduling, and required attendance summaries. QR onsite verification is a separate feature if it’s in scope.
Add leave management: requests, approvals, balances, history, and calendars.
Add ticketing: overtime, leave, timesheet, payroll-dispute, HR, and support queues as required.
Add supervisor/team tools: rosters, schedules, team-scoped approvals, and auditable corrections.
Add HR lifecycle workflows: onboarding, offboarding, and employee changes.
Implement the Java payroll engine only after authoritative formulas, cut-offs, values, rounding rules, and worked examples are available.
Add payroll adjustments and approvals with effective dates, review, audit, and controlled reruns.
Generate payslips and reports and, if required, add secure delivery and retry tracking.
Replace the demo-only authorization model with approved roles, team/branch scoping, 2FA requirements, and PII approval controls.
Harden production operations: hosting, stable domain/HTTPS, monitoring, backup/restore, and security review.
Complete regression and submission evidence: requirement traceability, automated tests, browser/accessibility checks, and demo materials.

Already in place: live synthetic Firebase Auth/Firestore, employee search/detail, and raw attendance filtering with the earliest-to-latest date default from your older requirements. The current Tasks 1–3 foundation is about 85–90% complete; broad feature parity with the fuller peer projects is about 25–35%.

Two important gates remain: attendance summaries need clear classification/hour rules, and payroll outputs need authoritative calculation rules. I’ve kept those disabled as instructed; the older documents add useful fields and workflows but not enough policy to safely calculate pay. “100%” should mean every item selected in step 1 passes its acceptance test—not that every feature mentioned across every folder is copied.

package ph.motorph.web;

import java.util.Arrays;
import java.util.Collections;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Optional;

/** Temporary in-memory store containing only fictional demo employees. */
public final class InMemoryEmployeeStore implements EmployeeStore {
    private final List<Employee> employees = Collections.unmodifiableList(Arrays.asList(
        new Employee("DEMO-001", "Mara Rivera", "People Operations", "HR Coordinator", "Makati", "Active"),
        new Employee("DEMO-002", "Eli Santos", "Finance", "Payroll Associate", "Taguig", "Active"),
        new Employee("DEMO-003", "Noa Reyes", "Operations", "Operations Lead", "Quezon City", "On leave")
    ));

    @Override
    public List<Employee> findAll() {
        return employees;
    }

    @Override
    public Optional<Employee> findById(String id) {
        if (id == null) return Optional.empty();
        return employees.stream().filter(employee -> employee.getId().equals(id)).findFirst();
    }
}
package ph.motorph.web;

import java.util.Objects;

/** A small employee view model for the first synthetic-data prototype. */
public final class Employee {
    private final String id;
    private final String name;
    private final String department;
    private final String role;
    private final String location;
    private final String status;

    public Employee(String id, String name, String department, String role, String location, String status) {
        this.id = requireText(id, "id");
        this.name = requireText(name, "name");
        this.department = requireText(department, "department");
        this.role = requireText(role, "role");
        this.location = requireText(location, "location");
        this.status = requireText(status, "status");
    }

    private static String requireText(String value, String field) {
        Objects.requireNonNull(value, field + " must not be null");
        if (value.trim().isEmpty()) throw new IllegalArgumentException(field + " must not be blank");
        return value.trim();
    }

    public String getId() { return id; }
    public String getName() { return name; }
    public String getDepartment() { return department; }
    public String getRole() { return role; }
    public String getLocation() { return location; }
    public String getStatus() { return status; }
}
package ph.motorph.web;

import com.sun.net.httpserver.HttpExchange;
import com.sun.net.httpserver.HttpServer;

import java.io.IOException;
import java.io.OutputStream;
import java.net.InetSocketAddress;
import java.net.URLDecoder;
import java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets;
import java.nio.file.Files;
import java.nio.file.Path;
import java.nio.file.Paths;
import java.time.LocalDate;
import java.time.format.DateTimeParseException;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Optional;
import java.util.concurrent.Executors;

/** Java 11 HTTP backend for the browser-based MotorPH prototype. */
public final class AppServer {
    private final Path webRoot;
    private final String firebaseProjectId;
    private final EmployeeService localEmployeeService = new EmployeeService(new InMemoryEmployeeStore());
    private final EmployeeScheduleStore localScheduleStore = new InMemoryEmployeeScheduleStore();
    private final AttendanceStore localAttendanceStore = new InMemoryAttendanceStore();
    private HttpServer server;
    private java.util.concurrent.ExecutorService executor;

    public AppServer() {
        this(System.getenv().getOrDefault("FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID", ""),
            Paths.get(System.getenv().getOrDefault("WEB_ROOT", "web")));
    }

    AppServer(String firebaseProjectId, Path webRoot) {
        this.firebaseProjectId = firebaseProjectId == null ? "" : firebaseProjectId.trim();
        if (webRoot == null) throw new IllegalArgumentException("webRoot must not be null");
        this.webRoot = webRoot.toAbsolutePath().normalize();
    }

    public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception {
        int port = Integer.parseInt(System.getenv().getOrDefault("PORT", "8080"));
        String host = System.getenv().getOrDefault("HOST", "0.0.0.0");
        AppServer app = new AppServer();
        app.start(host, port);
        Runtime.getRuntime().addShutdownHook(new Thread(app::stop));
    }

    HttpServer start(String host, int port) throws IOException {
        if (server != null) throw new IllegalStateException("server is already started");
        server = HttpServer.create(new InetSocketAddress(host, port), 0);
        server.createContext("/api/health", this::handleHealth);
        server.createContext("/api/employees", this::handleEmployees);
        server.createContext("/api/attendance", this::handleAttendance);
        server.createContext("/api/demo/seed", this::handleSeedDemo);
        server.createContext("/", this::handleStaticFiles);
        executor = Executors.newFixedThreadPool(8);
        server.setExecutor(executor);
        server.start();
        System.out.println("MotorPH Java API listening on " + host + ":" + server.getAddress().getPort());
        System.out.println("Mode: " + (firebaseProjectId.isEmpty() ? "local synthetic demo" : "Firebase-authenticated user sandbox"));
        System.out.println("Serving browser files from " + webRoot);
        return server;
    }

    void stop() {
        if (server != null) {
            server.stop(0);
            server = null;
        }
        if (executor != null) {
            executor.shutdownNow();
            executor = null;
        }
    }

    private void handleHealth(HttpExchange exchange) throws IOException {
        if (!"GET".equals(exchange.getRequestMethod())) {
            sendJson(exchange, 405, "{\"error\":\"Method not allowed\"}");
            return;
        }
        String mode = firebaseProjectId.isEmpty() ? "local-synthetic-demo" : "firebase-user-sandbox";
        sendJson(exchange, 200, "{\"status\":\"ok\",\"mode\":\"" + mode + "\"}");
    }

    private void handleEmployees(HttpExchange exchange) throws IOException {
        if (!"GET".equals(exchange.getRequestMethod())) {
            sendJson(exchange, 405, "{\"error\":\"Method not allowed\"}");
            return;
        }
        try {
            RequestServices services = servicesFor(exchange);
            String path = exchange.getRequestURI().getPath();
            if ("/api/employees".equals(path) || "/api/employees/".equals(path)) {
                String query = queryParameter(exchange.getRequestURI().getRawQuery(), "q");
                List<Employee> matches = services.employeeService.searchEmployees(query);
                int total = services.employeeService.listEmployees().size();
                sendJson(exchange, 200, employeesToJson(matches, total));
                return;
            }
            String id = path.substring("/api/employees/".length());
            if (id.isEmpty() || id.contains("/")) {
                sendJson(exchange, 404, "{\"error\":\"Employee not found\"}");
                return;
            }
            Optional<Employee> employee = services.employeeService.findEmployee(id);
            if (!employee.isPresent()) {
                sendJson(exchange, 404, "{\"error\":\"Employee not found\"}");
                return;
            }
            sendJson(exchange, 200, "{\"item\":" + employeeToJson(employee.get()) + "}");
        } catch (FirestoreException ex) {
            sendApiError(exchange, ex);
        }
    }

    private void handleAttendance(HttpExchange exchange) throws IOException {
        if (!"GET".equals(exchange.getRequestMethod())) {
            sendJson(exchange, 405, "{\"error\":\"Method not allowed\"}");
            return;
        }
        String employeeId = queryParameter(exchange.getRequestURI().getRawQuery(), "employeeId");
        if (employeeId == null || employeeId.trim().isEmpty()) {
            sendJson(exchange, 400, "{\"error\":\"employeeId is required\"}");
            return;
        }
        try {
            RequestServices services = servicesFor(exchange);
            LocalDate from = parseOptionalDate(queryParameter(exchange.getRequestURI().getRawQuery(), "from"));
            LocalDate to = parseOptionalDate(queryParameter(exchange.getRequestURI().getRawQuery(), "to"));
            AttendanceService attendanceService = new AttendanceService(services.employeeService,
                localScheduleStore, services.attendanceStore);
            List<AttendanceRecord> records = attendanceService.findForEmployee(employeeId, from, to);
            sendJson(exchange, 200, attendanceToJson(records));
        } catch (DateTimeParseException ex) {
            sendJson(exchange, 400, "{\"error\":\"Dates must use YYYY-MM-DD\"}");
        } catch (IllegalArgumentException ex) {
            sendJson(exchange, 400, "{\"error\":\"" + escapeJson(ex.getMessage()) + "\"}");
        } catch (java.util.NoSuchElementException ex) {
            sendJson(exchange, 404, "{\"error\":\"Employee not found\"}");
        } catch (FirestoreException ex) {
            sendApiError(exchange, ex);
        }
    }

    private void handleSeedDemo(HttpExchange exchange) throws IOException {
        if (!"POST".equals(exchange.getRequestMethod())) {
            sendJson(exchange, 405, "{\"error\":\"Method not allowed\"}");
            return;
        }
        if (firebaseProjectId.isEmpty()) {
            sendJson(exchange, 400, "{\"error\":\"Firebase is not configured for this server.\"}");
            return;
        }
        try {
            FirestoreRestClient client = firestoreClientFor(exchange);
            DemoSeedService.SeedResult result = new DemoSeedService(client).seedMissingSyntheticRecords();
            sendJson(exchange, 200, "{\"employeesCreated\":" + result.getEmployeesCreated()
                + ",\"attendanceCreated\":" + result.getAttendanceCreated()
                + ",\"syntheticOnly\":true}");
        } catch (FirestoreException ex) {
            sendApiError(exchange, ex);
        }
    }

    private RequestServices servicesFor(HttpExchange exchange) {
        if (firebaseProjectId.isEmpty()) {
            return new RequestServices(localEmployeeService, localAttendanceStore);
        }
        FirestoreRestClient client = firestoreClientFor(exchange);
        return new RequestServices(new EmployeeService(new FirestoreEmployeeStore(client)), new FirestoreAttendanceStore(client));
    }

    private FirestoreRestClient firestoreClientFor(HttpExchange exchange) {
        String authorization = exchange.getRequestHeaders().getFirst("Authorization");
        String uid = exchange.getRequestHeaders().getFirst("X-Firebase-UID");
        if (authorization == null || !authorization.startsWith("Bearer ") || uid == null || uid.trim().isEmpty()) {
            throw new FirestoreException("Sign in with your Firebase account to continue.", 401);
        }
        String token = authorization.substring("Bearer ".length()).trim();
        if (token.length() > 8192 || uid.length() > 128 || uid.contains("/")) {
            throw new FirestoreException("Invalid Firebase session information.", 401);
        }
        return new FirestoreRestClient(firebaseProjectId, uid, token);
    }

    private static LocalDate parseOptionalDate(String value) {
        return value == null || value.trim().isEmpty() ? null : LocalDate.parse(value.trim());
    }

    private static String attendanceToJson(List<AttendanceRecord> records) {
        StringBuilder json = new StringBuilder("{\"items\":[");
        for (int i = 0; i < records.size(); i++) {
            AttendanceRecord record = records.get(i);
            if (i > 0) json.append(',');
            json.append("{\"attendanceId\":").append(record.getAttendanceId())
                .append(",\"scheduleId\":").append(record.getScheduleId())
                .append(",\"date\":\"").append(record.getDate())
                .append("\",\"timeIn\":\"").append(record.getTimeIn())
                .append("\",\"timeOut\":\"").append(record.getTimeOut())

function setAuthError(message) {
  authError.textContent = message;
  authError.hidden = !message;
}

function friendlyAuthError(error) {
  const code = error && error.code || '';
  if (code === 'auth/operation-not-allowed') return 'Email/Password sign-in is disabled. Enable it in Firebase Console → Authentication → Sign-in method.';
  if (code === 'auth/unauthorized-domain') return 'This preview domain is not authorized. Add its host under Firebase Console → Authentication → Settings → Authorized domains, or test on localhost.';
  if (code === 'auth/invalid-api-key' || code === 'auth/api-key-not-valid.-please-pass-a-valid-api-key.') return 'The Firebase Web API key in .env.local is missing or invalid.';
  if (code === 'auth/email-already-in-use') return 'That email already has a Firebase account. Use Sign in instead.';
  if (code === 'auth/weak-password') return 'Use a password with at least six characters.';
  if (code === 'auth/invalid-credential' || code === 'auth/wrong-password' || code === 'auth/user-not-found') return 'Email or password is incorrect.';
  return error && error.message ? error.message : 'Firebase sign-in could not be completed.';
}

async function signIn() {
  setAuthError('');
  try {
    await signInWithEmailAndPassword(auth, authEmail.value.trim(), authPassword.value);
  } catch (error) {
    setAuthError(friendlyAuthError(error));
  }
}

async function createDevAccount() {
  setAuthError('');
  try {
    await createUserWithEmailAndPassword(auth, authEmail.value.trim(), authPassword.value);
  } catch (error) {
    setAuthError(friendlyAuthError(error));
  }
}

async function apiHeaders(extra = {}) {
  const headers = { Accept: 'application/json', ...extra };
  if (state.user) {
    const token = await state.user.getIdToken();
    headers.Authorization = `Bearer ${token}`;
    headers['X-Firebase-UID'] = state.user.uid;
  }
  return headers;
}

function showWorkspace(user) {
  state.user = user;
  authGate.hidden = true;
  appShell.hidden = false;
  document.getElementById('sign-out-button').hidden = !user;
  document.getElementById('operator-label').textContent = user ? 'USER SANDBOX' : 'LOCAL PREVIEW';
  document.getElementById('operator-avatar').textContent = user ? (user.email || 'D').slice(0, 1).toUpperCase() : 'D';
  loadEmployees();
}

function showSignIn(message = '') {
  state.user = null;
  appShell.hidden = true;
  authGate.hidden = false;
  setAuthError(message);
}

const rows = document.getElementById('employee-rows');
const search = document.getElementById('employee-search');
const count = document.getElementById('employee-count');
const resultCount = document.getElementById('result-count');
const seedDemoButton = document.getElementById('seed-demo-button');
const dialog = document.getElementById('employee-dialog');
const dialogTitle = document.getElementById('dialog-title');
const dialogContent = document.getElementById('dialog-content');
const attendanceRows = document.getElementById('attendance-rows');
const attendanceEmployee = document.getElementById('attendance-employee');
const attendanceFrom = document.getElementById('attendance-from');
const attendanceTo = document.getElementById('attendance-to');
const attendanceResultCount = document.getElementById('attendance-result-count');

function initials(name) {
  return name.trim().split(/\s+/).slice(0, 2).map(part => part[0]).join('').toUpperCase();
}

function makeCell(content) {
  const cell = document.createElement('td');
  if (content instanceof Node) cell.append(content);
  else cell.textContent = content;
  return cell;
}

function showTableMessage(message) {
  rows.replaceChildren();
  const row = document.createElement('tr');
  const cell = document.createElement('td');
  cell.colSpan = 6;
  cell.className = 'table-message';
  cell.textContent = message;
  row.append(cell);
  rows.append(row);
}

function renderEmployees() {
  rows.replaceChildren();
  if (state.employees.length === 0) {
    showTableMessage(search.value.trim() ? 'No employee records match that search.' : 'No demo records are available.');
  } else {
    state.employees.forEach(employee => {
      const row = document.createElement('tr');
      row.className = 'employee-row';
      // Preserve convenient pointer activation while keeping native table semantics.
      row.addEventListener('click', () => openEmployee(employee));

      const person = document.createElement('div');
      person.className = 'person-cell';
      const avatar = document.createElement('span');
      avatar.className = 'person-initials';
      avatar.setAttribute('aria-hidden', 'true');
      avatar.textContent = initials(employee.name);
      const nameBlock = document.createElement('span');
      const name = document.createElement('span');
      name.className = 'person-name';
      name.textContent = employee.name;
      const id = document.createElement('span');
      id.className = 'person-id';
      id.textContent = employee.id;
      nameBlock.append(name, id);
      person.append(avatar, nameBlock);
      row.append(makeCell(person));
      row.append(makeCell(employee.department));
      row.append(makeCell(employee.role));
      row.append(makeCell(employee.location));

      const status = document.createElement('span');
      status.className = `status-pill${employee.status.toLowerCase() === 'active' ? '' : ' leave'}`;
      status.textContent = employee.status;
      row.append(makeCell(status));
      const openButton = document.createElement('button');
      openButton.type = 'button';
      openButton.className = 'row-open-button';
      openButton.setAttribute('aria-label', `Open ${employee.name}, ${employee.id}`);
      openButton.addEventListener('click', event => {
        event.stopPropagation();
        openEmployee(employee);
      });
      const arrow = document.createElement('span');
      arrow.className = 'row-arrow';
      arrow.setAttribute('aria-hidden', 'true');
      arrow.textContent = '›';
      openButton.append(arrow);
      row.append(makeCell(openButton));
      rows.append(row);
    });
  }

  count.textContent = String(state.totalEmployees).padStart(2, '0');
  const overviewCount = document.getElementById('overview-employee-count');
  if (overviewCount) overviewCount.textContent = String(state.totalEmployees).padStart(2, '0');
  resultCount.textContent = `${state.employees.length} ${state.employees.length === 1 ? 'record' : 'records'} shown`;
}

function openEmployee(employee) {
  state.selected = employee;
  dialogTitle.textContent = employee.name;
  dialogContent.replaceChildren();
  const fields = [
    ['EMPLOYEE ID', employee.id],
    ['EMPLOYMENT STATUS', employee.status],
    ['DEPARTMENT', employee.department],
    ['ROLE', employee.role],
    ['LOCATION', employee.location],
    ['DATA SOURCE', 'Synthetic demo record']
  ];
  const grid = document.createElement('div');
  grid.className = 'detail-grid';
  fields.forEach(([labelText, valueText]) => {
    const item = document.createElement('div');
    item.className = 'detail-item';
    const label = document.createElement('span');
    label.textContent = labelText;
    const value = document.createElement('strong');
    value.textContent = valueText;
    item.append(label, value);
    grid.append(item);
  });
  dialogContent.append(grid);
  dialog.showModal();
}

function populateAttendanceEmployees() {
  if (!attendanceEmployee) return;
  const current = attendanceEmployee.value;
  attendanceEmployee.replaceChildren();
  state.allEmployees.forEach(employee => {
    const option = document.createElement('option');
    option.value = employee.id;
    option.textContent = `${employee.id} — ${employee.name}`;
    attendanceEmployee.append(option);
  });
  if (state.allEmployees.some(employee => employee.id === current)) attendanceEmployee.value = current;
}

function showAttendanceMessage(message) {
  attendanceRows.replaceChildren();
  const row = document.createElement('tr');
  const cell = document.createElement('td');
  cell.colSpan = 6;
  cell.className = 'table-message';
  cell.textContent = message;
  row.append(cell);
  attendanceRows.append(row);
}

function applyDefaultAttendanceRange(records) {
  if (!records.length || attendanceFrom.value || attendanceTo.value) return;
  const dates = records.map(record => String(record.date))
    .filter(date => /^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$/.test(date))
    .sort();
  if (!dates.length) return;
  // The legacy MO-IT108 requirement says the attendance view defaults to its full available date span.
  // This is not a pay-period calendar and does not derive hours or payroll values.
  attendanceFrom.value = dates[0];
  attendanceTo.value = dates[dates.length - 1];
}

function renderAttendance(records) {
  applyDefaultAttendanceRange(records);
  attendanceRows.replaceChildren();
  if (records.length === 0) {
    showAttendanceMessage('No attendance entries match this employee and date range.');
  } else {
    records.forEach(record => {
      const row = document.createElement('tr');
      [record.date, String(record.attendanceId), String(record.scheduleId), record.timeIn, record.timeOut, record.dayType]
        .forEach(value => row.append(makeCell(value)));
      attendanceRows.append(row);
    });
  }
  attendanceResultCount.textContent = `${records.length} raw ${records.length === 1 ? 'entry' : 'entries'} loaded`;
}

function applyDefaultAttendanceRange(records) {
  if (!records.length || attendanceFrom.value || attendanceTo.value) return;
  const dates = records.map(record => String(record.date))
    .filter(date => /^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$/.test(date))
    .sort();
  if (!dates.length) return;
  // The legacy MO-IT108 requirement says the attendance view defaults to its full available date span.
  // This is not a pay-period calendar and does not derive hours or payroll values.
  attendanceFrom.value = dates[0];
  attendanceTo.value = dates[dates.length - 1];
}

function renderAttendance(records) {
  applyDefaultAttendanceRange(records);
  attendanceRows.replaceChildren();
  if (records.length === 0) {
    showAttendanceMessage('No attendance entries match this employee and date range.');
  } else {
    records.forEach(record => {
      const row = document.createElement('tr');
      [record.date, String(record.attendanceId), String(record.scheduleId), record.timeIn, record.timeOut, record.dayType]
        .forEach(value => row.append(makeCell(value)));
      attendanceRows.append(row);
    });
  }
  attendanceResultCount.textContent = `${records.length} raw ${records.length === 1 ? 'entry' : 'entries'} loaded`;
}

async function loadAttendance() {
  const employeeId = attendanceEmployee.value;
  if (!employeeId) {
    showAttendanceMessage('Load the employee directory first.');
    return;
  }
  const requestNumber = ++state.attendanceRequestNumber;
  showAttendanceMessage('Loading raw attendance records…');
  attendanceResultCount.textContent = 'Loading';
  const params = new URLSearchParams({ employeeId });
  const from = attendanceFrom.value;
  const to = attendanceTo.value;
  if (from) params.set('from', from);
  if (to) params.set('to', to);
  try {
    const response = await fetch(`/api/attendance?${params.toString()}`, { headers: await apiHeaders() });
    const payload = await response.json();
    if (!response.ok) throw new Error(payload.error || `Request failed (${response.status})`);
    if (requestNumber !== state.attendanceRequestNumber) return;
    renderAttendance(Array.isArray(payload.items) ? payload.items : []);
  } catch (error) {
    if (requestNumber !== state.attendanceRequestNumber) return;
    showAttendanceMessage(error.message || 'Could not load attendance records.');
    attendanceResultCount.textContent = 'Could not load records';
  }
}

async function loadEmployees() {
  const requestNumber = ++state.requestNumber;
  const query = search.value.trim();
  showTableMessage('Loading employee records…');
  resultCount.textContent = 'Loading';
  try {
    const url = query ? `/api/employees?q=${encodeURIComponent(query)}` : '/api/employees';
    const response = await fetch(url, { headers: await apiHeaders() });
    const payload = await response.json();
    if (!response.ok) throw new Error(payload.error || `Request failed (${response.status})`);
    if (!payload || !Array.isArray(payload.items)) throw new Error('Unexpected employee response');
    if (requestNumber !== state.requestNumber) return;
    state.employees = payload.items;
    state.totalEmployees = Number.isInteger(payload.total) ? payload.total : payload.items.length;
    if (!query) {
      state.allEmployees = payload.items;
      populateAttendanceEmployees();
    }
    seedDemoButton.hidden = !(state.user && state.totalEmployees === 0 && !query);
    renderEmployees();
  } catch (error) {
    if (requestNumber !== state.requestNumber) return;
    state.employees = [];
    seedDemoButton.hidden = true;
    renderEmployees();
    showTableMessage(error.message || 'Could not reach the Java service. Check that the prototype server is running, then refresh.');
    resultCount.textContent = 'Could not load records';
  }
}

async function seedSyntheticDemoData() {
  seedDemoButton.disabled = true;
  seedDemoButton.textContent = 'Writing synthetic records…';
  try {
    const response = await fetch('/api/demo/seed', { method: 'POST', headers: await apiHeaders() });
    const payload = await response.json();
    if (!response.ok) throw new Error(payload.error || `Request failed (${response.status})`);
    resultCount.textContent = `${payload.employeesCreated} employees and ${payload.attendanceCreated} attendance entries added`;
    await loadEmployees();
  } catch (error) {
    showTableMessage(error.message || 'Could not write the synthetic demo records.');
    resultCount.textContent = 'Demo setup failed';
  } finally {
    seedDemoButton.disabled = false;
    seedDemoButton.textContent = 'Add synthetic demo data';
  }
}

function switchView(view) {
  const labels = { overview: 'Overview', employees: 'Employees', attendance: 'Attendance', payroll: 'Payroll' };
  if (!labels[view]) return;
  document.querySelectorAll('.page-view').forEach(page => {
    page.hidden = page.id !== `${view}-view`;
  });
  document.querySelectorAll('.nav-item').forEach(nav => {
    const active = nav.dataset.view === view;
    nav.classList.toggle('active', active);
    if (active) nav.setAttribute('aria-current', 'page');
    else nav.removeAttribute('aria-current');
  });
  document.getElementById('crumb-current').textContent = labels[view];
  document.title = `${labels[view]} — MotorPH Payroll Office`;
  if (view === 'attendance' && attendanceEmployee.value) loadAttendance();
}

document.querySelectorAll('.nav-item').forEach(item => {
  item.addEventListener('click', () => switchView(item.dataset.view));
});

const LEAVE_TYPES = Object.freeze(['Vacation', 'Medical', 'Personal', 'Unpaid']);

// Routes reflect the queues described in the legacy project materials. These are
// labels for a browser-only demo, not real authorization or delivery routing.
const TICKET_QUEUES = Object.freeze({
  'Overtime request': 'Team Lead',
  'Leave request': 'Team Lead',
  'Timesheet correction': 'Team Lead',
  'Payroll inquiry': 'Payroll Staff',
  'HR inquiry': 'HR',
  'Technical support': 'IT Admin'
});

const MAX_NOTE_LENGTH = 240;

export function createWorkflowState() {
  return {
    leaveRequests: [],
    tickets: [],
    nextLeaveNumber: 1,
    nextTicketNumber: 1
  };
}

function requireState(state) {
  if (!state || !Array.isArray(state.leaveRequests) || !Array.isArray(state.tickets)) {
    throw new TypeError('Workflow state is invalid.');
  }
}

function findEmployee(employeeId, employees) {
  const employee = Array.isArray(employees) && employees.find(item => item && item.id === employeeId);
  if (!employee) throw new Error('Choose an employee from the synthetic demo directory.');
  return employee;
}

function isValidDate(value) {
  if (typeof value !== 'string' || !/^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$/.test(value)) return false;
  const date = new Date(`${value}T00:00:00.000Z`);
  return !Number.isNaN(date.valueOf()) && date.toISOString().slice(0, 10) === value;
}

function cleanOptionalText(value, field) {
  const text = String(value ?? '').trim();
  if (text.length > MAX_NOTE_LENGTH) throw new Error(`${field} must be ${MAX_NOTE_LENGTH} characters or fewer.`);
  return text;
}

function dateStamp(value) {
  const date = value instanceof Date ? value : new Date(`${value}T00:00:00.000Z`);
  if (Number.isNaN(date.valueOf())) throw new Error('Submission date is invalid.');
  return date.toISOString().slice(0, 10);
}

export function submitLeaveRequest(state, input, employees, submittedAt = new Date()) {
  requireState(state);
  if (!input || !LEAVE_TYPES.includes(input.leaveType)) throw new Error('Choose a valid leave type.');
  const employee = findEmployee(input.employeeId, employees);
  if (!isValidDate(input.startDate) || !isValidDate(input.endDate)) throw new Error('Enter a valid date for both leave dates.');
  if (input.startDate > input.endDate) throw new Error('The start date must be on or before the end date.');
  const note = cleanOptionalText(input.note, 'Note');
  const request = {
    id: `LV-${String(state.nextLeaveNumber).padStart(4, '0')}`,
    employeeId: employee.id,
    employeeName: String(employee.name || employee.id),
    leaveType: input.leaveType,
    startDate: input.startDate,
    endDate: input.endDate,
    note,
    status: 'Pending review',
    submittedAt: dateStamp(submittedAt)
  };
  return {
    state: { ...state, leaveRequests: [...state.leaveRequests, request], nextLeaveNumber: state.nextLeaveNumber + 1 },
    request
  };
}

export function cancelLeaveRequest(state, requestId, employeeId) {
  requireState(state);
  const request = state.leaveRequests.find(item => item.id === requestId);
  if (!request) throw new Error('Leave request was not found.');
  if (request.employeeId !== employeeId) throw new Error('You can only cancel your own request.');
  if (request.status !== 'Pending review') throw new Error('Only a pending leave request can be cancelled.');
  const leaveRequests = state.leaveRequests.map(item => item.id === requestId ? { ...item, status: 'Cancelled' } : item);
  return { ...state, leaveRequests };
}

export function submitTicket(state, input, employees, submittedAt = new Date()) {
  requireState(state);
  const ticketType = input && input.ticketType;
  if (!Object.hasOwn(TICKET_QUEUES, ticketType)) throw new Error('Choose a valid ticket type.');
  const employee = findEmployee(input.employeeId, employees);
  const summary = cleanOptionalText(input.summary, 'Message');
  if (!summary) throw new Error('Add a short message before submitting the ticket.');
  const ticket = {
    id: `TK-${String(state.nextTicketNumber).padStart(4, '0')}`,
    employeeId: employee.id,
    employeeName: String(employee.name || employee.id),
    ticketType,
    queue: TICKET_QUEUES[ticketType],
    summary,
    status: 'Open',
    submittedAt: dateStamp(submittedAt)
  };
  return {
    state: { ...state, tickets: [...state.tickets, ticket], nextTicketNumber: state.nextTicketNumber + 1 },
    ticket
  };
}

export function cancelTicket(state, ticketId, employeeId) {
  requireState(state);
  const ticket = state.tickets.find(item => item.id === ticketId);
  if (!ticket) throw new Error('Ticket was not found.');
  if (ticket.employeeId !== employeeId) throw new Error('You can only cancel your own ticket.');
  if (ticket.status !== 'Open') throw new Error('Only an open ticket can be cancelled.');
  const tickets = state.tickets.map(item => item.id === ticketId ? { ...item, status: 'Cancelled' } : item);
  return { ...state, tickets };
}

export { LEAVE_TYPES, MAX_NOTE_LENGTH, TICKET_QUEUES };

function setAuthError(message) {
  authError.textContent = message;

function friendlyAuthError(error) {
  const code = error && error.code || '';
  if (code === 'auth/operation-not-allowed') return 'Email/Password sign-in is disabled. Enable it in Firebase Console → Authentication → Sign-in method.';
  if (code === 'auth/unauthorized-domain') return 'This preview domain is not authorized. Add its host under Firebase Console → Authentication → Settings → Authorized domains, or test on localhost.';
  if (code === 'auth/invalid-api-key' || code === 'auth/api-key-not-valid.-please-pass-a-valid-api-key.') return 'The Firebase Web API key in .env.local is missing or invalid.';
  if (code === 'auth/email-already-in-use') return 'That email already has a Firebase account. Use Sign in instead.';
  if (code === 'auth/weak-password') return 'Use a password with at least six characters.';
  if (code === 'auth/invalid-credential' || code === 'auth/wrong-password' || code === 'auth/user-not-found') return 'Email or password is incorrect.';
  return error && error.message ? error.message : 'Firebase sign-in could not be completed.';
}

# MotorPH MS2 — browser payroll foundation

An original browser-based prototype with an HTML/CSS interface and Java 11 backend. Employee and attendance data are synthetic. Payroll remains gated until the supplied course materials define complete calculation rules and expected-value examples.

## Run locally

Requires JDK 11+, Node.js 20.19+ (or a current supported Node release), and npm.

```sh
npm install
./run.sh
```

Then open <http://localhost:8080>. `run.sh` builds the Vite frontend and serves it from the Java server. Set `PORT` to choose a different HTTP port.

For development with Vite hot reload, use two terminals:

```sh
# terminal 1: Java backend
./run-api.sh

# terminal 2: frontend
npm run dev
```

Open <http://localhost:5173>. Vite proxies `/api` calls to the Java service. Set `HOST=127.0.0.1` for the Java backend when Vite is proxying it locally.

Run Java domain checks:

```sh
./test.sh
```

The app uses a small vendored Gson JAR for the Java Firestore REST adapter; its license is recorded in `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` and `third_party/licenses/`.

## Firebase development sandbox

- `.env.local` contains the Firebase **Web** app config used by the browser SDK; `.gitignore` lists this file. The user-supplied Web API key for `motorph-jd` is installed assistant-side. The user does not need to edit `.env.local`.
- The Web API key is a public client identifier, not a server credential. Do not add a service-account key or Admin SDK credentials.
- Authentication uses Email/Password and in-memory browser persistence. Live sign-up/password sign-in and the browser sign-in flow passed with disposable synthetic accounts, which were deleted. Do not use real staff accounts or data.
- Firestore requests are made by the Java backend through the REST API, forwarding the signed-in user's Firebase ID token. Firestore Security Rules authorize those requests; no privileged server identity bypasses the rules.
- The app uses only `users/{uid}/demoEmployees` and `users/{uid}/demoAttendance`. A user can access only their own sandbox. The opt-in “Add synthetic demo data” action writes fictional records; it does not modify or import real employee data.
- The user reports publishing `docs/firestore.rules`. Live requests confirmed that the app can seed/read its own synthetic employee and attendance records while cross-user paths, payroll paths, and extra salary fields remain denied. These are **development-only** rules, not production role/HR policy.
- If Firebase is not configured locally, the app uses the in-memory synthetic fixture. No Firebase writes are made in that mode.
- `measurementId` / Firebase Analytics is not used.
- Browser auth is verified on `localhost`. The current Arena preview host is `8080-is3s38ic4lxn7e4e77g8b.e2b.app`; its authorized-domain status could not be tested from the sandbox because Arena's traffic-access token is injected only in the user preview session. If the preview reports `auth/unauthorized-domain`, add that exact host under Firebase Console → Authentication → Settings → Authorized domains.

See `docs/firebase-setup-guide.md` for the console checkpoint and `docs/firestore.rules` for the development rules.

## What works

- Overview, employee directory, employee detail dialog, read-only attendance, and a payroll rules gate. Employee details open from a native keyboard-operable button without overriding table semantics; employee and attendance result counts announce asynchronous updates politely to screen readers.
- Java `EmployeeService` and `AttendanceService` with in-memory local fixtures; in Firebase mode the same Java services use user-scoped Firestore REST stores.
- Server-side employee search/detail and inclusive raw-attendance date filtering for a selected employee. The date fields default to that employee's earliest/latest available records, following the earlier MO-IT108 Requirements Analysis; the user can narrow the range. This is not a payroll-period calendar. No paid hours, deductions, or pay are calculated.
- Firebase email/password sign-in and development-account creation UI; the UI stays behind the sign-in gate when Firebase config is complete.
- `/api/health`, employee list/search/detail, attendance query, and opt-in demo seed endpoint.
- `./test.sh`: 13 employee-domain, 16 attendance-domain, 15 Firestore REST adapter checks, and 23 HTTP integration checks (**67 total**; automated Firebase adapter/integration tests use local endpoints). Live synthetic API tests verified seed/list/detail/raw attendance, repeat-seed idempotency, input errors, and denied cross-user/payroll/extra-salary access. Headless Chromium verified real Firebase sign-in, employee search/detail, raw attendance date filtering, the payroll gate, no console/page errors, and responsive views from 320–1024 px. All temporary Auth users and Firestore documents were deleted.

## Not implemented / important limits

- No production hosting, HR authorization roles, admin controls, audit trail, backup, or production security review. The built-in JDK HTTP server is a learning prototype, not a hardened public service.
- No live employee, attendance, or payroll information. Do not use this prototype for payroll processing.
- No work-hour derivation algorithm, payroll formulas, rates, pay-period calendar, payslips, or payroll calculations. The supplied material does not define a complete attendance algorithm or exact semi-monthly cut-offs, so the program will not infer them.
- Employee edits, attendance imports, and approved source-system integration are not implemented.

## Source and attribution

`docs/source-grounding-and-open-rules.md` records supplied-source facts, scope boundaries, and unresolved ambiguities. `docs/legacy-mo-it108-traceability.md` maps the user's earlier MotorPH requirements/design documents to the current prototype and explains the feature-parity estimate. `docs/peer-parity-roadmap.md` lists the remaining phases and acceptance gates to reach broad peer-level feature parity. The restrained title stripe adapts a small MIT-licensed `system.css` motif; exact attribution and licenses are listed in `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`.
# Roadmap to full peer-level MotorPH feature parity

**How to read “100%”:** the nine submitted folders do not share one feature set, so there is no single objective peer-completion percentage. This roadmap uses the richest relevant comparison: the payroll/attendance/leave workflows in the stronger MO-IT110-style submissions (especially folders 6 and 9), plus the user's earlier MO-IT108 Requirements Analysis and System Design. It is a feature-completion target, not a grade.

**Current user constraints remain in force:** synthetic data only; no payroll calculations until authoritative rules are provided; no guessed pay-period calendar; no Firebase Console changes by the assistant. The legacy Terminal Assessment proposal contains template placeholders and is not treated as a detailed specification. `The Code.pdf` is unrelated C++ inventory work and is excluded.

## Already done — current foundation

- Firebase Email/Password Auth and user-scoped Firestore access live-tested with synthetic accounts.
- Employee list, search, and detail selection work; data remains fictional and scoped to the signed-in sandbox.
- Raw attendance records are selectable by employee and inclusive date range; default range spans that employee's earliest/latest available records, following the older Requirements Analysis.
- Payroll stays gated. The default attendance range is not a pay period.
- 67 Java checks, production build, live API checks, browser E2E, and responsive checks pass.

## Ordered tasks to reach the broader target

### 1. Freeze a traceable acceptance baseline

- Map the active MO-IT110 rubric to the legacy MO-IT108 requirement groups and only the peer features we actually intend to match.
- Mark every requirement as required, optional, or excluded; record source, owner, and acceptance example.
- Reconcile conflicting legacy sources (for example, old role/2FA workflows vs the current Firebase sandbox).
- Preserve the current boundary: synthetic records only; no payroll or attendance-derived pay output until rules are approved.

**Done when:** every target feature has a source and observable pass/fail acceptance criterion; proposals and template text are not presented as approved policy.

### 2. Complete the employee and organization foundation

- Define the approved synthetic employee, department/position/branch, schedule, and supervisor models.
- Add HR-style create/update/deactivate/search workflows if they are part of the target; record changes and validate required fields.
- Keep government identifiers and real personal data out of the demo sandbox.
- Decide how users map to employees and teams before moving beyond per-user isolated demo data.

**Done when:** synthetic employee lifecycle operations are validated, auditable, and limited by the approved role policy.

### 3. Finish attendance capture and summaries

- Add time-in/time-out and attendance correction flows only if required; distinguish remote/offsite from verified onsite clocking if matching the legacy design.
- Implement QR-based onsite verification only if it is an acceptance requirement; define expiry, replay protection, and device flow.
- Add schedule/day-type, grace-period, present/absent/tardy, leave, overtime, and undertime summaries only after each rule is specified.
- Define missing/duplicate punches, breaks, overnight shifts, time zone, rounding, corrections, and date boundaries.
- Keep user-selected dates inclusive and the earliest/latest default; never substitute an assumed payroll cutoff.

**Gate:** attendance classifications and hour totals require written rules and an approved worked example. Until then, keep raw entries only.

**Done when:** approved test cases cover normal, late, absent, leave, holiday/rest day, missing punch, duplicate, correction, and boundary scenarios.

### 4. Add leave management

- Define synthetic leave types, balances/accrual, eligibility, request/cancel states, and approval roles.
- Build employee requests, supervisor decisions, balance history, and employee/team leave calendars.
- Make approvals auditable and ensure only approved leave affects any later payroll input.

**Gate:** leave accrual, carry-over, monetization, and payroll treatment need an authoritative policy.

**Done when:** request, approve/reject/cancel, balance update, calendar, and audit tests pass.

### 5. Add ticketing and dispute workflows

- Define ticket types, fields, routing, queue position, statuses, cancellation rules, and resolution history.
- Implement overtime, leave, timesheet, payroll-dispute, HR/general inquiry, and technical-support forms only for in-scope roles.
- Notify requestors and handlers, and retain an audit trail.

**Done when:** each included ticket type has tested routing, authorization, state changes, and user-visible status.

### 6. Add team and supervisor workflows

- Define employee-to-team/branch membership and the supervisor's permitted scope.
- Build rosters, availability, schedule viewing/editing, pending-request review, and timesheet correction workflow.
- Record reasons and before/after values for every correction; notify affected employees.

**Done when:** supervisor actions are limited to assigned teams and are fully auditable.

### 7. Add HR onboarding/offboarding and employee administration

- Add synthetic onboarding, profile/branch/position changes, deactivation, clearance queues, and search/update screens if required.
- Define effective dates and the effect of mid-cycle changes without guessing payroll behavior.
- Ensure inactive accounts lose access according to an approved policy.

**Done when:** employee lifecycle changes are validated, role-limited, and tested against audit/history requirements.

### 8. Implement the Java payroll engine — currently blocked

- Obtain authoritative rules for pay-cycle boundaries, salary conversion, regular/OT/PTO/holiday/rest-day/undertime treatment, incentives, deductions, statutory contributions, tax, effective dates, and rounding.
- Obtain independent worked expected-value cases, including edge cases; reconcile any conflicting legacy or peer formulas.
- Implement versioned Java domain/calculation services using exact decimal arithmetic; keep formulas out of browser code and Firebase adapters.
- Test each rule independently, then test combined payroll results and reproducibility.

**Hard gate:** the old documents name payroll components and snapshot fields but do not provide enough arithmetic, current values, or exact cutoffs to calculate correctly. Do not activate this task's outputs until those inputs exist and the user's “keep calculations disabled” instruction is explicitly lifted.

**Done when:** independent golden cases match every component and a repeat run uses the same saved rule version.

### 9. Add payroll supervision, adjustments, and approval

- Define rate/incentive/deduction adjustment scope (individual/team/branch/global), approvers, separation of duties, and effective dates.
- Build review/approve/reject flows with immutable audit events and controlled payroll reruns/corrections.
- Generate payroll summaries only from approved, versioned inputs.

**Gate:** depends on approved payroll formulas, values, roles, and correction policy.

### 10. Add payslips, reports, and distribution

- Define the required payslip fields and privacy rules.
- Generate the required output format, store a stable result reference, and verify read-back.
- Add payroll reports/monthly summaries only if required.
- Add email delivery and retry/status tracking only if required and a safe delivery service is configured.

**Gate:** no payslip values until the calculation engine is approved.

### 11. Replace demo isolation with approved identity, RBAC, and PII controls

- Define account-to-employee mapping, roles, team/branch scopes, session policy, account recovery, and 2FA requirements.
- Implement least-privilege authorization in backend and Firebase Rules; do not rely on UI hiding.
- If the older two-person PII approval requirement is adopted, implement explicit requests, two distinct authorized approvals, audit, and emergency policy.
- Add access logging, abuse limits, and tests for own/team/branch/unauthorized access.

**Done when:** an authorization matrix is implemented and every allow/deny path is covered by live or rules-emulator tests.

### 12. Production hosting and operational safety

- Replace the learning JDK server with an appropriately hardened deployment architecture; configure a stable domain, HTTPS, allowed origins, protected configuration, and environment-specific Firebase settings.
- Add monitoring, structured error handling, rate/abuse controls, backup/restore, and data-retention procedures.
- Load-test the approved scale target; the legacy document mentions 100 concurrent employee records, but the active target must be confirmed before treating that as a release criterion.
- Complete a security/privacy review before any real employee or payroll data is used.

**Done when:** deployment, recovery, performance, and security acceptance tests pass outside the development sandbox.

### 13. Final regression and submission evidence

- Run domain/unit, API integration, Firestore rules, browser E2E, accessibility/keyboard, mobile/tablet, and failure-path tests.
- Compare outputs to approved source examples, not just another team's implementation.
- Prepare requirement-to-code traceability, architecture/design artifacts, test results, and demo steps without exposing secrets or real data.

**Done when:** every required acceptance item is evidenced and no unapproved feature or calculation is enabled.

## Completion rule

Do not mark “100%” until all tasks selected in Step 1 have passed their acceptance criteria. Tasks 3–10 are broader than current Tasks 1–3; task 8 and all downstream payroll outputs remain blocked by missing rules and the user's current no-calculation constraint. The current prototype is a strong foundation, not yet a complete payroll system.

## Percent estimate: two different denominators

There is no single valid percentage “against the submitted folders”: those projects have different feature sets, tech stacks, and course scopes, and several are near-duplicates. The ranges below are **feature-completeness estimates, not a grade or quality score**.

- **Agreed current Tasks 1–3 scope: about 85–90%.** Task 1's live Firebase proof is complete. Task 2's browser sign-in and employee selection are verified on localhost, with the exact Arena preview-origin authorization still unverified. Task 3's employee/date inputs and raw-record path are complete; derived attendance-hour totals remain gated because their algorithm and test oracle are missing and payroll calculations must stay disabled.
- **Full legacy MO-IT108 functional breadth: about 20–30%.** The prototype has a real sign-in/data foundation, a read-only synthetic employee directory, and part of the attendance-view path. Clocking, leave, tickets, team/HR workflows, payroll calculations, payslips, reports, RBAC/2FA, and production operations are not implemented.
- **Compared with the more complete numbered submissions (especially folders 6 and 9): roughly 25–35% of end-to-end feature breadth.** This prototype is stronger in live Firebase Auth/Firestore integration, browser accessibility/responsiveness, and current test evidence; those reference projects include payroll engines/results and broader workflows that this app deliberately does not yet have. Compared with the smallest procedural/demo submissions, the comparison can reverse because this project already has a live web/data foundation.

The largest gap to “parity” is not another Firebase feature: it is the **unbuilt payroll/business workflow** (validated attendance summaries, approved pay rules, payroll results/payslips, and applicable roles). Do not close that gap by importing unverified formulas from another submission.

workflow-demo.test.js

import test from 'node:test';
import assert from 'node:assert/strict';

const moduleOrError = await import('../../web/workflow-demo.js').catch(error => ({ importError: error }));
const employees = [
  { id: 'DEMO-001', name: 'Mara Rivera' },
  { id: 'DEMO-002', name: 'Eli Santos' }
];

function api() {
  assert.ok(!moduleOrError.importError, 'workflow demo module should load');
  for (const name of ['createWorkflowState', 'submitLeaveRequest', 'cancelLeaveRequest', 'submitTicket', 'cancelTicket']) {
    assert.equal(typeof moduleOrError[name], 'function', `${name} should be exported`);
  }
  return moduleOrError;
}

test('creates a pending synthetic leave request without mutating prior state', () => {
  const { createWorkflowState, submitLeaveRequest } = api();
  const initial = createWorkflowState();
  const result = submitLeaveRequest(initial, {
    employeeId: 'DEMO-001', leaveType: 'Vacation', startDate: '2026-11-10', endDate: '2026-11-11', note: 'Fictional request'
  }, employees, '2026-11-03');

  assert.equal(initial.leaveRequests.length, 0);
  assert.equal(result.state.leaveRequests.length, 1);
  assert.equal(result.request.employeeName, 'Mara Rivera');
  assert.equal(result.request.status, 'Pending review');
  assert.equal(result.request.startDate, '2026-11-10');
});

test('rejects reversed or impossible leave dates', () => {
  const { createWorkflowState, submitLeaveRequest } = api();
  const initial = createWorkflowState();
  assert.throws(() => submitLeaveRequest(initial, {
    employeeId: 'DEMO-001', leaveType: 'Vacation', startDate: '2026-11-12', endDate: '2026-11-11', note: ''
  }, employees), /start date/i);
  assert.throws(() => submitLeaveRequest(initial, {
    employeeId: 'DEMO-001', leaveType: 'Vacation', startDate: '2026-02-30', endDate: '2026-03-01', note: ''
  }, employees), /valid date/i);
});

test('cancels only the requesting employee’s pending leave request', () => {
  const { createWorkflowState, submitLeaveRequest, cancelLeaveRequest } = api();
  const initial = createWorkflowState();
  const { state, request } = submitLeaveRequest(initial, {
    employeeId: 'DEMO-001', leaveType: 'Medical', startDate: '2026-11-12', endDate: '2026-11-12', note: ''
  }, employees, '2026-11-03');

  assert.throws(() => cancelLeaveRequest(state, request.id, 'DEMO-002'), /own request/i);
  const cancelled = cancelLeaveRequest(state, request.id, 'DEMO-001');
  assert.equal(state.leaveRequests[0].status, 'Pending review');
  assert.equal(cancelled.leaveRequests[0].status, 'Cancelled');
  assert.throws(() => cancelLeaveRequest(cancelled, request.id, 'DEMO-001'), /pending/i);
});

test('rejects unknown employees, leave types, and overlong notes', () => {
  const { createWorkflowState, submitLeaveRequest } = api();
  const state = createWorkflowState();
  const common = { leaveType: 'Vacation', startDate: '2026-11-10', endDate: '2026-11-10', note: '' };
  assert.throws(() => submitLeaveRequest(state, { ...common, employeeId: 'REAL-EMPLOYEE' }, employees), /synthetic demo directory/i);
  assert.throws(() => submitLeaveRequest(state, { ...common, employeeId: 'DEMO-001', leaveType: 'Unapproved type' }, employees), /leave type/i);
  assert.throws(() => submitLeaveRequest(state, { ...common, employeeId: 'DEMO-001', note: 'x'.repeat(241) }, employees), /240 characters/i);
});

test('routes each synthetic ticket type to its documented queue label', () => {
  const { createWorkflowState, submitTicket } = api();
  const expected = {
    'Overtime request': 'Team Lead',
    'Leave request': 'Team Lead',
    'Timesheet correction': 'Team Lead',
    'Payroll inquiry': 'Payroll Staff',
    'HR inquiry': 'HR',
    'Technical support': 'IT Admin'
  };
  Object.entries(expected).forEach(([ticketType, queue]) => {
    const result = submitTicket(createWorkflowState(), {
      employeeId: 'DEMO-002', ticketType, summary: 'Review a fictional record'
    }, employees, '2026-11-03');
    assert.equal(result.ticket.employeeName, 'Eli Santos');
    assert.equal(result.ticket.queue, queue);
    assert.equal(result.ticket.status, 'Open');
  });
});

test('rejects invalid ticket types or empty messages', () => {
  const { createWorkflowState, submitTicket } = api();
  const state = createWorkflowState();
  assert.throws(() => submitTicket(state, {
    employeeId: 'DEMO-001', ticketType: 'Payroll payout', summary: 'Do a calculation'
  }, employees), /ticket type/i);
  assert.throws(() => submitTicket(state, {
    employeeId: 'DEMO-001', ticketType: 'HR inquiry', summary: '   '
  }, employees), /short message/i);
  assert.throws(() => submitTicket(state, {
    employeeId: 'DEMO-001', ticketType: 'HR inquiry', summary: 'x'.repeat(241)
  }, employees), /240 characters/i);
});

test('prevents another employee cancelling a ticket and permits own open-ticket cancellation', () => {
  const { createWorkflowState, submitTicket, cancelTicket } = api();
  const initial = createWorkflowState();
  const { state, ticket } = submitTicket(initial, {
    employeeId: 'DEMO-001', ticketType: 'HR inquiry', summary: 'Synthetic test'
  }, employees, '2026-11-03');
  assert.throws(() => cancelTicket(state, ticket.id, 'DEMO-002'), /own ticket/i);
  const cancelled = cancelTicket(state, ticket.id, 'DEMO-001');
  assert.equal(state.tickets[0].status, 'Open');
  assert.equal(cancelled.tickets[0].status, 'Cancelled');
  assert.throws(() => cancelTicket(cancelled, ticket.id, 'DEMO-001'), /open ticket/i);
});

package ph.motorph.web;

import java.util.Collections;
import java.util.HashMap;
import java.util.Map;
import java.util.OptionalInt;

/** Synthetic employee-to-schedule mapping; replace with the approved source later. */
public final class InMemoryEmployeeScheduleStore implements EmployeeScheduleStore {
    private final Map<String, Integer> scheduleByEmployee;

    public InMemoryEmployeeScheduleStore() {
        Map<String, Integer> values = new HashMap<>();
        values.put("DEMO-001", 101);
        values.put("DEMO-002", 102);
        values.put("DEMO-003", 103);
        scheduleByEmployee = Collections.unmodifiableMap(values);
    }

    @Override
    public OptionalInt findScheduleIdForEmployee(String employeeId) {
        Integer scheduleId = employeeId == null ? null : scheduleByEmployee.get(employeeId);
        return scheduleId == null ? OptionalInt.empty() : OptionalInt.of(scheduleId);
    }
}

# Roadmap to full peer-level MotorPH feature parity

**How to read “100%”:** the nine submitted folders do not share one feature set, so there is no single objective peer-completion percentage. This roadmap uses the richest relevant comparison: the payroll/attendance/leave workflows in the stronger MO-IT110-style submissions (especially folders 6 and 9), plus the user's earlier MO-IT108 Requirements Analysis and System Design. It is a feature-completion target, not a grade.

**Current user constraints remain in force:** synthetic data only; no payroll calculations until authoritative rules are provided; no guessed pay-period calendar; no Firebase Console changes by the assistant. The legacy Terminal Assessment proposal contains template placeholders and is not treated as a detailed specification. `The Code.pdf` is unrelated C++ inventory work and is excluded.

## Already done — current foundation

- Firebase Email/Password Auth and user-scoped Firestore access live-tested with synthetic accounts.
- Employee list, search, and detail selection work; data remains fictional and scoped to the signed-in sandbox.
- Raw attendance records are selectable by employee and inclusive date range; default range spans that employee's earliest/latest available records, following the older Requirements Analysis.
- Payroll stays gated. The default attendance range is not a pay period.
- Browser-only leave request and ticket demonstrations now validate inputs, show statuses, and allow cancellation. They hold fictional data in memory only and notify no reviewer; they do not satisfy the persistent/authorized workflow criteria below.
- Team roster and HR desk show read-only synthetic directory views; team membership, HR lifecycle actions, and roles remain undefined.
- Verification: 7 JavaScript workflow-domain tests, 67 Java checks, and the production build pass. Earlier foundation browser E2E/responsive checks passed. A new browser E2E for the workflow UI is still pending because the sandbox Chromium binary cannot launch without `libnspr4.so`.

## Ordered tasks to reach the broader target

### 1. Freeze a traceable acceptance baseline

- Map the active MO-IT110 rubric to the legacy MO-IT108 requirement groups and only the peer features we actually intend to match.
- Mark every requirement as required, optional, or excluded; record source, owner, and acceptance example.
- Reconcile conflicting legacy sources (for example, old role/2FA workflows vs the current Firebase sandbox).
- Preserve the current boundary: synthetic records only; no payroll or attendance-derived pay output until rules are approved.

**Done when:** every target feature has a source and observable pass/fail acceptance criterion; proposals and template text are not presented as approved policy.

### 2. Complete the employee and organization foundation

- Define the approved synthetic employee, department/position/branch, schedule, and supervisor models.
- Add HR-style create/update/deactivate/search workflows if they are part of the target; record changes and validate required fields.
- Keep government identifiers and real personal data out of the demo sandbox.
- Decide how users map to employees and teams before moving beyond per-user isolated demo data.

**Done when:** synthetic employee lifecycle operations are validated, auditable, and limited by the approved role policy.

### 3. Finish attendance capture and summaries

- Add time-in/time-out and attendance correction flows only if required; distinguish remote/offsite from verified onsite clocking if matching the legacy design.
- Implement QR-based onsite verification only if it is an acceptance requirement; define expiry, replay protection, and device flow.
- Add schedule/day-type, grace-period, present/absent/tardy, leave, overtime, and undertime summaries only after each rule is specified.
- Define missing/duplicate punches, breaks, overnight shifts, time zone, rounding, corrections, and date boundaries.
- Keep user-selected dates inclusive and the earliest/latest default; never substitute an assumed payroll cutoff.

**Gate:** attendance classifications and hour totals require written rules and an approved worked example. Until then, keep raw entries only.

**Done when:** approved test cases cover normal, late, absent, leave, holiday/rest day, missing punch, duplicate, correction, and boundary scenarios.

### 4. Add leave management

- Define synthetic leave types, balances/accrual, eligibility, request/cancel states, and approval roles.
- Build employee requests, supervisor decisions, balance history, and employee/team leave calendars.
- Make approvals auditable and ensure only approved leave affects any later payroll input.

**Gate:** leave accrual, carry-over, monetization, and payroll treatment need an authoritative policy.

**Done when:** request, approve/reject/cancel, balance update, calendar, and audit tests pass.

### 5. Add ticketing and dispute workflows

- Define ticket types, fields, routing, queue position, statuses, cancellation rules, and resolution history.
- Implement overtime, leave, timesheet, payroll-dispute, HR/general inquiry, and technical-support forms only for in-scope roles.
- Notify requestors and handlers, and retain an audit trail.

**Done when:** each included ticket type has tested routing, authorization, state changes, and user-visible status.

### 6. Add team and supervisor workflows

- Define employee-to-team/branch membership and the supervisor's permitted scope.
- Build rosters, availability, schedule viewing/editing, pending-request review, and timesheet correction workflow.
- Record reasons and before/after values for every correction; notify affected employees.

**Done when:** supervisor actions are limited to assigned teams and are fully auditable.

### 7. Add HR onboarding/offboarding and employee administration

- Add synthetic onboarding, profile/branch/position changes, deactivation, clearance queues, and search/update screens if required.
- Define effective dates and the effect of mid-cycle changes without guessing payroll behavior.
- Ensure inactive accounts lose access according to an approved policy.

**Done when:** employee lifecycle changes are validated, role-limited, and tested against audit/history requirements.

### 8. Implement the Java payroll engine — currently blocked

- Obtain authoritative rules for pay-cycle boundaries, salary conversion, regular/OT/PTO/holiday/rest-day/undertime treatment, incentives, deductions, statutory contributions, tax, effective dates, and rounding.
- Obtain independent worked expected-value cases, including edge cases; reconcile any conflicting legacy or peer formulas.
- Implement versioned Java domain/calculation services using exact decimal arithmetic; keep formulas out of browser code and Firebase adapters.
- Test each rule independently, then test combined payroll results and reproducibility.

**Hard gate:** the old documents name payroll components and snapshot fields but do not provide enough arithmetic, current values, or exact cutoffs to calculate correctly. Do not activate this task's outputs until those inputs exist and the user's “keep calculations disabled” instruction is explicitly lifted.

**Done when:** independent golden cases match every component and a repeat run uses the same saved rule version.

### 9. Add payroll supervision, adjustments, and approval

- Define rate/incentive/deduction adjustment scope (individual/team/branch/global), approvers, separation of duties, and effective dates.
- Build review/approve/reject flows with immutable audit events and controlled payroll reruns/corrections.
- Generate payroll summaries only from approved, versioned inputs.

**Gate:** depends on approved payroll formulas, values, roles, and correction policy.

### 10. Add payslips, reports, and distribution

- Define the required payslip fields and privacy rules.
- Generate the required output format, store a stable result reference, and verify read-back.
- Add payroll reports/monthly summaries only if required.
- Add email delivery and retry/status tracking only if required and a safe delivery service is configured.

**Gate:** no payslip values until the calculation engine is approved.

### 11. Replace demo isolation with approved identity, RBAC, and PII controls

- Define account-to-employee mapping, roles, team/branch scopes, session policy, account recovery, and 2FA requirements.
- Implement least-privilege authorization in backend and Firebase Rules; do not rely on UI hiding.
- If the older two-person PII approval requirement is adopted, implement explicit requests, two distinct authorized approvals, audit, and emergency policy.
- Add access logging, abuse limits, and tests for own/team/branch/unauthorized access.

**Done when:** an authorization matrix is implemented and every allow/deny path is covered by live or rules-emulator tests.

### 12. Production hosting and operational safety

- Replace the learning JDK server with an appropriately hardened deployment architecture; configure a stable domain, HTTPS, allowed origins, protected configuration, and environment-specific Firebase settings.
- Add monitoring, structured error handling, rate/abuse controls, backup/restore, and data-retention procedures.
- Load-test the approved scale target; the legacy document mentions 100 concurrent employee records, but the active target must be confirmed before treating that as a release criterion.
- Complete a security/privacy review before any real employee or payroll data is used.

**Done when:** deployment, recovery, performance, and security acceptance tests pass outside the development sandbox.

### 13. Final regression and submission evidence
