    private void handleAttendance(HttpExchange exchange) throws IOException {
        if (!"GET".equals(exchange.getRequestMethod())) {
            sendJson(exchange, 405, "{\"error\":\"Method not allowed\"}");
            return;
        }
        String employeeId = queryParameter(exchange.getRequestURI().getRawQuery(), "employeeId");
        if (employeeId == null || employeeId.trim().isEmpty()) {
            sendJson(exchange, 400, "{\"error\":\"employeeId is required\"}");
            return;
        }
        try {
            RequestServices services = servicesFor(exchange);
            LocalDate from = parseOptionalDate(queryParameter(exchange.getRequestURI().getRawQuery(), "from"));
            LocalDate to = parseOptionalDate(queryParameter(exchange.getRequestURI().getRawQuery(), "to"));
            AttendanceService attendanceService = new AttendanceService(services.employeeService,
                localScheduleStore, services.attendanceStore);
            List<AttendanceRecord> records = attendanceService.findForEmployee(employeeId, from, to);
            sendJson(exchange, 200, attendanceToJson(records));
        } catch (DateTimeParseException ex) {
            sendJson(exchange, 400, "{\"error\":\"Dates must use YYYY-MM-DD\"}");
        } catch (IllegalArgumentException ex) {
            sendJson(exchange, 400, "{\"error\":\"" + escapeJson(ex.getMessage()) + "\"}");
        } catch (java.util.NoSuchElementException ex) {
            sendJson(exchange, 404, "{\"error\":\"Employee not found\"}");
        } catch (FirestoreException ex) {
            sendApiError(exchange, ex);
        }
    }

    private void handleWorkflows(HttpExchange exchange) throws IOException {

                return;
            }

package ph.motorph.web;

import java.util.List;
import java.util.Locale;
import java.util.Optional;
import java.util.UUID;
import java.util.NoSuchElementException;
import java.util.stream.Collectors;

/** Employee use cases, separated from HTTP handling and the storage implementation. */
public final class EmployeeService {
    private final EmployeeStore store;

    public EmployeeService(EmployeeStore store) {
        if (store == null) throw new IllegalArgumentException("store must not be null");
        this.store = store;
    }

    public List<Employee> listEmployees() {
        return store.findAll();
    }

    public Optional<Employee> findEmployee(String id) {
        return store.findById(id == null ? null : id.trim());
    }

    /** Creates a fictional directory record inside the current owner's sandbox only. */
    public Employee createEmployee(String name, String department, String role, String location, String status) {
        MutableEmployeeStore mutable = mutableStore();
        Employee employee = validatedEmployee("DEMO-" + UUID.randomUUID().toString().replace("-", "")
            .substring(0, 12).toUpperCase(Locale.ROOT), name, department, role, location, status);
        return mutable.create(employee);
    }

    /** Updates only fields present in the synthetic directory model; no payroll/PII fields exist here. */
    public Employee updateEmployee(String id, String name, String department, String role, String location, String status) {
        String safeId = id == null ? "" : id.trim();
        if (!safeId.matches("DEMO-(?:[0-9]{3}|[A-F0-9]{12})")) throw new IllegalArgumentException("Employee ID is invalid.");
        if (!findEmployee(safeId).isPresent()) throw new NoSuchElementException("Employee not found.");
        return mutableStore().update(validatedEmployee(safeId, name, department, role, location, status));
    }

    private MutableEmployeeStore mutableStore() {
        if (!(store instanceof MutableEmployeeStore)) throw new IllegalStateException("This employee store is read-only.");
        return (MutableEmployeeStore) store;
    }

    private static Employee validatedEmployee(String id, String name, String department,
            String role, String location, String status) {
        return new Employee(id, requiredDirectoryText(name, "Name"), requiredDirectoryText(department, "Department"),
            requiredDirectoryText(role, "Role"), requiredDirectoryText(location, "Location"), validStatus(status));
    }

    private static String requiredDirectoryText(String value, String field) {
        String text = value == null ? "" : value.trim();
        if (text.isEmpty()) throw new IllegalArgumentException(field + " is required.");
        if (text.length() > 100) throw new IllegalArgumentException(field + " must be 100 characters or fewer.");
        return text;
    }

    private static String validStatus(String value) {
        String status = value == null ? "" : value.trim();
        if (!"Active".equals(status) && !"On leave".equals(status)) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Status must be Active or On leave.");
        }
        return status;
    }

    /** Empty query returns all; search is case-insensitive across the displayed fields. */
    public List<Employee> searchEmployees(String query) {
        if (query == null || query.trim().isEmpty()) return store.findAll();
        String normalized = query.trim().toLowerCase(Locale.ROOT);
        return store.findAll().stream()
            .filter(employee -> searchableText(employee).contains(normalized))
            .collect(Collectors.toList());
    }

    private String searchableText(Employee employee) {
        return (employee.getId() + " " + employee.getName() + " " + employee.getDepartment() + " "
            + employee.getRole() + " " + employee.getLocation() + " " + employee.getStatus())
            .toLowerCase(Locale.ROOT);
    }
}
package ph.motorph.web;

import java.util.List;

/** Storage boundary for raw attendance entries. */
public interface AttendanceStore {
    List<AttendanceRecord> findByScheduleId(int scheduleId);
}
package ph.motorph.web;

import com.google.gson.JsonElement;
import com.google.gson.JsonObject;

import java.time.LocalDate;
import java.time.LocalTime;
import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.stream.Collectors;

/** User-scoped synthetic attendance records read through Firestore REST. */
public final class FirestoreAttendanceStore implements AttendanceStore {
    private final FirestoreRestClient client;

    public FirestoreAttendanceStore(FirestoreRestClient client) {
        if (client == null) throw new IllegalArgumentException("client must not be null");
        this.client = client;
    }

    @Override
    public List<AttendanceRecord> findByScheduleId(int scheduleId) {
        List<AttendanceRecord> records = new ArrayList<>();
        for (JsonObject document : client.listDocuments(client.userCollection("demoAttendance"))) {
            records.add(fromDocument(document));
        }
        return records.stream().filter(record -> record.getScheduleId() == scheduleId).collect(Collectors.toList());
    }

    private static AttendanceRecord fromDocument(JsonObject document) {
        JsonObject fields = document.has("fields") ? document.getAsJsonObject("fields") : new JsonObject();
        return new AttendanceRecord(
            integerValue(fields, "attendanceId"), integerValue(fields, "scheduleId"),
            LocalDate.parse(stringValue(fields, "date")), LocalTime.parse(stringValue(fields, "timeIn")),
            LocalTime.parse(stringValue(fields, "timeOut")), stringValue(fields, "dayType"));
    }

    private static int integerValue(JsonObject fields, String name) {
        JsonElement element = fields.get(name);
        if (element == null || !element.isJsonObject()) return 0;
        JsonElement value = element.getAsJsonObject().get("integerValue");
        return value == null || value.isJsonNull() ? 0 : Integer.parseInt(value.getAsString());
    }

    private static String stringValue(JsonObject fields, String name) {
        return FirestoreEmployeeStore.stringValue(fields, name);
    }
}

package ph.motorph.web;

import java.time.LocalDate;
import java.time.LocalTime;
import java.util.HashSet;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.NoSuchElementException;
import java.util.Set;

public final class AttendanceServiceTest {
    private int checks;

    public static void main(String[] args) {
        new AttendanceServiceTest().run();
    }

    private void run() {
        EmployeeService employees = new EmployeeService(new InMemoryEmployeeStore());
        AttendanceService service = new AttendanceService(employees,
            new InMemoryEmployeeScheduleStore(), new InMemoryAttendanceStore());

        List<AttendanceRecord> all = service.findForEmployee("DEMO-001", null, null);
        equal(3, all.size(), "employee gets only their synthetic schedule entries");
        equal(101, all.get(0).getScheduleId(), "attendance is linked by schedule ID");
        equal("2026-10-01", all.get(0).getDate().toString(), "date is preserved without deriving hours");

        List<AttendanceRecord> oneDay = service.findForEmployee("DEMO-001",
            LocalDate.parse("2026-10-02"), LocalDate.parse("2026-10-02"));
        equal(1, oneDay.size(), "date filtering is inclusive at both ends");
        equal(5002, oneDay.get(0).getAttendanceId(), "date filter returns the right entry");

        equal(0, service.findForEmployee("DEMO-002", LocalDate.parse("2026-10-10"), null).size(),
            "open-ended lower date filter works");
        equal(1, service.findForEmployee("DEMO-003", null, LocalDate.parse("2026-10-02")).size(),
            "open-ended upper date filter works");
        equal(0, service.findForEmployee("DEMO-001", LocalDate.parse("2026-11-01"), null).size(),
            "no matches returns an empty list");

        Set<String> scheduleDates = new HashSet<>();
        for (AttendanceRecord record : new InMemoryAttendanceStore().findByScheduleId(101)) {
            check(scheduleDates.add(record.getScheduleId() + ":" + record.getDate()),
                "synthetic fixture respects schedule/date uniqueness");
        }

        expectIllegalArgument(() -> service.findForEmployee("DEMO-001",
            LocalDate.parse("2026-10-15"), LocalDate.parse("2026-10-01")), "from-after-to is rejected");
        expectNoSuchElement(() -> service.findForEmployee("UNKNOWN", null, null), "unknown employee is rejected");
        expectIllegalArgument(() -> new AttendanceRecord(0, 101, LocalDate.parse("2026-10-01"),
            LocalTime.of(8, 0), LocalTime.of(17, 0), "DEMO"), "attendance ID must be positive");
        expectIllegalArgument(() -> new AttendanceRecord(1, 101, LocalDate.parse("2026-10-01"),
            LocalTime.of(18, 0), LocalTime.of(17, 0), "DEMO"), "source timeIn <= timeOut rule is enforced");
        expectIllegalArgument(() -> new AttendanceRecord(1, 101, LocalDate.parse("2026-10-01"),
            LocalTime.of(8, 0), LocalTime.of(17, 0), " "), "dayType cannot be blank");

        System.out.println("PASS: " + checks + " attendance-domain checks");
    }

    private void equal(Object expected, Object actual, String message) {
        checks++;
        if (expected == null ? actual != null : !expected.equals(actual)) {
            throw new AssertionError(message + " (expected=" + expected + ", actual=" + actual + ")");
        }
    }

    private void check(boolean condition, String message) {
        checks++;
        if (!condition) throw new AssertionError(message);
    }

    private void expectIllegalArgument(Runnable action, String message) {
        checks++;
        try { action.run(); } catch (IllegalArgumentException expected) { return; }
        throw new AssertionError(message);
    }

    private void expectNoSuchElement(Runnable action, String message) {
        checks++;
        try { action.run(); } catch (NoSuchElementException expected) { return; }
        throw new AssertionError(message);
    }
}

    private static void localModeCreatesAndUpdatesOnlySyntheticDirectoryFields() throws Exception {
        AppServer app = new AppServer("", Paths.get("web"));
        HttpServer server = app.start("127.0.0.1", 0);
        try {
            URI base = URI.create("http://127.0.0.1:" + server.getAddress().getPort());
            String createBody = "{\"name\":\"Ira Demo\",\"department\":\"Operations\",\"role\":\"Coordinator\",\"location\":\"Taguig\",\"status\":\"Active\"}";
            HttpResponse<String> created = postJson(base.resolve("/api/employees"), createBody);
            check(created.statusCode() == 201, "local sandbox can create synthetic employee");
            com.google.gson.JsonObject createdItem = com.google.gson.JsonParser.parseString(created.body()).getAsJsonObject().getAsJsonObject("item");
            String id = createdItem.get("id").getAsString();
            check(id.matches("DEMO-[A-F0-9]{12}"), "employee ID is server-generated in a safe synthetic format");
            HttpResponse<String> attendance = get(base.resolve("/api/attendance?employeeId=" + id));
            check(attendance.statusCode() == 200 && attendance.body().contains("\"count\":0"),
                "new synthetic employees have no attendance until a schedule mapping is supplied");

            HttpResponse<String> injectedId = postJson(base.resolve("/api/employees"),
                "{\"id\":\"REAL-001\",\"name\":\"Fake\",\"department\":\"Ops\",\"role\":\"Role\",\"location\":\"City\",\"status\":\"Active\"}");
            check(injectedId.statusCode() == 400, "client cannot choose or inject an employee ID");
            HttpResponse<String> invalidStatus = postJson(base.resolve("/api/employees"),
                "{\"name\":\"Bad Status\",\"department\":\"Ops\",\"role\":\"Role\",\"location\":\"City\",\"status\":\"Terminated\"}");
            check(invalidStatus.statusCode() == 400, "unsupported synthetic status is rejected");

            HttpResponse<String> updated = putJson(base.resolve("/api/employees/" + id),
                "{\"name\":\"Ira Rivera\",\"department\":\"Operations\",\"role\":\"Lead\",\"location\":\"Makati\",\"status\":\"On leave\"}");
            check(updated.statusCode() == 200 && updated.body().contains("Ira Rivera"), "owner sandbox can update synthetic directory fields");
            HttpResponse<String> search = get(base.resolve("/api/employees?q=ira+rivera"));
            check(search.statusCode() == 200 && search.body().contains(id) && search.body().contains("On leave"),
                "updated synthetic employee appears in search results");
            HttpRequest delete = HttpRequest.newBuilder(base.resolve("/api/employees/" + id)).DELETE().build();
            HttpResponse<String> deleteResponse = HTTP.send(delete, HttpResponse.BodyHandlers.ofString(StandardCharsets.UTF_8));
            check(deleteResponse.statusCode() == 405, "employee deletion is not exposed");
        } finally {
            app.stop();
        }
    }

  state.attendanceRequestNumber += 1;
  state.reportRequestNumber += 1;

  attendanceResultCount.textContent = `${orderedRecords.length} raw ${orderedRecords.length === 1 ? 'entry' : 'entries'} loaded`;
}

async function loadAttendance() {
  const employeeId = attendanceEmployee.value;
  if (!employeeId) {
    state.rawAttendance = [];
    renderRawAttendanceSummary([]);
    document.getElementById('attendance-export-button').disabled = true;
    showAttendanceMessage('Load the employee directory first.');
    attendanceResultCount.textContent = 'No records loaded';
    return;
  }
  const requestNumber = ++state.attendanceRequestNumber;
  state.rawAttendance = [];
  renderRawAttendanceSummary([]);
  document.getElementById('attendance-export-button').disabled = true;
  showAttendanceMessage('Loading raw attendance records…');
  attendanceResultCount.textContent = 'Loading';
  const params = new URLSearchParams({ employeeId });
  const from = attendanceFrom.value;
  const to = attendanceTo.value;
  if (from) params.set('from', from);
  if (to) params.set('to', to);
  try {
    const response = await fetch(`/api/attendance?${params.toString()}`, { headers: await apiHeaders() });
    const payload = await response.json();
    if (!response.ok) throw new Error(payload.error || `Request failed (${response.status})`);
    if (requestNumber !== state.attendanceRequestNumber) return;
    renderAttendance(Array.isArray(payload.items) ? payload.items : []);
  } catch (error) {
    if (requestNumber !== state.attendanceRequestNumber) return;
    state.rawAttendance = [];
    renderRawAttendanceSummary([]);
    document.getElementById('attendance-export-button').disabled = true;
    showAttendanceMessage(error.message || 'Could not load attendance records.');
    attendanceResultCount.textContent = 'Could not load records';
  }
}

async function loadEmployees() {
  const requestNumber = ++state.requestNumber;
  const query = search.value.trim();
  showTableMessage('Loading employee records…');
  resultCount.textContent = 'Loading';
  try {
    const url = query ? `/api/employees?q=${encodeURIComponent(query)}` : '/api/employees';
    const response = await fetch(url, { headers: await apiHeaders() });
    const payload = await response.json();
    if (!response.ok) throw new Error(payload.error || `Request failed (${response.status})`);
    if (!payload || !Array.isArray(payload.items)) throw new Error('Unexpected employee response');
    if (requestNumber !== state.requestNumber) return;
    state.employees = payload.items;
    state.totalEmployees = Number.isInteger(payload.total) ? payload.total : payload.items.length;
    if (!query) {
      state.allEmployees = payload.items;
      populateAttendanceEmployees();
      populateWorkflowEmployees();
      renderDirectoryViews();
    }
    seedDemoButton.hidden = !(state.user && state.totalEmployees === 0 && !query);
    renderEmployees();

  if (!labels[view]) return;

    else nav.removeAttribute('aria-current');
  });

# Prototype API contract

All routes are same-origin JSON endpoints. In local mode, employee/attendance fixtures are synthetic and workflow records live only in the Java process memory (cleared on server restart). When `FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID` is configured, employee, attendance, and workflow routes require a signed-in Firebase user and use only that user's Firestore sandbox. The Java backend forwards the Firebase ID token to Firestore REST; Firestore Security Rules authorize every request. The project owner has published `docs/firestore.rules`; live smoke tests verified leave and ticket create/cancel persistence and cross-user denial. The assistant has not changed Firebase Console settings. Future rule-file changes still require owner publication.

In Firebase mode, browser requests include:

```text
Authorization: Bearer <Firebase ID token>
X-Firebase-UID: <signed-in Firebase UID>
```

The UID header is not trusted for authorization: Firestore Rules compare it to the UID in the verified ID token. Do not log or persist ID tokens.

## Health

`GET /api/health`

Local mode:

```json
{"status":"ok","mode":"local-synthetic-demo"}
```

Firebase mode reports `firebase-user-sandbox`.

## Employee directory

`GET /api/employees`

`GET /api/employees?q=finance`

```json
{
  "items": [
    {
      "id": "DEMO-002",
      "name": "Eli Santos",
      "department": "Finance",
      "role": "Payroll Associate",
      "location": "Taguig",
      "status": "Active"
    }
  ],
  "total": 3,
  "matched": 1
}
```

Search is case-insensitive across displayed fields. `total` is the full user-scoped demo directory size; `matched` is the returned count.

`GET /api/employees/{employeeId}` returns `{"item": {...}}` or `404 {"error":"Employee not found"}`.

`POST /api/employees` creates an owner-sandbox fictional record; `PUT /api/employees/{employeeId}` updates its allowed directory fields. Both accept only `name`, `department`, `role`, `location`, and `status` (`Active` or `On leave`). Unknown fields—including client-supplied IDs, payroll values, and government identifiers—are rejected. The server generates IDs in the `DEMO-<12 uppercase hex characters>` form. Responses are `201` and `200`, respectively, with `{"item": {...}}`. Firebase writes use only the caller's `users/{uid}/demoEmployees` path and existing owner rules; they do not grant HR/supervisor roles. Local mode has no user authentication and stores changes in a single process-memory demo store shared by callers of that API process. Delete, termination, schedule assignment, and audit-history routes are not implemented. A new record has no schedule mapping, so attendance returns an empty list until a separately approved schedule mapping is configured.

## Raw attendance

`GET /api/attendance?employeeId=DEMO-001`

Optional ISO date filters: `from=YYYY-MM-DD` and/or `to=YYYY-MM-DD`. If both are supplied, `from` must be on or before `to`; filtering is inclusive. `employeeId` is required.

```json
{
  "items": [
    {
      "attendanceId": 5001,
      "scheduleId": 101,
      "date": "2026-10-01",
      "timeIn": "08:01",
      "timeOut": "17:00",
      "dayType": "DEMO"
    }
  ],
  "count": 1,
  "hoursCalculated": false
}
```

Possible errors: `400` for missing employee ID, invalid date syntax, or reversed range; `404` for an unknown employee; `401` for missing/expired Firebase sign-in; `403` when Firestore Rules deny the request. Raw times only; no hours or pay are derived.

## Leave requests and tickets

`GET /api/workflows` returns only the current user's lists:

```json
{"leaveRequests":[],"tickets":[],"storage":"user-scoped-firestore"}
```

- `POST /api/workflows/leave` accepts `employeeId`, `leaveType`, `startDate`, `endDate`, and optional `note`. The server derives the employee name from the caller's own synthetic directory, validates supported leave types and ISO calendar dates, and creates a `Pending review` record.
- `POST /api/workflows/tickets` accepts `employeeId`, `ticketType`, and `summary`. The server derives the employee name and queue label and creates an `Open` record. No ticket is delivered or assigned to a real handler.
- `POST /api/workflows/leave/{requestId}/cancel` and `POST /api/workflows/tickets/{ticketId}/cancel` allow only the pending/open-to-cancelled transition. Delete, review, approve, reject, and resolve routes do not exist.
- Firebase records use `users/{uid}/demoLeaveRequests/{requestId}` and `users/{uid}/demoTickets/{ticketId}`. The candidate Firestore rules allow owner-only read/create/cancel; they deny deletes and all reviewer actions. Records are limited to the user's synthetic employee directory and contain no payroll calculations.
- Local mode returns `storage:"local-process-memory"`; these records survive page reloads while the Java process is running, but are lost when it stops.

Possible errors: `400` invalid request fields or dates; `401` missing/expired sign-in; `403` Firestore rules deny the operation (publish the updated `docs/firestore.rules`); `404` employee/request/ticket not found in the caller's sandbox; `409` invalid workflow transition.

## Opt-in demo seed

`POST /api/demo/seed`

Requires Firebase Authentication and Firestore mode. Creates missing fictional documents only in:

- `users/{uid}/demoEmployees/{employeeId}`
- `users/{uid}/demoAttendance/{attendanceId}`

The endpoint does not overwrite existing records and marks attendance with `dayType: "DEMO"`. It cannot create payroll documents. Firestore Rules are in `docs/firestore.rules`.

## Scope and security

- No production employee or payroll records.
- No service account, Admin SDK, or privileged credentials.
- Current user-owned sandbox rules are development-only, not an organizational role model.
- Payroll formulas, pay-period logic, and calculations remain blocked until specified by supplied course materials.

    private static void staticFilesExposeDefensiveHeadersAndRejectTraversal() throws Exception {
        AppServer app = new AppServer("", Paths.get("web"));
        HttpServer server = app.start("127.0.0.1", 0);
        try {
            URI base = URI.create("http://127.0.0.1:" + server.getAddress().getPort());
            HttpResponse<String> root = get(base.resolve("/"));
            check(root.statusCode() == 200, "static app root is served");
            check(root.headers().firstValue("Content-Security-Policy").orElse("").contains("default-src 'self'"),
                "static app root has a restrictive content security policy");
            check("nosniff".equalsIgnoreCase(root.headers().firstValue("X-Content-Type-Options").orElse("")),
                "static app root disables MIME sniffing");

            HttpResponse<String> envFile = get(base.resolve("/.env.local"));
            check(envFile.statusCode() == 404, "environment file is not served from the web root");
            HttpResponse<String> traversal = get(base.resolve("/%2e%2e/.env.local"));
            check(traversal.statusCode() == 404, "static path traversal cannot read outside the web root");
        } finally {
            app.stop();
        }
    }

    private static void firebaseModeRejectsUnauthenticatedReadsAndWritesBeforeFirestore() throws Exception {

            check(employeeUpdate.statusCode() == 401, "employee update requires Firebase sign-in");

            HttpResponse<String> attendance = get(base.resolve("/api/attendance?employeeId=DEMO-001"));
            check(attendance.statusCode() == 401, "attendance read requires Firebase sign-in");

            HttpResponse<String> workflows = get(base.resolve("/api/workflows"));
            check(workflows.statusCode() == 401, "workflow reads require Firebase sign-in");
            HttpResponse<String> workflowWrite = postJson(base.resolve("/api/workflows/leave"),
                "{\"employeeId\":\"DEMO-001\",\"leaveType\":\"Vacation\",\"startDate\":\"2026-11-10\",\"endDate\":\"2026-11-10\",\"note\":\"Test\"}");

            HttpRequest seed = HttpRequest.newBuilder(base.resolve("/api/demo/seed"))
                .POST(HttpRequest.BodyPublishers.noBody()).build();
            HttpResponse<String> seedResponse = HTTP.send(seed, HttpResponse.BodyHandlers.ofString(StandardCharsets.UTF_8));
            check(seedResponse.statusCode() == 401, "demo write requires Firebase sign-in");
        } finally {
            app.stop();
        }
    }

    private static final class FakeFirestoreServer implements AutoCloseable {
        private static final String EMPLOYEE_DOCUMENT = "{\"name\":\"projects/demo-project/databases/(default)/documents/users/user-77/demoEmployees/DEMO-001\","
            + "\"fields\":{\"id\":{\"stringValue\":\"DEMO-001\"},\"name\":{\"stringValue\":\"Mara Rivera\"},"
            + "\"department\":{\"stringValue\":\"People Operations\"},\"role\":{\"stringValue\":\"HR Coordinator\"},"
            + "\"location\":{\"stringValue\":\"Makati\"},\"status\":{\"stringValue\":\"Active\"}}}";
        private final HttpServer server;
        private final List<String> paths = new ArrayList<>();
        private final List<String> methods = new ArrayList<>();
        private final List<String> authorizations = new ArrayList<>();
        private final List<String> requestBodies = new ArrayList<>();

        FakeFirestoreServer() throws Exception {
            server = HttpServer.create(new java.net.InetSocketAddress("127.0.0.1", 0), 0);
            server.createContext("/", this::handle);
            server.start();
        }

        String apiRoot() { return "http://127.0.0.1:" + server.getAddress().getPort() + "/v1/projects/"; }

        private synchronized void handle(HttpExchange exchange) throws java.io.IOException {
            paths.add(exchange.getRequestURI().toString());
            methods.add(exchange.getRequestMethod());
            authorizations.add(exchange.getRequestHeaders().getFirst("Authorization"));
            String body = new String(exchange.getRequestBody().readAllBytes(), StandardCharsets.UTF_8);
            requestBodies.add(body);
            String path = exchange.getRequestURI().getPath();
            String response;
            int status = 200;
            if ("GET".equals(exchange.getRequestMethod()) && path.contains("/demoEmployees")) {
                response = "{\"documents\":[" + EMPLOYEE_DOCUMENT + "]}";
            } else if ("POST".equals(exchange.getRequestMethod()) && path.contains("/demoLeaveRequests")) {
                response = "{\"name\":\"projects/demo-project/databases/(default)/documents/users/user-77/demoLeaveRequests/LV-012345ABCDEF\"}";
            } else if ("POST".equals(exchange.getRequestMethod()) && path.contains("/demoEmployees")) {
                response = "{\"name\":\"projects/demo-project/databases/(default)/documents/users/user-77/demoEmployees/DEMO-FAKE000000\"}";
            } else if ("PATCH".equals(exchange.getRequestMethod()) && path.endsWith("/DEMO-001")) {
                response = EMPLOYEE_DOCUMENT;
            } else {
                status = 404;
                response = "{\"error\":{\"status\":\"NOT_FOUND\"}}";
            }
            byte[] bytes = response.getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8);
            exchange.getResponseHeaders().set("Content-Type", "application/json");
            exchange.sendResponseHeaders(status, bytes.length);
            exchange.getResponseBody().write(bytes);
            exchange.close();
        }

        @Override public void close() { server.stop(0); }
    }

    private static void check(boolean condition, String message) {
        checks++;
        if (!condition) throw new AssertionError(message);
    }
}

    private static HttpResponse<String> get(URI uri) throws Exception {
        HttpRequest request = HttpRequest.newBuilder(uri).GET().header("Accept", "application/json").build();
        return HTTP.send(request, HttpResponse.BodyHandlers.ofString(StandardCharsets.UTF_8));
    }

    private static HttpResponse<String> postJson(URI uri, String json) throws Exception {
        HttpRequest request = HttpRequest.newBuilder(uri).header("Accept", "application/json")
            .header("Content-Type", "application/json")
            .POST(HttpRequest.BodyPublishers.ofString(json, StandardCharsets.UTF_8)).build();
        return HTTP.send(request, HttpResponse.BodyHandlers.ofString(StandardCharsets.UTF_8));
    }

            .PUT(HttpRequest.BodyPublishers.ofString(json, StandardCharsets.UTF_8)).build();

## What works

- Overview with live sandbox counts, searchable employee directory/detail, raw attendance register and read-only attendance coverage report, Requests & tickets, Team roster, HR desk, and the payroll rules gate. Employee details open from a native keyboard-operable button without overriding table semantics; result counts and form feedback use polite status regions.
- Java employee/attendance services plus a workflow service. Local preview workflow records are held in Java process memory; Firebase mode uses the signed-in user’s Firestore subcollections.
- Leave requests and tickets validate inputs, derive employee names from the caller’s own synthetic directory, show documented queue labels, and support owner-sandbox cancellation. A monthly leave-request calendar displays pending/cancelled request dates only; it does not imply approval or leave balances. Client-side search and status filters narrow each history table without changing the calendar or the all-record CSV export. Both local and Firestore workflow histories are ordered newest first. No reviewer/approval/resolve/delete routes exist. The user has published the rules; live tests confirmed leave and ticket create/cancel persistence, plus cross-user denial.
- Read-only Team roster plus a synthetic directory editor. In Firebase mode, signed-in users can create/edit only name, department, role label, location, and demo status in their own sandbox. Local preview has no user authentication and shares one process-memory store for that API process. IDs are server-generated; delete, termination, schedule, salary, and government-ID fields are not exposed. New records receive no schedule mapping, so their raw attendance view is empty. This is not an HR role or a production employee-admin workflow.
- CSV export for currently visible synthetic employee results, loaded raw attendance rows, and owner-sandbox workflow records. CSV cells are quoted and spreadsheet-formula prefixes are neutralized; exports contain no derived hours or payroll values.
- Server-side employee search/detail, inclusive raw-attendance date filtering, a user-scoped attendance-coverage report (raw row counts and first/last record dates by configured mapping), and dynamic overview counts. Unmapped employees are labeled as unmapped, not absent. The attendance date fields default to that employee's earliest/latest available records, following the earlier MO-IT108 Requirements Analysis; the user can narrow the range. This is not a payroll-period calendar. No paid hours, deductions, or pay are calculated.
- Firebase email/password sign-in, development-account creation, and password-reset email UI; reset responses do not disclose whether an email has an account. The app stays behind the sign-in gate when Firebase config is complete.
- `/api/health`, employee list/search/detail plus owner-sandbox create/update, raw attendance query and coverage report, owner-scoped workflow list/create/cancel routes, and opt-in demo seed endpoint.
- Verification: `npm run test:web` passes 20 workflow/calendar/filter/CSV tests; `./test.sh` passes 167 Java checks; `npm run test:e2e` passes the local browser flow for employee create/edit, empty unscheduled attendance, reversed-date rejection, leave/ticket submit/cancel, request-calendar navigation, raw attendance summary/report filtering and CSV, simulated workflow authorization/service failure recovery, reload persistence, and mobile width; `npm run build` passes; `npm audit` reports 0 vulnerabilities. An isolated live Firebase auth-lifecycle browser check passed disposable account creation/sign-in, user-scoped empty Firestore reads, and sign-out on localhost; the account was deleted and no Firestore writes were made. The exact Arena preview-origin sign-in remains unverified.

## Already done — current foundation

- Firebase Email/Password Auth and user-scoped Firestore access were live-tested with synthetic accounts. The sign-in page now wires Firebase password-reset email with non-enumerating confirmation text; reset delivery has not been live-tested.
- Employee list, search, and detail selection work; data remains fictional and scoped to the signed-in sandbox.
- Raw attendance records are selectable by employee and inclusive date range; default range spans that employee's earliest/latest available records, following the older Requirements Analysis. A separate read-only coverage report summarizes raw row counts and date bounds by configured employee-to-schedule mapping; unmapped is not reported as absent.
- Payroll stays gated. The default attendance range is not a pay period.
- Leave request/ticket API routes now validate input, derive employee names from the user's synthetic directory, create records, show status, and allow only cancellation. A display-only personal request calendar shows pending/cancelled date ranges, not approved leave. Client-side search/status filters narrow each workflow table; local and Firestore lists order newest first; exports remain the full owner-sandbox dataset. Firebase paths are owner-scoped and have no reviewer/approval/delete access; after publication, live smoke testing verified employee create/update, leave and ticket create/cancel/read-back, and cross-user denial. One cancelled leave and one cancelled ticket remain under deleted disposable UIDs because workflow deletion is denied. Local preview stores these records in Java process memory and loses them when the process restarts.
- Team roster is read-only. The directory editor creates/updates only fictional name, department, role, location, and demo status. Firebase mode is user-scoped; local mode has one unauthenticated process-memory store. No team membership, HR authorization, delete, schedules, or lifecycle workflow exists.
- Verification: 20 Node.js workflow/calendar/filter/CSV-safety tests, 167 Java checks, local Playwright E2E, production build, and `npm audit` (0 vulnerabilities) pass. Local E2E covers employee create/edit, unscheduled attendance, raw attendance summaries and coverage report filtering/export, leave/ticket submit/cancel, table filters, calendar navigation, simulated workflow authorization/service errors and recovery, reload persistence, CSV download, and mobile width. Firebase browser sign-in, user-scoped empty reads, and sign-out pass on localhost with a deleted disposable account; actual rules/API failure states and exact Arena preview-origin sign-in remain unverified.

/home/user/motorph-ms2/docs/firestore-rules-review.md-25-1. **Self-service accounts:** the app offers development-account creation. Every account is limited to its own isolated sandbox, but there is no company membership, HR role, supervisor role, or admin workflow.
/home/user/motorph-ms2/docs/firestore-rules-review.md-26-2. **No organization-wide employee access:** per-user data is deliberately not shared between users. This is safe for testing, but not the eventual multi-user payroll design.

/home/user/motorph-ms2/docs/firestore-rules-review.md:28:4. **Domain constraints not fully expressible here:** the rules check date/time string formats, while Java parses dates/times. They do not enforce `timeIn <= timeOut` or uniqueness of `(scheduleId, date)` across separate documents. The current seed fixture is unique and the Java model validates time order; a future attendance-write feature needs an explicit, transaction-safe uniqueness design.
/home/user/motorph-ms2/docs/firestore-rules-review.md-29-5. **No employee identity binding:** accounts are scoped to their own sandbox, but there is no account-to-employee mapping. The user can select any synthetic employee in that same sandbox when creating a request. No reviewer can read or approve it; no workflow audit log or recovery mechanism exists.
/home/user/motorph-ms2/docs/firestore-rules-review.md-30-6. **Project administrators:** project owners and privileged Google Cloud IAM identities may access data through administrative channels; client Security Rules are not a replacement for IAM controls.
/home/user/motorph-ms2/docs/firestore-rules-review.md-31-7. **No App Check / production hardening:** not necessary for this isolated classroom prototype, but production deployment would require a broader security review, abuse controls, hosting review, monitoring, and an authorization design.

function setWorkflowStatus(id, message, error = false) {
  const element = document.getElementById(id);
  element.textContent = message;
  element.classList.toggle('workflow-error', error);
  element.classList.toggle('workflow-success', Boolean(message) && !error);
}

function showAttendanceMessage(message) {
  attendanceRows.replaceChildren();
  const row = document.createElement('tr');
  const cell = document.createElement('td');
  cell.colSpan = 6;
  cell.className = 'table-message';
  cell.textContent = message;
  row.append(cell);
  attendanceRows.append(row);
}

package ph.motorph.web;

import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.LinkedHashMap;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Map;
import java.util.NoSuchElementException;
import java.util.Optional;

/** Process-memory store containing only fictional demo employees. */
public final class InMemoryEmployeeStore implements MutableEmployeeStore {
    private final Map<String, Employee> employees = new LinkedHashMap<>();

    public InMemoryEmployeeStore() {
        addFixture(new Employee("DEMO-001", "Mara Rivera", "People Operations", "HR Coordinator", "Makati", "Active"));
        addFixture(new Employee("DEMO-002", "Eli Santos", "Finance", "Payroll Associate", "Taguig", "Active"));
        addFixture(new Employee("DEMO-003", "Noa Reyes", "Operations", "Operations Lead", "Quezon City", "On leave"));
    }

    @Override
    public synchronized List<Employee> findAll() {
        return new ArrayList<>(employees.values());
    }

    @Override
    public synchronized Optional<Employee> findById(String id) {
        return Optional.ofNullable(id == null ? null : employees.get(id.trim()));
    }

    @Override
    public synchronized Employee create(Employee employee) {
        if (employees.containsKey(employee.getId())) throw new IllegalStateException("Employee ID already exists.");
        employees.put(employee.getId(), employee);
        return employee;
    }

    @Override
    public synchronized Employee update(Employee employee) {
        if (!employees.containsKey(employee.getId())) throw new NoSuchElementException("Employee not found.");
        employees.put(employee.getId(), employee);
        return employee;
    }

    private void addFixture(Employee employee) {
        employees.put(employee.getId(), employee);
    }
}

38-### Attendance read-only model
39-
40-The supplied Data Dictionary lists these Attendance fields:
41-
42-- `attendanceID` — integer primary key;
43:- `scheduleID` — foreign key;
44:- `date` — date, unique in combination with `scheduleID`;
45-- `timeIn` and `timeOut` — time values, with the source check `timeIn <= timeOut`;
46-- `dayType` — enum, with members not specified.
47-
48:The prototype maps these to `AttendanceRecord` and validates positive synthetic identifiers, required values, `timeIn <= timeOut`, and unique `(scheduleID, date)` entries. A minimal employee-to-schedule mapping allows records to be viewed for an employee. The screen provides read-only inclusive date filtering and, following the older MO-IT108 Requirements Analysis, defaults to the selected employee's earliest/latest available record dates. This is a view convenience, not a claimed payroll-period calendar. `dayType` is shown as `DEMO`, not as an official enum value. No work hours, overtime, paid leave, undertime, or pay values are derived.
49-
50:The database-design PDF also describes attendance as tied to Schedule and the DFD routes attendance through Schedule and Time Tracking, then Timesheet Validation. The exact source/import mechanism and MS2 workflow are not asserted by this read-only fixture.
51-
52-### Payroll and payslip fields
53-
54-The source set names payroll components and storage fields, including:
55-
56-- `Payroll`: employee, wage/rebate/summary IDs, month, PTO maximum, hourly/daily/monthly rates, net pay;
57-- `Payslip`: payroll ID, period start/end, regular/overtime/holiday-overtime/PTO/undertime hours, worked days/holidays/rest days, gross income;
58-- `Earnings`: overtime/PTO/holiday/rest-day pay, subsidies/stipends, other incentives, total benefits;
59-- `Deductibles`, `Other Transactions`, `Government Deductibles`, `Contributions`, `Government Tally`, and `Summary` for deduction and contribution amounts/totals.
60-
61-The DFD labels Timesheet Validation, Leave Monetisation, Wage and Adjustments, Government Deductibles, Basic Payroll Computation, Payslip Generation & Distribution, and Monthly Summary Compilation. These descriptions establish the concept names and broad flow, not their exact computation.
62-
63-## Unresolved source conflicts kept open
64-
65-The PDFs disagree on several schema details. The prototype has not chosen a definitive production schema for these:
66-
67:- `Schedule.restDay SET` versus `Schedule.restDayID` plus a separate Rest Day table;
68-- direct Employee `departmentID` / `governmentID` versus deriving department via Position and linking Government via `Government.employeeID`;
69-- Address region stored directly versus derived through City;
70-- presence of `Supervisor.departmentID`;
71:- presence of `Leave.scheduleID`;
72-- key/version fields for Rates and Government Tally;
73-- some Holiday uniqueness and relationship-matrix cardinalities.
74-
75-See Sections 16 and 17 of the full synthesis for the complete discrepancies.
76-
77-## Payroll-rule status
78-
79-The source documents do **not** supply the arithmetic formula or current effective values for gross pay, salary conversion, overtime, holiday/rest-day rates, undertime, paid leave, leave monetisation, SSS, PhilHealth, Pag-IBIG, withholding tax, deductions, net pay, or rounding. They also do not provide an authoritative worked payslip example. The payroll screen therefore remains intentionally disabled. The nine GitHub submissions' formulas/tests are comparison evidence only, not a policy authority.
80-
81-## Scope boundary
82-
83-MO-IT107's DFD/database design is broad (five actors; employee management, payroll processing, and archival; PII approval intent; many database tables). The current project begins as a narrow web-based Java/OOP slice. Do not add every actor, all tables, two-person PII workflow, monthly reports, or archive deletion unless the active MO-IT110 milestone explicitly requires it. Keep such items traceable to the source and clearly labelled reference-only until scope is confirmed.

Source-grounded acceptance baseline (draft)

Purpose: record observable pass/fail behavior already implemented and define safe candidate acceptance criteria before tailoring. This is a working baseline, not an approved rubric interpretation. No standalone active MO-IT110 grading rubric was identified among the supplied files in the workspace; the older MO-IT108/107 documents and peer submissions inform scope, while the Terminal Assessment proposal is treated as placeholder material rather than an authoritative detailed specification.

Scope rules: fictional data only; use the signed-in user's sandbox in Firebase mode; keep local-preview persistence explicitly process-memory; do not invent attendance-hour/payroll calculations, pay periods, employee-to-account identity, supervisor/reviewer authority, or access boundaries. The user-published development rules remain unchanged.

function renderAttendance(records) {
  state.rawAttendance = [...records].sort((a, b) => String(a.date).localeCompare(String(b.date)));
  const orderedRecords = state.rawAttendance;
  document.getElementById('attendance-export-button').disabled = orderedRecords.length === 0;
  applyDefaultAttendanceRange(orderedRecords);
  renderRawAttendanceSummary(orderedRecords);
  attendanceRows.replaceChildren();
  if (orderedRecords.length === 0) {
    showAttendanceMessage('No attendance entries match this employee and date range.');
  } else {
    orderedRecords.forEach(record => {
      const row = document.createElement('tr');
      [record.date, String(record.attendanceId), String(record.scheduleId), record.timeIn, record.timeOut, record.dayType]
        .forEach(value => row.append(makeCell(value)));
      attendanceRows.append(row);
    });
  }
  attendanceResultCount.textContent = `${orderedRecords.length} raw ${orderedRecords.length === 1 ? 'entry' : 'entries'} loaded`;
}

async function loadAttendance() {
  const employeeId = attendanceEmployee.value;
  if (!employeeId) {
    state.rawAttendance = [];
    renderRawAttendanceSummary([]);
    document.getElementById('attendance-export-button').disabled = true;
    showAttendanceMessage('Load the employee directory first.');
    attendanceResultCount.textContent = 'No records loaded';
    return;
  }
  const requestNumber = ++state.attendanceRequestNumber;
  state.rawAttendance = [];
  renderRawAttendanceSummary([]);
  document.getElementById('attendance-export-button').disabled = true;
  showAttendanceMessage('Loading raw attendance records…');
  attendanceResultCount.textContent = 'Loading';
  const params = new URLSearchParams({ employeeId });
  const from = attendanceFrom.value;
  const to = attendanceTo.value;
  if (from) params.set('from', from);
  if (to) params.set('to', to);
  try {
    const response = await fetch(`/api/attendance?${params.toString()}`, { headers: await apiHeaders() });
    const payload = await response.json();
    if (!response.ok) throw new Error(payload.error || `Request failed (${response.status})`);
    if (requestNumber !== state.attendanceRequestNumber) return;
    renderAttendance(Array.isArray(payload.items) ? payload.items : []);
  } catch (error) {
    if (requestNumber !== state.attendanceRequestNumber) return;
    state.rawAttendance = [];
    renderRawAttendanceSummary([]);
    document.getElementById('attendance-export-button').disabled = true;
    showAttendanceMessage(error.message || 'Could not load attendance records.');
    attendanceResultCount.textContent = 'Could not load records';
  }
}

function renderAttendanceReport(items) {
  state.attendanceReport = items;
  const rows = document.getElementById('attendance-report-rows');
  rows.replaceChildren();
  if (!items.length) {
    showWorkflowTableMessage(rows, 6, 'No synthetic employees are available for this report.');
  } else {
    items.forEach(item => {
      const row = document.createElement('tr');
      row.append(makeCell(`${item.employeeName} · ${item.employeeId}`));
      row.append(makeCell(item.hasScheduleMapping ? `Schedule ${item.scheduleId}` : 'No mapping'));
      row.append(makeCell(String(item.rawRecordCount)));
      row.append(makeCell(item.firstRecordDate || '—'));
      row.append(makeCell(item.lastRecordDate || '—'));
      if (item.hasScheduleMapping) {
        const openButton = document.createElement('button');
        openButton.type = 'button';
        openButton.className = 'button button-quiet workflow-report-open';
        openButton.dataset.employeeId = item.employeeId;
        openButton.textContent = 'View rows';
        openButton.setAttribute('aria-label', `View raw entries for ${item.employeeId}`);
        row.append(makeCell(openButton));
      } else {
        row.append(makeCell('—'));
      }
      rows.append(row);
    });
  }
  const totalRawRows = items.reduce((total, item) => total + (Number.isInteger(item.rawRecordCount) ? item.rawRecordCount : 0), 0);
  document.getElementById('attendance-report-count').textContent = `${items.length} employee ${items.length === 1 ? 'row' : 'rows'} · ${totalRawRows} raw ${totalRawRows === 1 ? 'record' : 'records'} in range`;
  document.getElementById('attendance-report-export').disabled = items.length === 0;
}

async function loadAttendanceReport() {
  const requestNumber = ++state.reportRequestNumber;
  const status = document.getElementById('attendance-report-status');
  status.hidden = true;
  status.textContent = '';
  document.getElementById('attendance-report-count').textContent = 'Loading report';
  document.getElementById('attendance-report-export').disabled = true;
  showWorkflowTableMessage(document.getElementById('attendance-report-rows'), 6, 'Loading raw attendance summary…');
  const params = new URLSearchParams();
  const from = document.getElementById('attendance-report-from').value;
  const to = document.getElementById('attendance-report-to').value;
  if (from) params.set('from', from);
  if (to) params.set('to', to);
  const query = params.toString();
  try {
    const response = await fetch(`/api/reports/attendance${query ? `?${query}` : ''}`, { headers: await apiHeaders() });
    const payload = await response.json();
    if (!response.ok) throw new Error(payload.error || `Request failed (${response.status})`);
    if (!payload || !Array.isArray(payload.items) || payload.hoursCalculated !== false) {
      throw new Error('Unexpected attendance report response.');
    }
    if (requestNumber !== state.reportRequestNumber) return;
    renderAttendanceReport(payload.items);
    status.textContent = 'Loaded raw record counts and date coverage only; no hours or payroll values were calculated.';
    status.hidden = false;
  } catch (error) {
    if (requestNumber !== state.reportRequestNumber) return;
    state.attendanceReport = [];
    showWorkflowTableMessage(document.getElementById('attendance-report-rows'), 6, error.message || 'Could not load the raw attendance report.');
    document.getElementById('attendance-report-count').textContent = 'Could not load report';
    document.getElementById('attendance-report-export').disabled = true;
    status.textContent = error.message || 'Could not load the raw attendance report.';
    status.hidden = false;
  }
}

const serverChildren = [];
let browser;

function freePort() {
  return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
    const server = net.createServer();
    server.once('error', reject);
    server.listen(0, '127.0.0.1', () => {
      const { port } = server.address();
      server.close(error => error ? reject(error) : resolve(port));
    });
  });
}

function start(command, args, env, label) {
  const child = spawn(command, args, {
    cwd: projectRoot,
    env,
    detached: process.platform !== 'win32',
    stdio: ['ignore', 'pipe', 'pipe']
  });
  child.log = '';
  child.on('error', error => { child.log += `${label}: ${error.message}\n`; });
  for (const stream of [child.stdout, child.stderr]) {
    stream.setEncoding('utf8');
    stream.on('data', chunk => { child.log = (child.log + chunk).slice(-8000); });
  }
  serverChildren.push(child);
  return child;
}

async function waitForServer(url, child, label) {
  const end = Date.now() + timeoutMs;
  let lastError = 'no response';
  while (Date.now() < end) {
    if (child.exitCode !== null) throw new Error(`${label} exited early.\n${child.log}`);
    try {
      const response = await fetch(url);
      if (response.ok) return response;
      lastError = `HTTP ${response.status}`;
    } catch (error) {
      lastError = error.message;
    }
    await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 150));
  }
  throw new Error(`${label} did not become ready (${lastError}).\n${child.log}`);
}

function setWorkflowStatus(id, message, error = false) {
  const element = document.getElementById(id);
  element.textContent = message;
  element.classList.toggle('workflow-error', error);
  element.classList.toggle('workflow-success', Boolean(message) && !error);
}

function showAttendanceMessage(message) {
    attendanceResultCount.textContent = 'Could not load records';
  }
}

function renderAttendanceReport(items) {
  state.attendanceReport = items;
  const rows = document.getElementById('attendance-report-rows');
  rows.replaceChildren();
  if (!items.length) {
    showWorkflowTableMessage(rows, 6, 'No synthetic employees are available for this report.');
  } else {
    items.forEach(item => {
      const row = document.createElement('tr');
      row.append(makeCell(`${item.employeeName} · ${item.employeeId}`));
      row.append(makeCell(item.hasScheduleMapping ? `Schedule ${item.scheduleId}` : 'No mapping'));
      row.append(makeCell(String(item.rawRecordCount)));
      row.append(makeCell(item.firstRecordDate || '—'));
      row.append(makeCell(item.lastRecordDate || '—'));
      if (item.hasScheduleMapping) {
        const openButton = document.createElement('button');
        openButton.type = 'button';
        openButton.className = 'button button-quiet workflow-report-open';
        openButton.dataset.employeeId = item.employeeId;
        openButton.textContent = 'View rows';
        openButton.setAttribute('aria-label', `View raw entries for ${item.employeeId}`);
        row.append(makeCell(openButton));
      } else {
        row.append(makeCell('—'));
      }
      rows.append(row);
    });
  }
  const totalRawRows = items.reduce((total, item) => total + (Number.isInteger(item.rawRecordCount) ? item.rawRecordCount : 0), 0);
  document.getElementById('attendance-report-count').textContent = `${items.length} employee ${items.length === 1 ? 'row' : 'rows'} · ${totalRawRows} raw ${totalRawRows === 1 ? 'record' : 'records'} in range`;
  document.getElementById('attendance-report-export').disabled = items.length === 0;
}

async function loadAttendanceReport() {
  const requestNumber = ++state.reportRequestNumber;
  const status = document.getElementById('attendance-report-status');
  status.hidden = true;
  status.textContent = '';
  document.getElementById('attendance-report-count').textContent = 'Loading report';
  document.getElementById('attendance-report-export').disabled = true;
  showWorkflowTableMessage(document.getElementById('attendance-report-rows'), 6, 'Loading raw attendance summary…');
  const params = new URLSearchParams();
  const from = document.getElementById('attendance-report-from').value;
  const to = document.getElementById('attendance-report-to').value;
  if (from) params.set('from', from);
  if (to) params.set('to', to);
  const query = params.toString();
  try {
    const response = await fetch(`/api/reports/attendance${query ? `?${query}` : ''}`, { headers: await apiHeaders() });
    const payload = await response.json();
    if (!response.ok) throw new Error(payload.error || `Request failed (${response.status})`);
    if (!payload || !Array.isArray(payload.items) || payload.hoursCalculated !== false) {
      throw new Error('Unexpected attendance report response.');
    }
    if (requestNumber !== state.reportRequestNumber) return;
    renderAttendanceReport(payload.items);
    status.textContent = 'Loaded raw record counts and date coverage only; no hours or payroll values were calculated.';
    status.hidden = false;
  } catch (error) {
    if (requestNumber !== state.reportRequestNumber) return;
    state.attendanceReport = [];
    showWorkflowTableMessage(document.getElementById('attendance-report-rows'), 6, error.message || 'Could not load the raw attendance report.');
    document.getElementById('attendance-report-count').textContent = 'Could not load report';
    document.getElementById('attendance-report-export').disabled = true;
    status.textContent = error.message || 'Could not load the raw attendance report.';
    status.hidden = false;
  }
}

export function directoryLabelSummaryRows(employees) {
  if (!Array.isArray(employees)) return [];
  const counts = new Map();
  employees.forEach(employee => {
    if (!employee || typeof employee !== 'object') return;
    [['Status label', employee.status], ['Department label', employee.department]].forEach(([category, label]) => {
      if (typeof label !== 'string' || !label.trim()) return;
      const key = `${category}\u0000${label}`;
      counts.set(key, (counts.get(key) || 0) + 1);
    });
  });
  return [...counts.entries()]
    .map(([key, count]) => {
      const [category, label] = key.split('\u0000');
      return { category, label, employeeRecords: count };
    })
    .sort((a, b) => a.category.localeCompare(b.category) || a.label.localeCompare(b.label));
}

test('counts stored status and department labels independently and in stable order', () => {
  const result = directoryLabelSummaryRows([
    { status: 'Active', department: 'Operations' },
    { status: 'On leave', department: 'Operations' },
    { status: 'Active', department: 'Finance' }
  ]);
  assert.deepEqual(result, [
    { category: 'Department label', label: 'Finance', employeeRecords: 1 },
    { category: 'Department label', label: 'Operations', employeeRecords: 2 },
    { category: 'Status label', label: 'Active', employeeRecords: 2 },
    { category: 'Status label', label: 'On leave', employeeRecords: 1 }
  ]);
});

const WEEKDAYS = ['Monday', 'Tuesday', 'Wednesday', 'Thursday', 'Friday', 'Saturday', 'Sunday'];
const MONTH_FORMAT = new Intl.DateTimeFormat('en', { month: 'long', year: 'numeric' });

function dateKey(year, monthIndex, day) {
  return `${String(year).padStart(4, '0')}-${String(monthIndex + 1).padStart(2, '0')}-${String(day).padStart(2, '0')}`;
}

function validIsoDate(value) {
  if (typeof value !== 'string' || !/^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$/.test(value)) return false;
  const [year, month, day] = value.split('-').map(Number);
  const parsed = new Date(year, month - 1, day);
  return parsed.getFullYear() === year && parsed.getMonth() === month - 1 && parsed.getDate() === day;
}

/** Build a display-only month view of submitted request ranges; this is not an approved leave calendar. */
export function buildLeaveCalendar(monthDate, requests = [], today = new Date()) {
  if (!(monthDate instanceof Date) || Number.isNaN(monthDate.getTime())) {
    throw new TypeError('A valid month date is required.');
  }
  if (!Array.isArray(requests)) throw new TypeError('Requests must be an array.');

  const year = monthDate.getFullYear();
  const monthIndex = monthDate.getMonth();
  const daysInMonth = new Date(year, monthIndex + 1, 0).getDate();
  const mondayOffset = (new Date(year, monthIndex, 1).getDay() + 6) % 7;
  const todayKey = today instanceof Date && !Number.isNaN(today.getTime())
    ? dateKey(today.getFullYear(), today.getMonth(), today.getDate()) : '';

  const validRequests = requests.filter(request => request
    && validIsoDate(request.startDate)
    && validIsoDate(request.endDate)
    && request.startDate <= request.endDate);

  const cells = Array.from({ length: 42 }, (_, index) => {
    const day = index - mondayOffset + 1;
    const inMonth = day >= 1 && day <= daysInMonth;
    const key = inMonth ? dateKey(year, monthIndex, day) : '';
    const dayRequests = inMonth ? validRequests.filter(request => request.startDate <= key && key <= request.endDate) : [];
    return {
      date: key,
      day: inMonth ? day : null,
      inMonth,
      isToday: Boolean(key && key === todayKey),
      requests: dayRequests
    };
  });

  return {
    title: MONTH_FORMAT.format(new Date(year, monthIndex, 1)),
    weekdays: WEEKDAYS.slice(),
    weeks: Array.from({ length: 6 }, (_, index) => cells.slice(index * 7, index * 7 + 7))
  };
}

function renderLeaveCalendar() {
  const tbody = document.getElementById('leave-calendar-grid');
  if (!tbody) return;
  const calendar = buildLeaveCalendar(leaveCalendarMonth, state.workflow.leaveRequests);
  document.getElementById('leave-calendar-month').textContent = calendar.title;
  tbody.replaceChildren();
  calendar.weeks.forEach(week => {
    const row = document.createElement('tr');
    week.forEach(day => {
      const cell = document.createElement('td');
      cell.className = `calendar-day${day.inMonth ? '' : ' outside-month'}${day.isToday ? ' today' : ''}`;
      if (!day.inMonth) {
        cell.setAttribute('aria-hidden', 'true');
        row.append(cell);
        return;
      }
      cell.setAttribute('aria-label', `${day.date}${day.requests.length ? `, ${day.requests.length} request date${day.requests.length === 1 ? '' : 's'}` : ''}`);
      const dateNumber = document.createElement('span');
      dateNumber.className = 'calendar-date-number';
      dateNumber.textContent = String(day.day);
      cell.append(dateNumber);
      if (day.requests.length) {
        const list = document.createElement('ul');
        list.className = 'calendar-events';
        day.requests.forEach(request => {
          const event = document.createElement('li');
          event.className = `calendar-event${request.status === 'Cancelled' ? ' cancelled' : ''}`;
          event.textContent = `${request.leaveType} · ${request.status}`;
          event.title = `${request.employeeName} · ${request.employeeId} · request date only`;
          list.append(event);
        });
        cell.append(list);
      }
      row.append(cell);
    });
    tbody.append(row);
  });
}

export function filterWorkflowItems(items, { query = '', status = '', searchFields = [] } = {}) {
  if (!Array.isArray(items)) return [];
  const needle = String(query || '').trim().toLowerCase();
  const selectedStatus = String(status || '').trim();
  const fields = Array.isArray(searchFields) ? searchFields : [];
  return items.filter(item => {
    if (!item || typeof item !== 'object') return false;
    if (selectedStatus && item.status !== selectedStatus) return false;
    if (!needle) return true;
    return fields.some(field => {
      const value = item[field];
      return value !== null && value !== undefined && String(value).toLowerCase().includes(needle);
    });
  });
}

Optional live Firebase Auth lifecycle smoke test:

```sh
npm run test:firebase-auth
```

This uses `.env.local`, creates one uniquely named disposable Auth account, verifies sign-in, empty user-scoped reads, and sign-out on localhost, makes **no Firestore writes**, and deletes the Auth account in cleanup. It needs network access and should not be run concurrently with another live Auth test.

The app uses a small vendored Gson JAR for the Java Firestore REST adapter; its license is recorded in `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` and `third_party/licenses/`.

## Firebase development sandbox

- `.env.local` contains the Firebase **Web** app config used by the browser SDK; `.gitignore` lists this file. The user-supplied Web API key for `motorph-jd` is installed assistant-side. The user does not need to edit `.env.local`.
- The Web API key is a public client identifier, not a server credential. Do not add a service-account key or Admin SDK credentials.
- Authentication uses Email/Password and in-memory browser persistence. Live disposable-account creation/sign-in, empty user-scoped reads, and sign-out now pass on localhost; the test Auth account was deleted. Do not use real staff accounts or data.
- Firestore requests are made by the Java backend through the REST API, forwarding the signed-in user's Firebase ID token. Firestore Security Rules authorize those requests; no privileged server identity bypasses the rules.
- The app uses `users/{uid}/demoEmployees`, `demoAttendance`, `demoLeaveRequests`, and `demoTickets`. Workflow documents are owner-scoped with no reviewer or delete permission in the candidate rules. The opt-in seed writes fictional employee/attendance records only.
- The user published the updated `docs/firestore.rules`. Live Firebase smoke testing with disposable accounts verified owner-scoped employee create/update, leave and ticket create/cancel/read-back, and a cross-user denial (`403`). Both disposable Auth accounts and employee documents were deleted; one cancelled synthetic leave and one cancelled synthetic ticket remain under their deleted test UIDs because workflow deletes are intentionally denied (`LV-3502C01F0E60`, `TK-F05DD2B0D6CC`). No real employee data or credentials were used. These are **development-only** rules, not production role/HR policy.
- If Firebase is not configured locally, the app uses the in-memory synthetic fixture. No Firebase writes are made in that mode.
- `measurementId` / Firebase Analytics is not used.
- Browser auth is verified on `localhost`. The current Arena preview host is `8080-is3s38ic4lxn7e4e77g8b.e2b.app`; its authorized-domain status could not be tested from the sandbox because Arena's traffic-access token is injected only in the user preview session. If the preview reports `auth/unauthorized-domain`, add that exact host under Firebase Console → Authentication → Settings → Authorized domains.

See `docs/firebase-setup-guide.md` for the console checkpoint and `docs/firestore.rules` for the development rules.

## What works

- Overview with live sandbox counts, searchable employee directory/detail, HR directory search/status filters, a synthetic directory-label summary, raw attendance register and coverage report, Requests & tickets, searchable read-only Team roster, and the payroll rules gate. Employee details open from a native keyboard-operable button without overriding table semantics; result counts and form feedback use polite status regions.
- Java employee/attendance services plus a workflow service. Local preview workflow records are held in Java process memory; Firebase mode uses the signed-in user’s Firestore subcollections.
- Leave requests and tickets validate inputs, derive employee names from the caller’s own synthetic directory, show documented queue labels, and support owner-sandbox cancellation. A monthly leave-request calendar displays pending/cancelled request dates only; it does not imply approval or leave balances. Search/status filters narrow history tables only; they do not change the leave calendar or all-record exports. Row details reveal the submitted note/message and UTC timestamps without adding a reviewer workflow. Both local and Firestore workflow histories are ordered newest first. No reviewer/approval/resolve/delete routes exist. The user has published the rules; live tests confirmed leave and ticket create/cancel persistence, plus cross-user denial.
- Read-only Team roster plus a synthetic directory editor. In Firebase mode, signed-in users can create/edit only name, department, role label, location, and demo status in their own sandbox. Local preview has no user authentication and shares one process-memory store for that API process. IDs are server-generated; delete, termination, schedule, salary, and government-ID fields are not exposed. New records receive no schedule mapping, so their raw attendance view is empty. This is not an HR role or a production employee-admin workflow.
- CSV export for currently visible synthetic employee results and Team roster rows, loaded raw attendance rows, attendance coverage reports, and owner-sandbox workflow records. CSV cells are quoted and spreadsheet-formula prefixes are neutralized; exports contain no derived hours or payroll values.
- Server-side employee search/detail, HR table search/status filters, a user-scoped attendance-coverage report (raw row counts and first/last record dates by configured mapping), synthetic directory label counts by status/department, and dynamic overview counts. Unmapped employees are labeled as unmapped, not absent. The attendance date fields default to that employee's earliest/latest available records, following the earlier MO-IT108 Requirements Analysis; the user can narrow the range. This is not a payroll-period calendar. No paid hours, deductions, or pay are calculated.
- Firebase email/password sign-in, development-account creation, and password-reset email UI; reset responses do not disclose whether an email has an account. The app stays behind the sign-in gate when Firebase config is complete.
- `/api/health`, employee list/search/detail plus owner-sandbox create/update, raw attendance query and coverage report, owner-scoped workflow list/create/cancel routes, and opt-in demo seed endpoint.
- Verification: `npm run test:web` passes 20 workflow/calendar/filter/CSV tests; `./test.sh` passes 167 Java checks; `npm run test:e2e` passes the local browser flow for employee create/edit, HR/Team filters and roster CSV, empty unscheduled attendance, raw directory-label summary, reversed-date rejection, leave/ticket submit/cancel and detail disclosures, request-calendar navigation, raw attendance summary/report filtering, drill-through and CSV, simulated workflow authorization/service failure recovery, reload persistence, and mobile width; `npm run build` passes; `npm audit` reports 0 vulnerabilities. An isolated live Firebase auth-lifecycle browser check passed disposable account creation/sign-in, user-scoped empty Firestore reads, and sign-out on localhost; the account was deleted and no Firestore writes were made. The exact Arena preview-origin sign-in remains unverified.

## Not implemented / important limits

- No production hosting, HR authorization roles, admin controls, audit trail, backup, or production security review. The built-in JDK HTTP server is a learning prototype, not a hardened public service.
- No live employee, attendance, or payroll information. Do not use this prototype for payroll processing.
- No work-hour derivation algorithm, payroll formulas, rates, pay-period calendar, payslips, or payroll calculations. The supplied material does not define a complete attendance algorithm or exact semi-monthly cut-offs, so the program will not infer them.
- Leave/ticket records are persistent only in the signed-in user’s sandbox after the updated rules are published; the current local preview uses process memory. There is no supervisor/reviewer role, real queue delivery, approval, notification, audit trail, team assignment, HR lifecycle editing, attendance import, or approved source-system integration.

## Source and attribution

`docs/source-grounding-and-open-rules.md` records supplied-source facts, scope boundaries, and unresolved ambiguities. `docs/acceptance-baseline.md` captures the current source-grounded behavior and gates as a draft, not an approved rubric. `docs/legacy-mo-it108-traceability.md` maps the user's earlier MotorPH requirements/design documents to the current prototype and explains the feature-parity estimate. `docs/peer-parity-roadmap.md` lists the remaining phases and acceptance gates to reach broad peer-level feature parity. The restrained title stripe adapts a small MIT-licensed `system.css` motif; exact attribution and licenses are listed in `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`.

1181-## Quick comparison of the flows
1182-
1183:- **Mostly database/UI-driven:** folder 1 (SQLite); folders 2 and 5 (MySQL) calculate much of salary in Swing handlers.
1184-- **Small procedural examples:** folder 3 reads fixed/example values and prints arithmetic.
1185-- **CSV plus layered services:** folder 4.
1186-- **OOP payroll pipeline:** folder 6; folder 9 extends this with explicit repositories, service tests, and a documented CP2-to-MS2 bridge.
1187-- **CSV-heavy GUI:** folder 7.
1188-- **Two disconnected input channels:** folder 8 (local GUI CSVs vs online console sheets).
1189-
1190-The pseudocode is a map for understanding and QA—not evidence that any repository is the user's own work or a safe source to submit. Confirm authorship, course fit, current payroll rules, and reuse permission with the mentor before adopting code.

### 4. Payroll for one employee or all employees `[SOURCE]`

```text
select employee and pay-period start/end
retrieve matching attendance
calculate gross pay from employee rate and worked time
calculate statutory deductions (SSS table, PhilHealth, Pag-IBIG, tax)
net = gross + applicable allowances - deductions
create PaySlip
if batch requested:
    repeat for each employee
return payslips to view
```

### 5. Payslip and period reports `[SOURCE]`

```text
choose employee/period or weekly/monthly summary
ask PayrollService/ReportService for calculated data
format one payslip or aggregate report
show it in report/payslip panel
```

### 6. Leave screen `[PARTIAL]`

```text
open leave-related panel if selected
```

Leave-related classes/panel exist, but startup wiring did not connect a LeaveRequestService to the frame in the reviewed source. The retest reached MainFrame, but did not establish a complete leave submission/approval path. Maven reported zero automated tests; six manual helper programs passed after test-only compatibility adjustments.

## Folder 6 — explicit MS2 OOP payroll refactor

### 1. Startup, CSV loading, and login `[RUN: 167/167 tests; LoginFrame opened]`

```text
start MotorPH
CSVDataHandler loads employee CSV into Employee objects
CSVDataHandler loads attendance CSV into AttendanceRecord objects
show LoginFrame
on successful login:
    determine user/role
    show permitted employee or staff screens
```

### 2. Employee subtype behavior `[SOURCE]`

```text
Employee is the shared abstract/base type
if employee is RegularEmployee:
    use regular-employee pay/allowance behavior
else if employee is ProbationaryEmployee:
    use probationary-employee behavior
return behavior through the shared Employee interface
```

### 3. Attendance and pay-period aggregation `[RUN through suite]`

```text
for each attendance record belonging to employee and cutoff:
    determine if record belongs to cutoff
    accumulate worked hours/days and applicable time values
return cutoff totals
```

### 4. Payroll and deduction composition `[RUN through 167-check suite]`

```text
receive employee, attendance list, cutoff, and list of Deduction calculators
hours = aggregate matching attendance
gross = calculate employee/cutoff pay, including subtype allowance behavior
for each deduction calculator (SSS, PhilHealth, Pag-IBIG, tax):
    deductionAmount = calculator.calculate(gross, employee/context)
net = gross - sum(deductionAmount)
create immutable Payslip with period, gross, deductions, net
```

### 5. Role permissions and result persistence `[SOURCE]`

```text
if user is EmployeeUser:
    allow self/profile and permitted own-payroll view
if user is PayrollStaff:
    allow staff payroll view/save operations
when save requested:
    serialize calculated payroll results to payroll-results CSV
```

The retest confirmed the suite still passes 167 checks under Java 21. Its calculations should still be checked against the currently approved rubric; the test pass is internal consistency evidence, not a compliance ruling.

## Folder 7 — Swing/CSV payroll system

### 1. Startup and employee CSV loading `[RUN with expected-layout fixture]`

```text
if attendance.csv is absent/empty:
    create it with expected attendance header
load MotorPH_Employee Data.csv with OpenCSV
for each employee row shorter than 21 fields:
    pad missing fields with empty strings
store rows in static EmployeeData.records
open loginUI
```

### 2. Login `[RUN: compatible synthetic row reached DashboardUI]`

```text
read employee number and password
for each data row after the header:
    if row[0] matches employee number
       and row[19] (20th field) matches password:
        open DashboardUI for that employee
        stop
show login error if no row matches
```

The inventory row gets padded but does not become a valid employee record; mapping later tries to parse its text as an employee number and fails.

### 3. Employee profile and directory maintenance `[SOURCE]`

```text
select employee row
for profile: display the row's employee fields
for add/update/delete:
    validate/modify EmployeeData.records
    rewrite employee CSV from the shared list
    notify screens to refresh
```

### 4. Attendance clock-in/out/history `[SOURCE]`

```text
on clock-in:
    capture employee and current date/time
    append attendance event to attendance CSV
on clock-out:
    find open attendance event for employee/day
    add clock-out time
