package motorph.model;

import java.time.Duration;
import java.time.LocalDate;
import java.time.LocalTime;
import java.time.format.TextStyle;
import java.util.Locale;

/**
 * One day of attendance for one employee (one row of attendance.csv).
 * <p>
 * The CP2 time rules are hidden inside this class: logins from 8:00 to 8:10
 * count as 8:00 (grace period), and logouts after 5:00 PM count as 5:00 PM
 * (cap). Callers only ask for hours or minutes worked.
 * </p>
 */
public class AttendanceRecord {

    // === TIME RULES (from CP2 computeHoursWorked) ===
    private static final LocalTime WORK_START   = LocalTime.of(8, 0);
    private static final LocalTime GRACE_END    = LocalTime.of(8, 10);
    private static final LocalTime LOGOUT_CAP   = LocalTime.of(17, 0);

    // === CUTOFF RULES (days 1-15 = 1st cutoff, 16-month end = 2nd cutoff) ===
    private static final int FIRST_CUTOFF_END_DAY    = 15;
    private static final int SECOND_CUTOFF_START_DAY = 16;

    private final String employeeId;
    private final LocalDate date;
    private final LocalTime logIn;
    private LocalTime logOut;

    /**
     * Creates an attendance record. Throws IllegalArgumentException if a value
     * is missing or the logout is not after the login.
     */
    public AttendanceRecord(String employeeId, LocalDate date, LocalTime logIn, LocalTime logOut) {
        if (employeeId == null || employeeId.trim().isEmpty()) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Employee ID is required.");
        }
        if (date == null) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Date is required.");
        }
        if (logIn == null) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Log in time is required.");
        }
        this.employeeId = employeeId.trim();
        this.date = date;
        this.logIn = logIn;
        setLogOut(logOut);
    }

    // === GETTERS ===

    public String getEmployeeId() { return employeeId; }
    public LocalDate getDate()    { return date; }
    public LocalTime getLogIn()   { return logIn; }
    public LocalTime getLogOut()  { return logOut; }

    /** Updates the logout time. Must be after the login time. */
    public final void setLogOut(LocalTime logOut) {
        if (logOut == null) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Log out time is required.");
        }
        if (!logOut.isAfter(logIn)) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Log out time must be after log in time.");
        }
        this.logOut = logOut;
    }

    // === HOURS ===

    /**
     * Returns the minutes worked after applying the grace period and the
     * logout cap. Never negative. Whole minutes keep payroll math exact.
     */
    public long computeMinutesWorked() {
        long minutes = Duration.between(applyGracePeriod(logIn), applyLogoutCap(logOut)).toMinutes();
        return Math.max(0, minutes);
    }

    /** Returns the hours worked for the day after the time rules. Never negative. */
    public double computeHoursWorked() {
        return computeMinutesWorked() / 60.0;
    }

    /** Treats a login from 8:00 to 8:10 as 8:00. */
    private LocalTime applyGracePeriod(LocalTime time) {
        if (!time.isBefore(WORK_START) && !time.isAfter(GRACE_END)) {
            return WORK_START;
        }
        return time;
    }

    /** Caps a logout after 5:00 PM at 5:00 PM. */
    private LocalTime applyLogoutCap(LocalTime time) {
        return time.isAfter(LOGOUT_CAP) ? LOGOUT_CAP : time;
    }

    // === CUTOFF ===

    /**
     * Returns the payroll cutoff label for this record's date, for example
     * "June 1-15, 2024" or "June 16-30, 2024". Uses the real month length, so
     * February gives "16-29" in leap years and "16-28" otherwise.
     */
    public String getCutoffLabel() {
        String month = date.getMonth().getDisplayName(TextStyle.FULL, Locale.ENGLISH);
        if (date.getDayOfMonth() <= FIRST_CUTOFF_END_DAY) {
            return month + " 1-" + FIRST_CUTOFF_END_DAY + ", " + date.getYear();
        }
        return month + " " + SECOND_CUTOFF_START_DAY + "-" + date.lengthOfMonth() + ", " + date.getYear();
    }
}
package motorph.service;

import java.math.BigDecimal;
import java.math.MathContext;
import java.time.LocalDate;
import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.LinkedHashMap;
import java.util.LinkedHashSet;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Map;
import java.util.Set;
import java.util.TreeMap;
import motorph.deduction.Deduction;
import motorph.model.AttendanceRecord;
import motorph.model.Employee;
import motorph.model.Payslip;

/**
 * Runs the payroll workflow: hours -> gross pay -> deductions -> net pay -> Payslip.
 * <p>
 * Works only with parent types (Employee, Deduction), so there are no checks on
 * employee status or deduction type. The deductions are passed into the
 * constructor: a list of contributions computed on monthly gross (SSS,
 * PhilHealth, Pag-IBIG) and a separate withholding tax computed on taxable
 * income. Adding a new government contribution only needs a new Deduction
 * subclass in that list.
 * </p>
 * <p>
 * Cutoff rule (from CP2): the 1st cutoff (days 1-15) has no deductions and net
 * pay equals gross pay. The 2nd cutoff (day 16 to month end) takes the whole
 * month's deductions once, computed on the combined gross of both cutoffs.
 * </p>
 */
public class PayrollProcessor {

    // === SUMMARY KEYS (computePayrollSummary) ===
    public static final String SUMMARY_TOTAL_EMPLOYEES  = "Total Employees";
    public static final String SUMMARY_TOTAL_GROSS      = "Total Gross Pay";
    public static final String SUMMARY_TOTAL_DEDUCTIONS = "Total Deductions";
    public static final String SUMMARY_TOTAL_NET        = "Total Net Pay";
    public static final String SUMMARY_AVERAGE_NET      = "Average Net Pay";

    // Cutoff labels come from AttendanceRecord.getCutoffLabel(), e.g. "June 16-30, 2024"
    private static final String SECOND_CUTOFF_MARKER  = " 16-";
    private static final String SECOND_CUTOFF_PATTERN = " 16-\\d{2},";
    private static final String FIRST_CUTOFF_DAYS     = " 1-15,";

    private final List<Deduction> contributions;
    private final Deduction withholdingTax;

    /**
     * @param contributions  deductions computed on monthly gross, in payslip order
     * @param withholdingTax deduction computed last, on taxable income
     */
    public PayrollProcessor(List<Deduction> contributions, Deduction withholdingTax) {
        if (contributions == null || withholdingTax == null) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Contributions and withholding tax are required.");
        }
        for (Deduction contribution : contributions) {
            if (contribution == null) {
                throw new IllegalArgumentException("Contribution list must not contain empty entries.");
            }
        }
        this.contributions = List.copyOf(contributions);
        this.withholdingTax = withholdingTax;
    }

    /** Returns the deduction names in payslip order (contributions, then tax). */
    public List<String> getDeductionNames() {
        List<String> names = new ArrayList<>();
        for (Deduction contribution : contributions) {
            names.add(contribution.getName());
        }
        names.add(withholdingTax.getName());
        return names;
    }

    // === CUTOFFS AND HOURS ===

    /**
     * Returns every cutoff label found in the attendance records, oldest first.
     * Used to fill the cutoff selection list.
     */
    public List<String> getAvailableCutoffs(Map<String, List<AttendanceRecord>> attendanceByEmployee) {
        Map<LocalDate, String> labelsByDate = new TreeMap<>();
        for (List<AttendanceRecord> records : attendanceByEmployee.values()) {
            for (AttendanceRecord record : records) {
                labelsByDate.putIfAbsent(record.getDate(), record.getCutoffLabel());
            }
        }
        Set<String> cutoffs = new LinkedHashSet<>(labelsByDate.values());
        return new ArrayList<>(cutoffs);
    }

    /**
     * Sums the hours worked in one cutoff.
     *
     * @param records     one employee's attendance records
     * @param cutoffLabel the cutoff to total, for example "June 1-15, 2024"
     * @return total hours, or 0 if no records match
     */
    public double computeHoursForCutoff(List<AttendanceRecord> records, String cutoffLabel) {
        long minutes = 0;
        if (records != null) {
            for (AttendanceRecord record : records) {
                if (record.getCutoffLabel().equals(cutoffLabel)) {
                    minutes += record.computeMinutesWorked();
                }
            }
        }
        return minutes / 60.0;
    }

    /**
     * Returns the employees with no hours in the cutoff, so the GUI can warn once
     * before they are computed with 0 hours (CP2 behavior).
     */
    public List<Employee> findEmployeesWithoutAttendance(List<Employee> employees,
            Map<String, List<AttendanceRecord>> attendanceByEmployee, String cutoffLabel) {
        List<Employee> missing = new ArrayList<>();
        for (Employee employee : employees) {
            List<AttendanceRecord> records = attendanceByEmployee.get(employee.getEmployeeId());
            if (computeHoursForCutoff(records, cutoffLabel) <= 0) {
                missing.add(employee);
            }
        }
        return missing;
    }

    // === DEDUCTIONS AND NET PAY ===

    /**
     * Computes each deduction for one month, in order: every contribution on the
     * monthly gross, then withholding tax on taxable income (monthly gross minus
     * the contributions, floored at 0). No type checks: each Deduction runs its
     * own formula.
     *
     * @param monthlyGross combined gross of the 1st and 2nd cutoff
     * @return deduction name to amount, in payslip order
     */
    public Map<String, BigDecimal> computeDeductionBreakdown(BigDecimal monthlyGross) {
        Map<String, BigDecimal> breakdown = new LinkedHashMap<>();
        BigDecimal taxableIncome = monthlyGross;
        for (Deduction contribution : contributions) {
            BigDecimal amount = contribution.computeDeduction(monthlyGross);
            breakdown.put(contribution.getName(), amount);
            taxableIncome = taxableIncome.subtract(amount);
        }
        breakdown.put(withholdingTax.getName(), withholdingTax.computeDeduction(taxableIncome.max(BigDecimal.ZERO)));
        return breakdown;
    }

    /**
     * Totals all government deductions for one month: the sum of
     * computeDeductionBreakdown(), so the total always matches the itemized lines.
     */
    public BigDecimal computeTotalDeductions(BigDecimal monthlyGross) {
        return sum(computeDeductionBreakdown(monthlyGross));
    }

    /** Net pay = cutoff gross - deductions, never below 0. */
    public BigDecimal computeNetPay(BigDecimal cutoffGross, BigDecimal totalDeductions) {
        return cutoffGross.subtract(totalDeductions).max(BigDecimal.ZERO);
    }

    // === PAYSLIPS ===

    /**
     * Builds the payslip for one employee and one cutoff ("One Employee" mode).
     * Accepts any Employee subtype; allowances come from the subclass's own
     * computeAllowances().
     *
     * @param employee    the employee to pay
     * @param records     that employee's attendance records (may be empty)
     * @param cutoffLabel the cutoff to pay
     */
    public Payslip generatePayslip(Employee employee, List<AttendanceRecord> records, String cutoffLabel) {
        if (employee == null || cutoffLabel == null || cutoffLabel.trim().isEmpty()) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Employee and cutoff are required.");
        }
        double hoursWorked = computeHoursForCutoff(records, cutoffLabel);
        BigDecimal grossPay = employee.computeGrossPay(hoursWorked);

        Map<String, BigDecimal> breakdown;
        BigDecimal allowances;
        if (isSecondCutoff(cutoffLabel)) {
            // Monthly items are settled once, here: deductions on the combined gross of both cutoffs,
            // and the month's allowances (listed only; not added to net pay, as in CP2).
            double firstCutoffHours = computeHoursForCutoff(records, getFirstCutoffLabel(cutoffLabel));
            BigDecimal monthlyGross = employee.computeGrossPay(firstCutoffHours + hoursWorked);
            breakdown = computeDeductionBreakdown(monthlyGross);
            allowances = employee.computeAllowances();
        } else {
            breakdown = zeroBreakdown();
            allowances = BigDecimal.ZERO;
        }
        BigDecimal netPay = computeNetPay(grossPay, sum(breakdown));
        return new Payslip(employee, cutoffLabel, hoursWorked, grossPay, breakdown, allowances, netPay);
    }

    /**
     * Runs payroll for every employee in one cutoff ("All Employees" mode).
     * Same steps for every Employee subtype.
     */
    public List<Payslip> processPayroll(List<Employee> employees,
            Map<String, List<AttendanceRecord>> attendanceByEmployee, String cutoffLabel) {
        List<Payslip> payslips = new ArrayList<>();
        for (Employee employee : employees) {
            payslips.add(generatePayslip(employee, attendanceByEmployee.get(employee.getEmployeeId()), cutoffLabel));
        }
        return payslips;
    }

    /**
     * Totals a list of payslips: employee count, total gross, total deductions,
     * total net, and average net. Uses full-precision amounts (as CP2 did), so
     * the totals are rounded only when displayed.
     *
     * @throws IllegalArgumentException if the list is empty
     */

package motorphemployee;

import java.io.IOException;
import java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets;
import java.nio.file.AtomicMoveNotSupportedException;
import java.nio.file.Files;
import java.nio.file.Path;
import java.nio.file.Paths;
import java.nio.file.StandardCopyOption;
import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.Arrays;
import java.util.List;

/**
 * File-backed leave workflow for the MotorPH payroll screens.
 *
 * <p>The leave screens used to read and write {@code pendingleaves.csv},
 * {@code leaves.csv} and the leave-credit columns of {@code data.csv} on their
 * own. Two places knew the same CSV layout, so a single reversed argument
 * (Pending Leaves wrote the reason where the approval belonged) survived in one
 * call site after the other was fixed, and approving a request updated
 * {@code leaves.csv} while the request stayed in {@code pendingleaves.csv} until
 * somebody remembered to press Save.</p>
 *
 * <p>This class is the single writer for the approve and reject decisions. One call to
 * {@link #decide(int, boolean)} applies the whole decision - the request leaves
 * the pending file, one row is appended to the processed file with the columns
 * in header order, and the employee's leave credits move - and restores all
 * three files if any step fails.</p>
 *
 * <p>No Swing types are used here on purpose: the class can be exercised by a
 * console test without opening a window.</p>
 */
public class LeaveService {

    /** Value written in the {@code Approved?} column for an approved request. */
    public static final String APPROVED = "Yes";
    /** Value written in the {@code Approved?} column for a rejected request. */
    public static final String REJECTED = "No";

    /** Column order of pendingleaves.csv and of the processed leaves.csv. */
    public static final String[] LEAVE_COLUMNS = {"Employee ID", "Leave Type", "Days", "Reason", "Approved?"};

    public static final int COLUMN_EMPLOYEE_ID = 0;
    public static final int COLUMN_LEAVE_TYPE = 1;
    public static final int COLUMN_DAYS = 2;
    public static final int COLUMN_REASON = 3;
    public static final int COLUMN_APPROVAL = 4;

    private static final int COL_EMPLOYEE_ID = COLUMN_EMPLOYEE_ID;
    private static final int COL_LEAVE_TYPE = COLUMN_LEAVE_TYPE;
    private static final int COL_DAYS = COLUMN_DAYS;
    private static final int COL_REASON = COLUMN_REASON;

    private static final int DATA_LEAVE_CREDITS = 21;
    private static final int DATA_APPROVED_LEAVES = 22;
    private static final int DATA_REJECTED_LEAVES = 23;

    private final Path dataFile;
    private final Path pendingFile;
    private final Path leavesFile;

    public LeaveService(String dataFile, String pendingFile, String leavesFile) {
        this.dataFile = Paths.get(dataFile);
        this.pendingFile = Paths.get(pendingFile);
        this.leavesFile = Paths.get(leavesFile);
    }

    /** The three files the GUI uses, relative to the project directory. */
    public static LeaveService forProjectFiles() {
        return new LeaveService(
                "src/motorphemployee/data.csv",
                "src/motorphemployee/pendingleaves.csv",
                "src/motorphemployee/leaves.csv");
    }

    /** Rows of pendingleaves.csv, in file order. */
    public List<String[]> loadPending() throws IOException {
        return readRows(pendingFile);
    }

    /** Rows of leaves.csv (processed requests), in file order. */
    public List<String[]> loadProcessed() throws IOException {
        return readRows(leavesFile);
    }

    /**
     * Applies one decision to the request at {@code pendingIndex}.
     *
     * @param pendingIndex zero-based index into {@link #loadPending()}
     * @param approved     {@code true} to approve, {@code false} to reject
     * @return the row that was written to {@code leaves.csv}: employee id, leave
     *         type, days, reason, {@code Yes}/{@code No}
     * @throws IllegalArgumentException the row is gone, or the employee is unknown
     * @throws IllegalStateException    the employee has no leave credit left
     * @throws IOException              the files could not be written; all three
     *                                  files are restored before this is thrown
     */
    public String[] decide(int pendingIndex, boolean approved) throws IOException {
        return decide(pendingIndex, null, approved);
    }

    /**
     * Same as {@link #decide(int, boolean)}, but refuses when the row at
     * {@code pendingIndex} is not the request the screen showed, which happens
     * when the pending file changed while the window was open.
     *
     * @param expected the four cells the table displayed, or {@code null}
     */
    public String[] decide(int pendingIndex, String[] expected, boolean approved) throws IOException {
        List<String[]> pending = readRows(pendingFile);
        if (pendingIndex < 0 || pendingIndex >= pending.size()) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException(
                    "That leave request is no longer in the pending list. Reopen the window and try again.");
        }
        if (expected != null && !sameRequest(pending.get(pendingIndex), expected)) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException(
                    "The pending leave list changed while this window was open. Reopen the window and try again.");
        }

        String[] request = pending.get(pendingIndex);
        String employeeId = cell(request, COL_EMPLOYEE_ID);
        String leaveType = cell(request, COL_LEAVE_TYPE);
        String reason = reasonOf(request);
        int days = parseDays(cell(request, COL_DAYS));

        List<String[]> employees = readRows(dataFile);
        ensureUniformColumns(employees);
        int employeeRow = indexOfEmployee(employees, employeeId);
        if (employeeRow < 0) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Employee ID " + employeeId + " is not in the employee data file.");
        }
        String[] employee = employees.get(employeeRow);
        int credits = parseNumber(cell(employee, DATA_LEAVE_CREDITS), "leave credits", employeeId);
        int approvedLeaves = parseNumber(cell(employee, DATA_APPROVED_LEAVES), "approved leaves", employeeId);
        int rejectedLeaves = parseNumber(cell(employee, DATA_REJECTED_LEAVES), "rejected leaves", employeeId);
        if (approved && credits <= 0) {
            throw new IllegalStateException("Employee " + employeeId + " has no leave credit left.");
        }

        // New credit values are computed before the first write so a business-rule
        // failure cannot leave the three files half updated.
        employee[DATA_LEAVE_CREDITS] = String.valueOf(approved ? credits - 1 : credits);
        employee[DATA_APPROVED_LEAVES] = String.valueOf(approved ? approvedLeaves + 1 : approvedLeaves);
        employee[DATA_REJECTED_LEAVES] = String.valueOf(approved ? rejectedLeaves : rejectedLeaves + 1);

        String[] processed = new String[] {
            employeeId, leaveType, String.valueOf(days), reason, approved ? APPROVED : REJECTED
        };

        byte[] pendingBefore = readBytes(pendingFile);
        byte[] leavesBefore = readBytes(leavesFile);
        byte[] dataBefore = readBytes(dataFile);
        try {
            pending.remove(pendingIndex);
            writeRows(pendingFile, pending);
            appendRow(leavesFile, processed);
            writeRows(dataFile, employees);
        } catch (IOException | RuntimeException failure) {
            restore(pendingFile, pendingBefore);
            restore(leavesFile, leavesBefore);
            restore(dataFile, dataBefore);
            throw failure;
        }
        return processed;
    }

    /**
     * The reason text of a leave row. Older rows were written with the columns
     * reversed and a reason that can itself contain a comma, so everything from
     * the reason column onwards is joined back into one value.
     */
    public static String reasonOf(String[] row) {
        if (row.length <= COL_REASON) {
            return "";
        }
        String[] tail = Arrays.copyOfRange(row, COL_REASON, row.length);
        return String.join(",", tail).trim();
    }

    /** Pending row (Employee ID, Leave Type, Days, Reason) for the Pending Leaves table. */
    public static Object[] pendingTableRow(String[] row) {
        return new Object[] {
            cell(row, COL_EMPLOYEE_ID), cell(row, COL_LEAVE_TYPE), cell(row, COL_DAYS), reasonOf(row)
        };
    }

    /**
     * Processed row (Employee ID, Leave Type, Days, Reason, Approved?) for the
     * Leave Management table. The approval is the last field and the reason is
     * everything between the days and the approval, so a reason that contains a
     * comma still lands in one cell.
     */
    public static Object[] processedTableRow(String[] row) {
        String approval = row.length > COLUMN_APPROVAL ? row[row.length - 1].trim() : "";
        String reason = row.length > COLUMN_APPROVAL
                ? String.join(",", Arrays.copyOfRange(row, COL_REASON, row.length - 1)).trim()
                : reasonOf(row);
        return new Object[] {
            cell(row, COL_EMPLOYEE_ID), cell(row, COL_LEAVE_TYPE), cell(row, COL_DAYS), reason, approval
        };
    }

    /**
     * Refuses to rewrite an employee file whose rows do not all have the header's
     * column count. A field with an unescaped comma would shift every later
     * column, and writing the parsed rows back would turn that into lost data
     * (known issue 13 - the screens still split on every comma).
     */
    private static void ensureUniformColumns(List<String[]> rows) {
        if (rows.isEmpty()) {
            return;
        }
        int columns = rows.get(0).length;
        for (int i = 1; i < rows.size(); i++) {
            if (rows.get(i).length != columns) {
                throw new IllegalStateException("data.csv row " + (i + 1) + " has " + rows.get(i).length

                String.join(" / ", lines(work.resolve("pendingleaves.csv"))));
        check("leaves.csv got one row", 1, lines(work.resolve("leaves.csv")).size());
        check("leaves.csv row has the reason in column 4 and Yes in column 5", "23,Sick Leave,2,Sick,Yes",
                lines(work.resolve("leaves.csv")).get(0));
        List<String> dataRows = lines(work.resolve("data.csv"));
        check("data.csv keeps all 24 columns on the edited row", 24, dataRows.get(1).split(",", -1).length);
        check("leave credits 5 -> 4", "4", creditsOf("23"));
        check("approved leaves 0 -> 1", "1", approvedOf("23"));
        check("rejected leaves unchanged", "0", rejectedOf("23"));
    }

    private static void rejectWritesNoAndKeepsCredits() throws IOException {
        start("reject: same single write, No in the approval column, credit untouched");
        LeaveService service = fixture("13,Emergency Leave,2,Family trip\r\n", "", 5, 0, 0);

        String[] processed = service.decide(0, false);

        check("returned row keeps header order", "13|Emergency Leave|2|Family trip|No", String.join("|", processed));
        check("pending file is empty", 0, lines(work.resolve("pendingleaves.csv")).size());
        check("leaves.csv row has the reason in column 4 and No in column 5", "13,Emergency Leave,2,Family trip,No",
                lines(work.resolve("leaves.csv")).get(0));
        check("leave credits unchanged", "5", creditsOf("13"));
        check("approved leaves unchanged", "0", approvedOf("13"));
        check("rejected leaves 0 -> 1", "1", rejectedOf("13"));
    }

    private static void theSameRequestCannotBeProcessedTwice() throws IOException {
        start("the same request cannot be approved twice (the old duplicate-leave bug)");
        LeaveService service = fixture("23,Sick Leave,2,Sick\r\n", "", 5, 0, 0);

        service.decide(0, true);
        String pendingAfterFirst = String.join("|", lines(work.resolve("pendingleaves.csv")));
        String leavesAfterFirst = String.join("|", lines(work.resolve("leaves.csv")));
        int rowsAfterFirst = lines(work.resolve("leaves.csv")).size();

        boolean refused = false;
        String message = "";
        try {
            service.decide(0, true);
        } catch (IllegalArgumentException expected) {
            refused = true;
            message = expected.getMessage();
        }
        check("second decision on the same index is refused", true, refused);
        check("the refusal explains why", true, message.contains("no longer in the pending list"));
        check("pending file still empty", "", pendingAfterFirst);
        check("leaves.csv still has one row", rowsAfterFirst, lines(work.resolve("leaves.csv")).size());
        check("leaves.csv unchanged", leavesAfterFirst, String.join("|", lines(work.resolve("leaves.csv"))));
        check("leave credit was only deducted once", "4", creditsOf("23"));
    }

    private static void unknownEmployeeLeavesTheFilesUntouched() throws IOException {
        start("unknown employee: refused before any file is written");
        LeaveService service = fixture("99,Sick Leave,2,Sick\r\n", "", 5, 0, 0);
        String pendingBefore = String.join("|", lines(work.resolve("pendingleaves.csv")));
        String dataBefore = String.join("|", lines(work.resolve("data.csv")));

        boolean refused = false;
        try {
            service.decide(0, true);
        } catch (IllegalArgumentException expected) {
            refused = expected.getMessage().contains("not in the employee data file");
        }
        check("refused", true, refused);
        check("pending file untouched", pendingBefore, String.join("|", lines(work.resolve("pendingleaves.csv"))));
        check("data file untouched", dataBefore, String.join("|", lines(work.resolve("data.csv"))));
        check("leaves.csv still empty", 0, lines(work.resolve("leaves.csv")).size());
    }

    private static void employeeWithoutCreditIsRefused() throws IOException {
        start("employee with 0 leave credits: approval refused, nothing written");
        LeaveService service = fixture("23,Sick Leave,2,Sick\r\n", "", 0, 3, 1);
        String pendingBefore = String.join("|", lines(work.resolve("pendingleaves.csv")));

        boolean refused = false;
        try {
            service.decide(0, true);
        } catch (IllegalStateException expected) {
            refused = expected.getMessage().contains("no leave credit left");
        }
        check("refused", true, refused);
        check("pending file untouched", pendingBefore, String.join("|", lines(work.resolve("pendingleaves.csv"))));
        check("data file untouched", "0", creditsOf("23"));
        check("leaves.csv still empty", 0, lines(work.resolve("leaves.csv")).size());
    }

    private static void aStaleRowIsRefusedAfterTheFileChanged() throws IOException {
        start("a row that changed on disk is refused instead of processing the wrong request");
        LeaveService service = fixture("23,Sick Leave,2,Sick\r\n13,Emergency Leave,1,Family trip\r\n", "", 5, 0, 0);
        // The window showed row 0 as employee 23; the file is replaced underneath it.
        Files.write(work.resolve("pendingleaves.csv"),
                "13,Emergency Leave,1,Family trip\r\n".getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8));

        boolean refused = false;
        try {
            service.decide(0, new String[] {"23", "Sick Leave", "2", "Sick"}, true);
        } catch (IllegalArgumentException expected) {
            refused = expected.getMessage().contains("changed while this window was open");
        }
        check("refused", true, refused);
        check("no processed row was written", 0, lines(work.resolve("leaves.csv")).size());
        check("leave credits untouched", "5", creditsOf("23"));
    }

    private static void aRaggedEmployeeFileIsRefused() throws IOException {
        start("data.csv with a shifted row is refused instead of being rewritten");
        LeaveService service = fixture("23,Sick Leave,2,Sick\r\n", "", 5, 0, 0);
        // The shape a comma inside an address produces: one extra column on row 2.
        String shifted = employee("13", "Valencia", 5, 0, 0).replace(",Test,", ",Test Blk 5, Phase 2,");
        Files.write(work.resolve("data.csv"), (header() + "\r\n"
                + employee("23", "Racimo", 5, 0, 0) + "\r\n" + shifted + "\r\n").getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8));

        boolean refused = false;
        try {
            service.decide(0, true);
        } catch (IllegalStateException expected) {
            refused = expected.getMessage().contains("Fix the file before processing leaves");
        }
        check("refused", true, refused);
        check("pending file untouched", 1, lines(work.resolve("pendingleaves.csv")).size());
        check("leaves.csv still empty", 0, lines(work.resolve("leaves.csv")).size());
        check("shifted row kept its extra column (nothing rewritten)", 25,
                lines(work.resolve("data.csv")).get(2).split(",", -1).length);
    }

    private static void reasonWithACommaStaysInTheReasonColumn() throws IOException {
        start("a reason that contains a comma stays in the Reason column");
        LeaveService service = fixture("23,Sick Leave,2,Blk 5, Phase 2\r\n", "", 5, 0, 0);

        String[] processed = service.decide(0, true);

        check("reason rebuilt from the split fields", "Blk 5, Phase 2", processed[LeaveService.COLUMN_REASON]);
        check("approval still last", "Yes", processed[LeaveService.COLUMN_APPROVAL]);
        Object[] pendingCells = LeaveService.pendingTableRow(new String[] {"23", "Sick", "2", "Blk 5", " Phase 2"});
        check("pending table shows the whole reason", "Blk 5, Phase 2", String.valueOf(pendingCells[3]));
    }

    private static void windowsLineEndingsSurviveTheRewrite() throws IOException {
        start("CRLF files keep CRLF after the pending rewrite (no whole-file diff)");
        LeaveService service = fixture("23,Sick Leave,2,Sick\r\n13,Emergency Leave,1,Family trip\r\n", "", 5, 0, 0);

        service.decide(0, true);

        String pending = new String(Files.readAllBytes(work.resolve("pendingleaves.csv")), StandardCharsets.UTF_8);
        check("remaining line still ends with CRLF", true, pending.endsWith("\r\n"));
        check("no bare LF was introduced", false, pending.replace("\r\n", "").contains("\n"));
        String leaves = new String(Files.readAllBytes(work.resolve("leaves.csv")), StandardCharsets.UTF_8);
        check("appended row also uses CRLF", true, leaves.endsWith("\r\n"));
    }

Candidate policy review from prior submissions and current references

Status: research draft, not adopted or executable policy. The user has now invited candidate inference from prior submissions, with disclosure. This document records those candidates and their risks. It does not enable payroll calculations, attendance-hour derivation, approvals, or role-based access. No official MotorPH payroll rulebook or active grading rubric was found in the supplied set.

1. What the inspected MO-IT110 peer implementation says

The supplied peer review copy at /home/user/repo_review/full_repo/testingester-main/6/-/ contains an explicit, testable candidate model:

src/motorph/model/AttendanceRecord.java: first cutoff is days 1–15; second cutoff is day 16 through actual month end. Login from 08:00 through 08:10 is treated as 08:00; logout after 17:00 is capped at 17:00. It calculates elapsed time directly from those adjusted times and does not subtract a meal interval.
src/motorph/service/PayrollProcessor.java: the first cutoff has no deductions and net equals cutoff gross. On the second cutoff, it computes monthly contributions from the combined two-cutoff gross, computes withholding tax after those contributions, and subtracts the whole monthly deduction amount from the second-cutoff gross (floored at zero). Allowances are shown on the second-cutoff slip but excluded from net in that implementation.
src/motorph/model/Employee.java: gross is hourly rate times the calculated minutes. The course-project fixtures also supply semi-monthly and hourly rates.
The peer has substantial tests and CP2 compatibility comparisons, but its own behavior is still an implementation choice, not an authoritative MotorPH payroll rule.

Important defect/risk found in that candidate: an 08:00–17:00 record yields nine elapsed hours because the code caps at 17:00 but deducts no lunch. DOLE's source says normal work hours do not exceed eight hours a day and requires at least a 60-minute meal period off work; a pair of in/out times without a meal record cannot distinguish the unpaid break. The peer rule must not be copied as an hours-worked or overtime algorithm without resolving that mismatch.

The supplied peer review also records 473 of 476 comparison rows and 14 of 14 cutoff summaries matching the CP2 output; three row differences were ₱0.01 due to floating/half-centavo behavior. That is compatibility evidence, not legal-compliance evidence. See /home/user/repo_review/submission-comprehensive-report.md and /home/user/repo_review/submission-feature-pseudocode.md for the review context. No peer employee or government-ID data was copied into this app or document.

A public MO-IT110 repository surfaced the same 1–15 / 16–month-end pattern and second-cutoff deduction convention, but explicitly says its payroll tables/thresholds are copied from CP2 rather than independently verified. Treat it as corroboration of a course-project convention, not a company policy: https://github.com/fdtan/MO-IT110_OOP-MS2_TanFD.

2. Current official statutory references located

These sources can support statutory-component research, but they do not establish MotorPH's attendance import, pay-period, allowance, leave, or role policy:

Component	Source finding	Boundary before implementation
SSS	The SSS site publishes its contribution schedule effective Jan. 1, 2025: 15% total on MSC up to ₱35,000, split 5% employee / 10% employer; EC is employer-only. The schedule also distinguishes the MPF portion above ₱20,000.	Use the circular/table and verify every bracket and rounding boundary. Do not assume a new 2026 table without a newer official circular.
PhilHealth	The 2026 advisory states the 5% contribution rate effective Jan. 2025, with ₱10,000 floor and ₱100,000 ceiling. The 2025 employer advisory says use monthly basic salary and excludes overtime, allowances, 13th-month pay, bonuses and specified absence/undertime reductions from that base.	Confirm the formal-sector share split and exact payroll-period deduction method against the applicable circular.
Pag-IBIG	Circular 460 raises the Maximum Fund Salary to ₱10,000 effective February 2024; the employee rate is 1% at fund salary ≤₱1,500 and 2% above, while the employer rate is 2%.	Confirm applicable employee category and effective date; don't extrapolate to voluntary/other member types.
BIR withholding	Annex E to RR 11-2018 publishes daily, weekly, semi-monthly and monthly tables effective Jan. 1, 2023 onward.	The chosen tax base, payroll-period method, taxable allowances/benefits, year-end adjustment and rounding need explicit tests. A monthly-only example is not a semi-monthly payroll specification.
Hours/premiums	DOLE's official materials specify an eight-hour normal workday, a minimum 60-minute meal period off work, and statutory overtime/night/rest-day/holiday provisions.	The attendance schema lacks meal punches, a defined dayType enum, and an authoritative schedule/holiday assignment. Those facts must be supplied or explicitly selected as demo assumptions.
3. A net-pay reference found online — useful, but not a drop-in payroll engine

ph-payroll is the strongest technical reference located for statutory components: its README says it uses exact decimal arithmetic, effective-dated rules, source circulars, and fails closed outside covered periods; it documents support from 2026-01 because the 2026 PhilHealth rule is the most recent component. Its scope is monthly basic pay plus statutory contributions/tax, not attendance-hour computation, MotorPH's cutoff handling, leave treatment, or a payslip workflow. It is MIT-licensed and asks users to verify results before relying on it: https://github.com/earnieacts/ph-payroll.

Documented synthetic example from that reference

For monthly basic pay of ₱25,000, the library documents employee deductions of SSS ₱1,250, PhilHealth ₱625, Pag-IBIG ₱200, withholding tax ₱313.75, and net ₱22,611.25. A manual annualized arithmetic check gives taxable monthly income ₱22,925; annualized ₱275,100; 15% of the ₱25,100 annual amount above ₱250,000 is ₱3,765, or ₱313.75 per month. This is a reference example only—not this app's result or an approved MotorPH payslip.

Two caveats need reconciliation before adoption:

The BIR Annex E monthly table uses rounded peso breakpoints (₱20,833 and 15% above that), which yields ₱313.80 for ₱22,925 when read directly. The library's annualized method gives ₱313.75. The ₱0.05 difference needs a verified BIR-period/rounding interpretation and an independent approved example.
In the library source, employerCost is the sum of employer contributions (₱3,355 in its ₱25,000 example), not basic salary plus those contributions. Do not display that field as total employer payroll cost without changing/renaming it.

A second 2026 calculator repository also advertises complete deductions and net pay, but the repository surfaced with a single commit and no comparable validation evidence. It is a secondary cross-check, not a preferred authority: https://github.com/tenzerodev/rdcruz-ph-payroll.

4. Workflow/role patterns in peer submissions

The supplied peer corpus shows patterns, not a consistent permission contract: employee requests, an admin/manager review screen, approve/reject outcomes, leave-credit changes, and separate payroll/admin roles appear in different projects. Folder 9's LeaveService.java performs approve/reject and updates request files plus leave-credit counters transactionally, but the service itself has no authorization check. Other projects use different role labels and access patterns. These examples are not sufficient to invent secure Firebase roles or reviewer boundaries.

5. Safe recommendation / next decision
Keep production-style payroll, attendance-hour reports, approvals and reviewer controls disabled.
If the project needs a classroom demonstration before official rules are confirmed, expose the folder-6 conventions only as a clearly labelled, synthetic candidate profile, after the user confirms the meal-break, cutoff, deduction timing, allowance, and net-floor choices. Preserve the official statutory calculator as a separately sourced component and reconcile BIR withholding first.
Mark any inferred role/workflow matrix as a proposal based on the peer corpus; do not publish it as live authorization until the user approves the exact employee, HR/approver, payroll, and admin boundaries.
Keep the external payroll library as a comparison source, not a dependency or oracle; reproduce independent golden values and cite official circulars in this project before enabling any calculation.

Research update

I found a concrete course-project candidate, but not an approved MotorPH policy. The supplied folder-6 project uses cutoffs 1–15 and 16–month-end; grants a login grace period through 8:10; caps logout at 17:00; takes monthly deductions from the second cutoff; and excludes displayed allowances from net pay. Those are project-specific choices, not company rules.

A key flaw: its 8:00–17:00 attendance calculation counts nine hours because it doesn’t deduct a meal break. DOLE’s Book III describes an eight-hour normal workday and a meal period of at least 60 minutes off work, so those two attendance times alone don’t establish hours worked. DOLE Book III

I also found a current statutory net-pay reference, ph-payroll. Its documented synthetic example gives ₱22,611.25 net from ₱25,000 monthly basic pay, but it is not an end-to-end attendance or cutoff payroll system. Its annualized withholding result is ₱313.75; reading the rounded threshold in the BIR monthly table gives ₱313.80 for the same taxable amount. That ₱0.05 difference needs resolving before using it as an oracle. The library’s employerCost field is employer contributions only, not salary plus contributions. Library example · BIR Annex E

The SSS and PhilHealth sources are useful for statutory components, but they don’t settle MotorPH’s cutoff, attendance, allowance, or leave policies. SSS contribution schedule · PhilHealth 2026 advisory

I recorded the findings, source paths, limits, and candidate decisions in docs/candidate-policy-review.md, and updated the acceptance baseline and roadmap. It’s open in the file viewer.

                                                          2
1.​   Database Overview
      The MotorPH Payroll System database is built in a way to allow users to automate,
      organise, and streamline MotorPH payroll processes systematically to provide the
      prerogative of having minimal struggle in handling the payroll operations so that users
      may allocate efforts unto more substantially demanding tasks. Through the
      centralisation of most payroll-related data into a singular, secure, and scalable
      repository, the system facilitates rapid data retrieval and processing, which becomes
      indispensable for timely salary computations, tax management, and adherence to legal
      contributions and compliance. Thus, for this instance, we deliver an expectation that
      this database will not just bring about changes in improvement with data derivation
      and the alleviation of unnecessary exertion but also an effective means through which
      future growth of the organisation may be facilitated at incorporation through adaptive
      mechanisms for data expansion.
         1.​ Employee Management – Captures, updates, and maintains employee records,
             including employment status, department affiliation, salary structure, and
             personal information; this module serves as the primary reference for all
             modules, with nearly every module being eventually tied back to this module’s
             unique identifier.
         2.​ Payroll Processing – Automates payroll computation, taking into account
             attendance records, salary adjustments, overtime hours, tax deductions, and
             government-mandated contributions (SSS, PhilHealth, Pag-IBIG, Withholding
             Tax). The system

import java.util.Scanner;

public class PayrollCalculator {

    public static void calculatePayroll() {

        Scanner input = new Scanner(System.in);

        System.out.println("=== Payroll Calculator ===");

        System.out.print("Enter Hours Worked: ");
        double hoursWorked = input.nextDouble();

        System.out.print("Enter Hourly Rate: ");
        double hourlyRate = input.nextDouble();

        double grossSalary = hoursWorked * hourlyRate;

        double sss = grossSalary * 0.045;
        double philhealth = grossSalary * 0.02;
        double pagibig = 100;

        double totalDeductions = sss + philhealth + pagibig;
        double netSalary = grossSalary - totalDeductions;

        System.out.println("\n--- Payroll Details ---");
        System.out.println("Gross Salary: " + grossSalary);
        System.out.println("SSS Deduction: " + sss);
        System.out.println("PhilHealth Deduction: " + philhealth);
        System.out.println("Pag-IBIG Deduction: " + pagibig);
        System.out.println("Total Deductions: " + totalDeductions);
        System.out.println("Net Salary: " + netSalary);
    }
}

package motorph.deduction;

import java.math.BigDecimal;

/**
 * SSS contribution from the compensation range table used in CP2.
 * The first threshold the monthly gross is below sets the contribution;
 * at 24,750 and above the contribution is 1,125.
 */
public class SSSDeduction extends Deduction {

    private static final BigDecimal[] THRESHOLDS = amounts(
        "3250", "3750", "4250", "4750", "5250", "5750", "6250", "6750", "7250", "7750",
        "8250", "8750", "9250", "9750", "10250", "10750", "11250", "11750", "12250", "12750",
        "13250", "13750", "14250", "14750", "15250", "15750", "16250", "16750", "17250", "17750",
        "18250", "18750", "19250", "19750", "20250", "20750", "21250", "21750", "22250", "22750",
        "23250", "23750", "24250", "24750"
    );

    private static final BigDecimal[] CONTRIBUTIONS = amounts(
        "135", "157.5", "180", "202.5", "225", "247.5", "270", "292.5", "315", "337.5",
        "360", "382.5", "405", "427.5", "450", "472.5", "495", "517.5", "540", "562.5",
        "585", "607.5", "630", "652.5", "675", "697.5", "720", "742.5", "765", "787.5",
        "810", "832.5", "855", "877.5", "900", "922.5", "945", "967.5", "990", "1012.5",
        "1035", "1057.5", "1080", "1102.5"
    );

    private static final BigDecimal MAX_CONTRIBUTION = new BigDecimal("1125");

    public SSSDeduction() {
        super("SSS");
    }

    /** @param baseAmount combined monthly gross */
    @Override
    public BigDecimal computeDeduction(BigDecimal baseAmount) {
        validateBaseAmount(baseAmount);
        for (int i = 0; i < THRESHOLDS.length; i++) {
            if (baseAmount.compareTo(THRESHOLDS[i]) < 0) {
                return CONTRIBUTIONS[i];
            }
        }
        return MAX_CONTRIBUTION;
    }

    private static BigDecimal[] amounts(String... values) {
        BigDecimal[] result = new BigDecimal[values.length];
        for (int i = 0; i < values.length; i++) {
            result[i] = new BigDecimal(values[i]);
        }
        return result;
    }
}
### /home/user/repo_review/full_repo/testingester-main/6/-/src/motorph/deduction/PhilHealthDeduction.java
package motorph.deduction;

import java.math.BigDecimal;

/**
 * PhilHealth employee share: 3% of monthly gross, split 50/50 with the
 * employer, so the employee pays 1.5%. Minimum 150, maximum 900 (CP2 rules).
 */
public class PhilHealthDeduction extends Deduction {

    private static final BigDecimal PREMIUM_RATE   = new BigDecimal("0.03");
    private static final BigDecimal EMPLOYEE_SHARE = new BigDecimal("2");
    private static final BigDecimal MINIMUM        = new BigDecimal("150");
    private static final BigDecimal MAXIMUM        = new BigDecimal("900");

    public PhilHealthDeduction() {
        super("PhilHealth");
    }

    /** @param baseAmount combined monthly gross */
    @Override
    public BigDecimal computeDeduction(BigDecimal baseAmount) {
        validateBaseAmount(baseAmount);
        BigDecimal share = baseAmount.multiply(PREMIUM_RATE).divide(EMPLOYEE_SHARE);
        return share.max(MINIMUM).min(MAXIMUM);
    }
}
### /home/user/repo_review/full_repo/testingester-main/6/-/src/motorph/deduction/PagIbigDeduction.java
package motorph.deduction;

import java.math.BigDecimal;

/**
 * Pag-IBIG contribution: 1% if monthly gross is 1,500 or less, otherwise 2%,
 * capped at 100 (CP2 rules).
 */
public class PagIbigDeduction extends Deduction {

    private static final BigDecimal LOW_RATE      = new BigDecimal("0.01");
    private static final BigDecimal HIGH_RATE     = new BigDecimal("0.02");
    private static final BigDecimal LOW_THRESHOLD = new BigDecimal("1500");
    private static final BigDecimal MAXIMUM       = new BigDecimal("100");

    public PagIbigDeduction() {
        super("Pag-IBIG");
    }

    /** @param baseAmount combined monthly gross */
    @Override
    public BigDecimal computeDeduction(BigDecimal baseAmount) {
        validateBaseAmount(baseAmount);
        BigDecimal rate = baseAmount.compareTo(LOW_THRESHOLD) <= 0 ? LOW_RATE : HIGH_RATE;
        return baseAmount.multiply(rate).min(MAXIMUM);
    }
}
### /home/user/repo_review/full_repo/testingester-main/6/-/src/motorph/deduction/WithholdingTaxDeduction.java
package motorph.deduction;

import java.math.BigDecimal;

/**
 * Withholding tax from the BIR monthly brackets used in CP2.
 * <p>
 * Unlike the other deductions, the base amount is <b>taxable income</b>:
 * monthly gross minus SSS, PhilHealth, and Pag-IBIG. PayrollProcessor computes
 * those contributions first, then passes the taxable income here.
 * </p>
 */
public class WithholdingTaxDeduction extends Deduction {

    // Upper limit of each bracket (inclusive)
    private static final BigDecimal BRACKET_1_MAX = new BigDecimal("20832");
    private static final BigDecimal BRACKET_2_MAX = new BigDecimal("33332");
    private static final BigDecimal BRACKET_3_MAX = new BigDecimal("66666");
    private static final BigDecimal BRACKET_4_MAX = new BigDecimal("166666");
    private static final BigDecimal BRACKET_5_MAX = new BigDecimal("666666");

    // Amount over which the bracket rate applies
    private static final BigDecimal BRACKET_2_FLOOR = new BigDecimal("20833");
    private static final BigDecimal BRACKET_3_FLOOR = new BigDecimal("33333");
    private static final BigDecimal BRACKET_4_FLOOR = new BigDecimal("66667");
    private static final BigDecimal BRACKET_5_FLOOR = new BigDecimal("166667");
    private static final BigDecimal BRACKET_6_FLOOR = new BigDecimal("666667");

    // Fixed tax at the start of each bracket
    private static final BigDecimal BRACKET_3_BASE_TAX = new BigDecimal("2500");
    private static final BigDecimal BRACKET_4_BASE_TAX = new BigDecimal("10833");
    private static final BigDecimal BRACKET_5_BASE_TAX = new BigDecimal("40833.33");
    private static final BigDecimal BRACKET_6_BASE_TAX = new BigDecimal("200833.33");

    // Rate on the amount over the floor
    private static final BigDecimal BRACKET_2_RATE = new BigDecimal("0.20");
    private static final BigDecimal BRACKET_3_RATE = new BigDecimal("0.25");
    private static final BigDecimal BRACKET_4_RATE = new BigDecimal("0.30");
    private static final BigDecimal BRACKET_5_RATE = new BigDecimal("0.32");
    private static final BigDecimal BRACKET_6_RATE = new BigDecimal("0.35");

    public WithholdingTaxDeduction() {
        super("Withholding Tax");
    }

    /** @param baseAmount taxable income (monthly gross minus SSS, PhilHealth, Pag-IBIG) */
    @Override
    public BigDecimal computeDeduction(BigDecimal baseAmount) {
        validateBaseAmount(baseAmount);
        if (baseAmount.compareTo(BRACKET_1_MAX) <= 0) {
            return BigDecimal.ZERO;
        }
        if (baseAmount.compareTo(BRACKET_2_MAX) <= 0) {
            return baseAmount.subtract(BRACKET_2_FLOOR).multiply(BRACKET_2_RATE);
        }
        if (baseAmount.compareTo(BRACKET_3_MAX) <= 0) {
            return BRACKET_3_BASE_TAX.add(baseAmount.subtract(BRACKET_3_FLOOR).multiply(BRACKET_3_RATE));
        }
        if (baseAmount.compareTo(BRACKET_4_MAX) <= 0) {
            return BRACKET_4_BASE_TAX.add(baseAmount.subtract(BRACKET_4_FLOOR).multiply(BRACKET_4_RATE));
        }
        if (baseAmount.compareTo(BRACKET_5_MAX) <= 0) {
            return BRACKET_5_BASE_TAX.add(baseAmount.subtract(BRACKET_5_FLOOR).multiply(BRACKET_5_RATE));
        }
        return BRACKET_6_BASE_TAX.add(baseAmount.subtract(BRACKET_6_FLOOR).multiply(BRACKET_6_RATE));
    }
}
### /home/user/repo_review/full_repo/testingester-main/6/-/src/motorph/service/PayrollProcessor.java
package motorph.service;

import java.math.BigDecimal;
import java.math.MathContext;
import java.time.LocalDate;
import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.LinkedHashMap;
import java.util.LinkedHashSet;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Map;
import java.util.Set;
import java.util.TreeMap;
import motorph.deduction.Deduction;
import motorph.model.AttendanceRecord;
import motorph.model.Employee;
import motorph.model.Payslip;

/**
 * Runs the payroll workflow: hours -> gross pay -> deductions -> net pay -> Payslip.
 * <p>
 * Works only with parent types (Employee, Deduction), so there are no checks on
 * employee status or deduction type. The deductions are passed into the
 * constructor: a list of contributions computed on monthly gross (SSS,
 * PhilHealth, Pag-IBIG) and a separate withholding tax computed on taxable
 * income. Adding a new government contribution only needs a new Deduction
 * subclass in that list.
 * </p>
 * <p>
 * Cutoff rule (from CP2): the 1st cutoff (days 1-15) has no deductions and net
 * pay equals gross pay. The 2nd cutoff (day 16 to month end) takes the whole
 * month's deductions once, computed on the combined gross of both cutoffs.
 * </p>
 */
public class PayrollProcessor {

    // === SUMMARY KEYS (computePayrollSummary) ===
    public static final String SUMMARY_TOTAL_EMPLOYEES  = "Total Employees";
    public static final String SUMMARY_TOTAL_GROSS      = "Total Gross Pay";
    public static final String SUMMARY_TOTAL_DEDUCTIONS = "Total Deductions";
    public static final String SUMMARY_TOTAL_NET        = "Total Net Pay";
    public static final String SUMMARY_AVERAGE_NET      = "Average Net Pay";

    // Cutoff labels come from AttendanceRecord.getCutoffLabel(), e.g. "June 16-30, 2024"
    private static final String SECOND_CUTOFF_MARKER  = " 16-";
    private static final String SECOND_CUTOFF_PATTERN = " 16-\\d{2},";
    private static final String FIRST_CUTOFF_DAYS     = " 1-15,";

    private final List<Deduction> contributions;
    private final Deduction withholdingTax;

    /**
     * @param contributions  deductions computed on monthly gross, in payslip order
     * @param withholdingTax deduction computed last, on taxable income
     */
    public PayrollProcessor(List<Deduction> contributions, Deduction withholdingTax) {
        if (contributions == null || withholdingTax == null) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Contributions and withholding tax are required.");
        }
        for (Deduction contribution : contributions) {
            if (contribution == null) {
                throw new IllegalArgumentException("Contribution list must not contain empty entries.");
            }
        }
        this.contributions = List.copyOf(contributions);
        this.withholdingTax = withholdingTax;
    }

    /** Returns the deduction names in payslip order (contributions, then tax). */
    public List<String> getDeductionNames() {
        List<String> names = new ArrayList<>();
        for (Deduction contribution : contributions) {
            names.add(contribution.getName());
        }
        names.add(withholdingTax.getName());
        return names;
    }

    // === CUTOFFS AND HOURS ===

    /**
     * Returns every cutoff label found in the attendance records, oldest first.
     * Used to fill the cutoff selection list.
     */
    public List<String> getAvailableCutoffs(Map<String, List<AttendanceRecord>> attendanceByEmployee) {
        Map<LocalDate, String> labelsByDate = new TreeMap<>();
        for (List<AttendanceRecord> records : attendanceByEmployee.values()) {
            for (AttendanceRecord record : records) {
                labelsByDate.putIfAbsent(record.getDate(), record.getCutoffLabel());
            }
        }
        Set<String> cutoffs = new LinkedHashSet<>(labelsByDate.values());
        return new ArrayList<>(cutoffs);
    }

    /**
     * Sums the hours worked in one cutoff.
     *
     * @param records     one employee's attendance records
     * @param cutoffLabel the cutoff to total, for example "June 1-15, 2024"
     * @return total hours, or 0 if no records match
     */
    public double computeHoursForCutoff(List<AttendanceRecord> records, String cutoffLabel) {
        long minutes = 0;
        if (records != null) {
            for (AttendanceRecord record : records) {
                if (record.getCutoffLabel().equals(cutoffLabel)) {
                    minutes += record.computeMinutesWorked();
                }
            }
        }
        return minutes / 60.0;
    }

    /**
     * Returns the employees with no hours in the cutoff, so the GUI can warn once
     * before they are computed with 0 hours (CP2 behavior).
     */
    public List<Employee> findEmployeesWithoutAttendance(List<Employee> employees,
            Map<String, List<AttendanceRecord>> attendanceByEmployee, String cutoffLabel) {
        List<Employee> missing = new ArrayList<>();
        for (Employee employee : employees) {
            List<AttendanceRecord> records = attendanceByEmployee.get(employee.getEmployeeId());
            if (computeHoursForCutoff(records, cutoffLabel) <= 0) {
                missing.add(employee);
            }
        }
        return missing;
    }

    // === DEDUCTIONS AND NET PAY ===

    /**
     * Computes each deduction for one month, in order: every contribution on the
     * monthly gross, then withholding tax on taxable income (monthly gross minus
     * the contributions, floored at 0). No type checks: each Deduction runs its
     * own formula.
     *
     * @param monthlyGross combined gross of the 1st and 2nd cutoff
     * @return deduction name to amount, in payslip order
     */
    public Map<String, BigDecimal> computeDeductionBreakdown(BigDecimal monthlyGross) {
        Map<String, BigDecimal> breakdown = new LinkedHashMap<>();
        BigDecimal taxableIncome = monthlyGross;
        for (Deduction contribution : contributions) {
            BigDecimal amount = contribution.computeDeduction(monthlyGross);
            breakdown.put(contribution.getName(), amount);
            taxableIncome = taxableIncome.subtract(amount);
        }
        breakdown.put(withholdingTax.getName(), withholdingTax.computeDeduction(taxableIncome.max(BigDecimal.ZERO)));
        return breakdown;
    }

    /**
     * Totals all government deductions for one month: the sum of
     * computeDeductionBreakdown(), so the total always matches the itemized lines.
     */
    public BigDecimal computeTotalDeductions(BigDecimal monthlyGross) {
        return sum(computeDeductionBreakdown(monthlyGross));
    }

    /** Net pay = cutoff gross - deductions, never below 0. */
    public BigDecimal computeNetPay(BigDecimal cutoffGross, BigDecimal totalDeductions) {
        return cutoffGross.subtract(totalDeductions).max(BigDecimal.ZERO);
    }

    // === PAYSLIPS ===

    /**
     * Builds the payslip for one employee and one cutoff ("One Employee" mode).
     * Accepts any Employee subtype; allowances come from the subclass's own
     * computeAllowances().
     *
     * @param employee    the employee to pay
     * @param records     that employee's attendance records (may be empty)
     * @param cutoffLabel the cutoff to pay
     */
    public Payslip generatePayslip(Employee employee, List<AttendanceRecord> records, String cutoffLabel) {
        if (employee == null || cutoffLabel == null || cutoffLabel.trim().isEmpty()) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Employee and cutoff are required.");
        }
        double hoursWorked = computeHoursForCutoff(records, cutoffLabel);
        BigDecimal grossPay = employee.computeGrossPay(hoursWorked);

        Map<String, BigDecimal> breakdown;
        BigDecimal allowances;
        if (isSecondCutoff(cutoffLabel)) {
            // Monthly items are settled once, here: deductions on the combined gross of both cutoffs,
            // and the month's allowances (listed only; not added to net pay, as in CP2).
            double firstCutoffHours = computeHoursForCutoff(records, getFirstCutoffLabel(cutoffLabel));
            BigDecimal monthlyGross = employee.computeGrossPay(firstCutoffHours + hoursWorked);
            breakdown = computeDeductionBreakdown(monthlyGross);
            allowances = employee.computeAllowances();
        } else {
            breakdown = zeroBreakdown();
            allowances = BigDecimal.ZERO;
        }
        BigDecimal netPay = computeNetPay(grossPay, sum(breakdown));
        return new Payslip(employee, cutoffLabel, hoursWorked, grossPay, breakdown, allowances, netPay);
    }

    /**
     * Runs payroll for every employee in one cutoff ("All Employees" mode).
     * Same steps for every Employee subtype.
     */
    public List<Payslip> processPayroll(List<Employee> employees,
            Map<String, List<AttendanceRecord>> attendanceByEmployee, String cutoffLabel) {
        List<Payslip> payslips = new ArrayList<>();
        for (Employee employee : employees) {
            payslips.add(generatePayslip(employee, attendanceByEmployee.get(employee.getEmployeeId()), cutoffLabel));
        }
        return payslips;
    }

    /**
     * Totals a list of payslips: employee count, total gross, total deductions,
     * total net, and average net. Uses full-precision amounts (as CP2 did), so
     * the totals are rounded only when displayed.
     *
     * @throws IllegalArgumentException if the list is empty
     */
    public Map<String, BigDecimal> computePayrollSummary(List<Payslip> payslips) {
        if (payslips == null || payslips.isEmpty()) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("There are no payslips to summarize.");
        }
        BigDecimal totalGross = BigDecimal.ZERO;
        BigDecimal totalDeductions = BigDecimal.ZERO;
        BigDecimal totalNet = BigDecimal.ZERO;
        for (Payslip payslip : payslips) {
            totalGross = totalGross.add(payslip.getGrossPay());
            totalDeductions = totalDeductions.add(payslip.getTotalDeductions());
            totalNet = totalNet.add(payslip.getNetPay());
        }
        BigDecimal count = BigDecimal.valueOf(payslips.size());

        Map<String, BigDecimal> summary = new LinkedHashMap<>();
        summary.put(SUMMARY_TOTAL_EMPLOYEES, count);
        summary.put(SUMMARY_TOTAL_GROSS, totalGross);
        summary.put(SUMMARY_TOTAL_DEDUCTIONS, totalDeductions);
        summary.put(SUMMARY_TOTAL_NET, totalNet);
        summary.put(SUMMARY_AVERAGE_NET, totalNet.divide(count, MathContext.DECIMAL128));

### 4.4 Important visual-only schema details

The image makes several details especially clear:

1. `Schedule` contains `restDayID` rather than the `restDay` `SET` column described in the Data Dictionary and prose table list.
2. A standalone `Rest Day` table exists in the ERD, with seven weekday Boolean fields.
3. `Employee` in the ERD does not visibly contain `departmentID` or `governmentID`, although these are in the Data Dictionary's Employee field list.
4. `Address` in the ERD visibly contains `regionID`, although the Database Design prose definition of Address lists only `addressID`, `cityID`, `building`, `street`, and `postalCode`.
5. `Supervisor` in the ERD visibly contains `departmentID`, although the Database Design prose definition of Supervisor lists only `supervisorID` and `employeeID`.
6. `Rates` visibly marks `implementationYear` as the primary key, although the Database Design's table constraint section says the Rates table has no primary key, and the Data Dictionary does not list `implementationYear` at all.
7. `Government Deductibles` visibly shows both `monthID` and `governmentID` as key fields, consistent with a composite key.
8. `Contributions` visibly shows `(governmentID, contributor)` as a composite key.
9. `Government Tally` visibly shows `summaryID` and `contributor` as key fields, although the Data Dictionary calls `summaryID` its primary key “(assumed)”.

The exact consequences of these discrepancies are not resolved by the three documents. See [Section 16](#16-cross-document-discrepancies-and-unresolved-design-questions).

## 5. Visual reconstruction of the data-flow diagrams

**Source locations:** Data Flow Diagram PDF, pages 2–6. The actual diagrams are image-based; the following sections convert their labels, arrows, and visual groupings into text.

### 5.1 DFD notation and reading conventions

The worksheet expressly calls for **Gene & Sarson notation**. The diagrams use:

- rounded or rectangular cyan/teal shapes for external entities such as Employee, Supervisor, Human Resources, Payroll Staff, and System Admin;
- yellow/orange-topped process shapes for system processes, numbered `0.0`, `1.0`, `2.0`, `3.0`, and the decomposed Level 2 process numbers;
- lavender/purple data-store shapes, generally labelled with a `D` identifier and a store name; and
- directed connectors, with text labels describing the data or action moving along each connector.

The diagrams are process-and-data-flow views. They do not show every physical database column, and a data store in a DFD is not necessarily a one-to-one representation of a single relational table. The DFD uses larger logical stores such as `Employee Repository`, `Logs`, and `Payroll`, then subdivides them into named components in the Level 2 diagrams.

### 5.2 External entities

Five external actors appear across the DFDs:

| Actor | Role represented in the diagrams |
|---|---|
| **Employee** | Supplies attendance and time-in/time-out information; views employee information and payslips; views personal payslip information in the payroll Level 2 view. |
| **Supervisor** | Views team-member information and team payslips; adjusts team attendance; handles leave requests; handles or initiates leave monetisation; submits team-member wage and adjustment information; views team benefits/deductions. |
| **Human Resources** | Updates employee details; views employee and payroll details; participates in PII access approval and PII viewing/updating on approval; views relevant employee, attendance, and leave information. |
| **Payroll Staff** | Views and verifies employee and payroll details; views employee government PII on approval; updates payroll, payslip, benefits, and deductibles; validates and verifies payroll details and monthly reports. |
| **System Admin** | Manages configurations and users; views all employee information; participates in PII access approval; handles backup and archival; initiates the annual archival prompt; updates optional/system-controlled values in the detailed payroll diagram. |

The actors are distinct. The diagrams do not collapse HR, Payroll Staff, Supervisor, and System Admin into one generic administrator role.

### 5.3 Data stores in the DFD

| Identifier | Store name | Diagram placement / contents represented |
|---|---|---|
| `D1` | Employee Repository | Level 1 store for employee information. |
| `D1.1` | Employee Address | Level 2 subdivision for employee address data. |
| `D1.2` | Job Profile | Level 2 subdivision for employee job-profile data. |
| `D1.3` | Personally Identifiable Information | Level 2 subdivision for PII, shown beside Government Info Access. |
| `D2` | Logs | Level 1 store for operational logs, expanded into attendance, leave, changelog, and leave-monetisation logs. |
| `D2.1` | Attendance / Attendance Logs | Attendance and time activity used for work-hour derivation and timesheet validation. |
| `D2.2` | Leave / Leave Logs | Leave records used to derive paid-leave details and support leave management. |
| `D2.3` | Changelog / Changelogs | Employee-information change history. |
| `D2.4` | Leave Monetisation Logs | History of leave credits converted to monetary value. |
| `D3` | Payroll | Level 1 store containing wage, payroll, payslip, and benefits/deductibles information. |
| `D3.1` | Wage | Basic remunerative values and wage values. |
| `D3.2` | Benefits & Deductibles | Benefit and deduction values, including adjustments and computed deductions. |
| `D3.3` | Tax Table & Rates | Tax table and rates used to compute contributions. |
| `D3.4` | Payslip | Generated payslip records. |
| `D3.5` | Monthly Summary Report | Generated monthly summary report. |
| `D4` | Cold Storage | Destination for old logs and payroll records held for later compression. |

The Level 1 diagram names `D1 Employee Repository`, `D2 Logs`, `D3 Payroll`, and `D4 Cold Storage`. The Level 2 diagrams split the first three into more granular stores. These identifiers should be preserved when discussing the submitted diagrams.

### 5.4 Context-level DFD (`LV0: Context Diagram`)

**Source image:** DFD PDF, page 2. The context diagram represents the entire `MotorPH Payroll System` as one process, numbered `0.0`, surrounded by the five external entities.

#### 5.4.1 Employee flows

- **Employee → MotorPH Payroll System:** `Attendance and Time In/Out`.
- **MotorPH Payroll System → Employee:** `View Employee Information` (the information is supplied by the system in response to the employee's view/access activity).

The diagram therefore presents the employee as both an input source for attendance/time data and a recipient of employee information and payslip output.

- **Supervisor → MotorPH Payroll System:** `Adjust Team Attendance`.

The diagram distinguishes the supervisor's ability to view team information from the supervisor's submission or handling of team attendance, leave, monetisation, and benefits/deductions matters.

- **Human Resources → MotorPH Payroll System:** `Update PII (On Approval)`.

The approval condition is part of the flow labels. The diagram does not present PII viewing or updating as unrestricted operations.

**Important difference:** The Data Dictionary marks `holidayName` and `holidayDate` individually as unique fields. The Database Design instead specifies a composite unique combination of name and date. ### 11.4 `Months`

| Column | Data type / size | Description | Data Dictionary constraint |
|---|---|---|---|
| `monthID` | `Enum` | Unique month identifier. | The field is described as an enum; no additional field-level constraint stated. |
| `monthlyWorkdays` | `Integer`, size 2 | Number of workdays in the month. | `Min(1)`, `Max(31)`. |

**Database Design constraints:** PK `monthID`; no FK; no separate unique constraint because `monthID` is already an Enum; `monthlyWorkdays` must be between 1 and 31.

### 11.5 `Rates`

**Purpose:** Holds statutory rate values for Pag-ibig, PhilHealth, and SSS.

| Column | Data type / size | Description | Data Dictionary constraint |
|---|---|---|---|
| `piEmployerRate` | `Decimal(5,3)` | Global employer Pag-ibig rate. | `Min(0)`; `NOT NULL`. |
| `piEmployeeRate` | `Decimal(5,3)` | Global employee Pag-ibig rate. | `Min(0)`; `NOT NULL`. |
| `piMaxContribution` | `Decimal(5,3)` | Maximum Pag-ibig contribution. | `Min(0)`; `NOT NULL`. |
| `phRate` | `Decimal(5,3)` | Global PhilHealth rate. | `Min(0)`; `NOT NULL`. |
| `sssRate` | `Decimal(5,3)` | Global SSS rate. | `Min(0)`; `NOT NULL`. |

**Database Design additional field:** The Database Design prose table and ERD include `implementationYear`, data type `SmallInt` (shown as size 4 in the diagram), described as the year the rates were implemented. The Data Dictionary omits this field.

**Database Design constraint conflict:** Its prose table says PK `None`, FK `None`, Unique `None`; the check-constraint text says all fields must be provided (`NOT NULL`) and rates must be greater than or equal to zero. The ERD, however, visibly marks `implementationYear` as `PK`. The documents do not resolve whether implementation year is intended to identify each rate set.

**DFD role:** `D3.3 Tax Table & Rates` provides the rates used by Process `2.4 Government Deductibles` to compute contributions. The System Admin has an `Update Rates (opt*)` flow to the store.

### 11.6 `Tax Table`

| Column | Data type / size | Description | Data Dictionary constraint |
|---|---|---|---|
| `taxBracket` | `Integer` | Identifier for the tax bracket. | `Min(1)`; Primary Key. |
| `minCompensation` | `Decimal(19,4)` | Minimum income for the bracket. | `Min(0)`; `NOT NULL` in the Database Design constraints. |
| `maxCompensation` | `Decimal(19,4)` | Maximum income for the bracket. | `Min(0)`; `NOT NULL` in the Database Design constraints. |
| `bracketWidth` | `Decimal(19,4)` | Income range width for the bracket. | `Min(0)`. |
| `taxRate` | `Decimal(19,4)` | Tax rate for the bracket. | `Min(0)`; `NOT NULL` in the Database Design constraints. |

**Database Design constraints:** PK `taxBracket`; no FK; `taxBracket` uniquely identifies the withholding-tax criteria and consequent requirement. The check-constraint wording says `taxBracket` must “at least have and be greater than 1” (the source wording is unclear), that `minCompensation`, `maxCompensation`, and `taxRate` must be present, and that monetary values must be non-negative.

**Unresolved wording:** The Data Dictionary's `Min(1)` indicates a minimum of 1. The Database Design's prose has a malformed phrase that could be read as “at least have and be greater than 1”. It is unsafe to silently convert this to `>= 1` or `> 1` without an implementation decision.

### 11.7 `Leave Type`

**Purpose:** Defines the leave categories and their accrual rules.

| Column | Data type / size | Description | Data Dictionary constraint |
|---|---|---|---|
| `leaveType` | `Enum` | Classification of leave. | `NOT NULL`. |
| `mandatory` | `Boolean` | Indicates whether the leave type is mandatory. | No additional constraint stated. |
| `defaultAccrualRate` | `Decimal(4,2)` | Standard rate at which leave accrues for this type. | `Min(0)`. |
| `accrualFrequency` | `Enum` | Frequency of leave accrual. | No additional constraint stated. |
| `maxAccrual` | `Decimal(4,2)` | Maximum allowable accrual for the leave type. | `Min(0)`. |

7. The `Payroll` record links to the wage record through `wageID`.

The source uses both `Wage` and `Earnings` as naming conventions: `D3.1 Wage` is the DFD store name, while the relational table is called `Earnings` and holds `wageID`. The relationship matrix states Payroll → Earnings is 1:1.

### 14.6 Government deduction and contribution trace

1. The employee's Government record holds the identifiers used for government-related payroll processing.
2. `D3.3 Tax Table & Rates` stores the tax bracket and contribution-rate reference information.
3. System Admin has an `Update Rates (opt*)` flow in the Payroll Level 2 DFD.
4. Process `2.4 Government Deductibles` utilises rates to compute contributions.
5. It appends computed information to `D3.2 Benefits & Deductibles` through `Append to Deductibles`.
6. The relational `Government Deductibles` table holds employer contribution, employee contribution, and withholding tax by government record and month.
7. The `Contributions` table stores specific PhilHealth, Pag-ibig, and SSS amounts with a contributor identifier.
8. `Deductibles` stores the government link and total deductions.
9. `Government Tally` holds overall contribution totals by contributor and is linked to `Summary`.
10. The monthly summary compilation process collates payroll and contribution information and generates a Monthly Summary Report.

The table names and relationships distinguish individual government identifiers, monthly deductible amounts, contributor-specific contribution values, and monthly tally totals. The documents do not give the exact reconciliation formula between Government Deductibles, Contributions, Deductibles, Government Tally, and Summary, so the precise arithmetic relationship must not be assumed.

### 14.7 Basic payroll computation and payslip generation

1. Process `2.5 Basic Payroll Computation` receives Time Activity from Timesheet Validation.
2. It retrieves basic remunerative values from `D3.1 Wage`.
3. It applies adjustments from `D3.2 Benefits & Deductibles`.
4. It computes `Net Pay and Constituents` and sends them to `2.6 Payslip Generation & Distribution`.
5. Payroll Staff can `View, Validate, and Verify Payroll Details` at the computation stage.
6. Process `2.6` appends the payslip to `D3.4 Payslip`.
7. Employee can view personal payslip information, Supervisor can view team information, and HR can view payslip/report information.
8. The `Payslip` relational table records pay-period start and end dates, standard hours, overtime hours, holiday overtime hours, PTO hours, undertime, days worked, holidays worked, rest days worked, and gross income.
9. `Payroll.netPay` records final pay after deductions; the Database Design says `hourlyRate`, `dailyRate`, and `netPay` must be non-null.

- hourly, daily, or monthly salary conversion;
- ordinary overtime;
- holiday overtime;
- holiday pay;
- rest-day pay;
- paid time off compensation;
- undertime;
- benefits totals;
- deduction totals;
- withholding tax;
- SSS, PhilHealth, or Pag-ibig contributions;
- employer versus employee contribution shares;
- government disbursement totals; or
- employee/employer disbursement totals.

The schema provides fields where amounts are stored. The DFD identifies which processes use those amounts. Neither gives the arithmetic rules.

### 17.3 No actual rate schedules or tax brackets

The `Rates` and `Tax Table` tables define the places where rates and brackets are held. The PDFs do not provide actual statutory percentages, amounts, income thresholds, bracket widths, tax formulas, effective dates, or the date on which rate changes take effect.

### 17.4 No complete business rules for leave

The data model provides leave categories, accrual frequency, accrual rate, maximum accrual, leave balances, requests, approvals, and monetisation. It does not list the actual leave categories or define:

- how leave is earned within a period;
- when accrual is posted;
- whether accrual is prorated;
- how leaves are approved or rejected;
- how requests that exceed the balance are handled;
- whether a request reserves credits before approval;
- how overlapping leave requests are handled;
- which leave types can be monetised;
- how monetisation is valued; or
- how an approved leave request affects attendance data and payroll.

### 17.5 No complete security implementation

The overview identifies RBAC and a two-person approval requirement for PII, but does not provide a complete role-permission matrix, specific permission names, authentication factors, encryption method, key custody, logging retention, masking rules, access review cycle, or PII access-request workflow.

### 17.6 No complete archival policy

The DFD shows the labels `1YO`, `2YO`, an annual prompt, cold storage, later compression, and subsequent deletion. It does not define the precise age calculation, file format, compression method, archive integrity check, restore process, backup schedule, legal exceptions, or audit evidence.
