### /home/user/repo_review/full_repo/testingester-main/9/-/oop/src/motorphemployee/oop/GovernmentContributionCalculator.java
package motorphemployee.oop;

/**
 * GovernmentContributionCalculator - abstract base for every statutory deduction
 * (MS1 Week 3/4/5 CRC rows).
 *
 * PayrollCalculator works with THIS type only, never with SSSCalculator or any other
 * concrete subclass. Adding a new deduction later means adding a subclass and one line
 * in the calculator list - no change to the orchestrator.
 */
public abstract class GovernmentContributionCalculator {

    private final String contributionName;
    private final String contributionCode;
    private boolean isActive;

    protected GovernmentContributionCalculator(String contributionName, String contributionCode) {
        if (contributionName == null || contributionName.trim().isEmpty()) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("contributionName cannot be empty");
        }
        if (contributionCode == null || contributionCode.trim().isEmpty()) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("contributionCode cannot be empty");
        }
        this.contributionName = contributionName.trim();
        this.contributionCode = contributionCode.trim();
        this.isActive = true;
    }

    /** The polymorphic entry point: every deduction type implements only this. */
    public abstract double calculate(double grossSalary);

    public String getContributionName() {
        return contributionName;
    }

    public String getContributionCode() {
        return contributionCode;
    }

    public boolean isActive() {
        return isActive;
    }

    public void setActive(boolean isActive) {
        this.isActive = isActive;
    }

    /** Shared guard: a contribution on an invalid salary is a bug, not a zero. */
    protected double requireValidSalary(double grossSalary) {
        if (Double.isNaN(grossSalary) || grossSalary < 0) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException(contributionName + ": invalid salary " + grossSalary);
        }
        return grossSalary;
    }

    @Override
    public String toString() {
        return contributionName + " (" + contributionCode + ", " + (isActive ? "active" : "inactive") + ")";
    }
}
### /home/user/repo_review/full_repo/testingester-main/9/-/oop/src/motorphemployee/oop/SSSCalculator.java
package motorphemployee.oop;

/**
 * SSSCalculator - SSS contribution using the official 44-bracket table, capped at PHP 1,125
 * (MS1 Week 3 CRC: "SSSCalculator (Concrete Subclass)").
 *
 * The bracket table is private: outside code only sees calculate(). Brackets come from
 * Home_SSS_Matrix.xlsx (sheet "SSS Contribution Schedule"): lower bound 3,250 stepping by 500,
 * contribution 157.50 stepping by 22.50, "below 3,250" = 135.00, "over 24,750" = 1,125.00.
 *
 * Official matrix (2026-10-27): the official ranges are LOWER-bound inclusive ("3,250 - 3,749.99"),
 * so bracket i covers [lower, lower + 499.99]. CP2 used an upper-bound inclusive `<=` chain,
 * which under-deducted PHP 22.50 whenever the salary landed exactly on a bracket boundary -
 * Issue 5 in oop/matrix-verification.md.
 */
public class SSSCalculator extends GovernmentContributionCalculator {

    private static final double FIRST_LOWER_BOUND = 3250.0;
    private static final double LOWER_BOUND_STEP = 500.0;
    private static final double BELOW_TABLE_AMOUNT = 135.0;
    private static final double FIRST_BRACKET_AMOUNT = 157.5;
    private static final double AMOUNT_STEP = 22.5;
    private static final int BRACKETS = 43;              // 3,250 ... 24,250 + the "over 24,750" row
    private static final double MAX_CONTRIBUTION = 1125.0;

    private static final double[] LOWER_BOUNDS = new double[BRACKETS];
    private static final double[] AMOUNTS = new double[BRACKETS];

    static {
        for (int i = 0; i < BRACKETS; i++) {
            LOWER_BOUNDS[i] = FIRST_LOWER_BOUND + LOWER_BOUND_STEP * i;
            AMOUNTS[i] = FIRST_BRACKET_AMOUNT + AMOUNT_STEP * i;
        }
    }

    public SSSCalculator() {
        super("SSS Contribution", "SSS");
    }

    @Override
    public double calculate(double grossSalary) {
        double salary = requireValidSalary(grossSalary);
        if (salary < FIRST_LOWER_BOUND) {
            return BELOW_TABLE_AMOUNT;
        }
        for (int i = 0; i < BRACKETS; i++) {
            if (salary < LOWER_BOUNDS[i] + LOWER_BOUND_STEP) {
                return AMOUNTS[i];
            }
        }
        return MAX_CONTRIBUTION;
    }

    /** Read-only inspection of the table (used by the console test, never by payroll logic). */
    public int getBracketCount() {
        return BRACKETS + 2;                             // "below 3,250" + 43 rows + "over 24,750"
    }
}
### /home/user/repo_review/full_repo/testingester-main/9/-/oop/src/motorphemployee/oop/PhilHealthCalculator.java
package motorphemployee.oop;

/**
 * PhilHealthCalculator - PhilHealth employee share: 50% of the premium (3% rate with a PHP 300
 * floor and a PHP 1,800 ceiling), so the deduction runs from PHP 150 to PHP 900
 * (MS1 Week 3 CRC: "PhilHealthCalculator (Concrete Subclass)").
 *
 * Official matrix (2026-10-27): the premium formula is carried over from CP2 unchanged, but the
 * EMPLOYEE SHARE is applied. The official matrix states the premium is equally shared between
 * employee and employer (Home_Philhealth_Matrix.xlsx note A6; SAMPLE B10 = 375 on a 25,000
 * basic salary). CP2 returned the full premium, which over-deducted every payslip by 2x -
 * logged as Issue 2 in oop/matrix-verification.md.
 */
public class PhilHealthCalculator extends GovernmentContributionCalculator {

    private static final double EMPLOYEE_SHARE_RATE = 0.5;
    private static final double PREMIUM_RATE = 0.03;
    private static final double MIN_PREMIUM = 300.0;
    private static final double MAX_PREMIUM = 1800.0;
    private static final double LOWER_CAP_SALARY = 10000.0;
    private static final double UPPER_CAP_SALARY = 59999.99;

    public PhilHealthCalculator() {
        super("PhilHealth Contribution", "PH");
    }

    @Override
    public double calculate(double grossSalary) {
        double salary = requireValidSalary(grossSalary);

        // Official monthly premium: 3% of salary, floor 300, ceiling 1,800 (matrix A2:C4).
        double monthlyPremium;
        if (salary <= LOWER_CAP_SALARY) {
            monthlyPremium = MIN_PREMIUM;
        } else if (salary <= UPPER_CAP_SALARY) {
            monthlyPremium = Math.min(MIN_PREMIUM + (salary - LOWER_CAP_SALARY) * PREMIUM_RATE, MAX_PREMIUM);
        } else {
            monthlyPremium = MAX_PREMIUM;
        }

        // The employee pays HALF (matrix note A6: "equally shared"; SAMPLE B10 = 375 of 750).
        return monthlyPremium * EMPLOYEE_SHARE_RATE;
    }
}
### /home/user/repo_review/full_repo/testingester-main/9/-/oop/src/motorphemployee/oop/PagIbigCalculator.java
package motorphemployee.oop;

/**
 * PagIbigCalculator - Pag-IBIG EMPLOYEE share, tiered, with a PHP 100 cap
 * (MS1 Week 3 CRC: "PagIbigCalculator (Concrete Subclass)").
 *
 * Official matrix (2026-10-27): only the employee share is deducted - 1% for 1,000-1,500 and 2%
 * above 1,500, capped at 100 (Home_PagIBIG_Matrix.xlsx B2/B3 employee rates vs D2/D3 totals,
 * cap note A5). CP2 added the employer share (2%) and deducted the total 3%/4% from the
 * employee; that is Issue 3 in oop/matrix-verification.md.
 *
 * Salary below 1,000 has no row in the official matrix, so it returns 0.00 and stays
 * UNVERIFIED rather than guessing a rate.
 */
public class PagIbigCalculator extends GovernmentContributionCalculator {

    private static final double LOWER_BAND_MIN = 1000.0;
    private static final double LOWER_BAND_MAX = 1500.0;
    private static final double EMPLOYEE_RATE_LOW = 0.01;
    private static final double EMPLOYEE_RATE_HIGH = 0.02;
    private static final double MAX_CONTRIBUTION = 100.0;

    public PagIbigCalculator() {
        super("Pag-IBIG Contribution", "PAGIBIG");
    }

    @Override
    public double calculate(double grossSalary) {
        double salary = requireValidSalary(grossSalary);

        double employeeRate = 0.0;

        if (salary >= LOWER_BAND_MIN && salary <= LOWER_BAND_MAX) {
            employeeRate = EMPLOYEE_RATE_LOW;
        } else if (salary > LOWER_BAND_MAX) {
            employeeRate = EMPLOYEE_RATE_HIGH;
        }

        return Math.min(salary * employeeRate, MAX_CONTRIBUTION);
    }
}

## `PayrollCalculator` orchestrator (2026-10-28)

The payroll path is now one method: `calculatePayroll(employee, attendance, periodStart, periodEnd)`
returns an immutable `PayrollRecord`. Nothing in this class asks which calculator or which employee type
it is holding — `grep -c instanceof PayrollCalculator.java` = **0**.

| Phase | What runs | Type it works with (S1 design) |
|---|---|---|
| gross | `workedDays * hourlyRate * 8` | `AttendanceLog` + `Employee` |
| **phase 1** | SSS → PhilHealth → Pag-IBIG in **one loop** | `List<GovernmentContributionCalculator>` (abstract) |
| **phase 2** | BIR withholding tax on `gross - phase 1` | `GovernmentContributionCalculator` (abstract) |
| result | `new PayrollRecord(...)`, fully validated | immutable value object |

Verified run (`console-test-output.txt`, section I, 20 June 2024 working days, hourly rate 205.36):

| Field | Value | Where it comes from |
|---|---|---|
| gross income | **32,857.60** | 20 days × 205.36 × 8 |
| hours worked | **160.00** | 20 days × 8 |
| SSS | **1,125.00** | official cap |
| PhilHealth | **492.864** | (300 + (32,857.60 − 10,000) × 3%) / 2 |
| Pag-IBIG | **100.00** | official employee cap |
| withholding tax | **2,061.35** | 20% of (31,139.736 − 20,833) |
| **net pay** | **29,078.39** | gross − 3,779.21 deductions |

Section I also proves: the result is immutable (no setters), two employee types price differently through
one `Employee` parameter, the calculator list is injectable (SSS-only run changes only the SSS amount),
Issue 1 is refused, and the no-dates overload prices the most recent semi-monthly period.

## Known issues found by the console run

| ID | Issue | Evidence | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Issue 1** | At gross pay **0.00** the statutory minimums still apply (SSS 135 + PhilHealth 150 = 285), so net pay would be **-285.00** (a negative payslip). The calculators refuse a negative taxable income instead. The old program charged the full PhilHealth premium (300.00), which is why its recorded negative result is -435.00. | `cp2-parity-output.txt` line `NET\|0.00\|435.000000\|-435.000000` (CP2, before the PhilHealth fix) | ✅ **RESOLVED** (2026-10-28) — `PayrollCalculator.calculatePayroll` rejects a non-positive gross **before** any deduction runs; section I asserts the refusal. A second guard rejects the case where statutory deductions would consume the whole gross, so a negative net can never reach `PayrollRecord`. |
| **Issue 2** | PhilHealth deducted **100% of the premium**; the official employee share is **50%** (`Home_Philhealth_Matrix.xlsx` note `A6`, SAMPLE `B10` = 375 on 25,000). Every payslip was over-deducted by 2x. | `matrix-verification.md` §2 | ✅ **RESOLVED** — `PhilHealthCalculator` returns `premium / 2`; section H asserts 150 / 375 / 900 |
| **Issue 3** | Pag-IBIG deducted **employee + employer share** (3%/4%); the official employee share is **1%/2%**, cap 100 (`B2:B3` vs `D2:D3`, note `A5`). | `matrix-verification.md` §3 | ✅ **RESOLVED** — `PagIbigCalculator` uses the employee rate only; salary < 1,000 stays 0.00 and UNVERIFIED (no matrix row) |
| **Issue 4** | Withholding tax bracket 1 used the excess base **20,832** instead of **20,833** (`B3`, SAMPLE `B20` = 513.40) → +PHP 0.20 over-withheld in [20,833, 33,333]. | `matrix-verification.md` §4 | ✅ **RESOLVED** — `WithholdingTaxCalculator` uses 20,833 (and clamps the 20,832–20,833 gap so tax can never go negative) |
| **Issue 5** | SSS brackets were **upper-inclusive**; the official schedule is **lower-inclusive** ("3,250 - 3,749.99"), so a salary exactly on a boundary was under-deducted by PHP 22.50. | `matrix-verification.md` §1 | ✅ **RESOLVED** — `SSSCalculator` treats bracket *i* as `[lower, lower + 499.99)`; section H asserts 3,250 → 157.50 |

## Leave workflow fix (2026-10-31)

Two defects in the leave screens, both found by the group's tester after the Week 9 smoke test and
reported in the MS2 Known Issues List (rows 18 and 19).

| What | Evidence |
|---|---|
| Approving a request wrote `leaves.csv` and moved the leave credits immediately, but the request stayed in `pendingleaves.csv` until Save was pressed, so the same leave could be approved again and counted twice | before: `LeaveApproval.approvedActionPerformed` only did `model.removeRow(...)`; `saveActionPerformed` was the only writer of `pendingleaves.csv` |
| Once the approve call site was fixed (commit `683c9f0`), rejected leaves were still written with the reason and the approval swapped, because the reject call passed `(reason, approval)` into `writeToFile(..., approval, reason)` | `git show 683c9f0` touches one call site: a rejected row still lands as `Reason=No`, `Approved?=<reason>` |
| Fix | `LeaveService` is now the only writer on the approve and reject path. One `decide(index, approved)` call removes the request, appends the processed row in header order and moves the credits, and restores all three files if a write fails. `LeaveApproval` keeps the table view only, the manual Save button is gone, and `LeaveManagement` reads `leaves.csv` through the same service |
| Column order | `LeaveService.LEAVE_COLUMNS` is the single definition of `Employee ID, Leave Type, Days, Reason, Approved?`; approve and reject both go through it, so the two call sites cannot disagree again |
| Evidence | `oop/leave-fix-test-output.txt` — 44 assertions, 0 failures: approve, reject, double-processing refused, stale row refused, shifted (ragged) `data.csv` refused instead of being rewritten, unknown employee, zero-credit employee, comma inside a reason, CRLF preserved, rollback after a failed write |
| No regression | `ConsoleBackendTest` still reports **91 passed, 0 failed**; `data.csv` is rewritten with its 24 columns and its original CRLF line endings |
| GUI click-through | **verified 2026-10-31 21:15** (HR login, VS Code F5 → LandingPage): Leave Management → Pending Leaves processed one approve and one reject; both requests left `pendingleaves.csv` on that same click with no Save, the reject row landed as `Reason=Sick, Approved?=No`, and the credits moved `12,0,0 → 11,1,0` (approved) / `11,1,0 → 11,1,1` (rejected). Raw run: `oop/gui-retest-output.txt` |

Known issue 16 in the MS2 Known Issues List: the payroll screens recorded a fixed 08:00–16:00 day
on a 2024 calendar for every "worked day" of a hardcoded month table, so a payslip was never tied to
an actual timecard.

| What | Evidence |
|---|---|

| Employee numbers | the sheet uses 10001–10034 while `data.csv` uses 1–34 for the same 34 people (names identical, offset 10000), so the export is keyed to the ids `data.csv` already uses |
| Reader | `AttendanceRepository` turns rows into an `AttendanceLog`; the period picker offers only months that have rows, and worked days come from `AttendanceLog.getWorkedDays` — the same value `PayrollCalculator` prices |

| No regression | `ConsoleBackendTest` 91/91, leave evidence 44/44 |
| Numbers | for this dataset the timecard has the same working days as the old table (Jun 20, Jul 23, Aug 22, Sep 21, Oct 23, Nov 21, Dec 22), so payslip amounts for those months do not move — but they are now derived from the timecard, and a month with no rows is not offered at all |
| Not yet verified (2026-10-31) | GUI click-through of View Salary / Calculate Salary (compiled and console-tested, not clicked in this run — the 21:15 GUI retest covered the leave screens only, not these two) |

## Leave credit rule (matches the original program)

Approving a leave deducts exactly **one** credit, no matter how many days the request covers:
a 4-day leave moves the column from 11 to 10, a 2-day leave from 12 to 11. That is what the
baseline program does, so the refactor kept it on purpose.

```java
// baseline 655d43d, LeaveApproval.updateLeaveCredits(...)
if (isApproved) {
    if (leaveCredits > 0) {
        data[21] = String.valueOf(leaveCredits - 1); // Deduct 1 leave credit
        data[22] = String.valueOf(approvedLeaves + 1);
```

# Matrix verification (official vs CP2 vs OOP)

> Scope: 4 deduction formulas (SSS · PhilHealth · Pag-IBIG · Withholding Tax) checked against the 4 official xlsx matrices in `C:\Users\Paul\Documents\MotorPH Files\`.
> Source of "CP2" values: verbatim copy of the 4 static methods from `src/motorphemployee/Dashboard.java:1195–1356` (run under JDK 21). Source of "OOP" values: `oop/src/motorphemployee/oop/*.java` compiled with `javac -Xlint:all` (0 warnings), run through the same harness. CP2 and OOP agree on **all 66 inputs tested** (`run.txt`), so the OOP columns are identical to CP2 by construction.
> Official values are computed from the matrix rules and the matrix cell refs cited below; nothing guessed. Verdict tolerance: |Δ| ≤ 0.005.
> No repo file was modified except this one. Harness + raw output live in the scratch dir (`cache\scratch\q4\`), not in the repo.

## Summary

| Matrix | CP2 | OOP | Verdict | Mismatch count (16 base inputs) | Mismatch count (boundary points) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| SSS | `Dashboard.java:1195` / `MainMenu.java:1279` | `SSSCalculator` | 🟠 DEVIATION at exact bracket boundaries only | **0 / 16** | **44 / 44** lower bounds (3,250 … 24,750) |
| PhilHealth | `Dashboard.java:1294` / `MainMenu.java:1378` | `PhilHealthCalculator` | 🟠 DEVIATION — share, not formula | **16 / 16** | 4 / 4 (boundary set) |

| Withholding Tax | `Dashboard.java:1334` / `MainMenu.java:1418` | `WithholdingTaxCalculator` | 🟠 DEVIATION — bracket 1 off by ₱0.20 | **3 / 16** | 3 / 4 |

## 1. SSS

**(a) Official table** — `Home_SSS_Matrix.xlsx`, sheet `SSS Contribution Schedule`.
- `D2` = 135.00 for "Below 3,250".
- `A3:C46` = 44 rows, lower bound in `A`, upper in `C` (display only), contribution in `D`. Rows 3..46 step 500 from 3,250 (`D3`=157.50) to `A46`=24,750 (`D46`=1,125.00, "Over").
- Matrix ranges are written as `3,250 – 3,749.99` etc., i.e. **lower-bound inclusive**.
- Merged cells A1:C1 and A2:C2 are headers only; the data rows are not merged, so parsing was unambiguous.

**(b) CP2 code** — `Dashboard.java:1195–1292`: `if (totalSalary <= 3250) … else if (totalSalary <= 3750) …` (line 1198 onward), i.e. **upper-bound inclusive** `<=` chain, 45 branches, last branch `else → 1125` (line ~1290). Duplicate `MainMenu.java:1279` identical (diffed).

**(c) OOP code** — `SSSCalculator.java`: 44 bracket lower bounds `3250 + 500·i`, amounts `135 + 22.5·i`, returns `AMOUNTS[i]` when `salary <= LOWER_BOUNDS[i]`, else cap `1125`. Same upper-inclusive behavior as CP2 (proven by identical output on 66 inputs).

## 2. PhilHealth

**(a) Official table** — `Home_Philhealth_Matrix.xlsx`, sheet `Philhealth`.
- `A2:C2`: salary ≤ 10,000 → premium rate 3%, monthly premium **300** (floor).
- `A3:C3`: 10,000.01 – 59,999.99 → 3%, premium "300 up to 1,800" (i.e. 3% of salary, between those bounds).
- `A4:C4`: 60,000 → 1,800 (ceiling).
- `A6` NOTE: *"Monthly premium contribution payments are equally shared between the employee and employer."* → **employee share = 50% of premium.**
- `A7:B10` SAMPLE: basic 25,000 → 3% = 750 → **Employee Share (50%) = 375** (`B10`).
- Official employee deduction used below: `0.5 × clamp(0.03 × salary, 300, 1800)`.

**(b) CP2 code** — `Dashboard.java:1294–1310`: `premiumRate = 0.03`; `≤10,000 → 300`; `≤59,999.99 → min(300 + (salary−10,000)·0.03, 1800)`; `else 1800`. **Returns `monthlyPremium` = the full 100% premium**, with the comment "Employee and employer share equally" **but no ÷2 is applied** (line ~1305). The caller (`Dashboard.java:1013–1023`) subtracts this full amount from the employee's pay.

**(c) OOP code** — `PhilHealthCalculator.java`: `PREMIUM_RATE 0.03`, `MIN 300`, `MAX 1800`, same piecewise logic, returns the full premium. Identical to CP2 (javadoc says "carried over 1:1 from CP2").

**Formula check:** the CP2/OOP formula `300 + 0.03·(s−10,000)` = `0.03·s` for s ≥ 10,000, so the *premium* formula **matches the matrix** (verified at 15,000 → 450, 20,000 → 600, 25,000 → 750 ✓ official 750).

**(d) Verdict per test input:**

## 3. Pag-IBIG

**(a) Official table** — `Home_PagIBIG_Matrix.xlsx`, sheet `Pag-ibig Contribution`.
- `A2:D2` "At least 1,000 to 1,500": employee 1% (`B2`), employer 2% (`C2`), total 3% (`D2`).
- `A3:D3` "Over 1,500": employee 2% (`B3`), employer 2% (`C3`), total 4% (`D3`).
- `A5` NOTE: *"The maximum contribution amount is 100."*
- **No row for salary < 1,000** (matrix silent) → those inputs are ❓ UNVERIFIED, not assumed.
- Official employee deduction used below: `min(employee_rate × salary, 100)`.

**(b) CP2 code** — `Dashboard.java:1312–1332`: `1000 ≤ s ≤ 1500 → employee 0.01 + employer 0.02`; `s > 1500 → employee 0.02 + employer 0.02`; `min(s × (employee+employer), 100)` → **returns the TOTAL (employee + employer) 3%/4% capped at 100**. Caller at `Dashboard.java:1014` subtracts this from the employee's pay → employer share is being deducted from the employee.

**(c) OOP code** — `PagIbigCalculator.java`: same tiers, `totalRate = employeeRate + employerRate`, `min(salary × totalRate, 100)`. Identical to CP2.

public class ProbationaryEmployee extends Employee {

    private int probationMonths;
    private String startDate;
    private double evaluationScore;

    /** Same 19 fields as Employee + probationMonths, startDate, evaluationScore (MS1 Week 4 CRC). */
    public ProbationaryEmployee(int id,
                                String lastName,
                                String firstName,
                                String birthday,
                                String address,
                                String phoneNumber,
                                String sssNumber,
                                String philhealthNumber,
                                String tinNumber,
                                String pagIbigNumber,
                                String status,
                                String position,
                                String immediateSupervisor,
                                double basicSalary,
                                double riceSubsidy,
                                double phoneAllowance,
                                double clothingAllowance,
                                double grossSemiMonthlyRate,
                                double hourlyRate,
                                int probationMonths,
                                String startDate,
                                double evaluationScore) {
        super(id, lastName, firstName, birthday, address, phoneNumber, sssNumber, philhealthNumber,
                tinNumber, pagIbigNumber, status, position, immediateSupervisor, basicSalary,
                riceSubsidy, phoneAllowance, clothingAllowance, grossSemiMonthlyRate, hourlyRate);
        this.probationMonths = requireProbationMonths(probationMonths);
        this.startDate = requireStartDate(startDate);
        this.evaluationScore = requireEvaluationScore(evaluationScore);
    }

    public int getProbationMonths() {
        return probationMonths;
    }

    public void setProbationMonths(int probationMonths) {
        this.probationMonths = requireProbationMonths(probationMonths);
    }

    public String getStartDate() {
        return startDate;
    }

    public void setStartDate(String startDate) {
        this.startDate = requireStartDate(startDate);
    }

    public double getEvaluationScore() {
        return evaluationScore;
    }

    public void setEvaluationScore(double evaluationScore) {
        this.evaluationScore = requireEvaluationScore(evaluationScore);
    }

    private static int requireProbationMonths(int probationMonths) {
        if (probationMonths < 0 || probationMonths > 12) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("probationMonths out of range: " + probationMonths);
        }
        return probationMonths;
    }

    private static String requireStartDate(String startDate) {
        if (startDate == null || startDate.trim().isEmpty()) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("startDate cannot be null or empty");
        }
        return startDate.trim();
    }

    private static double requireEvaluationScore(double evaluationScore) {
        if (evaluationScore < 0 || evaluationScore > 100) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("evaluationScore must be 0-100: " + evaluationScore);
        }
        return evaluationScore;
    }

    /** Reduced rice subsidy during probation. */
    @Override
    public double getRiceSubsidy() {
        return 1000.0;
    }

    /** Reduced phone allowance during probation. */
    @Override
    public double getPhoneAllowance() {
        return 500.0;
    }

    /** Reduced annual leave credits. */
    @Override
    public int getAnnualLeaveCredits() {
        return 6;
    }

    /** Not promotable while on probation. */
    @Override
    public boolean isEligibleForPromotion() {
        return false;
    }
}

package motorphemployee.oop;

import java.time.Duration;
import java.time.LocalDate;
import java.time.LocalTime;
import java.time.format.DateTimeFormatter;
import java.time.format.DateTimeParseException;
import java.util.LinkedHashMap;
import java.util.Map;

/**
 * AttendanceLog - the input side of gross pay (MS1 Week 2 CRC: "AttendanceLog").
 *
 * Enforces the integrity rules from the approved design: one clock-in per day, clock-in
 * must come before clock-out, hours never exceed 24 per day, and no future-dated records.
 * Callers only get read-only summaries - there is no way to edit a saved record.
 *
 * Storage note (open question in the Refactoring Plan): CP2 hardcoded a
 * workingDays[] array (MainMenu.java:1066) and no timecard CSV has been imported yet, so
 * this class keeps the records in memory. The public API is CSV-ready: an adapter that
 * feeds rows from attendance.csv needs no change to PayrollCalculator. No attendance data
 * was invented to make this test pass.
 */
public class AttendanceLog {

    private static final DateTimeFormatter DATE = DateTimeFormatter.ofPattern("yyyy-MM-dd");
    private static final DateTimeFormatter TIME = DateTimeFormatter.ofPattern("HH:mm[:ss]");

    /** employeeId -> (date -> {clockIn, clockOut}) */
    private final Map<Integer, Map<String, String[]>> records = new LinkedHashMap<>();

    public void recordClockIn(int employeeId) {
        recordClockIn(employeeId, LocalDate.now().format(DATE), LocalTime.now().format(DateTimeFormatter.ofPattern("HH:mm:ss")));
    }

    public void recordClockOut(int employeeId) {
        recordClockOut(employeeId, LocalDate.now().format(DATE), LocalTime.now().format(DateTimeFormatter.ofPattern("HH:mm:ss")));
    }

    /** Testable overload: records a clock-in for an explicit date and time. */
    public void recordClockIn(int employeeId, String date, String time) {
        requireEmployee(employeeId);
        LocalDate day = parseDate(date);
        if (day.isAfter(LocalDate.now())) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("cannot clock in on a future date: " + date);
        }
        parseTime(time);

        Map<String, String[]> perDay = records.computeIfAbsent(employeeId, key -> new LinkedHashMap<>());
        String[] entry = perDay.computeIfAbsent(date, key -> new String[]{null, null});
        if (entry[0] != null) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("duplicate clock-in for employee " + employeeId + " on " + date);
        }
        entry[0] = time;
    }

    /** Testable overload: records a clock-out for an explicit date and time. */
    public void recordClockOut(int employeeId, String date, String time) {
        requireEmployee(employeeId);
        parseDate(date);
        LocalTime clockOut = parseTime(time);

        Map<String, String[]> perDay = records.get(employeeId);
        if (perDay == null || perDay.get(date) == null || perDay.get(date)[0] == null) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("cannot clock out without a clock-in: employee "
                    + employeeId + " on " + date);
        }
        String[] entry = perDay.get(date);
        if (entry[1] != null) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("duplicate clock-out for employee " + employeeId + " on " + date);
        }
        LocalTime clockIn = parseTime(entry[0]);
        if (!clockOut.isAfter(clockIn)) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("clock-out must be after clock-in: " + entry[0] + " -> " + time);
        }
        double hours = Duration.between(clockIn, clockOut).toMinutes() / 60.0;
        if (hours > 24) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("hours worked cannot exceed 24 in a day: " + hours);
        }
        entry[1] = time;
    }

    /** Validated hours for one employee on one date; 0 when there is no complete record. */
    public double getDailyHours(int employeeId, String date) {
        requireEmployee(employeeId);
        Map<String, String[]> perDay = records.get(employeeId);
        if (perDay == null) {
            return 0.0;
        }
        String[] entry = perDay.get(date);
        if (entry == null || entry[0] == null || entry[1] == null) {
            return 0.0;
        }
        return Duration.between(parseTime(entry[0]), parseTime(entry[1])).toMinutes() / 60.0;
    }

    /** Days with a complete clock-in/clock-out pair inside the period (inclusive). */
    public int getWorkedDays(int employeeId, String periodStart, String periodEnd) {
        requireEmployee(employeeId);
        LocalDate start = parseDate(periodStart);
        LocalDate end = parseDate(periodEnd);
        if (end.isBefore(start)) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("periodEnd cannot be before periodStart");
        }
        Map<String, String[]> perDay = records.get(employeeId);
        if (perDay == null) {
            return 0;
        }
        int days = 0;
        for (Map.Entry<String, String[]> entry : perDay.entrySet()) {
            String[] times = entry.getValue();
            if (times[0] == null || times[1] == null) {
                continue;
            }
            LocalDate day = parseDate(entry.getKey());
            if (!day.isBefore(start) && !day.isAfter(end)) {
                days++;
            }
        }
        return days;
    }

    private static void requireEmployee(int employeeId) {
        if (employeeId <= 0) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("employeeId must be positive: " + employeeId);
        }
    }

    private static LocalDate parseDate(String date) {
        try {
            return LocalDate.parse(date, DATE);
        } catch (DateTimeParseException ex) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("date must be yyyy-MM-dd: " + date);
        }
    }

    private static LocalTime parseTime(String time) {
        try {
            return LocalTime.parse(time, TIME);
        } catch (DateTimeParseException ex) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("time must be HH:mm or HH:mm:ss: " + time);
        }
    }
}

package motorphemployee.oop;

import java.time.LocalDate;
import java.time.ZoneId;
import java.time.ZonedDateTime;
import java.time.format.DateTimeParseException;
import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.Collections;
import java.util.LinkedHashMap;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Map;

/**
 * PayrollCalculator - the orchestrator: attendance + employee in, one immutable PayrollRecord out
 * (MS1 Week 4/5 CRC: "PayrollCalculator (Service Class Using Abstraction)"; Method Dictionary rows
 * calculatePayroll / calculateGross / calculateNetPay).
 *
 * This class is the refactored home of the payroll logic that CP2 copy-pasted into BOTH
 * MainMenu (1,558 lines) and Dashboard (1,442 lines) - four calculate*() formulas, twice. After the
 * After the GUI rewiring there is exactly one implementation of each formula in the whole project.
 *
 * Uses abstraction, not concrete types: the statutory deductions are held as
 * List<GovernmentContributionCalculator>, so a new deduction is a new subclass plus one line in
 * the constructor - this class never changes and never asks "which calculator are you?".
 *
 * Two phases (Refactoring Plan design):
 *   phase 1 - SSS, PhilHealth, Pag-IBIG are computed on GROSS pay (one polymorphic loop)
 *   phase 2 - withholding tax is computed on the TAXABLE income (gross minus phase 1)
 *
 * Official matrices (2026-10-27): the four calculators follow the OFFICIAL government matrices, not
 * CP2, so a CP2 mismatch is expected and documented in oop/matrix-verification.md.
 */
public class PayrollCalculator {

    /** Standard MotorPH work day used by CP2 (MainMenu.java:1090: workedDays * hourlyRate * 8). */
    private static final double HOURS_PER_WORK_DAY = 8.0;

    /** Default payroll period length when the caller does not pass an explicit one. */
    private static final int DEFAULT_PERIOD_DAYS = 15;

    private static final ZoneId PAYROLL_ZONE = ZoneId.of("Asia/Manila");

    /** Contribution codes from the approved design; used to name the amounts, never to branch on type. */
    private static final String CODE_SSS = "SSS";
    private static final String CODE_PHILHEALTH = "PH";
    private static final String CODE_PAGIBIG = "PAGIBIG";

    private final List<GovernmentContributionCalculator> statutory;
    private final GovernmentContributionCalculator withholdingTax;

    /** Production default: the three statutory deductions plus BIR withholding tax. */
    public PayrollCalculator() {
        this(defaultStatutory(), new WithholdingTaxCalculator());
    }

    /**
     * Injectable composition - the constructor a test or a future payroll variant uses.
     * Because the field type is the abstract parent, the caller can swap any calculator.
     */
    public PayrollCalculator(List<GovernmentContributionCalculator> statutory,
                             GovernmentContributionCalculator withholdingTax) {
        if (statutory == null || statutory.isEmpty()) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("at least one statutory calculator is required");
        }
        for (GovernmentContributionCalculator calculator : statutory) {
            if (calculator == null) {
                throw new IllegalArgumentException("statutory calculator list cannot contain null");
            }
        }
        if (withholdingTax == null) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("withholdingTax calculator is required");
        }
        this.statutory = Collections.unmodifiableList(new ArrayList<>(statutory));
        this.withholdingTax = withholdingTax;
    }

    // ---------------------------------------------------------------- public API

    /**
     * Payroll for the most recent semi-monthly period (overload without dates).
     * Same computation as the 4-argument overload - only the period differs.
     */
    public PayrollRecord calculatePayroll(Employee employee, AttendanceLog attendance) {
        requireEmployee(employee);
        requireAttendance(attendance);

        LocalDate periodEndDay = LocalDate.now(PAYROLL_ZONE);
        LocalDate periodStartDay = periodEndDay.minusDays(DEFAULT_PERIOD_DAYS - 1L);
        return calculatePayroll(employee, attendance, periodStartDay.toString(), periodEndDay.toString());
    }

    /**
     * Payroll for an explicit period - the single public entry point of the whole computation.
     *
     * @throws IllegalArgumentException when the employee or attendance is missing, when the period
     *         is invalid, when the computed gross pay is not positive (Issue 1 fix), or
     *         when the statutory deductions would consume the entire gross pay.
     */
    public PayrollRecord calculatePayroll(Employee employee,
                                          AttendanceLog attendance,
                                          String periodStart,
                                          String periodEnd) {
        requireEmployee(employee);
        requireAttendance(attendance);
        LocalDate start = parsePeriodDate(periodStart, "periodStart");
        LocalDate end = parsePeriodDate(periodEnd, "periodEnd");
        if (end.isBefore(start)) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("periodEnd cannot be before periodStart: "
                    + periodStart + " -> " + periodEnd);
        }

        int employeeId = employee.getId();
        double hourlyRate = employee.getHourlyRate();
        int workedDays = attendance.getWorkedDays(employeeId, periodStart, periodEnd);
        double grossIncome = calculateGross(attendance, employeeId, hourlyRate, periodStart, periodEnd);

        // Issue 1: a non-positive gross pay must never reach the deduction tables,
        // otherwise the statutory minimums turn a 0.00 payslip into a negative one.
        if (!(grossIncome > 0)) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("cannot compute payroll for employee " + employeeId
                    + ": gross pay is " + grossIncome + " because " + workedDays
                    + " day(s) of attendance were found in " + periodStart + ".." + periodEnd);
        }

        // ---- phase 1: the three statutory deductions, one loop over the ABSTRACT type ----
        Map<String, Double> statutoryAmounts = new LinkedHashMap<>();
        double statutoryTotal = 0.0;
        for (GovernmentContributionCalculator calculator : statutory) {
            if (!calculator.isActive()) {
                continue;
            }
            double amount = calculator.calculate(grossIncome);
            statutoryAmounts.put(calculator.getContributionCode(), amount);
            statutoryTotal += amount;
        }

        double sss = amountOf(statutoryAmounts, CODE_SSS);
        double philhealth = amountOf(statutoryAmounts, CODE_PHILHEALTH);
        double pagibig = amountOf(statutoryAmounts, CODE_PAGIBIG);

        if (statutoryTotal >= grossIncome) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("statutory deductions (" + statutoryTotal
                    + ") would consume the whole gross pay (" + grossIncome
                    + ") for employee " + employeeId + " - no payslip can be produced");
        }

        // ---- phase 2: BIR withholding tax on the income already net of the three above ----
        double taxableIncome = grossIncome - statutoryTotal;
        double tax = withholdingTax.isActive() ? withholdingTax.calculate(taxableIncome) : 0.0;

        double totalDeductions = sss + philhealth + pagibig + tax;
        double netIncome = calculateNetPay(grossIncome, totalDeductions);

        ZonedDateTime issueDate = ZonedDateTime.now(PAYROLL_ZONE);
        return new PayrollRecord(
                employeeId,
                issueDate,
                start.atStartOfDay(PAYROLL_ZONE),
                end.atTime(23, 59).atZone(PAYROLL_ZONE),
                employee.getBasicSalary(),
                employee.getPhoneAllowance(),
                employee.getRiceSubsidy(),
                employee.getClothingAllowance(),
                grossIncome,
                employee.getGrossSemiMonthlyRate(),
                netIncome,
                sss,
                philhealth,
                pagibig,
                tax,
                employee.getAnnualLeaveCredits(),
                workedDays * HOURS_PER_WORK_DAY,
                hourlyRate,
                0L);                 // absences: no attendance.csv yet (open question), never invented
    }

    @Override
    public String toString() {
        return "PayrollCalculator{statutory=" + statutory + ", tax=" + withholdingTax + "}";
    }

    // ---------------------------------------------------------------- private computation

    /** gross = workedDays * hourlyRate * 8 (Method Dictionary row "calculateGross"). */
    private double calculateGross(AttendanceLog attendance,
                                  int employeeId,
                                  double hourlyRate,
                                  String periodStart,
                                  String periodEnd) {
        int workedDays = attendance.getWorkedDays(employeeId, periodStart, periodEnd);
        return workedDays * hourlyRate * HOURS_PER_WORK_DAY;
    }

    /** net = gross - all deductions (Method Dictionary row "calculateNetPay"). */
    private double calculateNetPay(double gross, double deductions) {
        if (Double.isNaN(gross) || Double.isNaN(deductions)) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("gross and deductions must be numbers");
        }
        if (deductions < 0) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("deductions cannot be negative: " + deductions);
        }
        return gross - deductions;
    }

    // ---------------------------------------------------------------- helpers

    private static List<GovernmentContributionCalculator> defaultStatutory() {
        List<GovernmentContributionCalculator> calculators = new ArrayList<>();
        calculators.add(new SSSCalculator());
        calculators.add(new PhilHealthCalculator());
        calculators.add(new PagIbigCalculator());
        return calculators;
    }

    private static double amountOf(Map<String, Double> amounts, String code) {
        Double amount = amounts.get(code);
        return amount == null ? 0.0 : amount;
    }

    private static void requireEmployee(Employee employee) {
        if (employee == null) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("employee is required");
        }
    }

    private static void requireAttendance(AttendanceLog attendance) {
        if (attendance == null) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("attendance is required");
        }
    }
package motorphemployee.oop;

/**
 * WithholdingTaxCalculator - BIR progressive withholding tax, 6 brackets up to 35%
 * (MS1 Week 3 CRC: "WithholdingTaxCalculator (Concrete Subclass)").
 *
 * Applied AFTER SSS/PhilHealth/Pag-IBIG, so the input is the salary already net of those
 * three contributions - same as CP2 MainMenu.java:1418 / Dashboard.java:1334.
 *
 * Official matrix (2026-10-27): bracket 1 uses the official excess base of 20,833, not CP2's
 * 20,832 (Home_WithholdingTax_Matrix.xlsx bracket text B3 and SAMPLE B20: taxable 23,400 ->
 * 513.40). CP2 over-withheld PHP 0.20 for every taxable income in [20,833, 33,333] - Issue 4.
 * Brackets 2-6 were already exact and are unchanged.
 */
public class WithholdingTaxCalculator extends GovernmentContributionCalculator {

    /** BIR brackets: upper bound of the bracket, base tax, excess over the previous bound, marginal rate. */
    private static final double[] UPPER_BOUNDS = {20832.0, 33333.0, 66667.0, 166667.0, 666667.0};
    private static final double[] BASE_TAX = {0.0, 0.0, 2500.0, 10833.0, 40833.33};
    private static final double[] LOWER_BOUNDS = {0.0, 20833.0, 33333.0, 66667.0, 166667.0};
    private static final double[] MARGINAL_RATES = {0.0, 0.20, 0.25, 0.30, 0.32};
    private static final double TOP_LOWER_BOUND = 666667.0;
    private static final double TOP_BASE_TAX = 200833.33;
    private static final double TOP_MARGINAL_RATE = 0.35;

    public WithholdingTaxCalculator() {
        super("Withholding Tax", "TAX");
    }

    @Override
    public double calculate(double taxableIncome) {
        double income = requireValidSalary(taxableIncome);

        for (int i = 0; i < UPPER_BOUNDS.length; i++) {
            if (income <= UPPER_BOUNDS[i]) {
                // max(0, ...) guards the 20,832.01-20,832.99 gap between the exempt ceiling and
                // the official 20,833 excess base, so the tax can never come out negative.
                return Math.max(0.0, BASE_TAX[i] + (income - LOWER_BOUNDS[i]) * MARGINAL_RATES[i]);
            }
        }
        return TOP_BASE_TAX + (income - TOP_LOWER_BOUND) * TOP_MARGINAL_RATE;
    }
}

const projectRoot = path.resolve(path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), '../..');
const sourceDir = path.join(projectRoot, 'src/main/java/ph/motorph/web');
const gsonJar = path.join(projectRoot, 'lib/gson-2.13.2.jar');
const timeoutMs = 15_000;
const javaClasses = mkdtempSync(path.join(tmpdir(), 'motorph-e2e-classes-'));
const serverChildren = [];
let browser;

function freePort() {
  return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
    const server = net.createServer();
    server.once('error', reject);
    server.listen(0, '127.0.0.1', () => {
      const { port } = server.address();
      server.close(error => error ? reject(error) : resolve(port));
    });
  });
}

function start(command, args, env, label) {
  const child = spawn(command, args, {
    cwd: projectRoot,
    env,
    detached: process.platform !== 'win32',
    stdio: ['ignore', 'pipe', 'pipe']
  });
  child.log = '';
  child.on('error', error => { child.log += `${label}: ${error.message}\n`; });
  for (const stream of [child.stdout, child.stderr]) {
    stream.setEncoding('utf8');
    stream.on('data', chunk => { child.log = (child.log + chunk).slice(-8000); });
  }
  serverChildren.push(child);
  return child;
}

async function waitForServer(url, child, label) {
  const end = Date.now() + timeoutMs;
  let lastError = 'no response';
  while (Date.now() < end) {
    if (child.exitCode !== null) throw new Error(`${label} exited early.\n${child.log}`);
    try {
      const response = await fetch(url);
      if (response.ok) return response;
      lastError = `HTTP ${response.status}`;
    } catch (error) {
      lastError = error.message;
    }
    await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 150));
  }
  throw new Error(`${label} did not become ready (${lastError}).\n${child.log}`);
}

async function stop(child) {
  if (!child || child.exitCode !== null) return;
  try {
    if (process.platform === 'win32') child.kill('SIGTERM');
    else process.kill(-child.pid, 'SIGTERM');
  } catch { /* already stopped */ }
  await Promise.race([
    new Promise(resolve => child.once('exit', resolve)),
    new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 2500))
  ]);
  if (child.exitCode === null) {
    try {
      if (process.platform === 'win32') child.kill('SIGKILL');
      else process.kill(-child.pid, 'SIGKILL');
    } catch { /* already stopped */ }
  }
}

import { calculatePayrollPreview2026, formatPesoCents } from './payroll-preview-2026.js';

function byId(id) {
  return document.getElementById(id);
}

function value(id) {
  return byId(id).value.trim();
}

function setMoney(id, cents) {
  byId(id).textContent = formatPesoCents(cents);
}

function addBreakdownRow(body, label, employeeCents, employerCents, note) {
  const row = document.createElement('tr');
  const cells = [label, employeeCents === null ? '—' : formatPesoCents(employeeCents),
    employerCents === null ? '—' : formatPesoCents(employerCents), note];
  cells.forEach((text, index) => {
    const cell = document.createElement(index === 0 ? 'th' : 'td');
    if (index === 0) cell.scope = 'row';
    cell.textContent = text;
    row.append(cell);
  });
  body.append(row);
}

export function initPayrollPreview() {
  const form = byId('payroll-preview-form');
  if (!form) return;
  const status = byId('payroll-preview-status');
  const results = byId('payroll-preview-results');

  form.addEventListener('submit', event => {
    event.preventDefault();
    status.classList.remove('payroll-preview-error');
    results.hidden = true;
    const input = {
      period: value('payroll-preview-period'),
      grossCashPay: value('payroll-preview-gross'),
      sssCompensation: value('payroll-preview-sss'),
      philHealthBasicSalary: value('payroll-preview-ph'),
      pagIbigFundSalary: value('payroll-preview-pagibig'),
      taxableCompensation: value('payroll-preview-taxable')
    };

    try {
      const result = calculatePayrollPreview2026(input);
      byId('payroll-results-ruleset').textContent = `${result.rulesetId} · ${result.period}`;
      setMoney('payroll-result-net', result.netPayCents);
      setMoney('payroll-result-employee-total', result.totalEmployeeDeductionsCents);
      setMoney('payroll-result-employer-total', result.totalEmployerContributionsCents);
      setMoney('payroll-result-employer-cost', result.employerCashCostCents);

      const lines = byId('payroll-result-lines');
      lines.replaceChildren();
      addBreakdownRow(lines, 'SSS Social Security + MPF', result.sss.employeeCents,
        result.sss.employerRegularCents, `MSC ${formatPesoCents(result.sss.mscCents)}; 5% employee / 10% employer`);
      addBreakdownRow(lines, 'SSS Employees’ Compensation', 0n, result.sss.ecCents,
        'Employer-only; included in employer contributions total');
      addBreakdownRow(lines, 'PhilHealth premium', result.philHealth.employeeCents,
        result.philHealth.employerCents,
        `5% of MBS base ${formatPesoCents(result.philHealth.premiumBaseCents)}, split equally`);
      addBreakdownRow(lines, 'Pag-IBIG monthly savings', result.pagIbig.employeeCents,
        result.pagIbig.employerCents,
        `Fund Salary base ${formatPesoCents(result.pagIbig.baseCents)} after ₱10,000 cap`);
      addBreakdownRow(lines, 'BIR withholding tax', result.withholdingTaxCents, null,
        `Monthly taxable base ${formatPesoCents(result.taxableAfterEmployeeContributionsCents)} after employee shares`);
      results.hidden = false;
      status.textContent = 'Preview calculated from the entered synthetic bases. Nothing was saved or sent to the API.';
    } catch (error) {
      status.textContent = error instanceof Error ? error.message : 'Could not calculate preview.';
      status.classList.add('payroll-preview-error');
    }
  });
}

  await ticketRow.getByRole('button', { name: new RegExp(`Cancel ${ticketId}`) }).click();
  await page.locator('#ticket-filter-status').selectOption('Cancelled');
  await page.waitForFunction(id => {
    const row = [...document.querySelectorAll('#ticket-rows tr')].find(item => item.textContent.includes(id));
    return row && row.textContent.includes('Cancelled');
  }, ticketId, { timeout: timeoutMs });
  console.log('PASS: ticket submit/queue/cancel flow.');

  await page.reload();
  await page.waitForSelector('#app-shell:not([hidden])', { timeout: timeoutMs });
  await page.waitForFunction(() => document.querySelectorAll('#employee-rows tr').length === 4, { timeout: timeoutMs });
  await page.locator('[data-view="requests"]').click();
  await page.waitForFunction(id => [...document.querySelectorAll('#leave-request-rows tr')]
    .some(row => row.textContent.includes(id) && row.textContent.includes('Cancelled')), leaveId, { timeout: timeoutMs });
  await page.waitForFunction(id => [...document.querySelectorAll('#ticket-rows tr')]
    .some(row => row.textContent.includes(id) && row.textContent.includes('Cancelled')), ticketId, { timeout: timeoutMs });
  console.log('PASS: employee and workflow data survive reload while the local API process runs.');

  const [download] = await Promise.all([
    page.waitForEvent('download'),
    page.locator('#leave-export-button').click()
  ]);
  assert.match(download.suggestedFilename(), /\.csv$/);
  await page.setViewportSize({ width: 390, height: 844 });
  const widths = await page.evaluate(() => ({ viewport: innerWidth, document: document.documentElement.scrollWidth }));
  assert.ok(widths.document <= widths.viewport, `mobile layout overflows: ${JSON.stringify(widths)}`);
  assert.deepEqual(pageErrors, [], `browser errors: ${pageErrors.join('; ')}`);
  console.log(`PASS: CSV download (${download.suggestedFilename()}), mobile width (${widths.document}px), and no page errors.`);
}

try {
  await main();
} finally {
  if (browser) await browser.close().catch(() => {});
  for (const child of serverChildren.reverse()) await stop(child);
  rmSync(javaClasses, { recursive: true, force: true });
}

- Define employee-to-team/branch membership and the supervisor's permitted scope.

### 7. Add HR onboarding/offboarding and employee administration

- Add synthetic onboarding, profile/branch/position changes, deactivation, clearance queues, and search/update screens if required.
- Define effective dates and the effect of mid-cycle changes without guessing payroll behavior.
- Ensure inactive accounts lose access according to an approved policy.

**Done when:** employee lifecycle changes are validated, role-limited, and tested against audit/history requirements.

### 8. Implement the Java payroll engine — currently blocked

- Obtain authoritative rules for pay-cycle boundaries, salary conversion, regular/OT/PTO/holiday/rest-day/undertime treatment, incentives, deductions, statutory contributions, tax, effective dates, and rounding.
- Obtain independent worked expected-value cases, including edge cases; reconcile any conflicting legacy or peer formulas.
- Implement versioned Java domain/calculation services using exact decimal arithmetic; keep formulas out of browser code and Firebase adapters.
- Test each rule independently, then test combined payroll results and reproducibility.

**Hard gate:** the old documents name payroll components and snapshot fields but do not provide enough arithmetic, current values, or exact cutoffs to calculate correctly. Do not activate this task's outputs until those inputs exist and the user's “keep calculations disabled” instruction is explicitly lifted.

**Done when:** independent golden cases match every component and a repeat run uses the same saved rule version.

### 9. Add payroll supervision, adjustments, and approval

- Define rate/incentive/deduction adjustment scope (individual/team/branch/global), approvers, separation of duties, and effective dates.
- Build review/approve/reject flows with immutable audit events and controlled payroll reruns/corrections.
- Generate payroll summaries only from approved, versioned inputs.

**Gate:** depends on approved payroll formulas, values, roles, and correction policy.

### 10. Add payslips, reports, and distribution

- Define the required payslip fields and privacy rules.
- Generate the required output format, store a stable result reference, and verify read-back.
- Add payroll reports/monthly summaries only if required.
- Add email delivery and retry/status tracking only if required and a safe delivery service is configured.

# MotorPH MS2 — browser payroll foundation

An original browser-based prototype with an HTML/CSS interface and Java 11 backend. Employee and attendance data are synthetic. It includes a disposable, client-only 2026 statutory preview with editable/versioned rules; attendance-derived payroll, persisted runs, and payslips remain gated.

## Run locally

Requires JDK 11+, Node.js 20.19+ (or a current supported Node release), and npm.

```sh
npm install
./run.sh
```

Then open <http://localhost:8080>. `run.sh` builds the Vite frontend and serves it from the Java server. Set `PORT` to choose a different HTTP port.

For development with Vite hot reload, use two terminals:

```sh
# terminal 1: Java backend
./run-api.sh

# terminal 2: frontend
npm run dev
```

Open <http://localhost:5173>. Vite proxies `/api` calls to the Java service at `http://127.0.0.1:8080` by default; set `API_PROXY_TARGET` to use a different backend. Set `HOST=127.0.0.1` for the Java backend when Vite is proxying it locally.

Run Java domain checks:

```sh
./test.sh
```

Run browser end-to-end checks (the suite starts isolated local API/Vite processes, uses only synthetic in-memory records, and cleans them up on exit):

```sh
npx playwright-core install chromium
# Linux, if system libraries are missing:
sudo npx playwright-core install-deps chromium
npm run test:e2e
```

Optional live Firebase Auth lifecycle smoke test:

```sh
npm run test:firebase-auth
```

This uses `.env.local`, creates one uniquely named disposable Auth account, verifies sign-in, empty user-scoped reads, and sign-out on localhost, makes **no Firestore writes**, and deletes the Auth account in cleanup. It needs network access and should not be run concurrently with another live Auth test.

The app uses a small vendored Gson JAR for the Java Firestore REST adapter; its license is recorded in `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` and `third_party/licenses/`.

## Firebase development sandbox

- `.env.local` contains the Firebase **Web** app config used by the browser SDK; `.gitignore` lists this file. The user-supplied Web API key for `motorph-jd` is installed assistant-side. The user does not need to edit `.env.local`.
- The Web API key is a public client identifier, not a server credential. Do not add a service-account key or Admin SDK credentials.
- Authentication uses Email/Password and in-memory browser persistence. Live disposable-account creation/sign-in, empty user-scoped reads, and sign-out now pass on localhost; the test Auth account was deleted. Do not use real staff accounts or data.
- Firestore requests are made by the Java backend through the REST API, forwarding the signed-in user's Firebase ID token. Firestore Security Rules authorize those requests; no privileged server identity bypasses the rules.
- The app uses `users/{uid}/demoEmployees`, `demoAttendance`, `demoLeaveRequests`, and `demoTickets`. Workflow documents are owner-scoped with no reviewer or delete permission in the candidate rules. The opt-in seed writes fictional employee/attendance records only.
- The user published the updated `docs/firestore.rules`. Live Firebase smoke testing with disposable accounts verified owner-scoped employee create/update, leave and ticket create/cancel/read-back, and a cross-user denial (`403`). Both disposable Auth accounts and employee documents were deleted; one cancelled synthetic leave and one cancelled synthetic ticket remain under their deleted test UIDs because workflow deletes are intentionally denied (`LV-3502C01F0E60`, `TK-F05DD2B0D6CC`). No real employee data or credentials were used. These are **development-only** rules, not production role/HR policy.
- If Firebase is not configured locally, the app uses the in-memory synthetic fixture. No Firebase writes are made in that mode.
- `measurementId` / Firebase Analytics is not used.
- Browser auth is verified on `localhost`. The current Arena preview host is `8080-is3s38ic4lxn7e4e77g8b.e2b.app`; its authorized-domain status could not be tested from the sandbox because Arena's traffic-access token is injected only in the user preview session. If the preview reports `auth/unauthorized-domain`, add that exact host under Firebase Console → Authentication → Settings → Authorized domains.

See `docs/firebase-setup-guide.md` for the console checkpoint and `docs/firestore.rules` for the development rules.

## What works

- Overview with live sandbox counts, searchable employee directory/detail, HR directory search/status filters, a synthetic directory-label summary, raw attendance register and coverage report, Requests & tickets, searchable read-only Team roster, and the payroll rules gate. Employee details open from a native keyboard-operable button without overriding table semantics; result counts and form feedback use polite status regions.
- Java employee/attendance services plus a workflow service. Local preview workflow records are held in Java process memory; Firebase mode uses the signed-in user’s Firestore subcollections.
- Leave requests and tickets validate inputs, derive employee names from the caller’s own synthetic directory, show documented queue labels, and support owner-sandbox cancellation. A monthly leave-request calendar displays pending/cancelled request dates only and can draft form bounds from two selected dates; it does not imply approval, submit a request, calculate days, or show balances. Search/status and inclusive requested-date-overlap filters narrow the leave history table only; they do not change the calendar markers or all-record exports. Row details reveal the submitted note/message and UTC timestamps without adding a reviewer workflow. Both local and Firestore workflow histories are ordered newest first. No reviewer/approval/resolve/delete routes exist. The user has published the rules; live tests confirmed leave and ticket create/cancel persistence, plus cross-user denial.
- Read-only Team roster plus a synthetic directory editor. In Firebase mode, signed-in users can create/edit only name, department, role label, location, and demo status in their own sandbox. Local preview has no user authentication and shares one process-memory store for that API process. IDs are server-generated; delete, termination, schedule, salary, and government-ID fields are not exposed. New records receive no schedule mapping, so their raw attendance view is empty. This is not an HR role or a production employee-admin workflow.
- CSV export for currently visible synthetic employee results and Team roster rows, loaded raw attendance rows, attendance coverage reports, synthetic directory label-count summaries, and owner-sandbox workflow records. CSV cells are quoted and spreadsheet-formula prefixes are neutralized; exports contain no derived hours or payroll values.
- Server-side employee search/detail, HR table search/status filters, a user-scoped attendance-coverage report (raw row counts and first/last record dates by configured mapping), synthetic directory label counts by status/department with CSV export, and dynamic overview counts. Unmapped employees are labeled as unmapped, not absent. The attendance date fields default to that employee's earliest/latest available records, following the earlier MO-IT108 Requirements Analysis; the user can narrow the range. This is not a payroll-period calendar. No paid hours, deductions, or pay are calculated.
- Firebase email/password sign-in, development-account creation, and password-reset email UI; reset responses do not disclose whether an email has an account. The app stays behind the sign-in gate when Firebase config is complete.
- `/api/health`, employee list/search/detail plus owner-sandbox create/update, raw attendance query and coverage report, owner-scoped workflow list/create/cancel routes, and opt-in demo seed endpoint.
- Verification: `npm run test:web` passes 23 workflow/calendar/filter/CSV tests; `./test.sh` passes 167 Java checks; `npm run test:e2e` passes the local browser flow for employee create/edit, HR/Team filters and roster CSV, empty unscheduled attendance, raw directory-label summary/CSV, reversed-date rejection, leave/ticket submit/cancel and detail disclosures, calendar date drafting, inclusive leave-range filters, raw attendance summary/report filtering, drill-through and CSV, simulated workflow/report authorization and service failures with recovery, reload persistence, and mobile width; `npm run build` passes; `npm audit` reports 0 vulnerabilities. An isolated live Firebase auth-lifecycle browser check passed disposable account creation/sign-in, user-scoped empty Firestore reads, and sign-out on localhost; the account was deleted and no Firestore writes were made. The exact Arena preview-origin sign-in remains unverified.

## Not implemented / important limits

- No production hosting, HR authorization roles, admin controls, audit trail, backup, or production security review. The built-in JDK HTTP server is a learning prototype, not a hardened public service.
- No live employee, attendance, or payroll information. Do not use this prototype for payroll processing.
- A temporary 2026 monthly statutory preview is available with explicit synthetic inputs; its formulas/rates are isolated in `web/payroll-rules-2026.js` and `web/payroll-preview-2026.js`. There is still no work-hour derivation, attendance-to-gross formula, semi-monthly tax/split handling, saved payroll run, or payslip. The supplied material does not define the full attendance mechanics or exact cutoff/deduction allocation, so those are not inferred.
- Leave/ticket records are persistent only in the signed-in user’s sandbox after the updated rules are published; the current local preview uses process memory. There is no supervisor/reviewer role, real queue delivery, approval, notification, audit trail, team assignment, HR lifecycle editing, attendance import, or approved source-system integration.

## Source and attribution

`docs/source-grounding-and-open-rules.md` records supplied-source facts, scope boundaries, and unresolved ambiguities. `docs/acceptance-baseline.md` captures the current source-grounded behavior and gates as a draft, not an approved rubric. `docs/candidate-policy-review.md` reviews the user's database design and later calculator, peer assumptions, official statutory sources, and a net-pay reference; it distinguishes the enabled temporary monthly statutory preview from still-gated attendance/pay-period mechanics. `docs/legacy-mo-it108-traceability.md` maps the user's earlier MotorPH requirements/design documents to the current prototype and explains the feature-parity estimate. `docs/peer-parity-roadmap.md` lists the remaining phases and acceptance gates to reach broad peer-level feature parity. The restrained title stripe adapts a small MIT-licensed `system.css` motif; exact attribution and licenses are listed in `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`.

package motorphpayrollsystem;

public class ContributionCalculator {

    public ContributionCalculator() {
        // Helper class for payroll contributions and withholding tax.
    }

    // SSS contribution for one semi-monthly pay period.
    // Uses the original CP2 SSS contribution table.
    public double calculateSSS(double salary) {
        validateAmount(salary);

        double monthly = salary * 2.0;
        double monthlySSS;

        if (monthly < 3250) monthlySSS = 135.00;
        else if (monthly < 3750) monthlySSS = 157.50;
        else if (monthly < 4250) monthlySSS = 180.00;
        else if (monthly < 4750) monthlySSS = 202.50;
        else if (monthly < 5250) monthlySSS = 225.00;
        else if (monthly < 5750) monthlySSS = 247.50;
        else if (monthly < 6250) monthlySSS = 270.00;
        else if (monthly < 6750) monthlySSS = 292.50;

    // PhilHealth contribution for one semi-monthly pay period.
    // Preserves the original CP2 formula and cap.
    public double calculatePhilHealth(double salary) {
        validateAmount(salary);

        double monthly = salary * 2.0;
        double monthlyPhilHealth = Math.min(monthly * 0.015, 900.00);

        return monthlyPhilHealth / 2.0;
    }

    // Pag-IBIG contribution for one semi-monthly pay period.
    // Preserves the original CP2 percentage and cap.
    public double calculatePagIBIG(double salary) {
        validateAmount(salary);

        double monthly = salary * 2.0;
        double monthlyPagIBIG;

        if (monthly <= 1500) {
            monthlyPagIBIG = monthly * 0.01;
        } else {
            monthlyPagIBIG = Math.min(monthly * 0.02, 100.00);
        }

        return monthlyPagIBIG / 2.0;
    }

    // Adds the three government contributions.
    public double calculateTotalContributions(
            double sss,
            double philHealth,
            double pagIBIG) {

        validateAmount(sss);
        validateAmount(philHealth);
        validateAmount(pagIBIG);

        return sss + philHealth + pagIBIG;
    }

    // Withholding tax for one semi-monthly pay period.
    // Input must already be taxable income AFTER government contributions.
    // Uses the original CP2 withholding-tax brackets.
    public double calculateWithholdingTax(double taxableIncome) {
        validateAmount(taxableIncome);

        double taxable = taxableIncome * 2.0;
        double monthlyTax;

        if (taxable <= 20833) {
            monthlyTax = 0.0;
        } else if (taxable <= 33333) {
            monthlyTax = (taxable - 20833) * 0.20;
        } else if (taxable <= 66667) {
            monthlyTax = 2500 + (taxable - 33333) * 0.25;
        } else if (taxable <= 166667) {
            monthlyTax = 10833 + (taxable - 66667) * 0.30;
        } else if (taxable <= 666667) {
            monthlyTax = 40833 + (taxable - 166667) * 0.32;
        } else {
            monthlyTax = 200833 + (taxable - 666667) * 0.35;
        }

        return monthlyTax / 2.0;
    }

    // Prevent invalid amounts from entering payroll calculations.
    private void validateAmount(double amount) {
        if (!Double.isFinite(amount) || amount < 0) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException(
                    "Payroll amount must be valid and nonnegative."
            );
        }
    }
}
package motorphpayrollsystem;

public class PayrollCalculator {

    public PayrollCalculator() {
    }

    public double calculateRegularPay(Employee employee) {
        if (employee == null) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException(
                    "Employee cannot be null."
            );
        }

        double regularPay = employee.calculatePay();

        if (!Double.isFinite(regularPay) || regularPay < 0) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException(
                    "Regular pay must be a valid nonnegative amount."
            );
        }

        return regularPay;
    }

    public double calculateOvertimePay(
            Employee employee,
            AttendanceRecord attendance,
            OvertimeRequest overtime) {

        if (employee == null || attendance == null) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException(
                    "Employee and attendance are required."
            );
        }

        if (overtime == null || !overtime.isApproved()) {
            return 0.0;
        }

        double overtimeHours = attendance.calculateOvertimeHours();
        double approvedHours = overtime.getRequestedHours();

        double payableHours = Math.min(
                overtimeHours,
                approvedHours
        );

        if (payableHours <= 0) {
            return 0.0;
        }

        // Temporary base calculation.
        // Confirm the original CP2 overtime rate before final testing.
        return payableHours * employee.getHourlyRate();
    }

    public double calculateGrossPay(
            double regularPay,
            double overtimePay,
            Employee employee) {

        if (employee == null) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException(
                    "Employee cannot be null."
            );
        }

        if (!Double.isFinite(regularPay) || regularPay < 0 ||
                !Double.isFinite(overtimePay) || overtimePay < 0) {

            throw new IllegalArgumentException(
                    "Pay amounts must be valid and nonnegative."
            );
        }

        double allowances =
                employee.getRiceSubsidy()
                        + employee.getPhoneAllowance()
                        + employee.getClothingAllowance();

        return regularPay + overtimePay + allowances;
    }

# Roadmap to full peer-level MotorPH feature parity

**How to read “100%”:** the nine submitted folders do not share one feature set, so there is no single objective peer-completion percentage. This roadmap uses the richest relevant comparison: the payroll/attendance/leave workflows in the stronger MO-IT110-style submissions (especially folders 6 and 9), plus the user's earlier MO-IT108 Requirements Analysis and System Design. Yes—you did get to the contribution mechanics in a later prior project, and the database design you remembered covers the data structure around them.

Your MO-IT107 database design includes Rates and Tax Table reference data, separate employee/employer contributions, monthly government deductions, payroll, payslip, earnings, deductions, and summary tables. It describes where things go and the sequence of payroll steps, but not the actual rates or formulas. Its rate-versioning fields are also inconsistent across the design and data dictionary.
The later folder-9 project has a PayrollCalculator pipeline and separate contribution calculators. But those formulas are not current for 2026: for example, they use the old SSS maximum of ₱1,125, the prior PhilHealth 3% schedule, and the old Pag-IBIG ₱100 cap. The folder-9 tax calculator also uses 20% for the first taxable band, while the BIR monthly table specifies 15%. Folder 7 and folder 6 contain older CP2-style versions too. I documented the paths and findings in docs/candidate-policy-review.md; I did not copy employee data.

Temporary calculator added

The Payroll page in the current preview now has a disposable 2026 monthly statutory preview. It uses only manually entered fictional amounts, makes no payroll API calls, and saves nothing. Its rules are split so they’re easy to replace:

web/payroll-rules-2026.js — versioned rates, thresholds, tax bands, and source notes.
web/payroll-preview-2026.js — replaceable calculation logic using integer centavos.
The page also shows the sources and assumptions, including the provisional half-up rounding and monthly BIR table basis.

The profile uses the latest effective schedules I found for 2026—not necessarily rules newly issued in 2026: the SSS schedule currently posted is effective January 2025 SSS; PhilHealth’s advisory sets a 5% rate and ₱10,000/₱100,000 floor and ceiling PhilHealth; Pag-IBIG Circular 460 sets the ₱10,000 MFS cap Pag-IBIG; and the BIR monthly table is from Annex E BIR.

For a synthetic ₱25,000 monthly example—using ₱25,000 for each input basis—the preview shows:

Item	Employee	Employer
SSS	₱1,250	₱2,500 + ₱30 EC
PhilHealth	₱625	₱625
Pag-IBIG	₱200	₱200
BIR monthly withholding	₱313.80	—

That produces ₱22,611.20 net and ₱3,355 employer contributions. A third-party reference reports ₱22,611.25 for a similar example because it uses an annualized monthly tax method; the direct BIR monthly table differs by ₱0.05. The preview follows the published monthly table and calls out that discrepancy. Reference
